about: English for texts the Divinum Officium English data does not translate. src: do = the project's own English for the same Latin elsewhere; dr = Douay-Rheims (Challoner); ai = translated for this project.

eteritindieillaadicietdominussecundomanu.en: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall set his hand the second time to possess the remnant of his people, which shall be left from the Assyrians, and from Egypt, and from Phetros, and from Ethiopia, and from Elam, and from Sennaar, and from Emath, and from the islands of the sea.
eteritindieillaadicietdominussecundomanu.la: Et erit in die illa: adíciet Dóminus secúndo manum suam ad possidéndum resíduum pópuli sui, quod relinquétur ab Assýriis, et ab Ægýpto, et a Phetros, et ab Æthiópia, et ab Ælam, et a Sénnaar, et ab Emath, et ab ínsulis maris.

etlevabitsignuminnationesetcongregabitpr.en: And he shall set up a standard unto the nations, and shall assemble the fugitives of Israel, and shall gather together the dispersed of Juda from the four quarters of the earth.
etlevabitsignuminnationesetcongregabitpr.la: Et levábit signum in natiónes, et congregábit prófugos Israël, et dispérsos Juda cólliget a quátuor plagis terræ.

etaufereturzelusephraimethostesiudaperib.en: And the envy of Ephraim shall be taken away, and the enemies of Juda shall perish.
etaufereturzelusephraimethostesiudaperib.la: Et auferétur zelus Ephraim, et hostes Juda períbunt.

sanctumetterribilenomeneiusinitiumsapien.en: Holy and terrible * is His Name; the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.
sanctumetterribilenomeneiusinitiumsapien.la: Sanctum et terríbile * nomen ejus, inítium sapiéntiæ timor Dómini. Ps. 84

omnisquiinvocaveritnomendominisalvuserit.en: Whosoever shall call * on the name of the Lord shall be saved.
omnisquiinvocaveritnomendominisalvuserit.la: Omnis * qui invocáverit nomen Dómini, salvus erit. Ps. 47

egoautemindominogaudebetexsultaboindeoie.en: But I will rejoice * in the Lord: and I will joy in God my Jesus.
egoautemindominogaudebetexsultaboindeoie.la: Ego autem * in Dómino gaudébo, et exsultábo in Deo Jesu meo. Ps. 98

sacrificabohostiamlaudisetnomendominiinv.en: I will offer * the sacrifice of thanksgiving, and will call upon the Name of the Lord.
sacrificabohostiamlaudisetnomendominiinv.la: Sacrificábo * hóstiam laudis, et nomen Dómini invocábo. Ps. 263, 264, 265

innomineiesuomnegenuflectaturcelestiumte.en: At the name of Jesus let every knee bow, of things in heaven, of things on earth, and of things under the earth:
innomineiesuomnegenuflectaturcelestiumte.la: In nómine Jesu omne genu flectátur cæléstium, terréstrium et infernórum:

sequentiasanctievangeliisecundummattheum.en: Continuation + of the Holy Gospel according to Matthew

vespereabiisquimissevespertineincenadomi.en: Today, Vespers are not said by those who assist at the evening Mass of the Lord's Supper.
vespereabiisquimissevespertineincenadomi.la: Vesperæ ab iis qui Missæ vespertinæ in Cena Domini intersunt, hodie non dicuntur.

vespereabiisquisolemniactioniliturgicepo.en: Today, Vespers are not said by those who assist at the solemn afternoon liturgical action.
vespereabiisquisolemniactioniliturgicepo.la: Vesperæ ab iis qui solemni Actioni liturgicæ postmeridianæ intersunt, hodie non dicuntur.

quodsichristusnonresurrexitvanestfidesve.en: And if Christ be not risen again, your faith is vain, for you are yet in your sins.
quodsichristusnonresurrexitvanestfidesve.la: Quod si Christus non resurréxit, vana est fides vestra: adhuc enim estis in peccátis vestris.

ergetquidormieruntinchristoperierunt.en: Then they also that are fallen asleep in Christ, are perished.
ergetquidormieruntinchristoperierunt.la: Ergo et qui dormiérunt in Christo, periérunt.

siinhacvitatantuminchristosperantessumus.en: If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable.
siinhacvitatantuminchristosperantessumus.la: Si in hac vita tantum in Christo sperántes sumus, miserabilióres sumus ómnibus homínibus.

nuncautemchristusresurrexitamortuisprimi.en: But now Christ is risen from the dead, the firstfruits of them that sleep
nuncautemchristusresurrexitamortuisprimi.la: Nunc autem Christus resurréxit a mórtuis primítiæ dormiéntium,

quoniamquidemperhominemmorsetperhominemr.en: For by a man came death, and by a man the resurrection of the dead.
quoniamquidemperhominemmorsetperhominemr.la: quóniam quidem per hóminem mors, et per hóminem resurréctio mortuórum.

etsicutinadamomnesmoriunturitetinchristo.en: And as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all shall be made alive.
etsicutinadamomnesmoriunturitetinchristo.la: Et sicut in Adam omnes moriúntur, ita et in Christo omnes vivificabúntur.

sermosanctimaximiepiscopi.en: From the Sermons of St Maximus, Bishop [of Turin.]

quodautemsuscitaviteumamortuisampliusiam.en: And to shew that he raised him up from the dead, not to return now any more to corruption, he said thus: I will give you the holy things of David faithful.
quodautemsuscitaviteumamortuisampliusiam.la: Quod autem suscitávit eum a mórtuis, ámplius jam non reversúrum in corruptiónem, ita dixit: Quia dabo vobis sancta David fidélia.

ideoqueetaliasdicitnondabissanctumtuumvi.en: And therefore, in another place also, he saith: Thou shalt not suffer thy holy one to see corruption.
ideoqueetaliasdicitnondabissanctumtuumvi.la: Ideóque et álias dicit: Non dabis sanctum tuum vidére corruptiónem.

davideniminsuagenerationecumadministrass.en: For David, when he had served in his generation, according to the will of God, slept: and was laid unto his fathers, and saw corruption.
davideniminsuagenerationecumadministrass.la: David enim in sua generatióne cum administrásset, voluntáti Dei dormívit: et appósitus est ad patres suos, et vidit corruptiónem.

quemverodeussuscitavitamortuisnonviditco.en: But he whom God hath raised from the dead, saw no corruption.
quemverodeussuscitavitamortuisnonviditco.la: Quem vero Deus suscitávit a mórtuis, non vidit corruptiónem.

hocautemfactumestperbienniumitautomnesqu.en: And this continued for the space of two years, so that all they who dwelt in Asia, heard the word of the Lord, both Jews and Gentiles.
hocautemfactumestperbienniumitautomnesqu.la: Hoc autem factum est per biénnium, ita ut omnes qui habitábant in Asia audírent verbum Dómini, Judǽi atque gentíles.

virtutesquenonquaslibetfaciebatdeusperma.en: And God wrought by the hand of Paul more than common miracles.
virtutesquenonquaslibetfaciebatdeusperma.la: Virtutésque non quáslibet faciébat Deus per manum Pauli,

itautetiamsuperlanguidosdeferrenturacorp.en: So that even there were brought from his body to the sick, handkerchiefs and aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the wicked spirits went out of them.
itautetiamsuperlanguidosdeferrenturacorp.la: ita ut étiam super lánguidos deferréntur a córpore ejus sudária et semicínctia, et recedébant ab eis languóres, et spíritus nequam egrediebántur.

sermosanctiaugustiniepiscopi.en: From the Sermons of St. Augustine, Bishop (of Hippo.)

sedetsuperservosmeosetancillasindiebusil.en: Moreover upon my servants and handmaids in those days I will pour forth my spirit.
sedetsuperservosmeosetancillasindiebusil.la: Sed et super servos meos et ancíllas in diébus illis effúndam spíritum meum.

etdaboprodigiainceletinterrasanguinemeti.en: And I will shew wonders in heaven; and in earth, blood, and fire, and vapour of smoke.
etdaboprodigiainceletinterrasanguinemeti.la: Et dabo prodígia in cælo et in terra, sánguinem, et ignem, et vapórem fumi.

solconverteturintenebrasetlunainsanguine.en: The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood: before the great and dreadful day of the Lord doth come.
solconverteturintenebrasetlunainsanguine.la: Sol convertétur in ténebras, et luna in sánguinem, ántequam véniat dies Dómini magnus et horríbilis.

eteritomnisquiinvocaveritnomendominisalv.en: And it shall come to pass, that every one that shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved: for in mount Sion, and in Jerusalem shall be salvation, as the Lord hath said, and in the residue whom the Lord shall call.
eteritomnisquiinvocaveritnomendominisalv.la: Et erit: omnis qui invocáverit nomen Dómini, salvus erit: quia in monte Sion et in Jerúsalem erit salvátio, sicut dixit Dóminus, et in resíduis quos Dóminus vocáverit.

gloriatibidomine.en: Glory be to thee, O Lord,

quicordefundisgratiam.en: Who pourest grace forth from thy Heart,

cumpatreetsanctospiritu.en: With the Father and the Holy Ghost,

planxitautemdavidplanctumagnosupersaulet.en: And David lamented with a great lamentation over Saul and his sons, and said: How are the valiant fallen in battle,
planxitautemdavidplanctumagnosupersaulet.la: Planxit autem David planctu magno super Saül, et fílios ejus, et dixit: Quómodo cecidérunt fortes in bello,

etperieruntarmabellicainclytiisrelflete.en: And the weapons of war have perished; weep, ye renowned of Israel.
etperieruntarmabellicainclytiisrelflete.la: Et periérunt arma béllica; ínclyti Israël, flete.

montesgelbenecrosnecpluviasupervosdescen.en: Ye mountains of Gelboe, let neither dew nor rain come down upon you, where many wounded have fallen:
montesgelbenecrosnecpluviasupervosdescen.la: Montes Gélboë, nec ros nec plúvia super vos descéndant, ubi cecidérunt vulneráti multi:

nolitezelaremorteminerrorevitevestrenequ.en: Seek not death in the error of your life, neither procure ye destruction by the works of your hands.
nolitezelaremorteminerrorevitevestrenequ.la: Nolíte zeláre mortem in erróre vitæ vestræ, neque acquirátis perditiónem in opéribus mánuum vestrárum.

quoniamdeusmortemnonfecitnecletaturinper.en: For God made not death, neither hath he pleasure in the destruction of the living.
quoniamdeusmortemnonfecitnecletaturinper.la: Quóniam Deus mortem non fecit, nec lætátur in perditióne vivórum.

perquemmihimunduscrucifixusestetegomundo.en: By whom the world is crucified to me, and I to the world.
perquemmihimunduscrucifixusestetegomundo.la: Per quem mihi mundus crucifíxus est, et ego mundo.

benedictatuinmulieribusetbenedictusfruct.en: Blessed art thou * among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.
benedictatuinmulieribusetbenedictusfruct.la: Benedícta tu in muliéribus, et benedíctus fructus ventris tui

oculieiussicutcolumbesuperrivulosaquarum.en: His eyes as doves upon brooks of waters, which are washed with milk, and sit beside the plentiful streams.
oculieiussicutcolumbesuperrivulosaquarum.la: Oculi ejus sicut colúmbæ super rívulos aquárum, quæ lacte sunt lotæ, et résident juxta fluénta pleníssima.

dominesituesiubemevenireadtesuperaquaset.en: Lord, if it be Thou, bid me come unto thee on the water; And Jesus stretched forth His Hand,
dominesituesiubemevenireadtesuperaquaset.la: Dómine, † si tu es, jube me veníre ad te super aquas. Et exténdens manum apprehéndit eum,

etdixitiesusmodicefideiquaredubitasti.en: And Jesus said: O thou of little faith, why didst thou doubt?
etdixitiesusmodicefideiquaredubitasti.la: Et dixit Jesus : Modicæ fidei, quare dubitásti?

cumquevidissetventumvalidumvenientemtimu.en: But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid and, beginning to sink, he cried, saying: Lord, save me!
cumquevidissetventumvalidumvenientemtimu.la: Cumque vidísset ventum válidum veniéntem, tímuit; et, cum cœpísset mergi, clamávit dicens: Dómine, salvum me fac.

luxetdecusecclesie.en: Light and glory of the Church,

quostotmandatisinstruis.en: Those whom thou teachest by so many precepts.

sitpatrilausingenito.en: Praise be to the unbegotten Father,

situtriusqueparili.en: To the equal of them both,

utdigniefficiamurpromissionibuschristi.en: That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

gloriapatrigenitequeproli.en: Glory to the Father and to the begotten Son,

ettibicomparutriusquesemper.en: And to thee, equal of them both for ever,

spiritusalmedeusunusomni.en: O loving Spirit, one God, through every

etsimilitudoanimaliumaspectuseorumquasic.en: And as for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like that of burning coals of fire, and like the appearance of lamps. This was the vision running to and fro in the midst of the living creatures, a bright fire, and lightning going forth from the fire.
etsimilitudoanimaliumaspectuseorumquasic.la: Et similitúdo animálium, aspéctus eórum quasi carbónum ignis ardéntium, et quasi aspéctus lampadárum.

quisurrexistiamortuis.en: Who didst rise again from the dead,

coronaconfitentium.en: Crown of them that confess thee,

quirespuentesterrea.en: Who those that spurn the things of earth

ignoscequoddeliquimus.en: Forgive the wrong that we have done.

deopatrisitgloria.en: To God the Father be glory,

sanctispiritusetanimeiustorumhymnumdicit.en: O ye holy Spirits and Souls of the righteous, bless ye the Lord. Alleluia.
sanctispiritusetanimeiustorumhymnumdicit.la: Sancti spíritus * et ánimæ justórum, hymnum dícite Deo, allelúja.

adiutormeusestonederelinquasme.en: Be thou my helper, forsake me not.
adiutormeusestonederelinquasme.la: Adjútor meus esto, ne derelínquas me.

lectiosanctievangeliisecundummattheum.en: From the Holy Gospel according to Matthew

inillotemporedixitpetrusadiesumeccenosre.en: At that time: Peter said to Jesus: Behold we have left all things, and have followed thee: what therefore shall we have? And so on.
inillotemporedixitpetrusadiesumeccenosre.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Petrus ad Jesum: Ecce nos relíquimus ómnia, et secúti sumus te: quid ergo erit nobis? Et réliqua.

homiliasanctibedevenerabilispresbyteri.en: Homily by the Venerable Bede, Priest (at Jarrow.)

dabosanctismeislocumnominatuminregnopatr.en: I will give unto My Saints a place * in the kingdom of My Father, every one by his own name, saith the Lord.
dabosanctismeislocumnominatuminregnopatr.la: Dabo * Sanctis meis locum nominátum in regno Patris mei, dicit Dóminus.

quinatusesdevirgine.en: Who wast born of the Virgin,

hecdicitdominusexercituumadhuceritinloco.en: Thus saith the Lord of hosts: There shall be again in this place that is desolate without man, and without beast, and in all the cities thereof, an habitation of shepherds causing their flocks to lie down.
hecdicitdominusexercituumadhuceritinloco.la: Hæc dicit Dóminus exercítuum: Adhuc erit in loco isto desérto, absque hómine et absque juménto, et in cunctis civitátibus ejus, habitáculum pastórum accubántium gregum.

incivitatibusmontuosisetincivitatibuscam.en: And in the cities on the mountains, and in the cities of the plains, and in the cities that are towards the south: and in the land of Benjamin, and round about Jerusalem, and in the cities of Juda shall the flocks pass again under the hand of him that numbereth them, saith the Lord.
incivitatibusmontuosisetincivitatibuscam.la: In civitátibus montuósis, et in civitátibus campéstribus, et in civitátibus quæ ad austrum sunt, et in terra Béniamin, et in circúitu Jerúsalem, et in civitátibus Juda, adhuc transíbunt greges ad manum numerántis, ait Dóminus.

eccediesveniuntdicitdominusetsuscitabove.en: Behold the days come, saith the Lord, that I will perform the good word that I have spoken to the house of Israel, and to the house of Juda.
eccediesveniuntdicitdominusetsuscitabove.la: Ecce dies véniunt, dicit Dóminus, et suscitábo verbum bonum quod locútus sum ad domum Israël et ad domum Juda.

indiebusillisetintemporeillogerminarefac.en: In those days, and at that time, I will make the bud of justice to spring forth unto David, and he shall do judgment and justice in the earth.
indiebusillisetintemporeillogerminarefac.la: In diébus illis et in témpore illo germináre fáciam David germen justítiæ, et fáciet judícium et justítiam in terra.

indiebusillissalvabituriudetierusalemhab.en: In those days shall Juda be saved, and Jerusalem shall dwell securely: and this is the name that they shall call him, The Lord our just one.
indiebusillissalvabituriudetierusalemhab.la: In diébus illis salvábitur Juda, et Jerúsalem habitábit confidénter: et hoc est nomen quod vocábunt eum: Dóminus justus noster.

quiahecdicitdominusnoninteribitdedavidvi.en: For thus saith the Lord: There shall not be cut off from David a man to sit upon the throne of the house of Israel.
quiahecdicitdominusnoninteribitdedavidvi.la: Quia hæc dicit Dóminus: Non interíbit de David vir qui sédeat super thronum domus Israël.

eteritnomeneiusgloriosum.en: And His name shall be glorious.

deusalibanovenietetsanctusdemonteumbrose.en: God shall come from Lebanon, and the Holy One from the thick and shady mountain.
deusalibanovenietetsanctusdemonteumbrose.la: Deus a Líbano véniet, et Sanctus de monte umbróso et condénso.

etfactumestverbumdominiadieremiamdicens.en: And the word of the Lord came to Jeremias, saying:
etfactumestverbumdominiadieremiamdicens.la: Et factum est verbum Dómini ad Jeremíam, dicens:

hecdicitdominussiirritumpotestfieripactu.en: Thus saith the Lord: If my covenant with the day can be made void, and my covenant with the night, that there should not be day and night in their season:
hecdicitdominussiirritumpotestfieripactu.la: Hæc dicit Dóminus: Si írritum potest fíeri pactum meum cum die, et pactum meum cum nocte, ut non sit dies et nox in témpore suo,

etpactummeumirritumessepoteritcumdavidse.en: Also my covenant with David my servant may be made void, that he should not have a son to reign upon his throne, and with the Levites and priests my ministers.
etpactummeumirritumessepoteritcumdavidse.la: et pactum meum írritum esse póterit cum David servo meo, ut non sit ex eo fílius qui regnet in throno ejus, et Levítæ et sacerdótes minístri mei.

sicutienumerarinonpossuntstellecelietmet.en: As the stars of heaven cannot be numbered, nor the sand of the sea be measured: so will I multiply the seed of David my servant, and the Levites my ministers.
sicutienumerarinonpossuntstellecelietmet.la: Sícuti enumerári non possunt stellæ cæli, et metíri aréna maris, sic multiplicábo semen David servi mei, et Levítas minístros meos.

venidomineetnolitardarerelaxafacinoraple.en: O Lord, come and make no tarrying loose the bonds of thy people.
venidomineetnolitardarerelaxafacinoraple.la: Veni, Dómine, et noli tardáre, reláxa facínora plebi tuæ.

sermosanctiioannisdamasceni.en: From the Sermons of St. John of Damascus.

clamaveruntiustietdominusexaudiviteosete.en: When the just cry out the Lord hears them, and from all their distress He rescues them.
clamaveruntiustietdominusexaudiviteosete.la: Clamavérunt justi, et Dóminus exáudi-vit eos: et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus eórum liberávit eos.

homiliasanctileonispape.en: Homily by Pope St. Leo (the Great.)

sermoxxivdenativdominicapet.en: Sermon XXIV; 4th on the Nativity of the Lord; ch. 1 and 2
sermoxxivdenativdominicapet.la: Sermo XXIV; de Nativ. Dómini 4; cap. 1 et 2

sicutletantiumomniumnostrumhabitatiestin.en: O Holy Mother of God * all we who dwell in thee are in gladness.
sicutletantiumomniumnostrumhabitatiestin.la: Sicut lætántium * ómnium nostrum habitátio est in te, † sancta Dei Génetrix. Ps. 86

posuistidominesupercaputeiuscoronamdelap.en: O Lord, Thou hast set a crown * of precious stones upon his head.
posuistidominesupercaputeiuscoronamdelap.la: Posuísti, Dómine, super caput ejus corónam de lápide pretióso:

desideriumanimeeiustribuistieietvoluntat.en: You have granted him his heart's desire; You refused not the wish of his lips.
desideriumanimeeiustribuistieietvoluntat.la: Desidérium ánimæ ejus tribuísti ei, et voluntáte labiórum ejus non fraudásti eum.

inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuisvos.en: In that time Jesus said to His disciples: You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt lose its savour, wherewith shall it be salted? It is good for nothing any more but to be cast out, and to be trodden on by men. You are the light of the world. A city seated on a mountain cannot be hid. Neither do men light a candle and put it under a bushel, but upon a candlestick, that it may shine to all that are in the house. So let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven. Do not think that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets. I am not come to destroy, but to fulfill. For amen I say unto you, till heaven and earth pass, one jot, or one tittle shall not pass of the law, till all be fulfilled. He therefore that shall break one of these least commandments, and shall so teach men, shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven. But he that shall do and teach, he shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuisvos.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis: Vos estis sal terræ. Quod si sal evanúerit, in quo saliétur? ad níhilum valet ultra, nisi ut mittátur foras, et conculcétur ab homínibus. Vos estis lux mundi. Non potest cívitas abscóndi supra montem pósita, neque accéndunt lucérnam, et ponunt eam sub módio, sed super candelábrum, ut lúceat ómnibus qui in domo sunt. Sic lúceat lux vestra coram homínibus: ut vídeant ópera vestra bona, et gloríficent Patrem vestrum, qui in cælis est. Nolíte putáre quóniam veni sólvere legem aut prophétas: non veni sólvere, sed adimplére. Amen quippe dico vobis, donec tránseat cælum et terra, iota unum aut unus apex non præteríbit a lege, donec ómnia fiant. Qui ergo sólverit unum de mandátis istis mínimis, et docúerit sic hómines, mínimus vocábitur in regno cælórum: qui autem fécerit et docúerit, hic magnus vocábitur in regno cælórum.

stetitangelusiuxtaaramtemplihabensthurib.en: An Angel stood at the Altar * of the Temple, having a golden censer in his hand.
stetitangelusiuxtaaramtemplihabensthurib.la: Stetit Angelus * juxta aram templi, habens thuríbulum áureum in manu sua. Ps. 95

etresponditdominusangeloquiloquebaturinm.en: And the Lord answered the angel, that spoke in me, good words, comfortable words.
etresponditdominusangeloquiloquebaturinm.la: Et respóndit Dóminus ángelo qui loquebátur in me verba bona, verba consolatória.

etdixitadmeangelusquiloquebaturinmeclama.en: And the angel that spoke in me, said to me: Cry thou, saying: Thus saith the Lord of hosts: I am zealous for Jerusalem, and Sion with a great zeal.
etdixitadmeangelusquiloquebaturinmeclama.la: Et dixit ad me ángelus qui loquebátur in me: Clama, dicens: Hæc dicit Dóminus exercítuum: Zelátus sum Jerúsalem et Sion zelo magno.

etiramagnegoirascorsupergentesopulentasq.en: And I am angry with a great anger with the wealthy nations: for I was angry a little, but they helped forward the evil.
etiramagnegoirascorsupergentesopulentasq.la: Et ira magna ego iráscor super gentes opuléntas, quia ego irátus sum parum, ipsi vero adiuvérunt in malum.

proptereahecdicitdominusrevertaradierusa.en: Therefore thus saith the Lord: I will return to Jerusalem in mercies: my house shall be built in it, saith the Lord of hosts: and the building line shall be stretched forth upon Jerusalem.
proptereahecdicitdominusrevertaradierusa.la: Proptérea hæc dicit Dóminus: Revértar ad Jerúsalem in misericórdiis, et domus mea ædificábitur in ea, ait Dóminus exercítuum, et perpendículum extendétur super Jerúsalem.

ecceegomittoangelummeumquipreparabitviam.en: Behold I send My angel * which shall prepare My way before thy face.
ecceegomittoangelummeumquipreparabitviam.la: Ecce ego * mitto Angelum meum, qui præparábit viam meam ante fáciem tuam.

precedetqueteangelusmeus.en: And my angel shall go before thee.

gaudeteetexsultatequoniammercesvestracop.en: Rejoice, and be exceeding glad, for great is your reward in heaven.
gaudeteetexsultatequoniammercesvestracop.la: Gaudéte * et exsultáte quóniam merces vestra copiósa est in cælis.

sevumqueaverniprincipem.en: And the cruel prince of hell

deopatricumfilio.en: To God the Father with the Son,

sanctosimulparaclito.en: And likewise to the Holy Paraclete,

respicitefiliinationeshominumetscitotequ.en: My children behold the generations of men: and know ye that no one hath hoped in the Lord, and hath been confounded.
respicitefiliinationeshominumetscitotequ.la: Respícite fílii natiónes hóminum: et scitóte quia nullus sperávit in Dómino et confúsus est.

aseculononaudieruntnequeauribusperceperu.en: From the beginning of the world they have not heard, nor perceived with the ears: the eye hath not seen, O God, besides thee, what things thou hast prepared for them that wait for thee.
aseculononaudieruntnequeauribusperceperu.la: A sǽculo * non audiérunt, neque áuribus percepérunt: óculus non vidit, Deus, absque te, quæ præparásti exspectántibus te.

dignaremelaudaretevirgosacratadamihivirt.en: Holy Virgin, my praise by thee accepted be; * give me strength against thine enemies.
dignaremelaudaretevirgosacratadamihivirt.la: Dignáre me laudáre te, Virgo sacráta. da mihi virtútem contra hostes tuos.

gaudentincelisanimesanctorumquichristive.en: In heaven do rejoice the souls of the Saints * who have followed the steps of Christ; and because they shed their blood for the love of Christ, therefore shall they be made glad for ever with Christ.
gaudentincelisanimesanctorumquichristive.la: Gaudent in cælis * ánimæ Sanctórum, qui Christi vestígia sunt secúti: et quia pro ejus amóre sánguinem suum fudérunt, ídeo cum Christo exsúltant sine fine.

oquamgloriosumestregnuminquocumchristoga.en: Oh! how glorious is the kingdom * where all the Saints rejoice with Christ; clothed in white robes, they follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth!
oquamgloriosumestregnuminquocumchristoga.la: O quam gloriósum est regnum * in quo cum Christo gaudent omnes Sancti, amícti stolis albis sequúntur Agnum quocúmque íerit!

sitlauspatricumfilio.en: Praise be to the Father, with the Son,

omnesistiingenerationibusgentissuegloria.en: All these have gained glory in their generations, and were praised in their days.
omnesistiingenerationibusgentissuegloria.la: Omnes isti in generatiónibus gentis suæ glóriam adépti sunt, et in diébus suis habéntur in láudibus.

tesponseiesuvirginum.en: Thee, O Jesus, Spouse of virgins,

inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuispar.en: At that time, Jesus said to His disciples: The Kingdom of heaven shall be likened unto ten virgins, which took their lamps, and went forth to meet the Bridegroom and the Bride. And so on.
inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuispar.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis parábolam hanc: Símile erit regnum cælórum decem virgínibus, quæ, accipiéntes lámpades suas, exiérunt óbviam sponso et sponsæ. Et réliqua.

homiliasanctiaugustiniepiscopi.en: Homily by St. Augustine, Bishop (of Hippo.)

queestistaqueascenditdedesertodeliciisaf.en: Who is this that cometh up from the desert, flowing with delights, leaning upon her beloved?
queestistaqueascenditdedesertodeliciisaf.la: Quæ est ista, quæ ascéndit de desérto, delíciis áffluens, inníxa super diléctum suum?

triduanasadominopoposciinduciasutdomumme.en: I have asked the Lord for three days, * that I may consecrate my house as a Church.
triduanasadominopoposciinduciasutdomumme.la: Triduánas * a Dómino popósci indúcias, ut domum meam ecclésiam consecrárem. Ps. 86

accinxitfortitudinelumbossuosetroboravit.en: She hath girded * her loins with strength, and hath strengthened her arm: therefore her lamp shall not be put out for ever.
accinxitfortitudinelumbossuosetroboravit.la: Accínxit * fortitúdine lumbos suos, et roborávit bráchium suum; ideóque lucérna ejus non exstinguétur in sempitérnum. Ps. 98, 249, 250, 251

virgogloriosasemperevangeliumchristigere.en: The glorious maiden * carried the Gospel of Christ always in her breast, and meditated therein day and night talking with God and praying.
virgogloriosasemperevangeliumchristigere.la: Virgo gloriósa * semper Evangélium Christi gerébat in péctore suo, et non diébus neque nóctibus, a collóquiis divínis et oratióne cessábat.

prudentesvirginesaptatevestraslampades.en: Trim your lamps, O ye wise virgins.

eccesponsusvenitexiteobviamei.en: Behold, the Bridegroom cometh, go ye out to meet him.
eccesponsusvenitexiteobviamei.la: Ecce sponsus venit, exíte óbviam ei.

medianocteclamorfactusest.en: At midnight there was a cry made:

quoniamprevenistieuminbenedictionibusdul.en: For Thou hast prevented him with the blessings of sweetness: Thou hast set a crown of precious stones upon his head.
quoniamprevenistieuminbenedictionibusdul.la: Quóniam prævenísti eum in benedictiónibus dulcédinis, posuísti in cápite ejus corónam de lápide pretióso.

deexpositionesanctiambrosiiepiscopiinpsa.en: From the Exposition of the hundred-and-eighteenth Psalm by St. Ambrose, Bishop of Milan.
deexpositionesanctiambrosiiepiscopiinpsa.la: De Expositióne sancti Ambrósii Epíscopi in Psalmum centésimum décimum octávum

iustiauteminperpetuumviventetapuddominum.en: The righteous live * for evermore; their reward also is with the Lord.
iustiauteminperpetuumviventetapuddominum.la: Justi autem in perpétuum vivent, et apud Dóminum est merces eórum.

corporasanctoruminpacesepultasunt.en: Their bodies are buried in peace,
corporasanctoruminpacesepultasunt.la: Córpora Sanctórum in pace sepúlta sunt,

etnomineorumviventingenerationemetgenera.en: And their name liveth unto generation and generation.
etnomineorumviventingenerationemetgenera.la: Et nómina eórum vivent in generatiónem et generatiónem.

nemestquinesciatmartyrumgloriasadhocdivi.en: Every man knoweth how, by the good Providence of God, the diverse glories of His Martyrs are held in such esteem by His people, that the same His Saints in all places receive worthy honour, and before us is set, by the favour of Christ, the noble example of their courage: thus are we stirred up to consider, on the occasion of these Holidays, how great glory doth abide them in heaven, whose birthdays are thus kept upon earth: thereby, also, we are roused to strive to be like them, brave, godly, and true: so that, in the strength of Christ, we, like them, may wrestle with, and conquer our enemy, and, when we have gained the same victory that they gained, may with them at last be glorified in the kingdom of heaven.
nemestquinesciatmartyrumgloriasadhocdivi.la: Nemo est, qui nésciat, Mártyrum glórias ad hoc divíno consílio a Dei pópulis frequentári, ut et illis débitus honor dicétur, et nobis virtútis exémpla, favénte Christo, monstréntur; ut, dum hæc ita celebrári perspícimus, cognoscámus quanta eos glória máneat in cælis, quorum natalítia táliter celebrántur in terris; quo possímus, étiam ipsi, tálibus provocári exémplis, virtúte pari, devotióne consímili ac fide; ut, Christo præstánte, dimicáre et víncere hostem possímus, ut, parta victória, cum iísdem Sanctis in regnis cæléstibus triumphémus.

quisestenimquieorumvolensmeritocopularin.en: For what man is there willing to share their reward, that if he do not first lay hold on their steadfastness, follow after the example of their faith, and imitate their brave patience, can either seek or find their glory by likeness to their lives? But whosoever doth so follow them, let him not doubt but that, though in very deed he gain not the crown of martyrdom, he is yet able by good works to make himself meet therefor. For we have a most merciful God, Which either giveth Martyrdom unto such as be willing, or, without Martyrdom, doth make them joint heirs with the Saints in the kingdom of God.
quisestenimquieorumvolensmeritocopularin.la: Quis est enim, qui eórum volens mérito copulári, nisi prius constántiam eórum téneat, sectétur fidem, imitétur virtútem passiónis; eórum glóriam páribus vitæ lineaméntis aut invéniat aut exquírat? Qui, etsi martýrio par esse non possit, tamen múneris tanti dignitáte se quisque bonis áctibus dignum præbeat. Adest enim clementíssimus Deus, qui desiderántibus suis aut martýrium præbeat, aut, sine martýrio, cum Sanctis præmia divína retríbuat.

lectiosanctievangeliisecundumlucam.en: From the Holy Gospel according to Luke

homiliasanctihilariiepiscopi.en: Homily by St. Hilary, Bishop of Poitiers.

libdesermonedominiinmontecap.en: Book 1 on the Lord's Sermon on the Mount, ch. 6
libdesermonedominiinmontecap.la: Lib. 1 de Sermóne Dómini in monte, cap. 6

domineprevenistieuminbenedictionibusdulc.en: O Lord, thou hast prevented him with blessings of sweetness:
domineprevenistieuminbenedictionibusdulc.la: Dómine, prævenísti eum in benedictiónibus dulcédinis,

posuistiincapiteeiuscoronamdelapidepreti.en: Thou hast set on his head a crown of precious stones.
posuistiincapiteeiuscoronamdelapidepreti.la: Posuísti in cápite ejus corónam de lápide pretióso.

desideriumanimeeiustribuistieidomine.en: Lord, Thou hast given him his heart's desire.
desideriumanimeeiustribuistieidomine.la: Desidérium ánimæ ejus tribuísti ei, Dómine:

etvoluntatelabiorumeiusnonfraudastieum.en: And hast not withholden the request of his lips.
etvoluntatelabiorumeiusnonfraudastieum.la: Et voluntáte labiórum ejus non fraudásti eum.

exlibromoraliumsanctigregoriipape.en: From the Book of Moral (Reflections on Job) written by Pope St. Gregory (the Great.)
exlibromoraliumsanctigregoriipape.la: Ex libro Moralium sancti Gregorii Papæ.

inillotemporedixitpetrusadiesumeccenosre.en: At that time, Peter said to Jesus, Behold, we have left all and followed You; what then shall we have? And Jesus said to them, Amen I say to you that you who have followed Me, in the regeneration when the Son of Man shall sit on the throne of His glory, shall also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve  tribes of Israel. And everyone who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for My name’s sake, shall receive a hundredfold, and shall possess life everlasting.
inillotemporedixitpetrusadiesumeccenosre.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Petrus ad Jesum: Ecce nos relíquimus ómnia, et secúti sumus te: quid ergo erit nobis? Jesus autem dixit illis: Amen dico vobis, quod vos, qui secúti estis me, in regeneratióne cum séderit Fílius hóminis in sede Majestátis suæ, sedébitis et vos super sedes duódecim, judicántes duódecim tribus Israël. Et omnis qui relíquerit domum, vel fratres, aut soróres, aut patrem, aut matrem, aut uxórem, aut fílios, aut agros propter nomen meum, céntuplum accípiet, et vitam ætérnam possidébit.

inillotemporevenitiesusinpartescesareeph.en: At that time: When Jesus came into the coasts of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, Whom do men say that I the Son of man am? And so on.
inillotemporevenitiesusinpartescesareeph.la: In illo témpore: Venit Jesus in partes Cæsaréæ Philíppi, et interrogábat discípulos suos, dicens: Quem dicunt hómines esse Fílium hóminis? Et réliqua.

homiliasanctibernardiabbatis.en: Homily by St. Bernard, Abbot (of Clairvaux)

hecestvirgosapiensetunadenumeroprudentum.en: This is one of the wise virgins, * one chosen out of the number of the careful.
hecestvirgosapiensetunadenumeroprudentum.la: Hæc est Virgo sapiens, et una de número prudéntum.

quoniamigituretmagnareseratacdeeaapudmul.en: Virginity then, being a thing in itself so great and so much esteemed among many, lest any man having attained unto it, and kept it undefiled, should think that he hath done all, and so leave the rest undone, the Lord putteth forth this parable, in order to show that if virginity, though it have all else, lack mercy, its owner will but have his portion without among the fornicators, among whom Christ doth justly place the heartless and pitiless celibate. The fornicator is entangled in lust after bodies, the other in lust after money. The lust for bodies and the lust for money are two very different things, whereof the fleshly is by far the keener and the stubborner appetite. They that strive with the weaker enemy are therefore much less excusable if they fall. Wherefore the Lord hath called such virgins foolish, for having first won the stern battle, and then been destroyed in the light one.
quoniamigituretmagnareseratacdeeaapudmul.la: Quóniam ígitur et magna res erat, ac de ea apud multos magna erat existimátio, ne quis, ea perfécta, se totum perfécisse putáret ac cetera negligeret, hanc parábolam pósuit; ut osténderet, virginitátem, quamvis cetera hábeat, si misericórdiæ bonis carúerit, cum fornicatóribus éjici. Ac mérito quidem inhumánum ac misericórdia caréntem cum illis cóllocat; fornicátor enim córporum, istæ vero pecuniárum cupiditáte vincúntur.

specietuetpulchritudinetuaintendeprosper.en: In thy comeliness and thy beauty, * go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.
specietuetpulchritudinetuaintendeprosper.la: Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.

astititreginaadextristuisinvestitudeaura.en: Upon thy right hand did stand the Queen in a vesture of gold wrought about with diverse colours.
astititreginaadextristuisinvestitudeaura.la: Astitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto, circúmdata varietáte.

accinxitfortitudinelumbossuosetroboravit.en: She hath girded her loins with strength, and hath strengthened her arm
accinxitfortitudinelumbossuosetroboravit.la: Accínxit fortitúdine lumbos suos, et roborávit bráchium suum;

adiuvabiteamdeusvultusuodeusinmedieiusno.en: God shall help * her with His countenance: God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved.
adiuvabiteamdeusvultusuodeusinmedieiusno.la: Adjuvábit eam Deus vultu suo, Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur.

inillotemporeingressusiesusperambulabati.en: At that time: Jesus entered and passed through Jericho. And, behold, there was a man named Zacchaeus, which was the chief among the publicans, and he was rich. And so on.
inillotemporeingressusiesusperambulabati.la: In illo témpore: Ingréssus Jesus perambulábat Jéricho. Et ecce vir nómine Zachǽus: et hic princeps erat publicanórum, et ipse dives. Et réliqua.

dehomiliasanctiambrosiiepiscopi.en: A Homily by St. Ambrose the Bishop

desermonesanctiaugustiniepiscopi.en: From the Sermons of St. Augustine, Bishop of Hippo.

homiliasanctigregoriipape.en: Homily by Pope St. Gregory (the Great,)

siveracitersapientesesseatqueipsamsapien.en: If we would be truly wise, and behold wisdom herself, we must humbly acknowledge ourselves to be fools. Let us cast away harmful wisdom, and learn praiseworthy folly. For this reason indeed is it written God hath chosen the foolish things of the world, to confound the wise. (1 Cor. 1:27) And again it is said If any man among you seemeth to be wise in this world, let him become a fool, that he may be wise. (3:18.) And unto this doth the very Gospel bear witness, wherein it is said that Zacchaeus sought to see Jesus, Who He was; and could not for the press, because he was little of stature. And he ran before, and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see Him; for He was to pass that way. For this name Sycamore, being interpreted, signifieth the Foolish Fig.
siveracitersapientesesseatqueipsamsapien.la: Si veraciter sapiéntes esse, atque ipsam sapiéntiam contemplári appetimus, stultos nos humíliter cognoscámus. Relinquamus noxiam sapiéntiam, discamus laudabilem fatuitatem. Hinc quippe scriptum est: Stulta mundi elégit Deus, ut confúndat sapiéntes. Hinc rursum dícitur: Si quis vidétur inter vos sápiens esse in hoc sǽculo, stultus fiat, ut sit sápiens. Hinc evangelicæ historiæ verba testantur: quia Zachǽus cum vidére præ turba nihil posset, sycomori árborem ascéndit, ut transeúntem Dóminum cerneret. Sycómorus quippe ficus fatua dícitur.

quasienimsycomorumnosascenderedominuspre.en: The Lord biddeth us, as it were, to climb up into the sycamore, where He saith Of him that taketh away thy goods, ask them not again. (Luke 6:30.) And again Whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also. ~(Matth. 5:39.) From the boughs of this sycamore tree, the Lord is seen passing by. He may indeed, as yet, not be seen face to Face, but by this wise folly the inward eye may see the Wisdom of God, as it were, passing by, even that Wisdom Which they that are wise in their own conceit cannot see. They are mixed up in the overbearing press of their own imaginations, and have not yet found the sycamore tree where into to climb up, if they would see the Lord.
quasienimsycomorumnosascenderedominuspre.la: Quasi enim sycómorum nos ascéndere Dóminus præcipit, cum dicit: Qui aufert quæ tua sunt, ne repetas. Et rursum: Si quis te percússerit in déxteram maxillam, præbe illi et álteram. Per sycomorum Dóminus transiens cérnitur: quia per hanc sapientem stultítiam, etsi necdum, ut est, solide, jam tamen per contemplatiónis lumen Dei sapiéntia quasi in transitu vidétur, quam vidére nequeunt qui sibi sapiéntes esse vidéntur: quia ad conspiciéndum Dóminum, in elata cogitatiónum suárum turba deprehensi, adhuc sycomori árborem non invenérunt.

dehomiliavenerabilisbedepresbyteri.en: Homily by the Venerable Bede, Priest (at Jarrow and Doctor of the Church).

dilectusmeusmisitmanumsuamperforamenetve.en: My beloved put his hand through the key hole, and my bowels were moved at his touch.
dilectusmeusmisitmanumsuamperforamenetve.la: Diléctus meus misit manum suam per forámen, et venter meus intrémuit ad tactum ejus.

surrexiutaperiremdilectomeomanusmeestill.en: I arose up to open to my beloved: my hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers were full of the choicest myrrh.
surrexiutaperiremdilectomeomanusmeestill.la: Surréxi ut aperírem dilécto meo: manus meæ stillavérunt myrrham, et dígiti mei pleni myrrha probatíssima.

pessulumostiimeiaperuidilectomeoatillede.en: I opened the bolt of my door to my beloved: but he had turned aside, and was gone. My soul melted when he spoke: I sought him, and found him not: I called, and he did not answer me.
pessulumostiimeiaperuidilectomeoatillede.la: Péssulum óstii mei apérui dilécto meo, at ille declináverat, atque transíerat. Anima mea liquefácta est, ut locútus est: quæsívi, et non invéni illum: vocávi, et non respóndit mihi.

inveneruntmecustodesquicircumeuntcivitat.en: The keepers that go about the city found me: they struck me: and wounded me: the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.
inveneruntmecustodesquicircumeuntcivitat.la: Invenérunt me custódes qui circúmeunt civitátem: percussérunt me, et vulneravérunt me. Tulérunt pállium meum mihi custódes murórum.

veniatdilectusmeusinhortumsuumetcomedatf.en: Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat the fruit of his apple trees. I am come into my garden, O my sister, my spouse, I have gathered my myrrh, with my aromatical spices: I have eaten the honeycomb with my honey, I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends, and drink, and be inebriated, my dearly beloved.
veniatdilectusmeusinhortumsuumetcomedatf.la: Véniat diléctus meus in hortum suum, et cómedat fructum pomórum suórum. Veni in hortum meum soror mea sponsa, méssui myrrham meam cum aromátibus meis: comédi favum cum melle meo, bibi vinum meum cum lacte meo: comédite amíci, et bíbite, et inebriámini caríssimi.

egodormietcormeumvigilatvoxdilectimeipul.en: I sleep, and my heart watcheth; the voice of my beloved knocking: Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is full of dew, and my locks of the drops of the nights.
egodormietcormeumvigilatvoxdilectimeipul.la: Ego dórmio, et cor meum vígilat. Vox dilécti mei pulsántis: Aperi mihi soror mea, amíca mea, colúmba mea, immaculáta mea: quia caput meum plenum est rore, et cincínni mei guttis nóctium.

exspoliavimetunicameaquomodoinduarillala.en: I have put off my garment, how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet, how shall I defile them?
exspoliavimetunicameaquomodoinduarillala.la: Exspoliávi me túnica mea, quómodo índuar illa? lavi pedes meos, quómodo inquinábo illos?

sermosanctibedevenerabilispresbyteri.en: From the Sermons of the Venerable Bede, Priest (at Jarrow.)

sermosanctibernardiabbatis.en: From the Sermons of St. Bernard, Abbot (of Clairvaux)

sermoindominfraoctassumptn.en: Sermon for the Sunday within the Octave of the Assumption, nn. 2-3
sermoindominfraoctassumptn.la: Sermo in dom. infra oct. Assumpt., n. 2-3

delaudibusvirginismatrishomn.en: On the Praises of the Virgin Mother, Homily 2, nn. 4-5
delaudibusvirginismatrishomn.la: De laudibus Virginis Matris Hom. 2, n. 4-5

diffusestgratiainlabiistuis.en: Grace is poured into thy lips.
diffusestgratiainlabiistuis.la: Diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis,

proptereabenedixittedeusineternum.en: God hath blessed thee for ever.
proptereabenedixittedeusineternum.la: Proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.

hortusconclususesdeigenitrixhortusconclu.en: You are a garden enclosed, O Mother of God, a garden enclosed, a fountain sealed up: arise quickly my love and come.
hortusconclususesdeigenitrixhortusconclu.la: Hortus conclúsus * es Dei Génitrix, hortus conclúsus, fons signátus: † surge própera, amíca mea, et veni.

terraapparuitaridetinmarirubroviasineimp.en: Dry land appeared, and, out of the Red Sea, a way without impediment.
terraapparuitaridetinmarirubroviasineimp.la: Terra apparuit arida, et in Mari Rubro via sine impedimento.

quoniampercussitpetrametfluxeruntaqueett.en: He smote the rock, and the waters gushed out, and the streams overflowed.
quoniampercussitpetrametfluxeruntaqueett.la: Quoniam percussit petram et fluxerunt aquæ et torrentes inundaverunt.

verberacarnificumnontimueruntsanctideimo.en: The Saints of God shrank not from the stripes of the executioners, but died for Christ's Name's sake
verberacarnificumnontimueruntsanctideimo.la: Verbera carnificum non timuerunt Sancti Dei, morientes pro Christi nomine:

utheredesfierentindomodomini.en: That they might be made joint-heirs in the house of the Lord.
utheredesfierentindomodomini.la: Ut heredes fierent in domo Domini.

tradideruntcorporasuapropterdeumadsuppli.en: They gave their bodies for God's sake to death.
tradideruntcorporasuapropterdeumadsuppli.la: Tradiderunt corpora sua propter Deum ad supplicia.

tamquamauruminfornaceprobavitelectosdomi.en: As gold in the furnace hath the Lord tried His chosen ones, and received them as a burnt-offering, and yet a while, and they shall be regarded;
tamquamauruminfornaceprobavitelectosdomi.la: Tamquam aurum in fornace probavit electos Dominus, et quasi holocausti hostiam accepit illos; et in tempore erit respectus illorum:

quoniamdonumetpaxestelectisdei.en: For the grace of God, and His peace, are with His chosen.
quoniamdonumetpaxestelectisdei.la: Quoniam donum et pax est electis Dei.

inillotemporedescendensiesusdemontesteti.en: At that time, Jesus came down from the mountain, and stood in the plain, and the company of His disciples, and a great multitude of people out of all Judea, and Jerusalem, and from the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon. And so on.
inillotemporedescendensiesusdemontesteti.la: In illo témpore: Descendens Jesus de monte, stetit in loco campestri, et turba discipulorum ejus, et multitudo copiosa plebis ab omni Judǽa, et Jerúsalem, et maritima, et Tyri, et Sidonis. Et réliqua.

homiliasanctipetricanisiipresbyteri.en: Homily of St. Peter Canisius, Priest

proptertestamentumdominietlegespaternass.en: Because of the covenant of the Lord, and the laws of their fathers, the Saints of God abode in brotherly love,
proptertestamentumdominietlegespaternass.la: Propter testamentum Domini et leges paternas, Sancti Dei perstiterunt in amóre fraternitatis:

quiaunusfuitsemperspiritusineisetunafide.en: For one spirit and one faith was ever in them.
quiaunusfuitsemperspiritusineisetunafide.la: Quia unus fuit semper spiritus in eis, et una fides.

eccequambonumetquamiucundumhabitarefratr.en: Behold how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity.
eccequambonumetquamiucundumhabitarefratr.la: Ecce quam bonum et quam jucundum habitare fratres in unum!

sanctimeiquiincarnepositicertamenhabuist.en: O ye My Saints, who, being in the flesh, didst have striving
sanctimeiquiincarnepositicertamenhabuist.la: Sancti mei, qui in carne positi certamen habuistis:

mercedemlaborisegoreddamvobis.en: I will render unto you a reward of your labours.

venitebenedictipatrismeipercipiteregnum.en: Come, ye blessed of My Father, inherit the kingdom
venitebenedictipatrismeipercipiteregnum.la: Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum.

principespersecutisuntmegratisetaverbist.en: Princes have persecuted me I without a cause; but my heart standeth in awe of thy word. These are rightly the words of a martyr, who beareth unjustly the torments of the persecutors, who hath robbed no man, who hath violently oppressed no man, who hath shed the blood of no man, who hath imagined to defile the bed of no man, who is debtor to the laws in nothing, and who is punished more grievously than if he were a robber: who speaketh righteousness, and there is none that will hear: who speaketh salvation, and all men fight against him: who is able to say: “When I spoke unto them, they fought against me without a cause.” (Ps. cxix. 7.) They fight against him without a cause, who can lay no sin to his charge; they fight against him as an evildoer, who is by their own acknowledgment righteous: they fight against him as a warlock, who glorieth in the name of the Lord, and who doeth all things well because he doeth all things for God's sake.
principespersecutisuntmegratisetaverbist.la: Príncipes persecúti sunt me gratis: et a verbis tuis trepidávit cor meum. Bene hoc Martyr dicit, quod injúste persecutiónum torménta sustineat; qui nihil rapúerit, nullum violentus oppresserit, nullius sánguinem fuderit, nullius torum putaverit esse violándum; qui nihil légibus debeat, et gravióra latronum sustinere cogátur supplícia; qui loquátur juste, et non audiátur; qui loquátur plena salútis, et impugnétur, ut possit dicere: Cum loquébar illis, impugnábant me gratis. Gratis ígitur persecutiónem pátitur, qui impugnátur sine crimine; impugnátur ut noxius cum sit in tali confessióne laudábilis; impugnátur quasi veneficus, qui in nómine Dómini gloriátur, cum pietas virtútum ómnium fundaméntum sit.

verefrustraimpugnaturquiapudimpiosetinfi.en: They fight against him in vain who is accused of ungodliness among the ungodly and the unfaithful, because he teacheth Faith. Verily, him that is fought against without a cause it behoveth to be strong and patient. Wherefore then saith he: My heart standeth in awe of thy word? Awe is the mark of the weak, the timid, and the fearful But there is also a weakness unto salvation, there is a fear which is an holy fear. O fear the Lord, all ye His Saints. (Ps. xxxiii. 10.) And again: Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord. (Ps. cxi. i.) And wherefore is he blessed? because he delighteth greatly in His commandments.
verefrustraimpugnaturquiapudimpiosetinfi.la: Vere frustra impugnátur, qui apud ímpios et infidos impietátis arcessitur, cum fidei sit magister. Verum, qui gratis impugnátur, fortis debet esse et constans; quómodo ergo subtexuit: Et a verbis tuis trepidávit cor meum? Trepidare infirmitátis est, timoris atque formidinis. Sed est étiam infirmitas ad salútem, est étiam timor sanctórum: Timéte Dóminum, omnes sancti ejus; et, Beátus vir, qui timet Dóminum. Qua ratióne beatus? Quia in mandatis ejus cupit nimis.

derideturiustisimplicitashuiusmundisapie.en: The simplicity of the righteous is made a subject of derision. The wisdom of this world hideth our true feelings by artifice, and useth language to conceal our thoughts this is the wisdom which demonstrated the truth of falsehood, and showeth the falsehood of the truth. This kind of shrewdness the young acquire by practice, and children pay for the learning it. Those who are good at this look down upon their neighbours those who are bad at it are humble and timid, and wonder at it in others they regard this astuteness too, wrong though it be, with wistful admiration, under softened epithets. Un-straightforwardness is called good breeding. The principles of the world teach those who entertain them, to try and rise to distinction, and when they have attained the bubble of glory which is so soon to pass away, to feel it sweet to have at their feet them on whom they may wreak rich revenge. These principles teach a man, as long as he is strong enough, to give way to nobody else, and, if he hath no chance by force, to try and attain his object by diplomacy.
derideturiustisimplicitashuiusmundisapie.la: Deridétur justi simplícitas. Hujus mundi sapiéntia est, cor machinatiónibus tégere, sensum verbis veláre: quæ falsa sunt, vera osténdere; quæ vera sunt, falsa demonstráre. Hæc nimírum prudéntia usu a juvénibus scitur hæc a púeris prétio díscitur; hanc qui sciunt, céteros despiciéndo supérbiunt: hanc qui nésciunt, subjécti et tímidi in áliis mirántur: quia ab eis hæc éadem duplicitátis iníquitas nómine palliáta dilígitur, dum mentis pervérsitas urbánitas vocátur. Hæc sibi obsequéntibus præcipit honórum cúlmina quærere, adépta temporális glóriæ vanitáte gaudére, irrogáta ab áliis mala multiplícius réddere: cum vires súppetunt, nullis resisténtibus cédere: cum virtútis possibílitas deest, quidquid explére per malítiam non valent, hoc in pacífica bonitáte simuláre.

atcontrasapientiaiustorumestnilperostens.en: The wisdom of the righteous is the contrary of all this. They seek to avoid deception, to give their thoughts a clear expression in their words, to love the truth because it is the truth, to avoid falsehood, and rather to suffer than to inflict evil. Such are they who seek not to avenge themselves for wrong, and deem it gain to be despised for the truth's sake. This their simplicity is made a subject of derision, for such as are wise in this world believe the purity of their virtue to be simple foolery. Whatsoever is done innocently, they consider without doubt stupid. Such works as the truth approveth are idiotic, when tried by carnal standards of wisdom. After all, what stupider thing is there in this world than to express our real thoughts in our words, to keep nothing quiet by skilful tact, to repay no injuries, to pray for them which curse us, to seek poverty, to give up property, to strive not with such as take from us, to turn the other cheek to the smiter
atcontrasapientiaiustorumestnilperostens.la: At contra, sapiéntia justórum est: nil per ostensiónem fíngere, sensum verbis aperíre, vera ut sunt dilígere, falsa devitáre; bona gratis exhibére, mala libéntius toleráre quam fácere; nullam injúriæ ultiónem quærere, pro veritáte contuméliam lucrum putáre. Sed hæc justórum simplícitas deridétur; quia ab hujus mundi sapiéntibus puritátis virtus fatúitas créditur. Omne enim quod innocénter ágitur, ab eis proculdúbio stultum putátur; et quidquid in ópere véritas ápprobat, carnáli sapiéntiæ fátuum sonat. Quid namque stúltius vidétur mundo, quam mentem verbis osténdere, nil cállida machinatióne simuláre, nullas injúriis contumélias réddere, pro maledicéntibus oráre, paupertátem quærere, posséssa relínquere, rapiénti non resístere, percutiénti álteram maxíllam præbére?

liberdeconsensuevang.en: Book ii., on the Harmony of the Evangelists.

elisabethimpletumesttempuspariendietpepe.en: Elisabeth's fullness of time came that she should deliver, and she brought forth a son. And her neighbours and her cousins heard how the Lord had showed great mercy upon her, and they rejoiced with her. And so on.
elisabethimpletumesttempuspariendietpepe.la: Elísabeth implétum est tempus pariéndi, et péperit fílium. Et audiérunt vicíni et cognáti ejus quia magnificávit Dóminus misericórdiam suam cum illa, et congratulabántur ei. Et réliqua.

dehomiliasaugustiniepiscopi.en: Homily by St. Augustine the Bishop

exlibdesermdominiinmontecapet.en: From Book 1 on the Lord's Sermon on the Mount, ch. 2 and 3.
exlibdesermdominiinmontecapet.la: Ex Lib. 1. de Serm. Domini in monte. Cap. 2.et 3.

paratusestoisrelinoccursumdominiquoniamv.en: Be ready, O Israel, to go forth to meet the Lord, for he cometh.
paratusestoisrelinoccursumdominiquoniamv.la: Parátus esto, Israël, in occúrsum Dómini, quóniam venit

formansmontesetcreansspiritusetannuntian.en: He that formeth the mountains and createth the winds, † and declareth among men his Christ according to his coming.
formansmontesetcreansspiritusetannuntian.la: Formans montes et creans spíritus, † et annúntians in homínibus Christum secúndum advéntum suum.

eccedominatordominuscumvirtuteveniet.en: Behold, the Lord the Ruler shall come with power.
eccedominatordominuscumvirtuteveniet.la: Ecce Dominátor Dominus, cum virtúte véniet.

adiutoriumnostruminnominedominialleluiaa.en: Our help is in the name of the Lord, * Alleluia, alleluia.
adiutoriumnostruminnominedominialleluiaa.la: Adjutórium nostrum in nómine Dómini, * Allelúja, allelúja.

gloriabunturinteomnesquidiliguntnomentuu.en: All they that love thy name shall glory in thee:
gloriabunturinteomnesquidiliguntnomentuu.la: Gloriabúntur in te omnes, qui díligunt nomen tuum:

quoniamtubenedicesiusto.en: For thou wilt bless the just.

domineutscutobonevoluntatistuecoronastin.en: O Lord, thou hast crowned us, as with a shield of thy good will.
domineutscutobonevoluntatistuecoronastin.la: Dómine, ut scuto bonæ voluntátis tuæ coronásti nos.

benedicanimameadomino.en: Bless the Lord, O my soul:

etomniaqueintramesuntnominisancteius.en: And let all that is within me bless his holy name.
etomniaqueintramesuntnominisancteius.la: Et ómnia, quæ intra me sunt, nómini sancto ejus.

benedicanimameadominetnolioblivisciomnes.en: Bless the Lord, O my soul: and never forget all he hath done for thee.
benedicanimameadominetnolioblivisciomnes.la: Bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino: et noli oblivísci omnes retibutiónes ejus.

innomineiesuchristinazarenicrucifixiquem.en: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, who was crucified, whom God hath raised from the dead:
innomineiesuchristinazarenicrucifixiquem.la: In nómine Jesu Christi Nazaréni crucifíxi, quem Deus suscitávit a mórtuis:

inhocestomniumsalus.en: In this is the salvation of all.

nonestaliudnomensubcelodatumhominibusinq.en: There is no other name under heaven given to men, whereby we must be saved.
nonestaliudnomensubcelodatumhominibusinq.la: Non est áliud nomen sub cælo datum homínibus, in quo opórteat nos salvos fíeri.

quiadominusiesuschristusingloriestdeipat.en: That the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father.
quiadominusiesuschristusingloriestdeipat.la: Quia Dóminus Jesus Christus in glória est Dei Patris.

inillotemporecumappropinquassetiesusiero.en: At that time: When Jesus drew nigh to Jerusalem, and was come to Bethphage, unto mount Olivet, then he sent two disciples, saying to them: Go ye into the village that is over against you, and immediately you shall find an ass tied, and a colt with her: loose them and bring them to me. And if any man shall say anything to you, say ye, that the Lord hath need of them: and forthwith he will let them go. Now all this was done that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying: Tell ye the daughter of Sion: Behold thy king cometh to thee, meek, and sitting upon an ass, and a colt the foal of her that is used to the yoke. And the disciples going, did as Jesus commanded them. And they brought the ass and the colt, and laid their garments upon them, and made him sit thereon. And a very great multitude spread their garments in the way: and others cut boughs from the trees, and strewed them in the way: and the multitudes that went before and that followed, cried, saying: Hosanna to the son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
inillotemporecumappropinquassetiesusiero.la: In illo témpore: Cum appropinquásset Jesus Jerosólymis, et venísset Béthphage ad montem Olivéti: tunc misit duos discípulos suos, dicens eis: Ite in castéllum, quod contra vos est, et statim inveniétis ásinam alligátam et pullum cum ea: sólvite et addúcite mihi: et si quis vobis áliquid dixerit, dícite, quia Dóminus his opus habet, et conféstim dimíttet eos. Hoc autem totum factum est, ut adimplerétur, quod dictum est per Prophétam, dicéntem: Dícite fíliæ Sion: Ecce, Rex tuus venit tibi mansuétus, sedens super ásinam et pullum, fílium subjugális. Eúntes autem discípuli, fecérunt, sicut præcépit illis Jesus. Et adduxérunt ásinam et pullum: et imposuérunt super eos vestiménta sua, et eum désuper sedére tecérunt. Plúrima autem turba stravérunt vestiménta sua in via: álii autem cædébant ramos de arbóribus, et sternébant in via: turbæ autem, quæ præcedébant et quæ sequebántur, clamábant, dicéntes: Hosánna fílio David: benedíctus, qui venit in nómine Dómini.

nonimmeritofratreshodiernadiepsalmushicl.en: Not without reason, brethren, is this Psalm read on this day, in which the Prophet biddeth us exult and rejoice. For holy David inviteth all creatures to the festival of this day. For on this day hell is opened through the resurrection of Christ; the earth is renewed through the newly baptized of the Church; heaven is unlocked through the Holy Ghost.
nonimmeritofratreshodiernadiepsalmushicl.la: Non immérito, fratres, hodiérna die Psalmus hic légitur, in quo Prophéta exsultándum præcipit et lætándum. Omnes enim creatúras ad hujus diéi festivitátem David sanctus invítat. Nam in hac die per resurrectiónem Christi aperítur tártarus, per neóphytos Ecclésiæ innovátur terra, cælum per Spíritum Sanctum reserátur.

apertusenimtartarusredditmortuosinnovata.en: For hell, being opened, giveth back the dead; the earth, renewed, buddeth forth them that rise again; heaven, unlocked, receiveth them that ascend. Lastly, the thief ascendeth into paradise; the bodies of the Saints enter into the holy city; the dead return unto the living; and by a certain advancement in the resurrection of Christ all the elements lift themselves up to higher things.
apertusenimtartarusredditmortuosinnovata.la: Apértus enim tártarus reddit mórtuos, innováta terra gérminat resurgéntes, cælum reserátum súscipit ascendéntes. Dénique ascéndit latro in paradísum, Sanctórum córpora ingrediúntur in sanctam civitátem: ad vivos mórtui revertúntur, et proféctu quodam in resurrectióne Christi ad altióra cuncta eleménta se tollunt.

tartarusquoshabetredditadsuperosterraquo.en: Whom hell holdeth, it giveth back to them above; whom the earth burieth, it sendeth unto heaven; whom heaven receiveth, it presenteth unto the Lord. And by one and the same working the passion of the Saviour lifteth up from the depths, raiseth up from earthly things, setteth in the heights. For the resurrection of Christ is life to the dead, pardon to sinners, glory to the Saints. Therefore holy David inviteth every creature to the festival of the resurrection of Christ: for he saith that we must exult and rejoice in this day, which the Lord hath made.
tartarusquoshabetredditadsuperosterraquo.la: Tártarus quos habet, reddit ad súperos; terra quos sépelit, mittit ad cælum; cælum quos súscipit, repræséntat ad Dóminum. Et una eadémque operatióne Salvatóris pássio élevat de imis, súscitat de terrénis, cóllocat in excélsis. Resurréctio enim Christi defúnctis est vita, peccatóribus vénia, Sanctis est glória. Omnem ergo creatúram ad festivitátem resurrectiónis Christi David sanctus invítat. ait enim exsultándum in hac die, quam fecit Dóminus, et lætándum.

igiturfratresomnesinhacdiesanctexsultare.en: Therefore, brethren, we ought all to exult on this holy day; let none withdraw himself from the common joy through the consciousness of his sins; let none be called back from the public prayers by the burden of his offences: for on this day the sinner ought not to despair of pardon; for great is this privilege. For if the thief merited paradise, why should not the Christian merit pardon? And if the Lord showed mercy unto him when he was being crucified, he will show mercy when he riseth again. And if the lowliness of the passion bestowed so much upon him that confessed, how much will the glory of the resurrection grant to him that prayeth? For, as you yourselves know, a joyful victory is wont to be more bountiful in giving than a captivity in bondage.
igiturfratresomnesinhacdiesanctexsultare.la: Igitur, fratres, omnes in hac die sancta exsultáre debémus; nullus se a commúni lætítia peccatórum consciéntia súbtrahat, nullus a públicis votis delictórum sárcina revocétur: étenim peccátor in hac die de indulgéntia non debet desperáre; est enim prærogatíva non parva. Si enim latro paradísum méruit, cur non mereátur véniam christiánus? Et si illi Dóminus, cum crucifígitur, miserébitur, cum resúrgit. Et si passiónis humílitas tantum præstitit confiténti, resurrectiónis glória quantum tríbuet deprecánti? Lárgior enim ad præstándum solet esse, sicut ipsi scitis, læta victória, quam addícta captívitas.

intersermonesineditossleonismagnippsermo.en: Among the unpublished Sermons of St. Leo the Great, Pope, Sermon IV; on Easter, II, nn. 1 and 2
intersermonesineditossleonismagnippsermo.la: Inter Sermones ineditos S. Leonis Magni Pp. Sermo IV; de Pascha II, n. 1 et 2

licetomnessolemnitatesdilectissimiqueine.en: Although all the solemnities, dearly beloved, which are celebrated in the Churches for the honour of God, be holy and worthy of veneration, yet this day of the Lord's resurrection hath a festival peculiar to itself. And this assuredly, because all other days contain in themselves the joy of the living only; this, the gladness of the dead also.
licetomnessolemnitatesdilectissimiqueine.la: Licet omnes solemnitátes, dilectíssimi, quæ in Ecclésiis pro Dei honóre celebrántur, sanctæ sint atque venerábiles: tamen hodiérna Domínicæ resurrectiónis dies peculiárem festivitátem habet. Ideo útique, quia omnes álii dies vivéntium in se tantum cóntinent gáudium: hæc lætítiam defunctórum.

communisestergoinfernissimulacsupernisis.en: This festival therefore is common to them below as well as to them above, because the Lord, rising from the dead, gave a festival both there, where he overcame death, and here, whither he returned a victor from death. And therefore well doth the Psalmist speak peculiarly of this day, saying: This is the day which the Lord hath made; let us be glad and rejoice therein.
communisestergoinfernissimulacsupernisis.la: Commúnis est ergo inférnis simul ac supérnis ista festívitas, quia resúrgens Dóminus a mórtuis, et illic festivitátem dedit, ubi mortem vicit: et istic, ubi victor a morte remeávit. Et ídeo bene Psalmísta lóquitur de hac peculiáriter die dicens: Hæc est dies, quam fecit Dóminus; exsultémus et lætémur in ea.

prenuntiansenimdominicamresurrectionemno.en: For, foretelling the Lord's resurrection, he proclaimed a day of saving gladness not to them above only, but to them below also. When the Lord descended into the dark gloom of hell, without doubt there also was then a most bright day, where the Saviour shone. Whence the Evangelist saith beautifully: And the light shineth in darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it. For although the Lord descended into darkness, yet he felt not the obscurity of the darkness.
prenuntiansenimdominicamresurrectionemno.la: Prænúntians enim Domínicam resurrectiónem, non supérnis tantum, sed et inférnis diem salutíferæ exsultatiónis indíxit. Descendénte in tenebrósam inferórum calíginem Dómino, étiam illic tunc absque dúbio dies splendidíssimus fuit, ubi Salvátor illúxit. Unde pulchre Evangelísta: Et lux, inquit, in ténebris lucet: et ténebræ eam non comprehendérunt. Quia licet in ténebras Dóminus descénderit, tenebrárum tamen obscúra non sensit.

tenuitinillonoctishorroreinviolabilemmai.en: In that horror of the night he kept the inviolable splendour of his majesty: he shone with the splendour of his everlasting nature, and so the light was not overcome by the night, but the night by the light. Let us therefore rejoice, dearly beloved, and exult in the Lord: for this day the light of salvation hath been given us by the Lord, according to that which the same Psalmist saith in what followeth: The Lord is God, and he hath shone upon us.
tenuitinillonoctishorroreinviolabilemmai.la: Ténuit in illo noctis horróre inviolábilem majestátis suæ splendórem: luxit sempitérnæ natúræ splendóre, ac sic non lux a nocte, sed nox a luce superáta est. Lætémur ergo, dilectíssimi, et exsultémus in Dómino: hódie enim nobis data est a Dómino lux salútis secúndum illud, quod idem Psalmísta in consequéntibus ait: Deus Dóminus et illúxit nobis.

tristitiaimplevitcorvestrumetgaudiumvest.en: Sorrow hath filled * your heart: and your joy no man shall take from you, alleluia, alleluia.
tristitiaimplevitcorvestrumetgaudiumvest.la: Tristítia implévit * cor vestrum: et gáudium vestrum nemo tollet a vobis, allelúja, allelúja.

venireadtevultdeusaudiipsumdicentemegetp.en: God willeth to come unto thee: hear him saying: I and the Father will come, and will make our abode with him.
venireadtevultdeusaudiipsumdicentemegetp.la: Veníre ad te vult Deus, audi ipsum dicéntem: Ego et Pater veniémus, et mansiónem apud eum faciémus.

mundatestdomusnonremaneatinanisnecumvacu.en: The house is cleansed; let it not remain empty, lest the deserter, finding it empty, bring with him seven others more wicked than himself, and the last state of that man become, as the Gospel saith, worse than the first.
mundatestdomusnonremaneatinanisnecumvacu.la: Mundáta est domus, non remáneat inánis, ne cum vácuam desértor invénerit addúcat secum álios septem nequióres se, et efficiántur hóminis illíus posterióra, ut evangélium loquit, peióra prióribus.

moxcumexclususfueritpessimusinvasorintro.en: As soon as the most wicked invader hath been shut out, let the best of possessors be brought in. Who is the invader? The devil. What did he invade? Man, whom he made not, and moreover deceived. He promised him immortality, and gave him iniquity to drink.
moxcumexclususfueritpessimusinvasorintro.la: Mox cum exclúsus fúerit péssimus invásor, introducátur óptimus posséssor. Quis est invásor? Diábolus. Quid invásit? Hóminem, quem non fecit, ínsuper decépit. Promísit ei immortalitátem, et propinávit iniquitátem.

sermoindiepentecostescapet.en: Sermon 267, on the day of Pentecost, chapters 1 and 2
sermoindiepentecostescapet.la: Sermo 267 in die Pentecostes, cap. 1 et 2

hodiernidieisolemnitasdominideimagnietma.en: The solemnity of this day maketh remembrance of the great Lord God, and of the great grace which hath been poured out upon us. For a solemnity is celebrated unto God, lest that which was once done be blotted out of memory. For a solemnity hath taken its name from that which is wont to be in the year: as the perennial flowing of a river is so called because it drieth not up in summer, but floweth through the whole year: hence perennial, that is, through the year: so also solemn, that which is wont to be celebrated in the year.
hodiernidieisolemnitasdominideimagnietma.la: Hodiérni diéi solémnitas Dómini Dei magni, et magnæ grátiæ, quæ superfúsa est super nos, recordatiónem facit. Deo enim solémnitas celebrátur: ne, quod semel factum est, de memória deleátur. Solémnitas enim ab eo, quod solet in anno, nomen accépit: quómodo perénnitas flúminis dícitur, quia non siccátur æstáte, sed per totum annum fluit:ideo perénne, id est, per annum: sic et solémne, quod solet in anno celebrári.

celebramushodieadventumspiritussanctidom.en: We celebrate this day the coming of the Holy Ghost: for the Lord sent from heaven the Spirit whom, being on earth, he had promised to send from heaven. He cannot come, saith he, unless I go away: but when I am gone, I will send him unto you. He suffered, he died, he rose again, he ascended: it remained that he should fulfil what he had promised.
celebramushodieadventumspiritussanctidom.la: Celebrámus hódie adventum Spíritus Sancti: Dóminus enim Spíritum de cælo misit, quem in terra promíserat de cælo esse missúrum. Non potest ille veníre, ait, nisi ego abíero: dum autem abíero, mittam illum ad vos. Passus est, mórtuus est, resurréxit, ascéndit: restábat, ut impléret, quod promísit.

hocexpectantesdiscipulieiusanimeutscript.en: His disciples were awaiting this, souls, as it is written, a hundred and twenty, the number of the Apostles tenfold: for he chose twelve, and upon a hundred and twenty he sent the Spirit. Awaiting therefore this promise, they were in one house, they prayed: for already they desired it by faith itself, by prayer itself, by spiritual desire itself: they were new bottles, new wine was awaited from heaven, and it came. For already that great cluster had been trodden and glorified. For we read in the Gospel: For as yet the Spirit was not given, because Jesus was not yet glorified.
hocexpectantesdiscipulieiusanimeutscript.la: Hoc expectántes discípuli ejus, ánimæ, ut scriptum est, centum vigínti, decupláto número Apostolórum: duódecim enim elégit, et in centum vigínti Spíritum misit. Hoc ergo promíssum exspectántes, in una domo erant, orábant: quia desiderábant jam ipsa fide, quod ipsa oratióne, ipso spiritáli desidério: utres novi erant, vinum novum de cælo exspectabátur, et venit. Jam enim fúerat magnus botrus ille calcátus, et glorificátus. Légimus enim in Evangélio: Spíritus enim nondum erat datus, quia Jesus nondum fúerat glorificátus.

iamquidresponditaudistismagnummiraculumo.en: Now ye have heard what he answered: a great miracle. All that were present had learned one tongue. The Holy Ghost came; they were filled; they began to speak in divers tongues of all nations, which they had not known nor learned; but he taught them, who had come: he entered in, they were filled, he poured forth. And then this was the sign: whosoever received the Holy Ghost, being suddenly filled with the Spirit, spake in the tongues of all, and not those hundred and twenty only.
iamquidresponditaudistismagnummiraculumo.la: Jam quid respóndit, audístis, magnum miráculum. Omnes, qui áderant, unam linguam didícerant. Venit Spíritus Sanctus, impléti sunt, cœpérunt loqui linguis váriis ómnium géntium, quas non nóverant, nec didícerant; sed docébat ille, qui vénerat: intrávit, impléti sunt, fudit. Et tunc hoc erat signum, quicúmque accipiébat Spíritum Sanctum, súbito implétus Spíritu, linguis ómnium loquebátur, non illi solum centum vigínti.

interspursermoiinpentecmignetomcol.en: Among the spurious works: Sermon I on Pentecost. Migne, vol. 52, col. 803
interspursermoiinpentecmignetomcol.la: Inter spur.: Sermo I in Pentec. Migne Tom. 52, col. 803

hodienobisterrafactestcelumnonstellisdec.en: This day the earth hath become heaven to us, not by the stars descending from heaven to earth, but by the Apostles ascending to heaven; for the abundant grace of the Holy Ghost hath been poured forth, and hath wrought the whole world into heaven, not changing its nature, but amending its will.
hodienobisterrafactestcelumnonstellisdec.la: Hódie nobis terra facta est cælum, non stellis de cælo in terram descendéntibus, sed Apóstolis ad cælos ascendéntibus, quia effúsa est copiósa grátia Spíritus Sancti, et univérsum orbem operáta est cælum, non immútans natúram, sed voluntátem eméndans.

invenitnamquepublicanumetevangelistameff.en: For he found a publican, and made him an Evangelist: he found a persecutor, and rendered him an Apostle: he found a thief, and brought him into paradise: he found a harlot, and made her equal to virgins: he found wise men, and showed them forth as Evangelists: he put malice to flight, and brought in kindness: he banished servitude, and brought in liberty: he forgave the debt, and bestowed the grace of God. Therefore hath heaven become earth; and, saying this again and again, I will not cease.
invenitnamquepublicanumetevangelistameff.la: Invénit namque publicánum, et Evangelístam effécit: invénit persecutórem, et Apóstolum réddidit: invénit latrónem, et in paradísum indúxit: invénit meretrícem, et virgínibus coæquávit: invénit magos, et Evangelístas osténdit: fugávit malítiam, et indúxit benignitátem: exterminávit servitútem, et indúxit libertátem: concéssit débitum, et íntulit grátiam Dei. Ideo cælum factum est terra, et hoc sæpius dicens, non cessábo.

etfactusestrepentedecelosonustamquamadve.en: And suddenly there came a sound from heaven, as of a mighty wind coming, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting. And there appeared to them parted tongues as it were of fire: not fire, but as it were of fire. If it was fire, saith he, how did they not burn? asketh the Jew. I also will ask the Jew: If it was fire, how did it not burn up the bush, a frail wood? What is more vehement than fire? what is viler than a bush? and yet neither was the wood burned up, nor was the fire put out.
etfactusestrepentedecelosonustamquamadve.la: Et factus est repénte de cælo sonus tamquam adveniéntis spíritus veheméntis, et replévit totam domum, ubi erant sedéntes. Et apparuérunt illis dispertítæ linguæ tamquam ignis: non ignis, sed tamquam ignis. Si ignis, inquit, quómodo non ardébant? intérrogat Judæus: interrogábo et ego Judæum: Si ignis erat, quómodo non comburébat rubum, frágile lignum? Quid igne veheméntius? quid rubo vílius? et newue lignum exurebátur, neque ignis exstinguebátur.

etquomodocorporatriumpuerorumignisnonexu.en: And how did the fire not burn the bodies of the three children, but the furnace was turned into dew, and the coals were thought to be as roses? There was a contest of fire and body, and yet the victory was the bodies': and that which was more soluble than wax was made firmer than iron. Interpret to me the things of old, for they went before, that ye might believe the truth. For the Holy Ghost appeared in fire because of the swift receiving of the mind: yet not for this only, but also as fire burneth thorns, so the Spirit destroyeth sins. Daniel was cast into the lions' den, and the divine power held back their savage fury.
etquomodocorporatriumpuerorumignisnonexu.la: Et quómodo córpora trium puerórum ignis non exússit, sed camínus in rorem versus est, et carbónes tamquam rosas arbitrabántur? Certámen ignis et córporis, et tamen córporum fiébat victória: et quod cera erat solubílius, ferro factum est fírmius. Interpretáre mihi vétera, étenim illa præcessérunt, ut credátis veritáti. Quóniam Spíritus Sanctus in igne appáruit, propter velócem mentis susceptiónem: non autem propter hoc solum, sed et sicut ignis spinas combúrit, sic et Spíritus peccáta dispérdit. Missus est Dániel in lacum leónum, et immánem rábiem illórum divína virtus représsit.

unuspanisetunumcorpusmultisumus.en: We, being many, are one bread and one body:
unuspanisetunumcorpusmultisumus.la: Unus panis, et unum corpus multi sumus:

omnesdeunopaneetdeunocaliceparticipamus.en: All that partake of one bread, and of one chalice.
omnesdeunopaneetdeunocaliceparticipamus.la: Omnes de uno pane, et de uno cálice participámus.

parastiindulcedinetuapauperideusquihabit.en: Thou hast provided in thy sweetness for the poor, O God, who makest men of one mind to dwell in a house.
parastiindulcedinetuapauperideusquihabit.la: Parásti in dulcédine tua páuperi, Deus, qui habitáre facis unánimes in domo.

libcapiniregc.en: Book IV, ch. 5, on I Kings, ch. 10
libcapiniregc.la: Lib. 4, cap. 5 in I Reg. c. 10

sinauteminquitcarnalesdivitiasquelabuntu.en: But if, saith he, ye dispense not well the carnal riches which pass away, who will entrust to you the true and eternal riches of the doctrine of God? And if ye have been unfaithful in these things which are another's (for all that is of the world is another's unto us), who will be able to entrust to you those things which are your own, and properly allotted unto man?
sinauteminquitcarnalesdivitiasquelabuntu.la: Sin autem, inquit, carnáles divítias, quæ labúntur, non bene dispensétis; veras æternásque divítias doctrínæ Dei quis credet vobis? Et si in his, aliéna quæ sunt (aliénum est autem nobis omne quod sǽculi est), infidels fuístis; ea, quæ vestra sunt, et próprie hómini deputáta, quis vobis crédere póterit?
