alleluiaalleluiaalleluiaalleluiaalleluia.la: Alleluia, * alleluia, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

perevangelicumverbumregnummareamureternu.en: Through the word of the Gospel may we merit the eternal kingdom.
perevangelicumverbumregnummareamureternu.la: Per Evangélicum verbum regnum mareámur ætérnum.

audistisenimconversationemmeamaliquandoi.en: For you have heard † of my conversation in time past in the Jews' religion: how that I made progress
audistisenimconversationemmeamaliquandoi.la: Audístis enim † conversatiónem meam aliquándo in Judaísmo: quóniam proficiébam.

supramultoscetaneosmeosingeneremeo.en: Above many of my equals in my own nation.
supramultoscetaneosmeosingeneremeo.la: Supra multos coætáneos meos in génere meo.

abundantiusemulatorexsistenspaternarumme.en: Being more abundantly zealous for the traditions of my fathers.
abundantiusemulatorexsistenspaternarumme.la: Abundántius æmulátor exsístens paternárum meárum traditiónum.

sciocuicredidietcertussumquiapotensestde.en: I know † whom I have believed, and I am certain that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him.
sciocuicredidietcertussumquiapotensestde.la: Scio † cui crédidi, et certus sum quia potens est depósitum meum serváre.

inillumdiemiustusiudex.en: Against that day, the just judge.

repositestmihicoronaiustitiequamreddetmi.en: There is laid up for me a crown of justice, which the Lord will render to me.
repositestmihicoronaiustitiequamreddetmi.la: Repósita est mihi coróna justítiæ, quam reddet mihi Dóminus.

magnussanctuspaulusvaselectionisveredign.en: Great † is holy Paul, a vessel of election, who is truly worthy to be glorified.
magnussanctuspaulusvaselectionisveredign.la: Magnus † sanctus Paulus, vas electiónis, vere digne est glorificándus.

quietmeruitthronumduodecimumpossidere.en: Who also merited to possess the twelfth throne.
quietmeruitthronumduodecimumpossidere.la: Qui et méruit thronum duodécimum possidére.

achristodecelovocatusetinterramprostratu.en: Called by Christ from heaven, and cast down upon the earth, from a persecutor he was made a vessel of election.
achristodecelovocatusetinterramprostratu.la: A Christo de caelo vocátus, et in terram prostrátus, ex persecutóre efféctus est vas electiónis.

mihiviverechristusestetmorilucrum.en: To me † to live is Christ, and to die is gain:
mihiviverechristusestetmorilucrum.la: Mihi vívere † Christus est, et mori lucrum:

gloriarimeoportetincrucedominimeiiesuchr.en: It behoveth me to glory in the cross of my Lord Jesus Christ.
gloriarimeoportetincrucedominimeiiesuchr.la: Gloriári me opórtet in cruce Dómini mei Jesu Christi.

gaudeamusomnesindominodiemfestumcelebran.en: Let us all rejoice † in the Lord, celebrating a festal day in honour of blessed Agatha the Virgin;
gaudeamusomnesindominodiemfestumcelebran.la: Gaudeámus † omnes in Dómino, diem festum celebrántes sub honóre beátæ Agathæ Vírginis;

decuiuspassionegaudentangelietcollaudant.en: At whose passion the Angels rejoice, and together praise the Son of God.
decuiuspassionegaudentangelietcollaudant.la: De cujus passióne gaudent Angeli, et colláudant Fílium Dei.

immaculatusdominusimmaculatamsibifamulam.en: The immaculate Lord hath mercifully consecrated unto himself an immaculate handmaid, set in this frail body.
immaculatusdominusimmaculatamsibifamulam.la: Immaculátus Dóminus immaculátam sibi fámulam in hoc frágili córpore pósitam misericórditer consecrávit.

quimedignatusestabomniplagacurareetmamil.en: He who hath vouchsafed † to cure me of every wound, and to restore my breast unto my bosom,
quimedignatusestabomniplagacurareetmamil.la: Qui me dignátus est † ab omni plaga curáre, et mamíllam meam meo péctori restitúere,

ipsuminvocodeumvivum.en: Him do I call upon, the living God.

medicinamcarnalemcorporimeonumquamexhibu.en: Bodily medicine have I never applied to my body, but I have the Lord Jesus Christ, who by his word alone restoreth all things.
medicinamcarnalemcorporimeonumquamexhibu.la: Medicínam carnálem córpori meo numquam exhíbui, sed hábeo Dóminum Jesum Christum, qui solo sermóne restáurat univérsa.

benedictusesdominequiliberasticorpusmeum.en: Blessed art thou, † O Lord, who hast delivered my body from defilement, and hast made me overcome the chain, the sword, and the fire:
benedictusesdominequiliberasticorpusmeum.la: Benedíctus es, † Dómine, qui liberásti corpus meum a pollutióne, et fecísti me víncere vínculum, gládium et ignem:

suscipemedomineinnumeroancillarumtuarum.en: Receive me, O Lord, into the number of thy handmaids.
suscipemedomineinnumeroancillarumtuarum.la: Súscipe me, Dómine, in número ancillárum tuárum.

laudemtibireferensgratiasagoquiliberasti.en: Giving praise unto thee, I give thanks to thee, who hast delivered my body from defilement.
laudemtibireferensgratiasagoquiliberasti.la: Laudem tibi réferens, grátias ago, qui liberásti corpus meum a pollutióne.

egrederemodofrateregrederesipotesetdimis.en: Go forth now, brother: * go forth, if thou canst: and leaving me, return to the monastery.
egrederemodofrateregrederesipotesetdimis.la: Egrédere modo, frater: * egrédere, si potes: et dímissa, ad monastérium recéde. Ps. 109

parcattibisororomnipotensdeusquidestquod.en: May almighty God * spare thee, sister: what is this that thou hast done?
parcattibisororomnipotensdeusquidestquod.la: Parcat tibi, soror, * omnípotens Deus: quid est quod fecísti? Ps. 112

ecceterogavietaudiremenoluistirogavidomi.en: Behold, I besought thee, * and thou wouldst not hear me; I besought my Lord, and he hath heard me.
ecceterogavietaudiremenoluistirogavidomi.la: Ecce te rogávi, * et audíre me noluísti; rogávi Dóminum meum, et audívit me. Ps. 121

loquamurnuncusquemanedecelestibuspersacr.en: Let us now speak * until morning of heavenly things, in the holy converse of the spiritual life.
loquamurnuncusquemanedecelestibuspersacr.la: Loquámur nunc * usque mane de cælestibus per sacra spritualis vitæ colloquia. Ps. 126

cumsanctusbenedictusposttriduumincellaco.en: When holy Benedict, * three days after, was standing in his cell, lifting up his eyes he saw the soul of his sister, gone forth from the body, entering the secret places of heaven in the likeness of a dove.
cumsanctusbenedictusposttriduumincellaco.la: Cum sanctus Benedíctus * post tríduum in cella consísteret, elevátis óculis, vidit soróris ánimam, de córpore egréssam, in colúmbæ spécie cæli secréta penetráre.

incolumbespeciescholasticeanimavisest.en: In the likeness of a dove * the soul of Scholastica was seen.
incolumbespeciescholasticeanimavisest.la: In colúmbæ spécie * Scholásticæ ánima visa est.

scholasticeanimavisest.en: The soul of Scholastica was seen.

tebeatasponsachristi.en: Thee, O blessed bride of Christ,

siderumtolluntcoloni.en: The dwellers of the stars extol

sceptramundicumcoronis.en: The sceptres of the world with their crowns

dogmafratrisinsecuta.en: Following the teaching of thy brother

exodoregratiarum.en: Drawn by the fragrance of graces,

astranostiquerere.en: Thou knewest how to seek the stars.

dumfluentislacrymarum.en: While with the streams of tears

cogisimbrescurrere.en: Thou compellest the rains to run,

orenursiniparentis.en: From the mouth of the father of Nursia

verbacelisuscipis.en: Thou receivest the words of heaven.

lucefulgesexpetita.en: Thou shinest with the light thou soughtest

inpolorumvertice.en: In the height of the heavens,

claraflammiscaritatis.en: Bright with the flames of charity,

iunctasponsoconquiescis.en: Joined to the Bridegroom, thou restest

nuncbenignapellenubes.en: Now graciously drive away the clouds

cordibusfidelium.en: From the hearts of the faithful,

sempiterneclaritatis.en: May fill us with the joys

gloriampatricanamus.en: Let us sing glory to the Father,

nutibuscuiuscreantur.en: To him by whose will are created

questistaqueutnubesvolat.en: Who is she that flieth as a cloud?
questistaqueutnubesvolat.la: Qua est ista, quæ ut nubes volat?

etquasicolumbaadfenestrassuas.en: And as a dove to her windows?
etquasicolumbaadfenestrassuas.la: Et quasi colúmba ad fenéstras suas?

exsultetomniumturbafideliumprogloriavirg.en: Let all the throng * of the faithful exult for the glory of the gracious virgin Scholastica; let the choirs of virgins above all rejoice, celebrating her solemnity, who, shedding tears, besought the Lord, and could do more with him, because she loved more.
exsultetomniumturbafideliumprogloriavirg.la: Exsúltet ómnium * turba fidélium pro glória vírginis almæ Scholásticæ; læténtur præcípue catérvæ vírginum, celebrántes ejus solemnitátem, quæ fundens lácrymas, Dóminum rogávit, et ab eo plus pótuit, quia plus amávit.

surgeamicameaspeciosameetvenicolumbameai.en: Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come: my dove in the clefts of the rock, in the hollow places of the wall, shew me thy face, let thy voice sound in my ears: for thy voice is sweet, and thy face comely.
surgeamicameaspeciosameetvenicolumbameai.la: Surge, amíca mea, speciósa mea, et veni, colúmba mea, in foramínibus petræ, in cavérna macériæ, osténde mihi fáciem tuam, sonet vox tua in áuribus meis: vox enim tua dulcis, et fácies tua decóra.

iamnoctisumbreconcidunt.en: Now the shadows of night fall away,

fuganturimbresnubibus.en: The rains are put to flight with the clouds,

vernantquecampisiderum.en: And the fields of the stars grow green

amorisauctorevocat.en: The author of love calleth her forth,

ardensadorisoscula.en: Burning for the kisses of his mouth,

quampulchragressumpromoves.en: How beautiful are thy steps as thou goest forth,

ocharaprolesprincipis.en: O dear offspring of the Prince!

gratesrependitnumini.en: And returneth thanks to the Godhead.

amplexasponsidexteram.en: Embracing the right hand of the Bridegroom,

metitcoronasdebitas.en: She reapeth the crowns that are her due,

immersarivisglorie.en: Plunged in the streams of glory,

deiquepotagaudiis.en: And filled with the joys of God.

techristeflosconvallium.en: Thee, O Christ, the flower of the valleys,

patremquecumparaclito.en: And the Father with the Paraclete,

cunctosperorbiscardines.en: Throughout all the bounds of the world

eccetupulchresamicamea.en: Behold, thou art fair, my love.
eccetupulchresamicamea.la: Ecce tu pulchra es, amíca mea.

eccetupulchresoculituicolumbarum.en: Behold, thou art fair; thy eyes are doves' eyes.
eccetupulchresoculituicolumbarum.la: Ecce tu pulchra es; óculi tui columbárum.

oquampreclarasuntmeritabeatescholasticeo.en: O how glorious are * the merits of blessed Scholastica! O how great the power of her tears, by which the renowned Virgin drew down a flood of rain from a cloudless sky.
oquampreclarasuntmeritabeatescholasticeo.la: O quam præclára sunt * mérita beátæ Scholásticæ! O quanta virtus lacrimárum, per quas ínclyta Virgo áeris serenitátem ad plúviæ traxit inundatiónem.

unestcolumbameaperfectameaviderunteamfil.en: One is my dove, my perfect one: the daughters of Sion saw her, and declared her most blessed, and the queens praised her.
unestcolumbameaperfectameaviderunteamfil.la: Una est colúmba mea, perfécta mea: vidérunt eam fíliæ Sion, et beatíssimam prædicavérunt et regínæ laudavérunt eam.

hodiesacravirgoscholasticainspeciecolumb.en: This day * the holy virgin Scholastica, in the likeness of a dove, went all joyful into the heavens: this day she meriteth to enjoy for ever, with her brother, the joys of the heavenly life.
hodiesacravirgoscholasticainspeciecolumb.la: Hódie * sacra virgo Scholástica in spécie colúmbæ, ad ǽthera tota festíva perréxit: hódie cœlestis vitæ gáudiis cum fratre suo pérfrui merétur in sempitérnum.

beatusgregoriusincathedrapetrisublimatus.en: Blessed Gregory, * raised to the chair of Peter, fulfilled by his deeds the name of Watchful.

inillotemporevenitiesusinpartescesareeph.en: At that time: Jesus came into the quarters of Caesarea Philippi: and he asked his disciples, saying: Whom do men say that the Son of man is? But they said: Some John the Baptist, and other some Elias, and others Jeremias, or one of the prophets. Jesus saith to them: But whom do you say that I am? Simon Peter answered and said: Thou art Christ, the Son of the living God. And Jesus answering, said to him: Blessed art thou, Simon Bar-Jona: because flesh and blood hath not revealed it to thee, but my Father who is in heaven. And I say to thee: That thou art Peter; and upon this rock I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. And I will give to thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven. And whatsoever thou shalt bind upon earth, it shall be bound also in heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt loose upon earth, it shall be loosed also in heaven.
inillotemporevenitiesusinpartescesareeph.la: In illo témpore: Venit Jesus in partes Cæsaréæ Philíppi, et interrogábat discípulos suos, dicens: Quem dicunt hómines esse Fílium hóminis? At illi dixérunt: Alii Joánnem Baptístam, alii autem Elíam, álii vero Jeremíam, aut unum ex prophétis. Dicit illis Jesus: Vos autem quem me esse dícitis? Respóndens Simon Petrus, dixit: Tu es Christus, Fílius Dei vivi. Respóndens autem Jesus, dixit ei: Beátus es, Simon Bar Jona: quia caro et sanguis non revelávit tibi, sed Pater meus, qui in cœlis est. Et ego dico tibi, quia tu es Petrus, et super hanc petram ædificábo Ecclésiam meam, et portæ ínferi non prævalébunt advérsus eam. Et tibi dabo claves regni cœlórum. Et quodcúmque ligáveris super terram, erit ligátum et in cœlis: et quodcúmque sólveris super terram, erit solútum et in cœlis.

fuitvirvitevenerabilisgratiabenedictuset.en: There was a man * of venerable life, Benedict by grace and by name, who from the very time of his boyhood, bearing the heart of an old man, surpassing his years by his ways, gave his mind to no pleasure.
fuitvirvitevenerabilisgratiabenedictuset.la: Fuit vir * vitæ venerábilis, grátia Benedíctus et nómine, qui ab ipso puerítiæ suæ témpore cor gerens seníle, ætátem móribus tránsiens, nulli ánimum voluptáti dedit.

beatusvirbenedictusplusappetiitmalamundi.en: The blessed man Benedict * desired rather to suffer the evils of the world than its praises; to be wearied with labours for God, than to be exalted by the favours of this life.

gloriosusconfessordominibenedictusvitama.en: The glorious * Confessor of the Lord, Benedict, leading an angelic life upon earth, was made a mirror of good works to the world: and therefore he now rejoiceth with Christ without end in heaven.
gloriosusconfessordominibenedictusvitama.la: Gloriósus * Confessor Dómini Benedíctus vitam angélicam gerens in terris, spéculum bonórum óperum factus est mundo: et ídeo cum Christo jam sine fine gaudet in cælis.

omnipotenssempiternedeusquihodiernadieca.en: O almighty, everlasting God, who on this day didst raise up to heaven thy most holy Confessor Benedict, delivered from the prison of the flesh: † grant, we beseech thee, to thy servants who celebrate this feast, the pardon of all their sins; * that they who with exulting souls rejoice together in his glory, may, by his intercession with thee, be made sharers also in his merits.

quamvispostaροstolossanctipatresetdoctor.en: Although, after the Apostles, many of our holy Fathers and Doctors say so many and such great things concerning the reason of our faith, to confute the foolishness and to break the hardness of unbelievers, and to feed those who, their hearts being already cleansed by faith, delight in the reason of that same faith, after which, its certainty once had, we ought to hunger; so that neither in our times nor in times to come may we hope for any equal to them in the contemplation of truth: yet I think none is to be blamed if, being established in the faith, he will exercise himself in searching out its reason. For they too, because the days of man are short, could not say all that they might have said, had they lived longer; and the reason of truth is so ample and so deep that it cannot be exhausted by mortals; and the Lord in his Church, with which he promiseth to be even to the consummation of the world, ceaseth not to impart the gifts of his grace.
quamvispostaροstolossanctipatresetdoctor.la: Quamvis post Aρόstolos sancti Patres et Doctóres nostri multi tot et tanta de fidei nostræ ratióne dicant ad confutándum insipiéntiam et frangéndum durítiam infidélium, et ad pascéndum eos, qui, jam corde fide mundáto, eiúsdem fídei ratióne, quam post ejus certitúdinem debémus esuríre, delectántur; ut nec nostris nec futúris tempóribus ullum illis parem in veritátis contemplatióne sperémus: nullum tamen reprehendéndum árbitror, si fide stabilítus, in ratiónis ejus indágine se volúerit exercére. Nam et illi, quia breves dies hóminis sunt, non ómnia quæ possent, si diútius vixíssent, dícere potuérunt; et veritátis rátio tam ampla tamque profúnda est, ut a mortálibus néqueat exhauríri; et Dóminus in Ecclésia sua, cum qua se esse usque ad consummatiónem sæculi promíttit, grátiæ suæ dona non désinit impertíri.

hicestanselmusdoctorpreclarussubdiscipli.en: This is † Anselm, the renowned Doctor, trained under the discipline of Lanfranc: who, when he was the beloved father of monks, was called to the dignity of a bishop;
hicestanselmusdoctorpreclarussubdiscipli.la: Hic est † Ansélmus, Doctor præclárus, sub disciplína Lanfránci institútus: qui cum esset monachorum pater amábilis, ad pontificáles ínfulas vocátus est;

etprolibertatesancteecclesiestrenuedecer.en: And he valiantly contended for the liberty of holy Church, alleluia.
etprolibertatesancteecclesiestrenuedecer.la: Et pro libertáte sanctæ Ecclésiæ strénue decertávit, allelúja.

nonancillamsedliberamessechristisponsami.en: With unconquered voice he maintained that the bride of Christ is not a handmaid, but free.
nonancillamsedliberamessechristisponsami.la: Non ancillam, sed liberam esse Christi sponsam, invícta voce asserébat.

etutaliataceamquibussacrapaginanosadinve.en: And, to say nothing of other places in which the sacred page inviteth us to search out the reason, where it saith: Unless you believe, you shall not understand, it plainly admonisheth us to stretch forth our intention unto understanding, when it teacheth how we ought to advance toward it. Lastly, since I understand that the understanding which we attain in this life is a mean between faith and sight, I judge that the more any one advanceth toward it, the nearer he draweth to that sight for which we all long. Strengthened therefore by this consideration, although I be a man of very little knowledge, I strive to rise up somewhat, as far as heavenly grace vouchsafeth to grant me, to behold the reason of those things which we believe; and when I find anything which before I saw not, I willingly open it to others, that by the judgment of another I may learn what I ought securely to hold.
etutaliataceamquibussacrapaginanosadinve.la: Et, ut alia taceam, quibus sacra pagina nos ad investigandum rationem invitat, ubi dicit: Nisi cre-didéritis, non intellegetis, aperte nos monet intentionem ad intellectum extendere, cum docet qualiter ad illum debeamus profícere. Dénique quoniam inter fidem et speciem in-telléctum, quem in hac vita cápimus, esse médium intellego: quanto aliquís ad illum profícit, tanto eum propinquare speciéi, ad quam omnes anhelá-mus, existimo. Hac igitur ego consideratióne, licet sim homo parvæ nimis scientiæ, confortátus, ad eórum quæ crédimus, ra-tiónem intuendam, quantum supérna grátia mihi dare dignátur, aliquántum conor assúrgere; et cum aliquod, quod prius non videbam, repério, id áliis libénter apério, quátenus, quid secúre tenére débe-am, aliéno discam judício.

epistdeincarnverbii.en: Epistle on the Incarnation of the Word, I

sedpriusquamdequestionedisseramaliquidpr.en: But before I discourse of the question, I will set down somewhat beforehand to restrain the presumption of those who with wicked rashness dare to dispute against any of those things which the Christian faith confesseth, because they cannot grasp it with the understanding; and with foolish pride judge rather that that can in no wise be which they cannot understand, than with humble wisdom confess that many things may be which they themselves are not able to comprehend. For no Christian ought to dispute how that which the Catholic Church believeth with the heart and confesseth with the mouth is not; but, ever holding the same faith without doubting, loving it, and living according to it, he ought humbly, as far as he can, to seek the reason how it is. If he can understand, let him give thanks to God; if he cannot, let him not thrust out his horns to toss, but bow down his head to adore.
sedpriusquamdequestionedisseramaliquidpr.la: Sed priúsquam de quæstióne disseram, aliquid præmittam ad compescéndam præsumptiónem eórum, qui nefánda temeritáte audent disputáre contra áliquid eórum, quæ fides christiána confitétur, quóniam id intelléctu cápere néqueunt, et pótius insipiénti supérbia júdicant nullátenus posse esse, quod nequeunt intellégere, quam húmili sapiéntia fateántur esse multa posse, quæ ipsi non váleant comprehendere. Nullus quippe christiánus debet disputáre, quómodo, quod cathólica Ecclésia corde credit et ore confitétur, non sit; sed semper eandem fidem indubitánter tenéndo, amándo et secúndum illam vivéndo, humíliter quantum potest, quærere ratiónem, quómodo sit. Si potest intellégere, Deo grátias agat; si non potest, non immíttat córnua ad ventilándum, sed submíttat caput ad venerándum.

beatusanselmusdixitmerensadepiscoposindo.en: Blessed Anselm † said sorrowfully to the bishops: Ye purpose to yoke an untamed bull and a weak sheep together to the plough: the bull will miserably tear the sheep, dragged through thorns and briars;
