etgaudiumvestrummoxinmestitiamconvertetu.la: Et gáudium vestrum mox in mæstítiam convertétur, allelúja.

tribulationesmemanentsednihilhorumvereor.en: Tribulations await me; but I fear none of these things, so that I may finish my course.
tribulationesmemanentsednihilhorumvereor.la: Tribulatiónes me manent; sed nihil horum véreor, dúmmodo consúmmem cursum meum.

priusergofidemundandumestcorsicutdicitur.en: First therefore the heart must be cleansed by faith, as it is said of God: Purifying their hearts by faith; and first must the eyes be enlightened through the keeping of the Lord's commandments, because the commandment of the Lord is lightsome, enlightening the eyes; and first, through humble obedience to the testimonies of God, we must become little ones, that we may learn the wisdom which the testimony of the Lord, being faithful, giveth, giving wisdom to little ones. Whence the Lord saith: I confess to thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them to little ones. First, I say, putting behind us the things that are of the flesh, let us live according to the spirit, before we judge and discuss the deep things of faith; for he that liveth according to the flesh is carnal or sensual, of whom it is said: The sensual man perceiveth not these things that are of the Spirit of God. But he that by the spirit mortifieth the deeds of the flesh is made spiritual; of whom we read that the spiritual man judgeth all things, and he himself is judged of no man.
priusergofidemundandumestcorsicutdicitur.la: Prius ergo fide mundandum est cor, sicut dicitur de Deo: Fide mundans corda eórum; et prius per præceptórum Dómini custódiam illuminándi sunt óculi, quia præcéptum Dómini lúcidum illúminans óculos; et prius per húmilem obedientiam testimoniórum Dei debémus fíeri párvuli, ut discámus sapiéntiam, quam dat testimónium Dómini fidéle, sapiéntiam præstans párvulis. Unde Dóminus: Confiteor tibi, Pater, Dómine cæli et terræ, quia abscondísti hæc a sapiéntibus et prudéntibus, et revelásti ea párvulis. Prius, inquam, ea, quæ carnis sunt, postponéntes, secúndum spíritum vivámus, quam profúnda fidei diiudicándo discutiámus; nam qui secundum carnem vivit, carnalis sive animalis est, de quo dicitur: Animalis homo non percipit ea, quæ sunt Spiritus Dei. Qui vero spiritu facta carnis mortificat, spiritualis efficitur; de quo legitur, quia spiritualis omnia júdicat, et ipse a nemine judicatur.

cumessentpatresinsynodocongregatiurbanus.en: When the Fathers † were gathered together in synod, Urban the Pontiff cried out: Father and master Anselm, archbishop of the English, where art thou?
cumessentpatresinsynodocongregatiurbanus.la: Cum essent † Patres in synodo congregati, Urbanus Pontifex clamavit: Pater et magister Anselme, Anglorum archiepiscope, ubi es?

ascendeusqueadnosetpugnanspromatretuetno.en: Come up even unto us; and fighting for thy Mother and ours, help us, alleluia.
ascendeusqueadnosetpugnanspromatretuetno.la: Ascende usque ad nos; et pugnans pro Matre tua et nostra, adjuva nos, alleluja.

benedictussitsensustuusetsermooristuisit.en: Blessed be thy understanding, and blessed be the speech of thy mouth.
benedictussitsensustuusetsermooristuisit.la: Benedictus sit sensus tuus, et sermo oris tui sit benedictus.

beatusanselmusseculiprincipesdocebatdice.en: Blessed Anselm * taught the princes of the world, saying: God loveth nothing more in this world than the liberty of his Church, alleluia.
beatusanselmusseculiprincipesdocebatdice.la: Beátus Ansélmus * sǽculi príncipes docébat, dicens: Nihil ámplius díligit Deus in hoc mundo, quam Ecclésiæ suæ libertátem, allelúja.

anselmusaugustepretorieinitalianatusapue.en: Anselm, born at Aosta in Italy, followed the study of letters from his boyhood; and when in a very short time he had made great progress therein, he left his country and betook himself to the monastery of Bec of the Order of St. Benedict, where, having for his master Lanfranc, the prior of the monastery, a man eminent in religion and wisdom, he joined sacred learning to secular, and in the same monastery became a monk in the twenty-seventh year of his age: but when Lanfranc was taken to govern the monastery of Caen, Anselm succeeded in his place, and having thus obtained a larger occasion of serving God, he spent himself wholly upon that charge and upon the needs of the brethren. Meanwhile he was so given to the contemplation of divine things, that, God revealing them to him, he most clearly perceived and explained questions concerning the Godhead most obscure and unheard of before that time.
anselmusaugustepretorieinitalianatusapue.la: Ansélmus Augústæ Prætóriæ in Itália natus, a puerítia stúdia litterárum sectátus, cum brevi ádmodum plúrimum in eis profecísset, relícta pátria, ad Beccénse monastérium Ordinis sancti Benedícti se cóntulit, ubi præceptóre usus Lanfránco, cœnóbii prióre, viro præstánti religióne et sapiéntia, sæculári litteratúræ sacram adjúnxit, ac in eódem cœnóbio vigésimo séptimo ætátis suæ anno mónachus effícitur: sed Lanfranco ad Cadoménsis cœnóbii régimen assúmpto, in ejus locum succéssit Ansélmus, sicque ampliórem Deo serviéndi nactus occasiónem, totum se ei múneri, fratrúmque necessitátibus impéndit. Divinárum ínterim rerum contemplatióni ádeo déditus fuit, ut obscuríssimas et ante id témporis inaudítas de Divinitáte quæstiónes, Deo reseránte, claríssime perspéxerit et explicáverit.

abstinentieetcontinentietantefuitutabini.en: So great was his abstinence and continence, that from the beginning of his priorship all allurement was utterly quenched in him; so much had he wasted his body with fasting. His sleep was very scanty: first, because, the day not sufficing for the giving of counsel, he was compelled to add a good part of the night; then, because at night he corrected the books of the monastery's library, which at that time were very badly written; lastly, because, exercising himself in holy meditations and pouring forth showers of tears, he for the most part took little or no sleep before the night vigils. Certain rivals, who were the elders in the monastery and took it ill that a young man had been preferred before them in the office of prior, he so overcame by humility and charity, that from enemies he made them well-wishers and his dearest friends. He very often visited the house of the sick, and himself ministered to each whatever they had need of.
abstinentieetcontinentietantefuitutabini.la: Abstinéntiæ et continéntiæ tante fuit, ut ab initio priorátus, illécebra in eo pénitus exstíncta sit; ádeo corpus inédia. maceráverat. Somnus illi parcíssimus, proptérea, quod die pro dandis consíliis non sufficiénte, noctis bonam áddere partem cogerétur; deínde, quod bibliothécæ monastérii libros, qui eo témpore péssime scripti erant, nocte corrigébat; demum, quod in sanctis meditatiónibus se exércens, lacrimárum imbres fundens plerúmque ante noctúrnas vigílias parum aut nihil somni capiébat. Æmulos quosdam ægre feréntes, júvenem sibi, qui senióres in monastério erant, in prioris officio prælátum, ádeo humilitáte et caritáte vicit, ut ex inimícis sibi benévolos et amicíssimos rédderet. Infirmórum domum frequentíssime invisébat, quæque síngulis opus erant, ipse per se ministrábat.

defunctoherluinobeccensiabbateineiuslocu.en: When Herluin, abbot of Bec, was dead, Anselm was chosen in his place by the votes of all; and when, casting himself at their feet, he besought them to turn that burden away from him as being unworthy, he was compelled by them, they likewise casting themselves upon the ground, to give his consent. Soon, having committed the business of the monastery to the care of brethren whom he knew to be diligent and fit, he began to give himself wholly to the instruction, admonition and correction of the brethren, and to divine contemplation. He was so zealous in receiving guests according to the prescription of the Rule, that sometimes he bade food be taken from the tables of the brethren to be set before the guests, God ever relieving the need of the monks by frequent miracles.
defunctoherluinobeccensiabbateineiuslocu.la: Defuncto Herluíno Beccénsi abbáte, in ejus locum ómnium suffragiis suffícitur Ansélmus, qui, cum pédibus eórum provolútus, ut a se útpote indígno id óneris avérterent, obsecráret, ab eísdem páriter in terram se prosternéntibus, ut assénsum præbéret, coáctus est. Qui mox monastérii negotiis sollicitúdini fratrum, quos ipse strénuos et idóneos nóverat, delegátis, totus eruditióni, admonitióni et correctióni fratrum,divinæque contemplatióni vacáre cœpit. Hóspitum suscipiendórum juxta præscríptum Régulæ ádeo studiósus fuit, ut nonnúmquam cibos de mensis fratrum jússerit auférri, ut hospítibus apponeréntur, Deo semper monachórum indigéntiæ frequéntibus miráculis subveniénte.

mortuodeindelanfrancoquiexabbatecadomens.en: Then, when Lanfranc was dead, who from abbot of Caen had been made archbishop of Canterbury, Anselm succeeded him there also, to the great joy of the whole kingdom, in the year one thousand and ninety-three. But soon, a dissension arising between William, king of England, who unjustly claimed for himself the rights of the Church, and Anselm, who defended the liberty of the Church, he was compelled to go into exile once and again; he came to Rome, and being honourably received by Urban the Second, he was present at the Council of Bari, and there by the strength of his doctrine he refuted the Greeks who erred concerning the procession of the Holy Ghost. At length, under Paschal the Second, who succeeded Urban, William, king of England, having been taken from among men by a dreadful death, he was recalled into England by Henry his brother, and obtained the liberty of the Church for which he had laboured. He greatly furthered the festival of the Conception of the Virgin Mary, which a little before had begun to be celebrated in England by the abbot Elpinus, admonished by a divine revelation; on which also he put forth an excellent commentary. He died at last on the eleventh day before the Kalends of May, in the year of the Lord one thousand one hundred and nine, renowned for doctrine and miracles.
mortuodeindelanfrancoquiexabbatecadomens.la: Mortuo deinde Lanfranco, qui ex abbate Cadomensi factus fuerat archiepiscopus Cantuariensis, et etiam successit Anselmus, magna totius regni gratulatione anno millesimo nonagesimo tercio. Sed mox dissidio orto inter Willelmum Angliæ regem, Ecclesiae jura inique sibi vindicantem, et Anselmum, Ecclesiae libertatem tuentem semel et iterum exsulare compulsus, Roman venit, honorificeque ab Urbano secundo exceptus, Concilio Barensis interfuit. Graecosque ibi, circa processionem Spiritus Sancti errantes, doctrina sua robore coercuit. Tandem sub Paschale secundo, qui successit Urbano, horrenda morte ex humanis sublato Willelmmo Angliæ rege, ab Henrico ejus fratre in Angliam revocatur, et libertatem Ecclesiae, pro qua laboraverat, adeptus est. Favit plurimum festivitati Conceptionis Virginis Mariae, paulo ante in Anglia ab Elpino abbate divina revelatione admonito,celebrari coeptae, de qua etiam egrégium edidit commentarium. Móritur demum undecimo Kalendas Maji, anno Domini millésimo centesimo nono, doctrina et miraculis clarus.

surrexitodoplenusspiritusanctetmontastic.en: Odo arose, * full of the Holy Ghost, and the glory of the monastic Order was renewed throughout the world, alleluia.
surrexitodoplenusspiritusanctetmontastic.la: Surréxit Odo * plenus Spíritu Sancto, et montástici Ordínis decus per orbem renovátum est, allelúja.

maioluscaritateredundansacgratiasanctita.en: Majolus, * overflowing with charity and grace, emulating the holiness of the Angels, was borne in virtue above men, alleluia.
maioluscaritateredundansacgratiasanctita.la: Májolus, * caritáte redúndans ac grátia, sanctitátem angélicam æmulétus, virtúte super hómines ferebátur, allelúja.

qualemcaritatemcordeservaretodilomiredem.en: What charity * Odilo kept in his heart he wondrously showed, who, grieving with the torments of the faithful departed, decreed that every year they should be cherished with sweet refreshment, alleluia.
qualemcaritatemcordeservaretodilomiredem.la: Qualem caritátem * corde serváret Odílo mire demonstrávit, qui defunctórum fidélium cruciátibus cóndolens, eos quotánnis dulci refrigério fovéri decrévit, allelúja.

cumindiemagnisabbatibeatushugosacrisinte.en: When on the day * of the great Sabbath blessed Hugh was present at the sacred rites, he saluted the pillar of the new light, praying with frequent sighs that he might happily come unto the land of promise, alleluia.
cumindiemagnisabbatibeatushugosacrisinte.la: Cum in die * magni Sábbati beátus Hugo sacris interésset, colúmnam novæ lucis salutábat crebis exórans suspíriis, ut ad terram promissiónis felíciter perveníret, allelúja.

confessionecordium.en: Who by the confession of their hearts

deusquinossanctorumtuorumetsolemnitatele.en: O God, who both gladdenest us by the solemnity of thy Saints, and stirrest us up to progress by their imitation: grant that we may follow by the example of a holy life those whom we honour by our service.
deusquinossanctorumtuorumetsolemnitatele.la: Deus, qui nos Sanctórum tuórum et solemnitáte lætíficas, et imitatióne súscitas ad proféctum: præsta; ut quos venerámur offício, étiam piæ conversatiónis sequámur exémplo.

posuitoculumsuumsupercordaillorumostende.en: He set his eye upon their hearts to shew them the greatness of his works, that they might praise the name which he hath sanctified.
posuitoculumsuumsupercordaillorumostende.la: Pósuit óculum suum super corda illórum, osténdere illis magnália óperum suórum, ut nomen sanctificatiónis colláudent.

subtantispatribuscluniacilausperomnesdif.en: Under such great fathers the praise of Cluny was spread through all the churches; † the holy Rule shone with new beauty, the monasteries that were growing old flourished again,
subtantispatribuscluniacilausperomnesdif.la: Sub tantis pátribus Cluníaci laus per omnes diffundebátur ecclésias, † sancta Régula novo decóre refúlsit, monastéria veterascéntia refloruérunt,

etperorbemmonachorumexercitussacrofedere.en: And throughout the world the army of monks, bound together by a sacred covenant, did battle, alleluia.
etperorbemmonachorumexercitussacrofedere.la: Et per orbem monachórum exércitus sacro fœdere devínctus militávit, allelúja.

edificatestcluniacidomusutcivitasillucas.en: The house of Cluny is built as a city: † thither did the tribes of the Lord go up to praise the name of the Lord.
edificatestcluniacidomusutcivitasillucas.la: Ædificáta est Cluníaci domus ut cívitas: † illuc ascendérunt tribus Dómini ad confiténdum nómini Dómini.

exepistolasanctipetridamianiepiscopi.en: From the Epistle of St. Peter Damian, Bishop
exepistolasanctipetridamianiepiscopi.la: Ex Epístola sancti Petri Damiáni Epíscopi

quidaliudcluniacensemonasteriumnisiagrum.en: What else should I call the monastery of Cluny but a field of the Lord full, where, as it were a heap of heavenly harvests, is the choir of so many monks living in charity? That field is broken up daily by the hoe of holy preaching, and in it the seeds of the heavenly word are scattered. There the increase of spiritual fruits is heaped up, that it may afterwards be borne into the heavenly granaries. Cluny, moreover, is a certain spiritual field where heaven and earth meet together, and as it were an arena of combat, where, after the manner of a spiritual wrestling-ground, the frail flesh wrestleth against the powers of the air. For our wrestling is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers of the world of this darkness, against the spirits of wickedness in the high places. There Josue, not that son of Nun, but the leader of the heavenly army, who is the instructor of spiritual warriors, teacheth his soldiers to tread upon the proud necks of the five kings: over whom, in truth, they are known to obtain a triumphal victory, who restrain as many senses of the body by the discipline of a strict guard.
quidaliudcluniacensemonasteriumnisiagrum.la: Quid áliud Cluniacénse monastérium, nisi agrum Dómini plenum díxerim, ubi velut acérvus est cæléstium ségetum, chorus tot in caritáte degéntium monachórum? Ager ille cotidiáno sanctæ prædicatiónis ligóne proscindítur, et in eo cæléstis elóquii sémina conspergúntur. Illic spirituálium frugum provéntus aggéritur, ut hórreis póstmodum cæléstibus inferátur. Cluniácus prætérea ager spirituális quidam campus est, ubi cælum et terra congréditur, ac velut aréna certáminis, ubi spirituális more palǽstræ caro frágilis advérsus potestátes aéreas colluctátur. Non est enim nobis colluctátio advérsus carnem et sánguinem, sed advérsus mundi rectóres tenebrárum harum, contra spirituália nequítiæ, in cæléstibus. Illic Jósue, non ille fílius Nun, sed cæléstis ductor exércitus, et qui spirituálium instrúctor est bellatórum, suos édocet mílites, supérbas quinque regum calcáre cervíces: super quos nimírum triumphálem noscúntur obtinére victóriam, qui tótidem sensus córporum per distríctæ custódiæ cóhibent disciplínam.

supernivemdealbabuntursanctituidomineall.en: Thy Saints, O Lord, * shall be made whiter than snow, alleluia.
supernivemdealbabuntursanctituidomineall.la: Super nivem * dealbabúntur sancti tui, Dómine, allelúja.

iusticonfitebunturnominituethabitabuntre.en: The just shall give glory * to thy name, and the upright shall dwell with thy countenance, alleluia.
iusticonfitebunturnominituethabitabuntre.la: Justi confitebúntur * nómini tuo, et habitábunt recti cum vultu tuo, allelúja

sanctimeiquiinistoseculocertamenhabuisti.en: My Saints, * who in this world have had the conflict, I render unto you the reward of your labours, alleluia.
sanctimeiquiinistoseculocertamenhabuisti.la: Sancti mei, * qui in isto sǽculo certámen habuístis, mercédem labórum ego reddo vobis, allelúja.

sanctiestisdicitdominusmultiplicabonumer.en: Ye are holy, * saith the Lord: I will multiply your number, that ye may pray for my people in this place, alleluia.
sanctiestisdicitdominusmultiplicabonumer.la: Sancti estis * dicit Dóminus multiplicábo numerum vestrum ut orétis pro pópulo meo in loco isto, allelúja.

creavitillisscientiamspiritussensuimplev.en: He created in them the science of the spirit, he filled their heart with wisdom, and shewed them both good and evil.
creavitillisscientiamspiritussensuimplev.la: Creávit illis sciéntiam spíritus, sensu implévit cor illórum, et mala et bona osténdit illis.

diesreduxitannua.en: The yearly day hath brought back,

quipuramentisacie.en: Who with pure keenness of mind,

mundidevictoprincipe.en: The prince of the world being overcome,

iammessistenentgaudia.en: Now possess the joys of the harvest.

iuxtadictumapostoli.en: According to the saying of the Apostle,

mucronesanctispiritus.en: With the sword of the Holy Ghost

hostesprosternuntinvidos.en: They lay low their envious foes.

fulgebuntiustiettamquamscintilleinarundi.en: The just shall shine, * and shall run to and fro like sparks among the reeds; they shall judge nations, and shall reign for ever, alleluia.
fulgebuntiustiettamquamscintilleinarundi.la: Fulgébunt justi, * et tamquam scintíllæ in arundinéto discúrrent, judicábunt natiónes, et regnábunt in ætérnum, allelúja.

omniaoperaillorumvelutsolinconspectudeie.en: All their works are as the sun in the sight of God: and his eyes are continually upon their ways.
omniaoperaillorumvelutsolinconspectudeie.la: Ómnia ópera illórum velut sol in conspéctu Dei: et óculi ejus sine intermissióne inspiciéntes in viis eórum.

exaudivocemmeamquaclamaviadte.en: Hear † my voice, with which I have cried to thee:
exaudivocemmeamquaclamaviadte.la: Exáudi † vocem meam, qua clamávi ad te:

misereremeietexaudimealleluia.en: Have mercy on me, and hear me, alleluia.
misereremeietexaudimealleluia.la: Miserére mei, et exáudi me, allelúja.

tantotemporevobiscumsumetnoncognovistism.en: Have I been so long a time with you, and have you not known me?
tantotemporevobiscumsumetnoncognovistism.la: Tanto témpore vobíscum sum, et non cognovístis me?

philippequividetmevidetetpatremmeumallel.en: Philip, he that seeth me seeth my Father also, alleluia: † Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and the Father in me? † alleluia, alleluia.
philippequividetmevidetetpatremmeumallel.la: Philíppe, qui videt me, videt et Patrem meum, allelúja: † Non créditis quia ego in Patre, et Pater in me est? † allelúja, allelúja.

domineostendenobispatremetsufficitnobis.en: Lord, shew us the Father, and it is enough for us.
domineostendenobispatremetsufficitnobis.la: Dómine, osténde nobis Patrem, et súfficit nobis.

conciodeprobitatedoctorumecclesieabiniti.en: Discourse 9, on the uprightness of the Doctors of the Church; from the beginning
conciodeprobitatedoctorumecclesieabiniti.la: Concio 9, de probitate Doctorum Ecclesiae; ab initio

basiliusnobiliscappadoxathenisunacumgreg.en: Basil, a noble of Cappadocia, having been instructed in secular letters at Athens together with Gregory Nazianzen, his dearest friend, and afterwards in sacred learning in a monastery, was called into Pontus to preach the Gospel of Jesus Christ. Soon, being taken as his helper by Eusebius, Bishop of Caesarea, he succeeded in his place. He defended the Son as consubstantial with the Father, and by miracles so moved the emperor Valens, who was angered against him, that he constrained him to withdraw the sentence of exile.
basiliusnobiliscappadoxathenisunacumgreg.la: Basilíus nóbilis Cáppadox, Athénis una cum Gregório Nazianzéno, ejus amicíssimo, sæculáribus lítteris, deínde in Monastério sacris erudítus, ad prædicándum Jesu Christi Evangélium in Pontum fuit accersítus. Mox ab Eusébio Cæsaréæ Epíscopo, adjútor adhíbitus, in ejus locum succéssit. Fílium Patri consubstantiálem esse deféndit, ac Valéntem imperatórem sibi irátum, miráculis ádeo flexit, ut ab exílii senténtia discédere coégerit.

abstinentietcontinentiafuitadmirabiliuni.en: He was of admirable abstinence and continence: he was content with a single tunic: constant in fasting and prayer, he kept his virginity perpetually. Having built monasteries, he so ordered the institute of the Monks, that he excellently joined together the advantages of the solitary and of the active life. He wrote much and with learning, and none, as Gregory Nazianzen beareth witness, hath explained the books of holy Scripture more truly or more richly. He died on the Kalends of January, when, living so much by the spirit, he seemed to consist of no part of the body besides skin and bones.
abstinentietcontinentiafuitadmirabiliuni.la: Abstinéntia et continéntia fuit admirábili: única túnica conténtus erat: in jejúnio et oratióne assíduus, virginitátem perpétuo cóluit. Monastériis extrúctis, ita Monachórum institútum temperá­vit‚ ut solitáriæ atque actuósæ vitæ utilitátes præcláre simul conjúngeret. Multa erudíte scripsit, ac nemo, teste Gregório Nazianzéno, sacræ Scriptúræ libros vérius aut ubérius explicávit. Obiit Kaléndis Januárii, cum tantum spíritu vivens, præter ossa et pellem, nulla prætérea córporis parte constáre viderétur.

pauloautemuniversusmunduscrucifixuserate.en: But to Paul the whole world was crucified, and he to the world. So he that is held by a vehement desire of following Christ can be turned to nothing more of this life: not to the love of parents or kinsfolk, where it is contrary to the precepts of the Lord (for then that saying hath place: If any man come to me, and hate not his father and mother, and the rest); nor to human fear, that for its sake we should withhold anything that is profitable; as the Saints accomplished, who said: We ought to obey God rather than men.
pauloautemuniversusmunduscrucifixuserate.la: Paulo autem univérsus mundus crucifíxus erat, et ipse mundo. Sic, qui veheménter cupiditáte sequéndi Christum tenétur, ad nihil ámplius hujus vitæ convérti potest: non ad paréntum aut cognatórum amórem, ubi præcéptis Dómini contrárius fúerit; (tunc enim occasiónem habet illud: Si quis venit ad me, et non ódio habet patrem suum et matrem et réliqua); non ad humánum timórem, ut propter ipsum subtrahámus áliquid utílium, id quod perpetrárunt Sancti, qui dixérunt: Obedíre opórtet Deo magis quam homínibus.

sermodevitetexercitationemonastica.en: Sermon on the monastic life and its exercise
sermodevitetexercitationemonastica.la: Sermo de vita et exercitatione monastica

ingressozachariatemplumdominiapparuiteig.en: When Zachary had entered into the temple of the Lord, there appeared to him Gabriel the Angel,
ingressozachariatemplumdominiapparuiteig.la: Ingrésso Zacharía templum Dómini, appáruit ei Gábriel Angelus,

stansadextrisaltarisincensi.en: Standing on the right side of the altar of incense.

etzachariasturbatusestvidensettimormagnu.en: And Zachary seeing him was troubled, and great fear fell upon him:
etzachariasturbatusestvidensettimormagnu.la: Et Zacharías turbátus est videns, et timor magnus írruit super eum:

tractatusinioanneminmedio.en: Tractate 123 on John, in the middle

virdeibenedictussignumcrucisediditetvasp.en: The man of God, Benedict, * made the sign of the cross, and the vessel of deadly drink was broken, as if he had given a stone for a sign.
virdeibenedictussignumcrucisediditetvasp.la: Vir Dei Benedictus * signum crucis edidit, et vas pestiferi potus ita confractum est, ac si pro signo lapidem dedisset.

completaorationetrespetrasinlocoposuitet.en: His prayer ended, * he set three stones in the place; and almighty God brought forth water in the high rock of the mountain.
completaorationetrespetrasinlocoposuitet.la: Completa oratione, * tres petras in loco posuit; et omnipotens Deus in montis excelsa rupe aquam produxit.

gloriosusconfessordominiorationemfaciens.en: The glorious * Confessor of the Lord, making prayer, gave his blessing; and the stone, upon which the old enemy was sitting, was suddenly lifted up.
gloriosusconfessordominiorationemfaciens.la: Gloriosus * Confessor Domini, orationem faciens, benedictionem dedit; et lapis, super quem antiquus hostis sedebat, subito levatus est.

regredienteanimacorpusculumpuericontremu.en: The soul returning, * the little body of the boy trembled, and before the eyes of all that were present he appeared alive.
regredienteanimacorpusculumpuericontremu.la: Regrediente anima, * corpusculum pueri contremuit, et sub oculis omnium, qui aderant, vivus apparuit.

cumplacidusexaquatrahereturviditsupercap.en: When Placid * was being drawn out of the water, he saw above his head the Abbot's sheepskin, which brought him back from the wave.
cumplacidusexaquatrahereturviditsupercap.la: Cum Placidus * ex aqua traheretur, vidit super caput suum Abbatis melotem, qui eum ab unda reducebat.

gemmacelestispretiosaregis.en: Precious jewel of the heavenly King,

normaiustorumviamonachorum.en: Rule of the just, way of monks,

nosabimmundibenedictemundi.en: From the mire of the unclean world, O Benedict,

tusolumspernenscorinastrafigens.en: Thou, scorning the earth, fixing thy heart on the stars,
tusolumspernenscorinastrafigens.la: Tu solum spernens, cor in astra figens

cogisheredesfieriparentes.en: Dost make thy parents to become thy heirs.

vasdeoplenumrepardarefractum.en: A vessel full of God, the broken thing to mend

magnusinparviseremitamembris.en: A great hermit in small limbs,

vincisetatemsuperaslaborem.en: Thou conquerest thy age, thou overcomest toil;

arctadistricterudimentavite.en: The strait beginnings of a severe life

stragesaxorumpuerumsepultum.en: The boy buried beneath the fall of stones,

moxutorastiprecesuscitasti.en: As soon as thou hadst prayed, by thy prayer thou didst raise up:

sensushinccarnicarosanitati.en: Hence sense is restored to the flesh, and the flesh to health

iuresubblandespeciecolumbe.en: Rightly under the form of a gentle dove

nesciamfellisanimamsororis.en: The soul of thy sister, that knew not gall,

summastellatipenetrareceli.en: Piercing the highest summits of the starry heaven

ipsepostclarumreferenstriumphum.en: Thyself, bearing back a glorious triumph,

celsadevictopetisastramundo.en: Seekest the lofty stars, the world being overcome:

luceflammantemradiantecallem.en: The pathway flaming with radiant light

hominnatalisbenedictibisc.en: Homily 17, on the Birthday of St. Benet Biscop

duosuntordineselectoruminiudiciofuturiun.en: There are two orders of the elect in the judgment to come: one, of those who shall judge with the Lord, of whom he maketh mention in this place, who have left all things and followed him; the other, of those who shall be judged by the Lord, who did not indeed in like manner leave all their goods, but yet of those things which they had were careful to give daily alms to the poor of Christ; whence they also shall hear in the judgment: Come, ye blessed of my Father, possess you the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world; for I was hungry, and you gave me to eat: I was thirsty, and you gave me to drink, and the rest; of whom also the Lord made mention in the earlier part of this lesson, when, a certain ruler asking by doing what good he might possess eternal life, he said: If thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments. Therefore he that keepeth the commandments of the Lord entereth into life eternal: but he that keepeth also the counsel of the Lord shall not only himself receive life, but shall also judge with the Lord concerning the life of others.
duosuntordineselectoruminiudiciofuturiun.la: Duo sunt órdines electórum in judício futúri : unus judicántium cum Dómino, de quibus hoc loco mémorat, qui reliquérunt ómnia, et secúti sunt illum: álius judicatórum a Dómino qui non quidem ómnia sua páriter reliquérunt, sed de his tamen quæ habébant, quotidiánas dare eleemósynas Christi paupéribus curábant; unde et auditúri sunt in judício : Veníte, benedícti Patris mei, possidéte præparátum vobis regnum a constitutióne mundi; esurívi enim, et dedístis mihi manducáre: sitívi, et dedístis mihi bíbere, et cétera, quorum et in superióribus hujus lectiónis Dóminus méminit, cum, príncipe quodam interrogánte, quid boni faciéndo vitam possidéret ætérnam: Si vis, inquit, ad vitam íngredi, serva mandáta. Ergo qui mandáta Dómini servat, ad vitam ingréditur ætérnam: qui autem etiam consílium Dómini, non tantum vitam ipse percípiet, sed etiam de vita aliórum cure Dómino judicábit.

sedetreproberumduosibifuturosordinesdomi.en: But we find also, the Lord telling it, that there shall be two orders of the reprobate there: one of those who, initiated into the mysteries of the Christian faith, disdain to exercise the works of faith; to whom he testifieth in the judgment: Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire, which was prepared for the devil and his angels; for I was hungry, and you gave me not to eat. The other of those who either never received the faith and mysteries of Christ, or, having received them, forsook them by apostasy; of whom he saith: But he that doth not believe, is already judged, because he believeth not in the name of the only begotten Son of God.
sedetreproberumduosibifuturosordinesdomi.la: Sed et reprobérum duos ibi futúros órdines Dómino narránte comperímus: unum eorum qui fidei christiánæ mystériis initiáte ópera fidei exercére contémnunt, quibus in judício testátur: Discédite a me maledícti in ignem ætérnum, qui præparátus est diábolo et ángelis ejus; esurívi enim, et non dedístis mihi manducáre. Alterum eórum, qui fidem et mystéria Christi vel nunquam suscepére, vel suscéptam per apostasíam deseruére, de quibus dicit: Qui autem non credit, jam judicátus est, quia non credit in nómine unigéniti Fílii Dei.

verumhiscuretimoreetpavoredebitepaulispe.en: But these things having been briefly called to mind with due fear and trembling, let us rather turn our hearing to the most joyful promises of our Lord and Saviour. Let us see what rewards, by the grace of so great a goodness, he promiseth to his followers, not of eternal life only, but excellent gifts of the present life also. And every one, saith he, that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands for my name's sake, shall receive an hundredfold, and shall possess life everlasting.
verumhiscuretimoreetpavoredebitepaulispe.la: Verum his cure timóre et pavóre débite paulísper commemorátis, ad lætíssima pótius Dómini et Salvatòris nostri promíssa convertámus audítum. Videámus quæ tantæ gratim pietátis, non ætérnæ tantúmmodo vitæ prǽmia suis sequácibus, sed et præséntis múnera pollicétur exímia. Et omnis, inquit, qui relíquerit domum, vel fratres, aut soróres, aut patrem, aut matrem, aut uxórem, aut fílios, aut agros propter nomen meum ; céntuplum accípiet et vitam ætérnam possidébit.

quienimterrenisaffectibussivepossessioni.en: For he that for the sake of Christ's discipleship hath renounced earthly affections or possessions, the more he hath advanced in his love, the more shall he find who rejoice to receive him with inward affection and to sustain him with their substance: to wit, the sharers of his profession and life, who delight to receive into their houses and lands him that hath been made poor for Christ, and to cherish him with a devotion of charity far greater than that of a wife, a parent, a brother, or a son according to the flesh.
quienimterrenisaffectibussivepossessioni.la: Qui enim terrénis afféctibus sive possessiónibus pro Christi discipulátu renunciáverit, quo plus in ejus amórem profécerit, eo plures invéniet, qui se intérno suscípere afféctu, et suis gáudeant sustentáre substántiis: ejus nimírum professiónibus vitǽque consórtes, qui se pro Christo páuperem factum in suis dómibus agrísque recípere, et majóre prorsus quam uxor, parens, frater, aut fílius carnális devotióne caritátis refovére delecténtur.

quantainsummisaccipit.en: How great things doth he receive on high,

peramplamundiclimata.en: Through the wide regions of the world!

eiuscarentumgratia.en: Of them that lacked his grace

tellusvomitcadavera.en: The earth casteth forth the corpses;

devotisundaliquida.en: For the devout the liquid wave

totiusorbisambitum.en: The compass of the whole world

persolisvidetradium.en: He seeth in a ray of the sun;

mensinauctoreposita.en: The mind that is fixed upon its Maker

pronementisvisceribus.en: With the depths of a lowly mind,

utcelumdesascendere.en: That thou grant us to ascend to heaven,

quosterraindocesspernere.en: Whom thou teachest to despise the earth.

ocelestisnormavitedoctoretduxbenedictecu.en: O rule of heavenly life, Doctor and Leader, Benedict, whose spirit exulteth with Christ in heavenly places: keep thy flock, gracious Shepherd, strengthen it by thy holy prayer, and make it, under thy leading, to enter the heavens by the shining way.
ocelestisnormavitedoctoretduxbenedictecu.la: O cælestis norma vitæ, Doctor et Dux Benedicte, cujus cum Christo spiritus exsultat in cælestibus: gregem, Pastor alme, serva, sancta prece corrobora, via cælos clarescente fac, te duce, penetrare.

adlugdunenseconciliumabeatogregoriodecim.en: Being summoned to the council of Lyons by blessed Gregory the Tenth, and created cardinal bishop of Albano, he rendered excellent service in the weighty affairs of the council, whereby both the dissensions of the schism were composed and the dogmas of the Church vindicated. In these labours, in the fifty-third year of his age and in the year of salvation one thousand two hundred and seventy-four, he died, to the great sorrow of all, and was honoured with a funeral by the whole council, the Roman Pontiff himself being present. Sixtus the Fourth enrolled him, renowned for very many and very great miracles, in the number of the Saints. He wrote much, wherein, joining the highest learning with the ardour of piety, he moveth the reader while he teacheth him: wherefore he was deservedly distinguished by Sixtus the Fifth with the name of the Seraphic Doctor.
adlugdunenseconciliumabeatogregoriodecim.la: Ad Lugdunénse concílium a beáto Gregório décimo accersítus et cardinális epíscopus Albanénsis creátus, árduis concílii rebus egrégiam navávit óperam; qua et schísmatis dissídia, compósita sunt, et ecclesiástica dógmata vindicáta. Quibus in labóribus, anno ætátis suæ quinquagésimo tértio, salútis vero millésimo ducentésimo septuagésimo quarto, summo ómnium mæróre decéssit, ab univérso concílio, ipso præsénte Románo Pontífice, fúnere honestátus. Eum Xystus quartus, plúrimis maximísque clarum miráculis, in Sanctórum númerum rétulit. Multa scripsit, in quibus summam eruditiónem cum pietátis ardóre conjúngens, lectórem docéndo movet: quare a Xysto quinto Doctóris Seráphici nómine mérito est insignítus.

precespopulituiquesumusdominepropitiusre.en: Look graciously, we beseech thee, O Lord, upon the prayers of thy people: and through the intercession of blessed Leo, thy Confessor and Bishop, whose solemnity we keep this day, turn away the scourges of thy wrath which we deserve for our sins.
precespopulituiquesumusdominepropitiusre.la: Preces pópuli tui, quǽsumus, Dómine, propítius réspice: et intermissióne beáti Leónis Confessóris tui atque Pontíficis, cujus hódie solémnia cólimus; flagélla tue iracúndiæ, quæ pro peccátis nostris mereámur, averte.

ovirimisericordiequorumnonacceperuntobli.en: O men * of mercy, whose godly deeds have not been forgotten: their seed, and their children for their sakes, remain for ever with glory.
ovirimisericordiequorumnonacceperuntobli.la: O viri * misericordiæ, quorum non accepérunt obliviónem justítiæ, semen eórum et fílii propter eos in ætérnum cum glória pérmanent.

deusmisericordiarumpaterquiecclesietuead.en: O God, Father of mercies, who, for the holy nurturing of youth, didst provide thy Church with blessed Jerome, Joseph, and John Baptist, by a singular charity: grant us by their merits that we may faithfully keep the spirit of adoption, whereby we are called and are thy sons.
deusmisericordiarumpaterquiecclesietuead.la: Deus, misericordiárum pater, qui Ecclésiæ tuæ ad sancte fovéndum juventútem beátos Hierónymum, Joséphum et Joánnem Baptístam singulári caritáte providísti concéde nobis eórum méritis; ut spíritum adoptiónis, quo fílii tui nominámur et sumus, fidéliter custodiámus.

amendicovobisquoduniexminimismeisfecisti.en: Amen I say to you: * as long as you did it to one of these my least, you did it to me: come, ye blessed of my Father, possess you the kingdom prepared for you from the beginning of the world.
amendicovobisquoduniexminimismeisfecisti.la: Amen dico vobis: * quod uni ex mínimis meis fecístis, mihi fecístis: veníte, benedícti Patris mei, posidéte parátum vobis regnum ab inítio sǽculi.

nomensempiternumdabosanctismeisdicitdomi.en: An everlasting name * will I give to my Saints, saith the Lord, † they shall obtain joy and gladness for ever.
nomensempiternumdabosanctismeisdicitdomi.la: Nomen sempitérnum * dabo Sanctis meis dicit Dóminus, † gáudium et lætítiam obtinébunt in ætérnum.

iusticonfitebunturnominituethabitabuntre.en: The just * shall give glory to thy name, † and the upright shall dwell with thy countenance.
iusticonfitebunturnominituethabitabuntre.la: Justi * confitebúntur nómini tuo, † et habitábunt recti cum vultu tuo.

sapientiamsanctorumnarrantpopulietlaudes.en: The peoples shew forth * the wisdom of the Saints, † and all the church declareth their praise.
sapientiamsanctorumnarrantpopulietlaudes.la: Sapiéntiam * Sanctórum narrant pópuli, † et laudes eórum pronúntiat omnis ecclésia.

omnissanctorumconcio.en: Let all the assembly of the Saints

matremcollaudetvirginis.en: Praise together the Mother of the Virgin,

salusprocessithominis.en: The salvation of man came forth.

petiitapatreluminum.en: Asked offspring of the Father of lights,

matremregisiustitie.en: The Mother of the King of justice.

stirpsiesseclaradeluit.en: The illustrious stock of Jesse washed away

dumannaprolemgenuit.en: When Anne brought forth her child,

floremsanctorumomnium.en: The flower of all the Saints.

benedictionemomniumgentiumdeditillidomin.en: The blessing * of all nations the Lord gave him, and confirmed his covenant upon their heads.
benedictionemomniumgentiumdeditillidomin.la: Benedictiónem * ómnium géntium dedit illi Dóminus, et testaméntum suum confirmávit super cápita eórum.

deusquisanctosioachimetannamgloriosematr.en: O God, who didst choose Saints Joachim and Anne to be the parents of the glorious Mother of thine only-begotten Son: grant us by their prayers to praise thy clemency for ever in the fellowship of thine elect.
deusquisanctosioachimetannamgloriosematr.la: Deus, qui sanctos Jóachim et Annam glorióse Matris Unigéniti tui paréntes elegísti: da nobis eórum précibus, in tuórum consórtio electórum cleméntiam tuam perpétuo collaudáre.

christumregemfiliumdavidveniteadoremus.en: Christ the King, the Son of David, * Come, let us adore.
christumregemfiliumdavidveniteadoremus.la: Christum regem, Fílium David, * Veníte adorémus.

beatiquoniamconfisisuntdomino.en: Blessed are they, * for they have trusted in the Lord.
beatiquoniamconfisisuntdomino.la: Beáti, * quóniam confísi sunt Dómino. Ps. 2

gloriametmagnumdecoremimposuistisupereos.en: Glory * and great beauty hast thou laid upon them.
gloriametmagnumdecoremimposuistisupereos.la: Glóriam * et magnum decórem imposuísti super eos. Ps. 20

recordatusestdominusmisericordiesueetver.en: The Lord hath remembered * his mercy, and his truth toward the house of Israel.
recordatusestdominusmisericordiesueetver.la: Recordátus est * Dóminus misericórdiæ suæ, et veritátis suæ dómui Israël. Ps. 97, 249, 250, 251

ecceradixiesseascendetinsalutempopulorum.en: Behold, † the root of Jesse shall rise up for the salvation of the peoples; him shall the Gentiles beseech:
ecceradixiesseascendetinsalutempopulorum.la: Ecce † radix Jesse ascéndet in salútem populórum, ipsum Gentes deprecabúntur:

quaretardasdominevenietliberapopulumtuum.en: Why tarriest thou, † O Lord? come, and deliver thy people!
quaretardasdominevenietliberapopulumtuum.la: Quare tardas, † Dómine? veni, et líbera pópulum tuum!

teenimexspectatomnisisrel.en: For all Israel waiteth for thee.

oratioindormitionembmv.en: Oration 1 on the Falling-asleep of the B.V.M.

ioachimetannaparentesfueruntvirginisbeat.en: Joachim and Anne were the parents of the most blessed Virgin. Since Joachim was led by the Lord God as a sheep, he lacked none of those things which are best. But let none think that I speak of the things which please the most, and after which the mind of greedy men is ever wont to gape; which yet by their nature are neither lasting, nor know how to make a man better by whom they are held, although they abound to him in any plenty. Such are found to be the pleasures of this world, which surely can have no firm and stable strength, but fall swiftly away, and, as their wont is, slip away almost in the same hour in which they are born.
ioachimetannaparentesfueruntvirginisbeat.la: Joáchim et Anna paréntes fuérunt Vírginis beatíssimæ. Cum Joáchim a Dómino Deo tamquam ovis deducerétur, nullis eórum quæ óptima sunt, carébat. vero nemo me putet dícere, quæ plúrimis placent ac quibus avidiórum hóminum ánimus perpétuo solet inhiáre, quæ tamen natúra sua neque durabília sunt, neque meliórem præstáre norunt hóminem,a quo tenéntur, licet eídem áffluant quavis abundántia. Tália reperiúntur esse hujus mundi voluptátes, quæ sane vim firmam stabilémque habére néqueunt, sed raptim décidunt atque de more vix non eádem, qua nascúntur hora, étiam dilabúntur.

ofelixioachimgenuistiprolemquepariturera.en: O happy Joachim, † thou didst beget the offspring who was to bring forth the Redeemer of the world:
ofelixioachimgenuistiprolemquepariturera.la: O felix Jóachim, † genuísti prolem, quæ paritúra erat mundi Redemptórem :

gaudeetpronobisprecesporrigasreginecelor.en: Rejoice, and offer up prayers for us to the Queen of heaven.
gaudeetpronobisprecesporrigasreginecelor.la: Gaude, et pro nobis preces pórrigas Regínæ cælórum.

felixpaterfeliciorisfiliequeunigenitumde.en: Happy father of a happier daughter, who brought forth from herself the only-begotten Son of God made flesh.
felixpaterfeliciorisfiliequeunigenitumde.la: Felix Pater felicióris fíliæ, quæ Unigénitum Dei de se prótulit incarnátum.

absinthecanobisminimeconvenitnosistismov.en: Far be these things from us; it becometh us not at all to be moved by them, neither is such the portion of them that fear the Lord. Those in truth are goods which are truly sought and loved by men of sound counsel, which remain for ever, and at the same time delight the divine majesty, and will bring forth ripe fruit for their possessors. Such goods, I say, are the virtues, which shall give their fruit in due season, that is, life eternal in the world to come, to all who here have worthily cultivated them, and have bestowed their labour upon them according to their strength. For labour goeth before; eternal felicity shall follow.
absinthecanobisminimeconvenitnosistismov.la: Absint hæc a nobis; mínime convénit nos istis movéri, neque talis est pars timéntium Dóminum. Ea demum profécto bona sunt, quæ vere ab homínibus íntegri consílii quærúntur et adamántur, quæ in ætérnum manent, atque simul divínam majestátem obléctant, et fructum matúrum suis generábunt possessóribus. Cujúsmodi bona, inquam, appárent virtútes, quæ fructum in témpore suo, id est, vitam ætérnam in sǽculo futúro dabunt ómnibus, qui hic eos digne colúerint, in eásque pro víribus óperam suam contúlerint. Labor quippe præcédit, sequétur felícitas ætérna.

beatietmultohonoredigniquorumportiodeuse.en: Blessed † and worthy of much honour are they whose portion is God:
beatietmultohonoredigniquorumportiodeuse.la: Beáti, † et multo honóre digni, quorum pórtio Deus est:

quibusaprincipiopreparatumestregnumquoru.en: For whom the kingdom hath been prepared from the beginning, whose souls are in the hand of God.
quibusaprincipiopreparatumestregnumquoru.la: Quibus a princípio preparátum est regnum, quorum ánimæ in manu Dei sunt.

ioachimcogitationessuasintuspasceresoleb.en: Joachim was wont to feed his thoughts within in a place of pasture, that is, he abode in the contemplation of the sacred oracles. He refreshed his soul upon the water of refreshment of divine grace, and by this rule of life, turning his mind wholly away from unlawful things, he directed it into the paths of justice. And Anne his wife was joined to him no less by the bond of character than by that of marriage.
ioachimcogitationessuasintuspasceresoleb.la: Jóachim cogitatiónes suas intus páscere solébat in loco páscuæ, id est, in contemplatióne sacrórum eloquiórum commorabátur. Refovébat ánimam suam super aquam reflectiónis grátiæ divínæ, atque hac se geréndi norma mentem suam ab illícitis rebus plane declínans, ad sémitas justítiæ dirigebát. Anna vero conjux non minus morum, quam matrimónii vínculo, cum ipso copulabátur.

venerabilesacdeodigniioachimetannabeatam.en: Venerable † and worthy of God, Joachim and Anne begat blessed Mary,
venerabilesacdeodigniioachimetannabeatam.la: Venerábiles † ac Deo digni Jóachim et Anna beátam Maríam genuérunt,

etmagnassineintermissionedominogratiasre.en: And without ceasing they rendered great thanks unto the Lord.
etmagnassineintermissionedominogratiasre.la: Et magnas sine intermissióne Dómino grátias reddébant.

gloriosiparentesmuneresupernoditatisuntc.en: The glorious parents were enriched with a heavenly gift: the inviolate Mother of Christ the Saviour.
gloriosiparentesmuneresupernoditatisuntc.la: Gloriósi paréntes múnere supérno ditáti sunt: Christi Salvatóris invioláta Genitríce.

exlibrodefideorthodc.en: From Book 4 on the Orthodox Faith, ch. 15.
exlibrodefideorthodc.la: Ex libro 4 de fide orthod., c. 15.

ioachimergovenerandamillametsummislaudib.en: Joachim therefore had joined to himself in marriage that venerable woman, worthy of the highest praises, Anne. But as that Anne of old, when she suffered the affliction of barrenness, having made a vow, brought forth Samuel by promise, so this one in like manner, by supplication and divine promise, received the Mother of God. Wherefore, suffering no loss in the honour of motherhood, Anne shall be seen to be second to none of the illustrious matrons. Grace (for this is what the name Anne signifieth) bringeth forth the Lady: for so is the name of Mary interpreted; for truly she was made the Lady of all created things when she became the mother of the Creator.
ioachimergovenerandamillametsummislaudib.la: Jóachim ergo venerándam illam et summis laúdibus dignam mulíerem Annam matrimónio sibi conjúnxerat. Verum, quemádmodum prisca illa Anna, cum sterilitátis morbo laboráret, facto voto, per promissiónem Samuélem génuit, hæc símili modo per obsecratiónem et divínam promissiónem accépit Deíparam. Quare nullum in maternitátis honóre detriméntum pátiens, Anna nulli ex claris matrónis impar vidébitur. grátia, nam hoc sonat Annæ vocábulum, Dóminam parit: sic enim Maríæ nomen explanátur; vere nempe ómnium rerum conditárum Dómina facta est, cum Conditóris mater éxstitit.

nobilisetmiresalutarisvenerabilisannafru.en: Noble † and wondrously saving, venerable Anne, thy fruit is the Virgin Mary:
nobilisetmiresalutarisvenerabilisannafru.la: Nóbilis † et mire salutáris, venerábilis Anna, fructus tuus est Virgo María:

materdominisolamenmundiumbraculumdefessi.en: The Mother of the Lord, the solace of the world, a shade for the weary, and the hope of the wretched.
materdominisolamenmundiumbraculumdefessi.la: Mater Dómini, solámen mundi, umbráculum deféssis, ac spes miserórum.

gaudeetletarebeataparensnamprolestuest.en: Rejoice and be glad, blessed mother, for she is thine offspring.
gaudeetletarebeataparensnamprolestuest.la: Gaude et lætáre, beáta parens, nam proles tua est.

semperquidemdilectissimidiversismodismul.en: At all times indeed, dearly beloved, the divine goodness hath taken thought for mankind in divers manners and in many measures, and hath mercifully imparted many gifts of its providence in all the ages past; but in these last times it hath exceeded all the abundance of its wonted kindness, when in Christ mercy itself descended to sinners, truth itself to the erring, life itself to the dead: that that Word, coeternal and coequal with the Father, might take up into the unity of his Godhead the nature of our lowliness, and he that was born God of God might also be born man of man.
semperquidemdilectissimidiversismodismul.la: Semper quidem, dilectíssimi, divérsis modis multísque mensúris humáno géneri bónitas divína consúluit, et plúrima providéntiæ suæ múnera ómnibus retro sǽculis cleménter impértiit; sed in novíssimis tempóribus omnem abundántiam sólitæ benignitátis excéssit, quando in Christo, ipsa ad peccatóres misericórdia, ipsa ad errántes véritas, ipsa ad mórtuos vita descéndit: ut Verbum illud coætérnum et coæquále Genitóri in unitátem Deitátis suæ natúram nostræ humilitátis assúmeret, et Deus de Deo natus, idem étiam homo de hómine nascerétur.

disposuitestamentumelectismeisiuravidavi.en: I have made a covenant † with my elect: I have sworn to David my servant:
disposuitestamentumelectismeisiuravidavi.la: Dispósui † testaméntum eléctis meis, jurávi David, servo meo:

usqueineternumpreparabosementuum.en: Thy seed will I settle for ever.
usqueineternumpreparabosementuum.la: Usque in ætérnum præparábo semen tuum.

edificaboingenerationemetgenerationemsed.en: And I will build up thy throne unto generation and generation.
edificaboingenerationemetgenerationemsed.la: Ædificábo in generatiónem et generatiónem sedem tuam.

promissumquidemhocaconsstitutionemundiet.en: This indeed had been promised from the foundation of the world, and had ever been foretold by many signs of things and of words; but how small a portion of men would those figures and overshadowed mysteries have saved, had not Christ by his coming fulfilled the long and hidden promises! And that which, while yet to be done, profited a few believers, being now done would profit believers without number. Now therefore we are led to faith not by signs nor by images, but, being confirmed by the history of the Gospel, we adore that which we believe to have been done; the instruments of prophecy being added for our instruction, that we may in no wise hold as doubtful that which we know to have been foretold by such great oracles.
promissumquidemhocaconsstitutionemundiet.la: Promíssum quidem hoc a cons stitutióne mundi, et multis significatiónibus rerum atque verbórum semper fúerat prophetátum; sed quantam hóminum portiónem figúræ illæ ac mystéria obumbráta salvárent, nisi longa et occúlta promíssa advéntu suo Christus impléret! Et quod tunc paucis credéntibus prófuit faciéndum, innúmeris jam fidélibus prodésset efféctum. Jam ergo nos non signis neque imagínibus ad fidem dedúcimur, sed evangélica história confirmáti, quod factum crédimus, adorámus; accedéntibus ad eruditiónem nostram prophéticis instruméntis, ut nullo modo habeámus ambíguum, quod tantis oráculis scimus esse prædíctum.

exortumestintenebrislumenrectiscorde.en: To the righteous † a light is risen up in darkness:
exortumestintenebrislumenrectiscorde.la: Exórtum est † in ténebris lumen rectis corde:

misericorsetmiseratoretiustusdominus.en: The Lord is merciful, and compassionate, and just.
misericorsetmiseratoretiustusdominus.la: Miséricors, et miserátor, et justus Dóminus.

rectamfecitviamiustorumetpreparavititers.en: He hath made straight the way of the just, and prepared the path of the Saints.
rectamfecitviamiustorumetpreparavititers.la: Rectam fecit viam justórum, et præparávit iter Sanctórum.

tincenimestquoddominusabraheaitinseminet.en: Hence it is that the Lord saith to Abraham: In thy seed shall all the nations be blessed. Hence David with prophetic spirit singeth the promise of God, saying: The Lord hath sworn truth to David, and he will not make it void: Of the fruit of thy womb I will set upon thy throne. Hence the same Lord saith by Isaias: Behold, a virgin shall conceive in her womb, and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel: which, being interpreted, is God with us. And again: There shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up out of his root. In which rod without doubt the blessed Virgin Mary was foretold, who, sprung from the stock of Jesse and David and made fruitful by the Holy Ghost, brought forth the new flower of human flesh, from a mother's womb indeed, but by a virgin birth.
tincenimestquoddominusabraheaitinseminet.la: Tinc enim est, quod Dóminus Abrahæ ait: In sémine tuo benedicéntur omnes gentes. Hinc David promissiónem Dei prophético spíritu canit, dicens: Jurávit Dóminus David veritátem, et non frustrábitur eam: De fructu ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam. Hinc idem Dóminus per Isaíam: Ecce virgo, inquit, in útero accípiet, et páriet fílium, et vocábitur nomen ejus Emmánuel: quod interpretátur, Nobíscum Deus. Et íterum: Exiet virga de radíce Jesse, et flos de radíce ejus ascéndet. In qua virga non dúbie beáta Virgo María prædícta est, quæ de Jesse et David stirpe progénita, et Spíritu Sancto fecundáta, novum florem carnis humánæ, útero quidem matérno, sed partu est eníxa virgíneo.

oquamdulcisestpiestasdominiquevenerabile.en: O how † sweet is the goodness of the Lord, which hath borne the venerable Joachim and Anne from present tribulation into the court of heaven,
oquamdulcisestpiestasdominiquevenerabile.la: O quam † dulcis est píestas Dómini, quæ venerábiles Jósachim et Annam ex præsénti ærúmna in cæli transvéxit cúriam,

ubicumsacravirginemariasinefinedeumcolla.en: Where with the holy Virgin Mary they praise God together without end.
ubicumsacravirginemariasinefinedeumcolla.la: Ubi cum sacra Vírgine María sine fine Deum colláudant.

suscipitebeatidigniquedeoprecumlibaminaq.en: Receive, ye blessed and worthy of God, the offerings of our prayers, ye who have been translated into the glory of heaven.
suscipitebeatidigniquedeoprecumlibaminaq.la: Suscípite, beáti digníque Deo, precum libámina, qui in cæli glóriam estis transláti.

exsultentergoiustiindominetinlaudemdeico.en: Let the just therefore exult in the Lord, and the hearts of believers in the praise of God, and let the children of men confess his wonderful works: for in this work of God above all our lowliness knoweth how highly its Maker hath esteemed it. For though he gave much to the origin of man, in that he made us to his own image, he bestowed far more upon our restoration, when the Lord fitted himself to the form of a servant. For although whatever the Creator bestoweth upon the creature cometh of one and the same goodness, yet it is less wonderful that man should advance to divine things than that God should descend to human things.
exsultentergoiustiindominetinlaudemdeico.la: Exsúltent ergo justi in Domi no, et in laudem Dei corda credéntium, et mirabília ejus confiteántur fílii hóminum: quóniam in hoc præcípue Dei ópere humílitas nostra cognóscit, quanti eam suus cónditor æstimárit. Qui cum orígini humánæ multum déderit, quod nos ad imáginem suam fecit, reparatióni nostræ longe ámplius tríbuit, cum servíli formæ ipse se Dóminus coaptávit. Quamvis enim ex una eadémque pietáte sit, quidquid creatúræ Creátor impéndit, minus tamen mirum est, hóminem ad divína profícere, quam Deum ad humána descéndere.

incircuitutuodominelumenestquodnumquamde.en: Round about thee, † O Lord, is light that shall never fail, where thou hast established most bright mansions;
incircuitutuodominelumenestquodnumquamde.la: In circúitu tuo, † Dómine, lumen est, quod numquam defíciet, ubi constituísti lucidíssimas mansiónes

ibirequiescuntsanctorumanime.en: There rest the souls of the Saints.

magnusdominusetlaudabilisnimisincivitate.en: Great is the Lord, and exceedingly to be praised in the city of our God, in his holy mountain.
magnusdominusetlaudabilisnimisincivitate.la: Magnus Dóminus et laudábilis nimis, in civitáte Dei nostri, in monte sancto ejus.

hecdicitdominuscustoditeiudiciumetfacite.en: Thus saith the Lord: Keep ye judgment, and do justice: † for my salvation is near to come, * and my justice to be revealed.
hecdicitdominuscustoditeiudiciumetfacite.la: Hæc dicit Dóminus: Custodíte judícium, et fácite justítiam: † quia juxta est salus mea ut véniat, * et justítia mea ut revelétur.

succeditnoctilucifer.en: The morning star succeedeth the night,

solisortumprenuntians.en: Foretelling the rising of the sun

mundumlustrantislumine.en: That shineth upon the world with light.

christussolestiustitie.en: Christ is the sun of justice,

auroramatergratie.en: The dawn the Mother of grace,

quamannapreitrutilans.en: Whom thou, O Anne, goest before, glowing,

legispropellenstenebras.en: Driving away the darkness of the Law.

egosumdeuspatrumvestrorumdicitdominusvid.en: I am * the God of your fathers, saith the Lord: I have seen the affliction of my people, and I have heard their groaning, and I am come down to deliver them, alleluia.
egosumdeuspatrumvestrorumdicitdominusvid.la: Ego sum * Deus patrum vestrórum, dicit Dóminus: videns vidi afflictiónem pópuli mei, et gémitus ejus audívi, et descéndi liberáre eos, allelúja.

inclytastirpsiessevirgamproduxithmenamde.en: The glorious stock of Jesse * brought forth a fair rod, from which came forth a flower full of wondrous fragrance.
inclytastirpsiessevirgamproduxithmenamde.la: Inclyta stirps Jesse * virgam prodúxit hmœ́nam de qua procéssit flos miro plenus odóre.

deusquinosannuabeaticyriacimartyristuiso.en: O God, who gladdenest us by the yearly solemnity of blessed Cyriacus thy Martyr: mercifully grant, that we who keep his heavenly birthday may also imitate the strength of his passion.
deusquinosannuabeaticyriacimartyristuiso.la: Deus, qui nos annua beáti Cyríaci Mártyris tui solemnitáte lætíficas: concede propítius; ut, cujus natalícia colimus, virtútem quoque passiónis imitémur.

quiautemadministratsemenseminantietpanem.en: And he that ministereth seed to the sower, will both give you bread to eat, and will multiply your seed, and increase the growth of the fruits of your justice.
quiautemadministratsemenseminantietpanem.la: Qui autem adminístrat semen seminánti: et panem ad manducándum præstábit, et multiplicábit semen vestrum, et augébit increménta frugum justítiæ vestræ.

beatuslaurentiusdixitegomeobtulisacrific.en: Blessed Lawrence said: I have offered myself a sacrifice
beatuslaurentiusdixitegomeobtulisacrific.la: Beátus Lauréntius dixit: Ego me óbtuli sacrifícium

gaudeoplanequiahostiachristiefficimerui.en: I rejoice indeed that I have merited to be made a victim of Christ.
gaudeoplanequiahostiachristiefficimerui.la: Gáudeo plane quia hóstia Christi éffici mérui.

meruitessehostialevitalaurentiusquidumas.en: The levite Lawrence merited to be a victim, who, while he was being roasted, denied not the Lord;
meruitessehostialevitalaurentiusquidumas.la: Méruit esse hóstia levíta Lauréntius, qui dum assarétur, non negávit Dóminum

etideoinventusestsacrificiumlaudis.en: And therefore he was found a sacrifice of praise.
etideoinventusestsacrificiumlaudis.la: Et ídeo invéntus est sacrifícium laudis.

incraticulapositusdeumnonnegavitetadigne.en: Laid upon the gridiron he denied not God, and set to the fire he confessed Christ.
incraticulapositusdeumnonnegavitetadigne.la: In cratícula pósitus Deum non negávit, et ad ignem applicátus Christum conféssus est.

sanctimartyristiburtiinosdominefoveantco.en: May the continual protection of thy holy Martyr Tiburtius cherish us, O Lord: for thou ceasest not mercifully to look upon those whom thou hast granted to be helped by such aids.
sanctimartyristiburtiinosdominefoveantco.la: Sancti Mártyris Tibúrtii nos, Dómine, fóveant continuáta præsídia: quia non désinis propítius intuéri; quos tálibus auxíliis concésseris adjuvári.

demariadeiparavirginelibc.en: On Mary, the Virgin Mother of God, book 5, ch. 6
demariadeiparavirginelibc.la: De Maria Deipara Virgine, lib. 5, c. 6

hicgratiamirabilis.en: He, a grace to be wondered at,

pastorardensutfacula.en: O Shepherd, burning as a torch.

manentincelicuria.en: Abide in the court of heaven.

lactishuiusmellishuius.en: Of this milk, of this honey,

fundestillaspleniore.en: Pour down the drops, who of a fuller

summasummolausparenti.en: Highest praise to the highest Father,

summalausetfilio.en: Highest praise also to the Son:

fartibisitsanctemanans.en: Equal be to thee, O holy

utfuitnuncetperevum.en: As it was, now and for ever,
utfuitnuncetperevum.la: Ut fuit, nunc et per ævum

deusquibeatumbernardumabbatemaseculipomp.en: O God, who didst make blessed Bernard the Abbot, called from the pomp of the world to the love of solitude, a victim of charity in a pitiable pestilence among the people: we beseech thee that we, walking in his footsteps, may be granted to be partakers of the same charity and glory.
deusquibeatumbernardumabbatemaseculipomp.la: Deus, qui beátum Bernárdum Abbátem a sǽculi pompa ad amórem solitúdinis evocátum, in miseránda pópuli contagióne caritátis víctimam efficísti: quǽsumus, ut per ejus vestígia gradiéntes, ejúsdem caritátis et glóriæ tríbuas esse consórtes.

auxiliumtuumnobisdominequesumusplacatusi.en: Graciously bestow upon us thy help, O Lord, we beseech thee: and, at the intercession of blessed Timothy thy Martyr, stretch forth over us the right hand of thy mercy.
auxiliumtuumnobisdominequesumusplacatusi.la: Auxílium tuum nobis, Dómine, quǽsumus, placátus impende: et, intercedéntibus beáto Mártyre tuo Timótheo, déxteram super nos tuæ propitiatiónis exténde.

scienseumvirumiustumetsanctumetcustodieb.en: Knowing him to be a just and holy man: and he kept him.
scienseumvirumiustumetsanctumetcustodieb.la: Sciens eum virum justum et sanctum: et custodiébat eum.

etauditeomultafaciebatetlibentereumaudie.en: And when he heard him, he did many things, and he heard him willingly.
etauditeomultafaciebatetlibentereumaudie.la: Et audíto eo, multa faciébat, et libénter eum audiébat.

posuitcoronamcapitimeetcircumdeditmevest.en: He hath set a crown upon my head, and hath clothed me with the garment of salvation,
posuitcoronamcapitimeetcircumdeditmevest.la: Pósuit corónam cápiti meo, et circúmdedit me vestiménto salútis,

adexpugnandasgentesetomnesinimicos.en: To overcome the Gentiles and all mine enemies.
adexpugnandasgentesetomnesinimicos.la: Ad expugnándas Gentes et omnes inimícos.

iudicadominenocentesmeexpugnaimpugnantes.en: Judge thou, O Lord, them that wrong me: overthrow them that fight against me. Take hold of arms and shield: and rise up to help me.
iudicadominenocentesmeexpugnaimpugnantes.la: Júdica, Dómine, nocéntes me, expúgna impugnántes me, apprehénde arma et scutum, et exsúrge in adjutórium mihi.

vitampetiitateettribuistieiinseculumsecu.en: He asked life of thee, and thou hast given it him for ever and ever.
vitampetiitateettribuistieiinseculumsecu.la: Vitam pétiit a te, et tribuísti ei in sǽculum sǽculi.

sponsachristihildegardisdoctrinesalutari.en: Hildegard, * the spouse of Christ, enlightened holy Church with the lamp of saving doctrine.
sponsachristihildegardisdoctrinesalutari.la: Sponsa Christi * Hildegárdis, doctrínæ salutáris lámpade sanctam illuminávit Ecclésiam.

deusquibeatamhildegardemvirginemtuamdoni.en: O God, who didst adorn blessed Hildegard thy Virgin with heavenly gifts: grant, we beseech thee, that, following in her footsteps and teachings, we may merit to pass from the darkness of this present world unto thy delightful light.
deusquibeatamhildegardemvirginemtuamdoni.la: Deus, qui beátam Hildegárdem Vírginem tuam donis cæléstibus decorásti: tríbue, quæsumus; ut, ejus vestígiis et documéntis insisténtes, a præséntis sæculi calígine ad lucem tuam delectábilem transíre mereámur.

quodautemsequituriotaunumautunusapexnonp.en: And that which followeth: One jot or one tittle shall not pass of the law, till all be fulfilled; is shown by the figure of a letter: that even those things which are thought least in the law are full of spiritual mysteries, and all are summed up in the Gospel.
quodautemsequituriotaunumautunusapexnonp.la: Quod autem sequitur: Jota unum aut unus apex non praeteribit a lege, donec omnia fiant; ex figura litterae ostenditur,quod etiam quae minima putantur in lege, sacramentis spiritualibus plena sint, et omnia recapitulentur in Evangelio.

mittedomineangelumbonumantenosintimorebr.en: Send, O Lord, * a good Angel before us, in the fear of thine arm, that they that hate us may fear.
mittedomineangelumbonumantenosintimorebr.la: Mitte, Dómine, * Angelum bonum ante nos in timóre bráchii tui, ut métuant qui odérunt nos. Ps. 97

angelusmeusvobiscumestdicitdominusipseau.en: My Angel * is with you, saith the Lord: and he himself shall seek out your souls.
angelusmeusvobiscumestdicitdominusipseau.la: Angelus meus * vobíscum est, dicit Dóminus: ipse autem exquíret ánimas vestras. Ps. 98

viditiacobscalamstantemsuperterrametcacu.en: Jacob saw † a ladder standing upon the earth, and the top thereof touching heaven, and the Angels of God ascending by it, and the Lord leaning upon the ladder, saying to him:
viditiacobscalamstantemsuperterrametcacu.la: Vidit Jacob † scalam stantem super terram, et cacúmen illíus tangens cælum, Ángelosque Dei ascendéntes per eam, et Dóminum inníxum scalæ, dicéntem sibi:

egosumdominusdeustuusetprotectortuusquon.en: I am the Lord thy God, and thy keeper whithersoever thou goest.
egosumdominusdeustuusetprotectortuusquon.la: Ego sum Dóminus Deus tuus et protéctor tuus quóniam perréxeris.

iveruntiacobobviamangelideiquoscumvidiss.en: The Angels of God met Jacob; and when he saw them, he said: These are the camps of God, whereby God helpeth me, saying:
iveruntiacobobviamangelideiquoscumvidiss.la: Ivérunt Jacob óbviam Angeli Dei, quos, cum vidísset. ait: Castra Dei sunt hæc, per quæ auxiliátur mihi Deus, dicens.

siaudierisvocemmeametfecerisomniaqueloqu.en: If thou wilt hear † my voice, and do all that I speak, I will be an enemy to thy enemies, and will afflict them that afflict thee.
siaudierisvocemmeametfecerisomniaqueloqu.la: Si audíeris † vocem meam, et féceris ómnia quæ loquor, inimícus ero inimícis tuis, et affligéntes te afflígam.

etintroducetteinterramquampromisipatribu.en: And he shall bring thee into the land which I promised to thy fathers.
etintroducetteinterramquampromisipatribu.la: Et introdúcet te in terram, quam promísi pátribus tuis.

iustifulgebuntsicutsolinregnopatriseorum.en: The just * shall shine as the sun in the kingdom of their Father.
iustifulgebuntsicutsolinregnopatriseorum.la: Justi * fulgébunt sicut sol in regno Patris eórum.

gratiadeietmisericordiestinsanctoseiuset.en: The grace of God * and his mercy is with his Saints, and he hath respect to his chosen.
gratiadeietmisericordiestinsanctoseiuset.la: Grátia Dei, * et misericórdia est in Sanctos ejus, et respéctus in eléctos illíus.

ideoaccipientregnumdecorisetdiademaspeci.en: Therefore shall they receive * a kingdom of glory, and a crown of beauty at the hand of the Lord.
ideoaccipientregnumdecorisetdiademaspeci.la: Ideo accípient * regnum decóris, et diadéma speciéi de manu Dómini.

benidicitesanctiethumilescordedominolaud.en: Bless the Lord, * O ye holy and humble of heart: praise and exalt him above all for ever.
benidicitesanctiethumilescordedominolaud.la: Benidícite, * sancti et húmiles corde, Dómino ; laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.

oculidominisupermetuenteseum.en: The eyes of the Lord * are upon them that fear him.

etineisquisperantsupermisericordieius.en: And on them that hope in his mercy.
etineisquisperantsupermisericordieius.la: Et in eis, qui sperant super misericórdia ejus.

nesciamculpecoluerevitam.en: Led a life that knew not guilt,

indeiamgaudentmiserisadesse.en: Thence now they rejoice to succour the wretched,

flentiumterguntlacrimasmedentur.en: They wipe away the tears of them that weep, they heal

mentiumplagisvitiatareddunt.en: The wounds of minds, and restore to health
