quipiapergantopenosiuvare.en: Who continue to help us with loving aid
quipiapergantopenosiuvare.la: Qui pia pergant ope nos juváre

sitdeosolidecusetpotestas.en: To God alone be glory and power,
sitdeosolidecusetpotestas.la: Sit Deo soli decus et potéstas,

lausinexcelsishonoracperennis.en: Praise in the highest, and honour everlasting,
lausinexcelsishonoracperennis.la: Laus in excélsis honor ac perénnis,

legibusorbem.en: The whole world by his laws.

concedequesumusomnipotensdeusutadmeliore.en: Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God, that the examples of blessed Maurus and Placid, thy Confessors, may stir us up to a better life; that we may also imitate the deeds of those whose memory we keep.
concedequesumusomnipotensdeusutadmeliore.la: Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut ad meliórem vitam beatórum Mauri et Plácidi Confessórum tuórum exémpla nos próvocent; quátenus, quorum memóriam ágimus, étiam actus imitémur.

quitimetisdominumsperateinillumetinoblec.en: Ye that fear the Lord, hope in him: and mercy shall come to you for your delight. Ye that fear the Lord, love him, and your hearts shall be enlightened.
quitimetisdominumsperateinillumetinoblec.la: Qui timétis Dóminum, speráte in illum: et in oblectatiónem véniet vobis misericórdia. Qui timétis Dóminum, dilígite illum: et illuminabúntur corda vestra.

accediteadeumetilluminamini.en: Come ye to him and be enlightened.

etfaciesvestrenonconfundentur.en: And your faces shall not be confounded.

prolapsuinlacumplacidomaurusadvolansspir.en: Placid having fallen into the lake, Maurus, hastening thither, † was borne by the Spirit of God upon the waters,
prolapsuinlacumplacidomaurusadvolansspir.la: Prolápsu in lacum Plácido, Maurus ádvolans, † spíritu Dei ferebátur super aquas,

dumpatrisuoinaudituaurisobediret.en: While at the hearing of the ear he obeyed his Father.
dumpatrisuoinaudituaurisobediret.la: Dum Patri suo in audítu auris obedíret.

aquemultenonpotueruntextinguerecaritatem.en: Many waters could not quench his charity, † neither could the floods drown it.
aquemultenonpotueruntextinguerecaritatem.la: Aquæ multæ non potuérunt extínguere caritátem ejus, † neque flúmina eam obrúere.

delibrosecundodialogorumsanctigregoriipa.en: From the second book of the Dialogues of St. Gregory, Pope
delibrosecundodialogorumsanctigregoriipa.la: De libro secúndo Dialogórum sancti Gregórii Papæ

quadamverodiedumidemvenerabilisbenedictu.en: Now on a certain day, while the same venerable Benedict was abiding in his cell, the boy Placid, a monk of the holy man, went out to draw water from the lake: who, carelessly letting down into the water the vessel which he held, himself also followed it by falling. Him the wave forthwith carried away, and drew him out from the land almost the length of a bowshot. But the man of God, being within his cell, straightway knew this, and hastily called Maurus, saying: Brother Maurus, run, for that boy who went to draw water hath fallen into the lake, and already the wave is carrying him further off. A wonderful thing, and unheard of since the Apostle Peter! For, having asked and received the blessing, Maurus went in haste at the command of his Father, and as far as the place whither the boy was being carried by the wave, thinking that he went upon the land, he ran upon the water, and taking him by the hair, returned with swift course. Who, as soon as he touched the land, coming to himself, looked behind him, and perceived that he had run upon the waters: and that which he could not have presumed to do, he marvelled and trembled that it had been done. Returning therefore to his Father, he related what had happened. But the venerable man Benedict began to ascribe this not to his own merits, but to the other's obedience; but Maurus, on the contrary, said that it was done by his command alone, and that he was not conscious of that power which he had wrought unknowing. But in this friendly contest of mutual humility the boy who had been rescued came as judge; for he said: When I was being drawn out of the water, I saw above my head the Abbot's sheepskin, and I perceived that it was he who brought me out of the waters.
quadamverodiedumidemvenerabilisbenedictu.la: Quadam vero die dum idem venerábilis Benedíctus in cella consísteret, Plácidus puer, sancti viri mónachus, ad hauriéndam de lacu aquam egréssus est: qui vas, quod tenébat, in aquam incáute submíttens, ipse quoque cadéndo secútus est. Quem mox unda rápuit, et pæne ad uníus sagíttæ cursum, eum a terra intrórsus traxit. Vir autem Dei intra cellam pósitus, hoc prótinus agnóvit, et Maurum festíne vocávit, dicens: Frater Maure, curre, quia puer ille, qui ad hauriéndam aquam perréxerat, in lacum cécidit: jamque eum lóngius unda trahit. Res mira, et post Petrum Apóstolum inusitáta! Benedictióne étenim postuláta atque percépta, ad Patris sui impérium cóncitus perréxit Maurus, atque usque ad eum locum quo ab unda deducebátur puer, per terram se ire exístimans, super aquam cucúrrit, eúmque per capíllos tenens, cursu rápido rédiit. Qui mox ut terram tétigit, ad se revérsus, post tergum respéxit, et quia super aquas cucurrísset agnóvit: et quod præsúmere non potuísset ut fíeret, mirátus extrémuit factum. Revérsus ítaque ad Patrem, rem gestam rétulit. Vir autem venerábilis Benedíctus hoc non suis méritis, sed illíus obediéntiæ deputáre coepit; at contra Maurus pro solo ejus império factum dicébat: seque cónscium in illa virtúte non esse, quam néscius feciíset. Sed in hac mútuæ humilitátis et amíca contentióne accéssit árbiter puer, qui eréptus est, namque dicébat: Ego cum ex aqua tráherer, super caput meum Abbátis melótem vidébam, atque ipsum me ex aquis edúcere considerábam.

metuentesdominumsustinetemisericordiamei.en: Ye that fear the Lord, wait for his mercy: and go not aside from him, lest ye fall. Ye that fear the Lord, believe him: and your reward shall not be made void.
metuentesdominumsustinetemisericordiamei.la: Metuéntes Dóminum, sustinéte misericórdiam ejus: et non deflectátis ab illo, ne cadátis. Qui timétis Dóminum, crédite illi: et non evacuábitur merces vestra.

firmamentumestdominustimentibuseum.en: The Lord is a firmament * To them that fear him.

ettestamentumipsiusutmanifesteturillis.en: And his covenant shall be made manifest to them.
ettestamentumipsiusutmanifesteturillis.la: Et testaméntum ipsíus ut manifestétur illis.

auditequaseffundimus.en: Hear ye, which we pour forth,

amorechristiperciti.en: Smitten with the love of Christ,

spevistisartesdemonum.en: Ye scorned the arts of demons;

migrastisintersidera.en: Ye passed away among the stars.

adestevotisomnium.en: Be present to the prayers of all

utchristerexpiissime.en: That thou, O Christ, most loving King,

iusticonfitebunturnominituodomine.en: The just shall give glory to thy name, O Lord.

ethabitabuntrecticumvultutuo.en: And the upright shall dwell with thy countenance.
ethabitabuntrecticumvultutuo.la: Et habitábunt recti cum vultu tuo.

beatiserviilliquoscumveneritdominusinven.en: Blessed are those servants * whom the Lord, when he cometh, shall find watching.
beatiserviilliquoscumveneritdominusinven.la: Beáti servi illi * quos, cum vénerit Dóminus, invénerit vigilántes.

conservabatmariaomniaverbaheccþnferensin.en: Mary kept * all these words, pondering them in her heart.
conservabatmariaomniaverbaheccþnferensin.la: Conservábat María * ómnia verba hæc, cþnferens in corde suo. Ps. 47

crucisimperiumsuperhumerumeiuslivoreeius.en: The government of the cross * is upon his shoulder: by his bruises we are healed.
crucisimperiumsuperhumerumeiuslivoreeius.la: Crucis impérium * super húmerum ejus: livóre ejus sanáti sumus. Ps. 96

diciteingentibusquiadominusregnavitalign.en: Say ye * among the Gentiles: The Lord hath reigned from the wood.
diciteingentibusquiadominusregnavitalign.la: Dícite * in géntibus: quia Dóminus regnávit a ligno Ps. 97, 249, 250, 251

cunctasheresessolainteremistiinuniversom.en: Thou alone hast destroyed all heresies in the whole world.
cunctasheresessolainteremistiinuniversom.la: Cunctas hǽreses sola interemísti in univérso mundo.

virgamhancsumeinmanutuainquafacturusessi.en: Take this rod in thy hand, wherewith thou shalt do the signs.
virgamhancsumeinmanutuainquafacturusessi.la: Virgam hanc sume in manu tua, in qua factúrus es signa.

pulchreseddecorafiliaierusalem.en: Thou art beautiful † and comely, O daughter of Jerusalem,
pulchreseddecorafiliaierusalem.la: Pulchra es † ed decóra, fília Jerúsalem,

terribilisutcastrorumaciesordinata.en: Terrible as an army set in array.

netimeasmariainvenistienimgratiamapuddom.en: Fear not, Mary, † for thou hast found grace with the Lord:
netimeasmariainvenistienimgratiamapuddom.la: Ne tímeas, María, † invenísti enim grátiam apud Dóminum:

ecceconcipiesetpariesetvocabisnomeneiusi.en: Behold, thou shalt conceive, and shalt bring forth, and thou shalt call his name Jesus.
ecceconcipiesetpariesetvocabisnomeneiusi.la: Ecce concípies, et páries, et vocábis nomen ejus Jesus.

spiritussanctussupervenietinteetvirtusal.en: The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the most High shall overshadow thee.
spiritussanctussupervenietinteetvirtusal.la: Spiritus Sanctus supervéniet in te, et virtus Altíssimi obumbrávit tibi.

fulgebuntiustisicutsolinregnopatriseorum.en: The just shall shine * as the sun in the kingdom of their Father, saith the Lord.
fulgebuntiustisicutsolinregnopatriseorum.la: Fulgébunt justi * sicut sol in regno Patris eórum, dicit Dóminus.

beatieritiscumvosoderinthominesetcumsepa.en: Blessed shall you be * when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man's sake: be glad and rejoice; for behold, your reward is great in heaven.
beatieritiscumvosoderinthominesetcumsepa.la: Beáti éritis, * cum vos óderint hómines, et cum separáverint vos, et exprobráverint, et ejécerint nomen vestrum tamquam malum propter Fílium hóminis: gaudéte et exsultáte; ecce enim merces vestra multa est in cælis.

sanctidominidominumbenedciteineternum.en: Ye Saints of the Lord, * bless the Lord for ever.
sanctidominidominumbenedciteineternum.la: Sancti Dómini * Dóminum benedcite in ætérnum.

vosauramatrisvirginis.en: You the breath of the Virgin Mother

vosangelorumcurie.en: You the courts of the Angels

cinguntchoreaperpetim.en: Encircle with their dance for ever,

invallemestadebiles.en: In the vale of sorrow strengthen us,

simulquedulciflamini.en: And together to the sweet Spirit,

exsultetomniumturbafideliumprogloriaalmi.en: Let all the throng * of the faithful exult for the glory of our gracious Father Benedict, and of all who have followed in his footsteps: let the companies of monks above all rejoice, celebrating their feast on earth, in whose fellowship the Saints rejoice together in heaven.
exsultetomniumturbafideliumprogloriaalmi.la: Exsúltet ómnium * turba fidélium pro glória almi Patris Benedícti, et eórum ómnium, qui ejus vestígia sunt secúti: læténtur præcipue catérvæ monachórum, celebrántes eórum festa in terris, de quorum societáte Sancti congáudent in cælis.

concedequesumusomnipotensdeusutadmeliore.en: Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God, that the examples of the holy Monks may stir us up to a better life: † that we who keep their solemnity * may also imitate their deeds.
concedequesumusomnipotensdeusutadmeliore.la: Concéde, quǽsumus omnípotens Deus, ut ad meliórem vitam sanctórum Monachórum exémpla nos próvocent: † quátenus, quorum solémnia ágimus, * étiam actus imitémur.

ecceegetpuerimeiquosdeditmihidominusinsi.en: Behold I and my children, whom the Lord hath given me for a sign, and for a wonder in Israel from the Lord of hosts, who dwelleth in mount Sion.
ecceegetpuerimeiquosdeditmihidominusinsi.la: Ecce ego et púeri mei quos dedit mihi Dóminus in signum, et in porténtum Israël a Dómino exercítuum, qui hábitat in monte Sion.

filiieorumpropterillosusqueineternummane.en: Their children for their sakes remain for ever: their seed and their glory shall not be forsaken.
filiieorumpropterillosusqueineternummane.la: Fílii eórum propter illos usque in ætérnum manent: semen eórum et glória eórum non derelinquétur.

inregenerationecumsederitfiliushominisin.en: In the regeneration, when the Son of man shall sit on the seat of his majesty, you also shall sit on twelve seats, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
inregenerationecumsederitfiliushominisin.la: In regeneratióne, cum séderit Fílius hóminis in sede majestátis suæ, sedébitis et vos, super sedes duódecim, judicántes duódecim tribus Israël.

decimononokalendasfebruariilunavicesimaq.en: The nineteenth day before the Kalends of February. The twenty-fifth day of the moon. In the year of the Lord 2026
decimononokalendasfebruariilunavicesimaq.la: Décimo nono Kaléndas Februárii Luna vicésima quinta. Anno Dómini 2026

sanctihilariiepiscopipictaviensisconfess.en: Of Saint Hilary, Bishop of Poitiers, Confessor and Doctor of the Church; who on the day before this flew away to heaven.
sanctihilariiepiscopipictaviensisconfess.la: Sancti Hilárii, Epíscopi Pictaviénsis, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris; qui prídie hujus diéi evolávit in cælum.

noleincampanianatalissanctifelicispresby.en: At Nola, in Campania, the birthday of Saint Felix, Priest, who (as Saint Paulinus the Bishop writeth), having been cast into prison by the persecutors after torments, and lying bound upon shells and potsherds, was loosed in the night by an Angel and led forth; but afterwards, the persecution ceasing, having in the same place converted many to the faith of Christ by the example of his life and by his teaching, he rested in peace, renowned for miracles.
noleincampanianatalissanctifelicispresby.la: Nolæ, in Campánia, natális sancti Felícis Presbýteri, qui (ut sanctus Paulínus Epíscopus scribit), cum a persecutóribus post torménta in cárcerem missus esset, et cóchleis ac téstulis vinctus superpósitus jacéret, nocte ab Angelo solútus atque edúctus fuit; póstmodum vero, cessánte persecutióne, ibídem, cum multos ad Christi fidem exémplo vitæ ac doctrína convertísset, clarus miráculis quiévit in pace.

iniudeasanctimalachieprophete.en: In Judea, of Saint Malachias the Prophet.

inmontesinasanctorumtrigintaoctomonachor.en: On mount Sinai, of thirty-eight holy Monks, slain by the Saracens for the faith of Christ.
inmontesinasanctorumtrigintaoctomonachor.la: In monte Sina sanctórum trigínta octo Monachórum, a Saracénis ob Christi fidem interfectórum.

inrhaithiregioneinegyptosanctorumquadrag.en: In the region of Raithu, in Egypt, of forty-three holy Monks, who were slain by the Blemmyes for the Christian religion.
inrhaithiregioneinegyptosanctorumquadrag.la: In Rhaíthi regióne, in Ægýpto, sanctórum quadragínta trium Monachórum, qui, pro Christiána religióne, a Blémmiis occísi sunt.

mediolanisanctidatiiepiscopietconfessori.en: At Milan, of Saint Datius, Bishop and Confessor; of whom blessed Pope Gregory maketh mention.
mediolanisanctidatiiepiscopietconfessori.la: Medioláni sancti Dátii, Epíscopi et Confessóris; cujus méminit beátus Gregórius Papa.

inafricasanctieuphrasiiepiscopi.en: In Africa, of Saint Euphrasius, Bishop.

neocesareeinpontosanctemacrinediscipuleb.en: At Neocaesarea, in Pontus, of Saint Macrina, a disciple of blessed Gregory the Wonderworker, and grandmother of Saint Basil, who brought up the same Basil.
neocesareeinpontosanctemacrinediscipuleb.la: Neocæsaréæ, in Ponto, sanctæ Macrínæ, discípulæ beáti Gregórii Thaumatúrgi, et áviæ sancti Basilíi, quæ eúndem Basilíum educávit.

etalibialiorumplurimorumsanctorummartyru.en: And elsewhere, of many other holy Martyrs and Confessors, and holy Virgins.
etalibialiorumplurimorumsanctorummartyru.la: Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.

inmemoriaeterneruntiusti.en: The just shall be in everlasting remembrance.

abauditionemalanontimebunt.en: They shall not fear the evil hearing.

deusvenielargitorethumanesalutisamatorqu.en: O God, the giver of pardon and lover of man's salvation: we beseech thy clemency, that thou wouldst grant that the brethren of our congregation who have passed out of this world, blessed Mary ever virgin interceding with all thy saints, may come to the fellowship of everlasting blessedness. Through Christ our Lord.
deusvenielargitorethumanesalutisamatorqu.la: Deus, véniæ largítor et humánæ salútis amátor: quǽsumus cleméntiam tuam: ut nostræ congregatiónis fratres, qui ex hoc sǽculo transiérunt, beáta María semper vírgine intercedénte cum ómnibus sanctis tuis ad perpétuæ beatitúdinis consórtium perveníre concédas. Per Christum Dóminum nostrum.

castacolumbanidificansincavernamaceriesa.en: The chaste dove, * making her nest in the hollow of the wall of the sacred side of Jesus Christ, sucked most sweet honey from the rock.
castacolumbanidificansincavernamaceriesa.la: Casta colúmba * nidíficans in cavérna macériæ sacri láteris Jesu Christi, mel suavíssimum de petra sugébat. Ps. 109

loquebaturchristusaddilectamgertrudemfac.en: Christ spake * to his beloved Gertrude face to face, as a man is wont to speak to his friend.
loquebaturchristusaddilectamgertrudemfac.la: Loquebátur Christus * ad diléctam Gertrúdem fácie ad fáciem, sicut solet loqui homo ad amícum suum. Ps. 112

beategertrudisverbadivinierantamorisiacu.en: The words of blessed Gertrude * were darts of divine love: her lamps were lamps of fire and of flames.
beategertrudisverbadivinierantamorisiacu.la: Beátæ Gertrúdis verba * divíni erant amóris jácula: lámpades ejus, lámpades ignis atque flammárum. Ps. 121

dilecteanimamecarcerecorporisexeuntemacc.en: The soul of his beloved, * going forth from the prison of the body, Christ received into his arms, and lovingly opened his heart to her.
dilecteanimamecarcerecorporisexeuntemacc.la: Diléctæ ánimam * e cárcere córporis exeúntem accépit Christus in ulnas suas, et cor suum illi amánter apéruit. Ps. 126

sponsoqueiunctavirginum.en: Joined to the Bridegroom of virgins,

danuptialispangere.en: Grant us to sing the chaste loves

quadrimachristonubilis.en: At four years old, betrothed to Christ,

inclaustraprompteconvolas.en: Thou fliest readily into the cloister;

sponsirequirisoscula.en: Thou seekest the kisses of the Bridegroom.

odoremulcessidera.en: Thou delightest the stars with thy fragrance,

regemdecorepertrahis.en: Drawest the King of them of heaven.

quivivitinsinupatris.en: He who liveth in the bosom of the Father,

tuoquecordipropria.en: And upon thy heart his own

beatalaudentagmina.en: Let the blessed hosts give praise;

patrisimulparaclito.en: To the Father, together with the Paraclete,

egrediminietvidetefiliesiongertrudemindi.en: Go forth * and see, ye daughters of Sion, Gertrude in the diadem wherewith Christ crowned her in the day of her espousals, and in the day of the joy of her heart.
egrediminietvidetefiliesiongertrudemindi.la: Egredímini * et vidéte, fíliæ Sion, Gertrúdem in diadémate quo coronávit illam Christus in die desponsatiónis illíus, et in die lætítiæ cordis ejus.

deusquiinpurissimocordebeategertrudisvir.en: O God, who in the most pure heart of blessed Gertrude thy Virgin didst prepare for thyself a pleasant dwelling: by her merits and intercession mercifully wipe away the stains of our heart; that it may merit to be made a worthy dwelling of thy divine majesty.
deusquiinpurissimocordebeategertrudisvir.la: Deus, qui in puríssimo corde beátæ Gertrúdis Vírginis tuæ jucúndam tibi habitatiónem præparásti; ejus méritis et intercessióne cordis nostri máculas cleménter abstérge; ut digna divínæ majestátis tuæ habitátio éffici mereátur.

gertrudisvirgoquinquennisinsacrereligion.en: Gertrude the Virgin, * planted at five years old in the garden of holy Religion as a shining lily, shone with the splendour of all virtues.
gertrudisvirgoquinquennisinsacrereligion.la: Gertrúdis Virgo, * quinquénnis in sacræ Religiónis horto velut candens lílium plantáta, ómnium virtútum splendóre refúlsit. Ps. 8

adsacrumbeatipatrisbenedictiordinemdivin.en: She was called by God to the holy Order of blessed Father Benedict, that she, who was to be filled with the gifts of the Holy Ghost, might set before herself for imitation the Patriarch full of the spirit of all the just.
adsacrumbeatipatrisbenedictiordinemdivin.la: Ad sacrum beáti Patris Benedícti Ordinem divínitus vocáta est, ut, quæ Spíritus Sancti donis replénda erat, Patriárcham ómnium justórum spíritu plenum, sibi imitándum propóneret. Ps. 18

factumestcoreiustamquamceraignemollitacu.en: Her heart became like wax softened by fire, whereupon Christ imprinted the seal of his Godhead.
factumestcoreiustamquamceraignemollitacu.la: Factum est cor ejus tamquam cera igne mollíta, cui Christus divinitátis suæ sigíllum impréssit. Ps. 23

spirituintelligentiereplevitgertrudemdom.en: With the spirit of understanding * the Lord filled Gertrude: he gave her the knowledge of the Saints, and put his spirit upon her.
spirituintelligentiereplevitgertrudemdom.la: Spíritu intelligéntiæ * replévit Gertrúdem Dóminus: dedit illi sciéntiam Sanctórum, et pósuit super eam spíritum suum. Ps. 44

ardentissimoanimarumzelestuabatetomnesin.en: She burned * with a most ardent zeal for souls, and longed after all in the bowels of Jesus Christ.
ardentissimoanimarumzelestuabatetomnesin.la: Ardentíssimo * animárum zelo æstuábat, et omnes in viscéribus Jesu Christi cupiébat. Ps. 45

ingruentempluviamverbocontinuitobediente.en: The rain that was falling * she held back by a word, the Lord obeying the prayers of his spouse.
ingruentempluviamverbocontinuitobediente.la: Ingruéntem plúviam * verbo contínuit, obediénte Dó mino sponsæ suæ précibus. Ps. 47

mundetsibimortueratgertrudisetviteiusabs.en: Gertrude was dead * to the world and to herself, and her life was hid with Christ in God.
mundetsibimortueratgertrudisetviteiusabs.la: Mundo * et sibi mórtua erat Gertrúdis, et vita ejus abscóndita cum Christo in Deo. Ps. 84

ancillesuesecretacelestiarevelavitdeuspe.en: To his handmaid * God revealed heavenly secrets by his Spirit.
ancillesuesecretacelestiarevelavitdeuspe.la: Ancíllæ suæ * secréta cæléstia revelávit Deus per Spíritum suum. Ps. 86

multefiliesubeiusdisciplinacongregaverun.en: Many daughters * under her discipline have gathered together riches: she hath surpassed them all.
multefiliesubeiusdisciplinacongregaverun.la: Multæ filiæ * sub ejus disciplína congregavérunt divítias: hæc supergréssa est univérsas. Ps. 95

labiagertrudiscustodiebantscientiametqui.en: The lips of Gertrude * kept knowledge, and they that were in distress sought comfort from her mouth.
labiagertrudiscustodiebantscientiametqui.la: Lábia Gertrudis * custodiébant sciéntiam, et qui in pressúra erant, solátium requirébant ex ore ejus. Ps. 96

sempermortificationemiesuchristiincorpor.en: She ever * bore about in her body the mortification of Jesus Christ, whose marks she carried imprinted upon her heart.
sempermortificationemiesuchristiincorpor.la: Semper * mortificatiónem Jesu Christi in córpore suo circumferébat, cujus stígmata cordi suo impréssa portábat. Ps. 97

gloriosavirgogertrudispostquammigravitad.en: The glorious Virgin * Gertrude, after she had departed to her Bridegroom, appeared in gilded clothing, surrounded with variety.
gloriosavirgogertrudispostquammigravitad.la: Gloriósa Virgo * Gertrúdis, postquam migrávit ad Sponsum, apparuit in vestítu deauráto circúmdata varietáte. Ps. 98

induitmedominusvestimentosalutisetindume.en: The Lord hath clothed me * with the garments of salvation: and with the robe of gladness he hath compassed me, as a bride adorned with her jewels.
induitmedominusvestimentosalutisetindume.la: Induit me Dóminus * vestiménto salútis: et induménto lætitiæ circúmdedit me, quasi sponsam ornátam monílibus suis. Ps. 249, 250, 251

miranocturnismodulantelingua.en: With tuneful tongue in the hours of night

gestagertrudiscelebremushoris.en: Let us celebrate the wondrous deeds of Gertrude,

quesacrisinstansprecibusperegit.en: Who, instant in holy prayers, passed

arvaiamdudumglacierigebant.en: The fields had long been stiff with ice,

cordecummestomiseranscolonos.en: When, pitying the husbandmen with sorrowful heart,

fervidisvirgolacrimisresolvit.en: The Virgin with fervent tears dissolved

nesegeslargovitieturimbre.en: Lest the crop be spoiled by too much rain,

seduliscelumprecibusserenat.en: By earnest prayers she maketh the sky serene,

etgraveslesigemebundaplacat.en: And, groaning, appeaseth the heavy wrath of the offended

igneismentespenetratsagittis.en: With fiery arrows she pierceth minds,

languidisconfertanimismedelam.en: She bringeth healing to languishing souls,

virginumsponsumsuperumqueregem.en: The Bridegroom of virgins and King of them above

virginumsanctecelebrentchoree.en: Let the holy choirs of virgins celebrate,

etsacramsupplextriademperevum.en: And the sacred Trinity, suppliant, for ever
etsacramsupplextriademperevum.la: Et sacram supplex Tríadem per ævum

sapientiamdeiloquebaturinterperfectasvir.en: She spake the wisdom of God among the perfect virgins, taught by Christ Jesus:
sapientiamdeiloquebaturinterperfectasvir.la: Sapiéntiam Dei loquebátur inter perféctas vírgines, a Christo Jesu edócta:

quemabipsainfantiainsponsumelegit.en: Whom from her very infancy she chose for her Bridegroom.
quemabipsainfantiainsponsumelegit.la: Quem ab ipsa infántia in Sponsum elégit.

spiritumhuiusmundinonaccepitsedspiritumq.en: She received not the spirit of this world, but the Spirit that is of God.
spiritumhuiusmundinonaccepitsedspiritumq.la: Spíritum hujus mundi non accépit, sed spíritum, qui ex Deo est.

gertrudisvirgoislebiiincomitatumansfeldi.en: Gertrude the virgin, born of most noble parents at Eisleben in the county of Mansfeld, at five years old consecrated her virginity to Christ, to whom she was already as one marriageable and ripe, in the monastery of the city of Rodarda, of the Order of the holy Father Benedict. From her very entrance into Religion she entered upon the manner of an angelic life, and being excellently trained in humane and divine letters, she attained to such perfection of doctrine as the most learned justly looked up to. Excellent was her contemplation, in which, enlightened by God with many revelations and heavenly visions, she, by his inspiration, wrote books full of divine wisdom.
gertrudisvirgoislebiiincomitatumansfeldi.la: Gertrúdis virgo, Islébii in comitátu Mansfeldiénsi nobilíssimis paréntibus nata, quinquénnis Christo, cui jam núbilis erat et matúra, in monastério urbis Rodárdæ, Ordinis sancti Patris Benedícti, virginitátem suam consecrávit. Ab ipso in Religiónem ingréssu angélicæ vitæ ratiónem íniit, et litteris humanióribus ac divínis appríme excúlta, ad eam doctrinæ perfectiónem pervénit, quam eruditíssimi quique mérito suspícerent. Exímia fuit ejus contemplátio, in qua multis revelatiónibus ac visis cæléstibus a Deo illustráta, eódem inspiránte, libros divínæ sapiéntiæ plenos conscrípsit.

christoconfixasumcruci.en: With Christ I am nailed to the cross:

egenimstigmatadominiiesuincordemeoporto.en: For I bear the marks of the Lord Jesus in my heart.
egenimstigmatadominiiesuincordemeoporto.la: Ego enim stígmata Dómini Jesu in corde meo porto.

vivoautemiamnonegovivitveroinmechristus.en: And I live, now not I; but Christ liveth in me.
vivoautemiamnonegovivitveroinmechristus.la: Vivo autem jam non ego, vivit vero in me Christus.

quamvisautemtantisnatureetgratiedotibuse.en: But although she shone with such great gifts of nature and of grace, enjoyed divine converse, and was distinguished with the gift of prophecy and with very many miracles, yet she was so mean in her own eyes, that among the chief miracles of the divine power she believed this one to be singular, that the earth bore her, a most unworthy sinner, as she was wont to say. When she was in her thirtieth year, she was chosen abbess, first of the monastery in which she had received the habit, and afterwards of that of Helfta. In which office for forty years she bore herself with such charity, prudence, and integrity of regular discipline, that the monastery seemed to be a house of God, wherein Angels in the body lived under Gertrude their mistress: who, although she was the mother of all, yet showed herself the servant of all.
quamvisautemtantisnatureetgratiedotibuse.la: Quamvis autem tantisnatúræ et grátiæ dótibus enitéret, divínis fruerétur collóquiis, prophetíæ dono et plúrimis esset insigníta miráculis; ádeo tamen sibi ipsa vilescébat, ut inter præcípua divínæ virtútis mirácula hoc unum singuláre créderet, quod se indigníssimam, ut dictitábat, terra peccatrícem sustinéret. Dum annum ágeret trigésimum, in abbatíssam ejus primum monastérii, in quo hábitum recéperat, deínde Elpediáni, sive ut vocant Elphiáni, elécta est. Quo in múnere per quadraginta annos ea caritáte, prudéntia, et reguláris disciplínæ integritáte se gessit, ut coenóbium domus Dei esse viderétur, in qua corporáti Angeli víverent sub Gertrúde magístra: quæ quamvis esset ómnium mater, ómnium tamen se minístram exhibébat.

cumasperrimogeluterradiuconcretanondaret.en: When the earth, long frozen with most bitter frost, yielded not its increase, blessed Gertrude, touched with sorrow of heart, prayed to the Bridegroom:
cumasperrimogeluterradiuconcretanondaret.la: Cum aspérrimo gelu terra diu concréta non daret germen suum, beáta Gertrudis tacta dolóre cordis orávit ad Sponsum:

etstatimsolutaglaciesecutestverisameenit.en: And straightway the ice was loosed, and the pleasantness of spring followed.
etstatimsolutaglaciesecutestverisameenit.la: Et statim solúta glácie, secúta est veris amæœnitas.

emisitdominusverbumsuumetliquefeciteamfl.en: The Lord sent out his word, and melted it: his spirit blew, and the waters ran.
emisitdominusverbumsuumetliquefeciteamfl.la: Emísit Dóminus verbum suum, et liquefécit eam flavit spíritus ejus, et fluxérunt aquæ.

celestissponsusineiuspurissimocordedelic.en: The heavenly Bridegroom set his delights in her most pure heart, upon which the divine Lover burned the marks of his own wounds with the fiery pen of love. Hence she spake of nothing but Christ, whom she bore in her heart; who declared that he was to be found nowhere more fittingly than in the sacrament of the altar, and next in the heart and soul of this his beloved. He confirmed the holiness of this same dearest Spouse by the oracle of his divine mouth, when he testified that there lived at that time upon earth no soul which, as it was more closely joined to him, was so pleasing and acceptable.
celestissponsusineiuspurissimocordedelic.la: Cæléstis Sponsus in ejus puríssimo corde delícias suas collocávit, cui suórum étiam vúlnerum stígmata ígneo amóris stylo divínus zelátor inússit. Hinc illa nihil nisi Christum loquebátur, quem in corde gestábat, qui nusquam se conveniéntius, quam in sacraménto altáris, ac deínde in hujus suæ diléctæ corde et ánima inveniéndum pronuntiávit. Ejúsdem caríssimæ Sponsæ sanctitátem divíni sui oris confirmávit oráculo, cum testátus est, nullam tunc témporis ánimam in terris vívere, quæ, ut illi conjunctior, ita grátior esset et accéptior.

messistemporecumimbresassiduifrugibuster.en: In the time of harvest, when continual rains were hurting the fruits of the earth, Gertrude poured out her heart like water before the face of the Lord:
messistemporecumimbresassiduifrugibuster.la: Messis témpore, cum imbres assídui frúgibus terræ nocérent, Gertrudis effúdit sicut aquam cor suum ante conspéctum Dómini:

etstatimfactestserenitasmagna.en: And straightway there was a great calm.
etstatimfactestserenitasmagna.la: Et statim facta est serénitas magna.

clausesuntcataractecelietprohibitesuntpl.en: The flood-gates of heaven were shut up, and the rain from heaven was restrained.
clausesuntcataractecelietprohibitesuntpl.la: Clausæ sunt cataráctæ cæli, et prohíbitæ sunt plúviæ de cælo.

deiparamvirginempeculiaribeneficioinmatr.en: The Virgin Mother of God, given to her by Christ by a special favour as her mother and advocate, whom with other citizens of heaven she often beheld, she honoured with singular devotion. Toward the most holy sacrament of the Eucharist and the passion of Christ she was moved with so great an ardour of love and gratitude, that she melted wholly into tears. The souls given over to the cleansing flames she relieved by daily suffrages and constant prayers. She burned continually with zeal for promoting the divine honour and for procuring the salvation of her neighbour. When therefore she languished rather with a most fervent love of God than with sickness, Christ came to her, accompanied by his most holy Mother, and the beloved disciple, and a most white choir of Virgins; and her soul, loosed from the bonds of the body, and received, by a wondrous opening of his breast, within the inmost recesses of his heart, he bore away to the heavenly bridechamber.
deiparamvirginempeculiaribeneficioinmatr.la: Deíparam Vírginem peculiári benefício in matrem et procuratrícem sibi a Christo datam, quam cum áliis cæli cívibus frequénter habébat spectábilem, singulári pietáte prosequebátur. Erga sanctíssimum Eucharistíæ sacraméntum et Christi passiónem tanto amóris et gratitúdinis afficiebátur ardóre, ut tota lácrimis liquésceret. Animas piaculáribus flammis addíctas quotidiánis suffrágiis et assíduis précibus sublevábat. Zelo divíni honóris promovéndi, et procurándæ salútis próximi júgiter ardébat. Cum ígitur ferventíssimo Dei amóre pótius quam morbo languéret, huic Christus, sanctíssima Matre, dilectóque discípulo, et candidíssimo Vírginum choro comitátus, áffuit, et ejus ánimam, córporis solútam compágibus, ac mirábili péctoris explicatióne intra cordis sui pene. trália recéptam, ad cæléstem thálamum tradúxit.

queperrevelationemiesuchristididicitgert.en: What Gertrude learned by the revelation of Jesus Christ, she wrote down by his inspiration:
queperrevelationemiesuchristididicitgert.la: Quæ per revelatiónem Jesu Christi dídicit Gertrúdis, eódem inspiránte conscrípsit:

quiabscondithecasapientibusetprudentibus.en: Who hideth these things from the wise and prudent, and revealeth them to little ones.
quiabscondithecasapientibusetprudentibus.la: Qui abscóndit hæc a sapiéntibus et prudéntibus, et revélat ea párvulis.

lingueiuscalamusscribevelociterscribenti.en: Her tongue is the pen of a scrivener that writeth swiftly.
lingueiuscalamusscribevelociterscribenti.la: Lingua ejus cálamus scribæ velóciter scribéntis.

sermodeverbdilciiiv.en: Sermon 93 on the Words of the Lord, ch. 2-4
sermodeverbdilciiiv.la: Sermo 93 de Verb. Dil c. II-IV

intelligamuscarissimiadomnesnosidestadun.en: Let us understand, dearly beloved, that this parable pertaineth to us all, that is, to the whole Church altogether; not to the rulers alone, nor to the people alone, but to all without exception. These five and five virgins are all the souls of Christians whatsoever. But, that we may tell you what by God's inspiration we perceive, not souls of whatever kind, but such souls as have the Catholic faith, and are seen to have good works in the Church of God: and yet of these very ones five are wise and five are foolish.
intelligamuscarissimiadomnesnosidestadun.la: Intelligámus, caríssimi, ad omnes nos, id est, ad univérsam omníno Ecclésiam, istam perti. nére parábolam, non ad solos præpósitos, nec ad solas plebes; sed prorsus ad omnes. Ista quinque et quinque vírgines omnes omníno sunt ánimæ Christianórum. Sed, ut dicámus vobis, quod Deo inspiránte sentímus, non qualescúmque ánimæ sed tales ánimæ, quæ haben Cathólicam fidem, et habére vidéntur bona ópera in Ecclésia Dei: et tamen ex ipsis quinque sunt prudéntes et quinque fátuæ.

indicanobisquemdiligitanimanostra.en: Shew us, whom our soul loveth,
indicanobisquemdiligitanimanostra.la: Indica nobis, quem díligit ánima nostra,

ubipascasubicubesinmeridie.en: Where thou feedest, where thou liest in the midday.
ubipascasubicubesinmeridie.la: Ubi pascas, ubi cubes in merídie.

incordegertrudisinvenietisme.en: In the heart of Gertrude ye shall find me.

quareergoappellatesuntquinqueetquarevirg.en: Let us first see, then, why they are called five, and why virgins. Every soul in the body is reckoned by the number five, because it useth five senses. He therefore that abstaineth from unlawful seeing, from unlawful hearing, from unlawful smelling, from unlawful tasting, from unlawful touching, hath received the name of virgin by reason of that very integrity. But if it is good to abstain from the unlawful motions of the senses, and therefore every Christian soul hath received the name of virgin, why are five admitted and five shut out?
quareergoappellatesuntquinqueetquarevirg.la: Quare ergo appellátæ sunt quinque; et quare vírgines, prius videámus. Omnis ánima in córpore ídeo quinário número censétur, quia quinque sénsibus útitur. Qui ergo se ábstinet ab illícito visu, ab illícito audítu, ab illícito odorátu, ab illícito gustátu, ab illícito tactu, propter ipsam integritátem vírginis nomen accépit. Sed si bonum est, abstinére ab illicitis sentiéndi mótibus,et ídeo unaquæque ánima Christiána vírginis nomen accépit: quare quinque admittúntur et quinque repellúntur?

placebatsibiininfirmitatibusetangustiisp.en: She pleased herself in infirmities and in distresses for Christ:
placebatsibiininfirmitatibusetangustiisp.la: Placébat sibi in infirmitátibus et angústiis pro Christo:

etvariislicetlanguoribusvexataomnibusqui.en: And though vexed with divers sicknesses, she bestowed the solace of charity on all that were in distress.
etvariislicetlanguoribusvexataomnibusqui.la: Et váriis licet languóribus vexáta, ómnibus, qui in pressúra erant, caritátis solátium impendébat.

cuminfirmabaturtuncpotenserat.en: When she was weak, then was she powerful.

etvirginessuntetrepellunturparumestquiav.en: They are virgins, and yet are shut out. It is little that they are virgins, and have lamps. Virgins by reason of abstinence from unlawful things of the senses, they have lamps by reason of good works. Of which works the Lord saith: Let your works shine before men. Likewise he saith to the disciples: Let your loins be girt, and lamps burning in your hands. In the girt loins, virginity; in the burning lamps, good works. If therefore abstinence from unlawful things is good, whence virginity hath received its name; and good works are praiseworthy, which are signified by the lamps; why are five admitted and five shut out?
etvirginessuntetrepellunturparumestquiav.la: Et vírgines sunt, et repellúntur. Parum est, quia vírgines sunt, et lámpades habent. Vírgines propter abstinentiam ab illícitis, sénsibus, lámpades habent propter ópera bona. De qui{us opéribus Dóminus dicit: Lúceant ópera vestra coram homínibus. Item discípulis dicit: Sint lumbi vestri accíncti, et lucérnæ ardéntes. In lumbis accínctis, virgínitas; in lucérnis ardéntibus ópera bona. Si ergo ab illícitis abstinéntia bona est; unde virgínitas nomen accépit: et ópera bona laudabília sunt, quæ significántur lampádibus: quare quinque admittuntur et quinque repellúntur?

apparueruntcelestesspiritusquigertrudema.en: There appeared heavenly spirits, who invited Gertrude to the marriage of the Lamb, saying:
apparueruntcelestesspiritusquigertrudema.la: Apparuérunt cæléstes spíritus, qui Gertrúdem ad Agni núptias invitábant, dicéntes:

venidominaquiateexspectantcelidelicie.en: Come, O lady, for the delights of heaven await thee.
venidominaquiateexspectantcelidelicie.la: Veni, dómina, quia te exspéctant cæli delíciæ.

venidelibanosponsavenidelibanovenicorona.en: Come from Libanus, my spouse; come from Libanus, come: thou shalt be crowned.
venidelibanosponsavenidelibanovenicorona.la: Veni de Líbano, Sponsa; veni de Líbano, veni, coronáberis.

aliasdixitprudentesaliasastultasundeintu.en: Some he called wise, others foolish. Whence do we see it? whence do we discern it? By the oil. Oil signifieth something great, yea very great. Thinkest thou it is charity? We say this by way of inquiry; we do not hasten to a judgment. Why oil seemeth to me to signify charity, I will tell you. The Apostle saith: And I shew unto you yet a more excellent way. If I speak with the tongues of men and of Angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal. This is the more excellent way, that is, charity, which is rightly signified by oil. For oil riseth above all liquids.
aliasdixitprudentesaliasastultasundeintu.la: Alias dixit prudéntes, álias Astultas. Unde intuémur? unde discérnimus? De óleo. Aliquid magnum signíficat óleum, et valde magnum. Putas, num cáritas est? Quæréndo dícimus, non sententiam præcipitámus. Unde mihi videátur óleum caritátem significáre, dicam vobis. Apóstolus dicit: Adhuc supereminentiórem vobis viam demónstro. Si linguis hóminum loquar et Angelórum, caritátem autem non hábeam, factus sum æraméntum sonans, aut cýmbalum tínniens. Ipsa est superéminens via: id est cáritas, quæ mérito óleo significátur. Omnibus enim humóribus óleum superéminet.

cumbeatagertrudisdeiamorelangueretapparu.en: When blessed Gertrude languished with the love of God, the Bridegroom whom she loved appeared to her:
cumbeatagertrudisdeiamorelangueretapparu.la: Cum beáta Gertrúdis Dei amóre languéret, appáruit ei Sponsus, quem diligébat:

quieamincordissuisacrariumadmissamadcele.en: Who, having admitted her into the sanctuary of his heart, bore her away to the heavenly bridechamber.
quieamincordissuisacrariumadmissamadcele.la: Qui eam in cordis sui sacrárium admíssam, ad cæléstem thálamum tradúxit.

laudetletarefiliasionquiecceegoveniethab.en: Sing praise, * and rejoice, O daughter of Sion: for behold I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee, saith the Lord.
laudetletarefiliasionquiecceegoveniethab.la: Lauda * et lætáre, fília Sion, quia ecce ego vénio, et habitábo in médio tui, dicit Dóminus.

obeataanimaquemeruitessesedessapientiecu.en: O blessed soul, * who merited to be the seat of wisdom, whose delights are to be with the children of men!
obeataanimaquemeruitessesedessapientiecu.la: O beáta ánima, * quæ méruit esse sedes sapiéntiæ, cujus delíciæ sunt esse cum fíliis hóminum!

annulisseptemsubarrhavitmedominusmeusies.en: With seven rings * hath my Lord Jesus Christ espoused me, and as a bride hath he adorned me with a crown.
annulisseptemsubarrhavitmedominusmeusies.la: Ánnulis septem subarrhávit me * Dóminus meus Jesus Christus, et tamquam sponsam decorávit me coróna.

habuitgertrudispotestatemclauderecelumnu.en: Gertrude had * power to shut up heaven with clouds, and to open its gates: for her tongue was made the key of heaven.
habuitgertrudispotestatemclauderecelumnu.la: Hábuit Gertrúdis * potestátem cláudere cælum núbibus, et aperíre portas ejus: quia lingua ejus clavis cæli facta est.

ancillafidelisetsponselectaintravitincor.en: The faithful handmaid * and chosen spouse hath entered into the heart and joy of her Lord, with whose love she languished.
ancillafidelisetsponselectaintravitincor.la: Ancílla fidélis * et sponsa elécta intrávit in cor et gáudium Dómini sui, cujus amóre languébat.

inveniquemdiligitanimameatenuieumnecdimi.en: I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him: and I will not let him go, till I bring him into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her that bore me.
inveniquemdiligitanimameatenuieumnecdimi.la: Invéni quem díligit ánima mea: ténui eum, nec dimíttam, donec introdúcam illum in domum matris meæ, et in cubículum genetrícis meæ.

adsacrosvirgothalamosanhelans.en: Panting for the sacred bridal chambers, the virgin

nuptiascelocelebraregestit.en: Longeth to celebrate her nuptials in heaven,

etpiisvotisnimiummorantem.en: And with loving prayers the hour that too long

egracumlanguetmanifestusadstat.en: When sick she languisheth, there standeth visible

celitumturmacomitantechristus.en: Christ, a troop of heavenly ones attending,

atquedivinirecreatiacentem.en: And her that lieth there refresheth with the light

surgeconclamatsororatquesponsa.en: Arise, he crieth aloud, my sister and spouse,

entibipandopenetralecordis.en: Lo, I open unto thee the inmost shrine of my heart,

uttriumphalireseratascandas.en: That, it being unlocked, thou mayest ascend in triumph

istavoxomnespenetratmedullas.en: This voice pierceth all the marrow,

atquecompagesanimiresolvit.en: And looseneth the bonds of the soul:

spirituslibervolatinreclusa.en: The spirit, set free, flieth into the opened

regiosagnithalamospetentem.en: Her that seeketh the royal bridechambers of the Lamb

iubilansstipatsuperumcorona.en: The crown of them above, rejoicing, throngeth about,

atquecomplexusetamicacantat.en: And she singeth the embraces and the loving

odignissimachristisponsaquamluxprophetie.en: O most worthy * spouse of Christ, whom the light of prophecy enlightened, apostolic zeal inflamed, the laurel of virgins crowned, the fire of divine love consumed.
odignissimachristisponsaquamluxprophetie.la: O digníssima * Christi sponsa, quam lux prophetíæ illustávit, zelus apostólicus inflammávit, láurea vírginum coronávit, divíni amóris incéndium consummávit.

ceciliamemisitadvosutostendatismihisanct.en: Cecilia * hath sent me to you, that you may shew me holy Urban; for I have secrets for him, which I am to deliver.
ceciliamemisitadvosutostendatismihisanct.la: Cæcília * me misit ad vos, ut ostendátis mihi sanctum Urbánum; quia ad ipsum hábeo secréta, quæ pérferam Ps. 84

dumaurorafinemdaretceciliadixit.en: When the dawn was ending the night, Cecilia said:
dumaurorafinemdaretceciliadixit.la: Dum auróra finem daret, Cæcília dixit:

eiamiliteschristiabiiciteoperatenebrarum.en: Come, ye soldiers of Christ, cast off the works of darkness, and put on the armour of light.
eiamiliteschristiabiiciteoperatenebrarum.la: Eja, mílites Christi, abjícite ópera tenebrárum, et induímini arma lucis.

ceciliavaledicensfratribusetexhortanseos.en: Cecilia, bidding farewell to the brethren and exhorting them, said:
ceciliavaledicensfratribusetexhortanseos.la: Cæcília valedícens frátribus, et exhórtans eos, dixit.

oremusomnesaddominumiesumchristumdixitbe.en: Let us all pray to the Lord Jesus Christ, said blessed Clement, that he would open a vein of a fountain for his Confessors:
oremusomnesaddominumiesumchristumdixitbe.la: Oremus omnes ad Dominum Jesum Christum, dixit beatus Clemens, ut Confessoribus suis fontis venam aperiat:

utdebeneficiissuisgratulemur.en: That we may give thanks for his benefits.

quipercussitindesertosinapetrametfluxeru.en: He who struck the rock in the desert of Sinai, and the waters flowed in abundance, may he impart unto us water and flowing streams.
quipercussitindesertosinapetrametfluxeru.la: Qui percussit in deserto Sina petram, et fluxerunt aquæ in abundantia, ipse nobis laticem, et fluenta impertiatur.

oculidominirespexeruntinpauperescumpecca.en: The eyes of the Lord * have looked upon the poor, † when the sinners bent their bows against them.
oculidominirespexeruntinpauperescumpecca.la: Oculi Dómini * respexérunt in páuperes, † cum peccatóres arcus suos in eos inténderent. Ps. 10

silvesterromanuspatrerufinosevienteperse.en: Silvester, a Roman, whose father was Rufinus, had hidden himself on mount Soracte while the persecution raged; and in the thirtieth year of his age was made priest of the holy Roman Church. When Pope Melchiades died, he succeeded in his place, under the emperor Constantine, who had before given peace to the Church of Christ by a public law. Silvester so encouraged him to protect and spread religion, that the emperor built many basilicas, and enriched them most munificently. Under this Pontiff was held the first council of Nicaea, confirmed by Silvester himself, whereby Arius was condemned. Renowned for holiness of life and kindness to the poor, he died in peace, and was buried in the cemetery of Priscilla.
silvesterromanuspatrerufinosevienteperse.la: Silvéster Románus, patre Rufíno, sæviénte persecutióne, in Sorácte monte latitáverat; et trigésimum annum agens, présbyter sanctæ Románæ Ecclésiæ est creátus. Melchíade Pontífice vita functo, in ejus locum succéssit, imperatóre Constantíno, qui ántea pacem Ecclésiæ Christi lege pública déderat. Quem Silvéster ad tuéndam propagandámque religiónem ita fovit, ut imperátor multas eréxerit basílicas, eásque municicentíssime locupletárit. Hoc Pontífice hábitum est concílim Nicænum primum, ab ipso Silvéstro confirmátum, quo Aríus condemnátus fuit. Vitæ sanctitáte et in páuperes benignitáte insígnis, óbiit in pace et sepúltus es in cœmetério Priscíllæ.

expropriumsanctorum.en: From the Proper of the Saints

gloriethonorecoronastieumdomineetconstit.en: Thou hast crowned him with glory and honour, O Lord: and hast set him over the works of thy hands:
gloriethonorecoronastieumdomineetconstit.la: Glória et honóre coronásti eum, Dómine, et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum:

omniasubiecistisubpedibuseius.en: Thou hast subjected all things under his feet.

principespersecutisuntmegratisetaverbist.en: Princes have persecuted me without cause: and my heart hath been in awe of thy words. Well doth the Martyr say this, who endureth unjustly the torments of persecution; who hath robbed nothing, hath oppressed no man with violence, hath shed no man's blood, hath thought no man's bed to be violated; who oweth nothing to the laws, and is compelled to endure punishments heavier than those of robbers; who speaketh justly, and is not heard; who speaketh things full of salvation, and is fought against, so that he can say: When I spoke to them, they fought against me without cause.
principespersecutisuntmegratisetaverbist.la: Príncipes persecúti sunt me gratis: et a verbis tuis trepidávit cor meum. Bene hoc Martyr dicit, quod injúste persecutiónum torménta sustineat; qui nihil rapúerit, nullum violentus oppresserit, nullius sánguinem fuderit, nullius torum putaverit esse violándum; qui nihil légibus debeat, et gravióra latronum sustinere cogátur supplícia; qui loquátur juste, et non audiátur; qui loquátur plena salútis, et impugnétur, ut possit dicere: Cum loquébar illis, impugnábant me gratis.

gratisigiturpersecutionempatiturquiimpug.en: He therefore suffereth persecution without cause who is assailed without crime; he is assailed as guilty, when in such a confession he is worthy of praise; he is assailed as a sorcerer, who glorieth in the name of the Lord, whereas godliness is the foundation of all virtues. Truly in vain is he assailed who among the ungodly and faithless is accused of ungodliness, whereas he is a master of the faith.
gratisigiturpersecutionempatiturquiimpug.la: Gratis ígitur persecutiónem pátitur, qui impugnátur sine crimine; impugnátur ut noxius cum sit in tali confessióne laudábilis; impugnátur quasi veneficus, qui in nómine Dómini gloriátur, cum pietas virtútum ómnium fundaméntum sit. Vere frustra impugnátur, qui apud ímpios et infidos impietátis arcessitur, cum fidei sit magister.

poneergomartyreminterpericulaconstitutum.en: Set therefore the Martyr in the midst of perils, when on the one side the savagery of the beasts roareth to strike terror, on another the hissing of red-hot plates and the flame of the burning furnace seetheth; on another side the dragging of heavy chains resoundeth, here the bloody executioner standeth by: Set him, I say, looking round upon all things full of torments, and then thinking upon the divine commandments, that everlasting fire, that endless burning of the faithless, that misery of punishment ever renewed; trembling in heart, lest, while he yieldeth to things present, he give himself up to everlasting destruction; troubled in mind, while he beholdeth, as it were in a vision, that terrible sword of the judgment to come. Doth not the confidence of one who desireth eternal things and trembleth at divine things concur with equal effect to this trembling of the trust of a steadfast man?
poneergomartyreminterpericulaconstitutum.la: Pone ergo Mártyrem inter perícula constitútum, cum inde immánitas bestiárum ad incutiéndum terrórem ínfremat, aliúnde stridor candéntium laminárum et flamma fornácis ardéntis exæstuet; ex parte ália pérsonent tractus grávium catenárum, hinc cárnifex cruéntus assístat: Pone, inquam, circumspectántem ómnia plena supplíciis, deínde cogitántem mandáta divína, illum ignem perpétuum, illud sine fine incéndium perfidórum, illam pœnæ recrudescéntis ærúmnam; trepidáre corde, ne, dum præséntibus cedat, perpétuis se dedat exítiis; perturbári ánimo, dum futúri judícii rhomphæam illam terríbilem quadam conspéctus spécie contuétur. Nonne ad hanc trepidatiónem fidúciæ viri constántis, æquális in eúmdem concúrrit efféctum confidéntia cupiéntis ætérna, et divína trepidántis?

fulgebuntiustisicutlilium.en: The just shall shine as the lily:

etsicutroseinierichoflorebuntantedominum.en: And as roses in Jericho shall they flourish before the Lord, alleluia.
etsicutroseinierichoflorebuntantedominum.la: Et sicut rosæ in Jéricho florébunt ante Dóminum, allelúja.

gaudeteiustiindominoalleluia.en: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye just, alleluia:

rectosdecetcollaudatioalleluiaalleluia.en: Praise becometh the upright, alleluia, alleluia.

cantateeicanticumnovumbenepsalliteeiinvo.en: Sing to him a new canticle, sing well unto him with a loud noise.
cantateeicanticumnovumbenepsalliteeiinvo.la: Cantáte ei cánticum novum: bene psállite ei in vociferatióne.

beatiquipersecutionempatiunturpropterius.en: Blessed are they * that suffer persecution for justice' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
beatiquipersecutionempatiunturpropterius.la: Beati, * qui persecutionem patiuntur propter iustitiam, quoniam ipsorum est regnum coelorum Ps. 259, 254, 255

sanctiperfidemviceruntregnaoperatisuntiu.en: The Saints by faith conquered kingdoms, wrought justice, obtained promises, and became valiant in battle:
sanctiperfidemviceruntregnaoperatisuntiu.la: Sancti per fidem vicérunt regna, operáti sunt justítiam, adépti sunt promissiónes, et fortes facti sunt in bello:

omnestestimoniofideiprobati.en: All approved by the testimony of faith.

castraverteruntexterorumeffugaveruntacie.en: They put to flight the armies of foreigners, they escaped the edge of the sword.
castraverteruntexterorumeffugaveruntacie.la: Castra vertérunt exterórum, effugavérunt áciem gládii.

certamenmagnumhabueruntsanctideitransier.en: The Saints of God had a great conflict: they passed through fire and water, and were saved:
certamenmagnumhabueruntsanctideitransier.la: Certámen magnum habuérunt Sancti Dei: transiérunt per ignem at aquam, et salvi facti sunt:

etcoronasacceperuntadominodeo.en: And they received crowns from the Lord God.
etcoronasacceperuntadominodeo.la: Et corónas accepérunt a Dómino Deo.

immanienimprochristoinsuiscorporibuspert.en: For they endured for Christ savage torments in their bodies.
immanienimprochristoinsuiscorporibuspert.la: Immánia enim pro Christo in suis corpóribus pertulérunt torménta.

sapientiamsanctorumnarrentpopulietlaudem.en: Let the peoples shew forth the wisdom of the Saints, and let all the Church declare their praise.
sapientiamsanctorumnarrentpopulietlaudem.la: Sapiéntiam Sanctórum narrent pópuli, et laudem eórum pronúntiet omnis Ecclésia.

daquesumusomnipotensdeusutquibeatorummar.en: Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God, that we who keep the solemnity of thy blessed Martyrs N. and N. may be helped by their intercession with thee.
daquesumusomnipotensdeusutquibeatorummar.la: Da, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui beatórum Mártyrum tuórum N. et N. solémnia cólimus, eórum apud te intercessiónibus adjuvémur.

uteniminfirmaturpeccatoradversisitaiustu.en: For as the sinner is weakened by adversity, so the just man is strengthened by temptations. Thus did the Saints fight against sin; thus were they made both stronger by labouring and victors by dying. No athlete can be called stronger without a contest, none can be crowned without a victory. No soldier hath subdued the enemy without battle; none without war hath deserved well of his commander.
uteniminfirmaturpeccatoradversisitaiustu.la: Ut enim infirmátur peccátor advérsis, ita justus tentatiónibus roborátur. Sic dimicárunt advérsus peccátum Sancti; sic, et laborándo fortióres, et moriéndo victóres effécti sunt. Nullus athlétes sine certámine fórtior dici, nullus sine victória póterit coronári. Nemo miles sine prœlio hostem subjécit; nemo sine bello imperatórem proméruit.

habeschristianecompetentiaarmaquibushost.en: Thou hast, O Christian, fit arms wherewith to overcome the foe; thou hast most strong weapons wherewith to vanquish the enemy. With these the Lord long since furnished thee by grace, and afterwards the Apostle Paul armed thee. These are the arms wherewith the Saints fought, whose virtues thou lovest and whose victories thou admirest. Imitate, O Christian, the Saints whom thou lovest; and follow the life and ways of those whose virtues thou celebratest. Be such after their example; for they too were made such after the example of those that went before them. For the virtue of any man cannot be imitated by him who hath not imitated his life.
habeschristianecompetentiaarmaquibushost.la: Habes, christiáne, competéntia arma, quibus hostem expúgnes; habes fortíssima tela, quibus inimícum debelles. His te jamdúdum Dóminus per grátiam ímbuit, et póstmodum Apóstolus Paulus armávit. Hæc sunt arma, quibus dimicárunt Sancti, quorum virtútes díligis et victórias admiráris. Imitáre, christiáne, quos díligis Sanctos; et quorum virtútes frequéntas, eórum vitam et institúta sectáre. Esto talis de eórum exémplo; quia et hi de superiórum tales effécti sunt. Nec enim virtus ab eo póterit imitári cujúsquam, qui ejus vitam non fúerit imitátus.

inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuisqui.en: At that time: Jesus said to his disciples: He that heareth you, heareth me; and he that despiseth you. And so on.
inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuisqui.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis: Qui vos audit, me audit: et qui vos spernit. Et réliqua.

utinadiendoquisquevelspernendevangeliipr.en: That each one, in hearing or despising the preacher of the Gospel, might learn that he despiseth or heareth, not persons of no account, but the Lord the Saviour, yea, the Father himself, he saith: He that heareth you, heareth me; and he that despiseth you, despiseth me. And he that despiseth me, despiseth him that sent me: because without doubt the Master is heard in the disciple, and the Father is honoured in the Son. It may also be understood thus: He that showeth not mercy to one of these my least brethren, showeth it not to me: because for their sakes I also took upon me the form of a servant and the garb of a poor man.
utinadiendoquisquevelspernendevangeliipr.la: Ut in adiéndo quisque, vel spernéndo Evangélii prædicatóre non viles quasque persónas, sed Dóminum Salvatórem, immo ipsum Patrem spérnere se, vel audíre dísceret, ait: Qui vos audit, me audit: et qui von spernit, me spernit. Qui autem me spernit, spernit eum, qui me misit: quia procul dúbio in disípulo Magíster audítur et in fílio Pater honrátur. Potest et ita intélligi: Qui non facit misericórdiam uni de frátribus meis mínimis, nec mihi facit: quia et ipse pro his formam servi, et páuperis hábitum suscépi.

reversisuntautemseptuagintaduocumgaudiod.en: And the seventy-two returned with joy, saying: Lord, the devils also are subject to us in thy name. Well indeed did they confess, giving honour to the name of Christ; but because, being yet weak in faith, they rejoiced in miracles, see what they hear. And he said to them: I saw Satan like lightning falling from heaven: not, I see now, but, I saw before, when he fell; and in that he saith, like lightning, it signifieth either his headlong fall from on high to the depths, or that, though cast down, he still transformeth himself into an angel of light.
reversisuntautemseptuagintaduocumgaudiod.la: Revérsi sunt autem septuagínta duo cum gáudio, dicéntes: Dómine, étiam dæmónia subjiciúntur nobis in nómine tuo. Bene quidem conféssi sunt, deferéntes honórem nómini Christi, sed quia infírma adhuc fide gaudébant virtútibus, vide, quid áudiunt. Et ait illis: Vidébam sátanam, sicut fulgur, de cælo cadéntem: non modo vídeo, sed prius vidébam, quando córruit; quod autem ait: sicut fulgur, vel præcípitem de supérnis ad ima lapsum signíficat, vel quia dejéctus adhuc transfigúrat se in ángelum lucis.

eccededivobispotestatemcalcandisupraserp.en: Behold, I have given you power to tread upon serpents and scorpions; that is, to cast out of possessed bodies every kind of unclean spirits: although it may also most rightly be taken according to the letter, seeing that Paul too, being seized by a viper, suffered no harm.
eccededivobispotestatemcalcandisupraserp.la: Ecce dedi vobis potestátem, calcándi supra serpéntes et scorpiónes, hoc est, omne genus immundórum spirítuum de obséssis corpóribus ejiciéndi: quamvis et ad lítteram rectíssime possit áccipi: síquidem et Paulus a vípera invásus, nihil advérsi pátitur.

hocsaneinterserpentesquidenteetscorpione.en: This, I think, is the difference between serpents, which hurt with the tooth, and scorpions, which hurt with the tail: that serpents, raging openly, and scorpions, lying in wait secretly, signify either men or demons: serpents, those who cast the poisons of wicked persuasion against virtues when they are beginning; scorpions, those who strive to corrupt at the end virtues that are perfected. But yet rejoice not in this, because to cast out spirits, as also to work other miracles, is sometimes not of the merit of him that worketh it; but the invocation of the name of Christ doth this.
hocsaneinterserpentesquidenteetscorpione.la: Hoc sane inter serpéntes, qui dente, et scorpiónes, qui cauda nocent, distáre árbitror: quod serpéntes apérte sæviéntes, scorpiónes clánculo insidiántes, vel hómines, vel dæmones signíficent: serpéntes, qui inchoándis virtútibus venéna pravæ persuasiónis objíciunt: scorpiónes, qui consummátas virtútes ad finem vitiáre conténdunt. Verúmtamen in hoc nolíte gaudére, quia spíritus ejícere, sicut et virtútes álias fácere, intérdum non est ejus mériti, qui operátur; sed invocátio nóminis Christi hoc agit.

homiliadeseusebiocircamedio.en: Homily 78, on St. Eusebius 2, about the middle
homiliadeseusebiocircamedio.la: Homilía 78, de S. Eusebio 2, circa medio

beatipatrisnmeritaiamintutopositasecurim.en: Let us without fear magnify the merits of the blessed Father N., now placed in safety; who, holding manfully the helm of faith, hath now cast the anchor of hope in a calm haven, and hath brought the ship, full of heavenly riches and eternal merchandise, to the longed-for shore; who held the shield of the fear of God unwearyingly against all adversaries, until he came to the victory.
beatipatrisnmeritaiamintutopositasecurim.la: Beáti Patris N. mérita, jam in tuto pósita, secúri magnificémus; qui, gubernáculum fídei viríliter tenens, ánchoram spei tranquílla jam in statióne compósuit, et plenam cæléstibus divítiis et ætérnis mércibus navem, optáto in líttore, collocávit; qui contra omnes adversários scutum timóris Dei támdiu infatigabíliter ténuit, donec ad victóriam perveníret.

quidenimfuittotusviteilliuscursusnisiuni.en: For what was the whole course of his life, but one conflict with a watchful enemy?
quidenimfuittotusviteilliuscursusnisiuni.la: Quid enim fuit totus vitæ illíus cursus, nisi uníus cum vígili hoste conflíctus?

quantishiccecisaviaveritatiserrantibuset.en: To how many blind, wandering from the way of truth and already hanging from the highest crag over the abyss, did he restore their lost sight, and repair that vision whereby Christ might be seen?
quantishiccecisaviaveritatiserrantibuset.la: Quantis hic cæcis, a via veritátis errántibus et de summa jam in profúndum rupe pendéntibus, amíssum réddidit visum; et illum, quo Christus viderétur, reparávit intúitum?

quantorumauribussurdisetinfidelitatisobt.en: Into the deaf ears of how many, condemned by the stopping of unbelief, did he pour the precious hearing to receive the voice of the heavenly commandments; that, when God called them to mercy, they might answer by obedience? How many wounded inwardly did he cure of their infirmity by the art of his angelic mouth and of his prayers?
quantorumauribussurdisetinfidelitatisobt.la: Quantórum áuribus surdis et infidelitátis obturatióne damnátis, ad percipiéndam vocem cæléstium mandatórum, pretiósum infúdit audítum; ut, vocánti Deo ad misericórdiam, respondérent per obediéntiam? Quantos intrínsecus vulnerátos, angélici oris arte et oratiónum, ab infirmitáte curávit?

quantosperlongamincuriampeccatolaberesol.en: How many, dissolved through long carelessness by the stain of sin, and as it were overspread with the contagion of leprosy, did he cleanse, purifying them by chastisements and exhortations, God working in him? The souls of how many, already dead though living in the body, and overwhelmed and buried under the mass of their sins, did he raise up to God by calling them to amendment as to the light; that, a wonderful imitator of his Lord, he might in turn put to death to sin, by a life-giving death, those that had been dead to God?
quantosperlongamincuriampeccatolaberesol.la: Quantos, per longam incúriam peccáto labe resolútos et quadam lepræ contgióne perfúsos, castigatiónibus et exhortatiónibus expiándo, Deo in se operánte, mundávit? Quantórum ánimas, vivéntes in córpore jam defúnctas et delictórum mole óbrutas ac sepúltas, ad emendatiónem tamquam ad lucem vocándo, Deo esuscitávit; ut, Dómini sui admirándus imitátor, jam mórtuas Deo, e contrário mortíficet, vitáli morte, peccáto?

inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuisvig.en: At that time: Jesus said to his disciples: Watch ye, because ye know not what hour your Lord will come. And so on.
inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuisvig.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis: Vigiláte, quia nescítis qua hora Dóminus vester ventúrus sit. Et réliqua.

commentinmatthcapinfine.en: Commentary on Matthew, ch. 26, at the end
commentinmatthcapinfine.la: Comment. in Matth., cap. 26 in fine‚

utignorantiamillamdieiomnibustacitinonsi.en: That we might know that that ignorance of the day, kept silent from all, is not without the reason of a profitable silence, the Lord admonished us to watch because of the coming of the thief, and, held fast by constancy in prayers, to cleave to all the works of his commandments. For he showeth that the thief is the devil, ever watchful to carry off spoils from us, and lying in wait for the houses of our bodies: that he may pierce them, while we are careless and given to sleep, with the darts of his counsels and allurements. It behoveth us therefore to be ready: for ignorance of the day should stir up the earnest care of a watchful expectation.
utignorantiamillamdieiomnibustacitinonsi.la: Ut ignorántiam illam diéi ómnibus táciti, non sine útilis siléntii ratióne esse scirémus, vigiláre nos Dóminus propter advéntum furis admónuit, et oratíonum assiduitáte deténtos ómnibus præceptórum suórum opéribus inhærére. Furem enim esse osténdit zábulum, ad detrahénda ex nobis spólia pervígilem, et córporum nostrórum dómibus insidiántem: ut ea incuriósis nobis, et somno déditis, consiliórum suórum atque illecebrárum jáculis perfódiat. Parátos ígitur esse nos cónvenit: quia diéi ignorátio inténtam sollicitúdinem suspénsæ exspectatiónis exágitet.

quisnamestfidelisservusetprudensquemcons.en: Who, thinkest thou, is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord hath appointed over his family? Although he exhorteth us all in common to an unwearied care of watchfulness, yet he enjoineth a special solicitude upon the rulers of the people, that is, the bishops, in the expectation of his coming. For he signifieth that this faithful and wise servant is the one set over the household, who careth for the welfare and profit of the people committed to him.
quisnamestfidelisservusetprudensquemcons.la: Quisnam est fidélis servus et prudens, quem constítuit Dóminus super famíliam suam? Quamquam in commúne nos ad indeféssam vigilántiæ curam adhortétur: speciálem tamen pópuli princípibus, id est, epíscopis, in exspectatióne adventúque suo sollicitúdinem mandat. Hunc enim servum fidélem atque prudéntem, præpósitum famíliæ signíficat, cómmoda atque utilitátes commíssi sibi pópuli curántem.

quisidictoaudiensetpreceptisobedienserit.en: Who, if he shall hearken to the word and obey the commandments, that is, if by the fitness and truth of his doctrine he strengthen the weak, bind up the broken, convert the perverse, and dispense the word of life as the food of eternity for nourishing the household, and be found doing these things and abiding in them: he shall obtain glory from the Lord as a faithful steward and a profitable bailiff, and shall be set over all goods; that is, he shall be placed in the glory of God, for there is nothing beyond that is better.
quisidictoaudiensetpreceptisobedienserit.la: Qui si dicto áudiens, et præcéptis obédiens erit, id est, si doctrínæ opportunitáte et veritáte infírma confírmet, disrúpta consólidet, depraváta convértat, et verbum vitæ in æternitátis cibum aléndæ famíliæ dispéndat, atque hæc agens, hisque ímmorans deprehendátur: glóriam a Dómino tamquam dispensátor fidélis et víllicus útilis consequétur, et super ómnia bona constituétur; id est, in Dei glória collocábitur, quia nihil sit ultra, quod mélius sit.

quodsicontuenslongamdeipatientiamqueinpr.en: But if, beholding the long patience of God, which is extended for the advancement of man's salvation, he shall grow insolent against his fellow servants, and give himself over to the evils and vices of the world, exercising his care upon present things only in the service of the belly; the Lord shall come on a day he looketh not for, and shall divide him from the goods which he had promised, and shall appoint his portion with the hypocrites in the eternity of punishment: because he despaired of his coming, because he obeyed not the commandments, because he was zealous for present things, because he lived the life of the Gentiles, because, despairing of the judgment, he vexed the household committed to him with hunger, thirst, and slaughter.
quodsicontuenslongamdeipatientiamqueinpr.la: Quod, si cóntuens longam Dei patiéntiam, quæ in proféctum humánæ salútis exténditur, advérsum consérvos insoléscet, et sæculi malus vitiísque se tradet, præséntium tantum curam in cultu ventris exércens; desperáta die Dóminus advéniet, eúmque a bonis, quæ spopónderat, dívidet, portionémque ejus cum hypócritis in pœnæ æternitáte constítuet: quia advéntum desperávit, quia mandátis non obtemperáverit, quia præséntibus studúerit, quia vita Géntium víxerit, quia desperatióne judícii commíssam sibi famíliam fame, siti, cæde vexáverit.

necimmeritodoctoressanctihyadumnuncupati.en: And not without reason are the holy Doctors signified by the name of the Hyades. For in the Greek tongue rain is called hyetos, and the Hyades took their name from rains, because when they rise they without doubt bring showers. Well therefore are they expressed by the name of the Hyades, who, brought to the state of the universal Church as it were to the face of heaven, have poured the showers of holy preaching upon the dry earth of the human breast.
necimmeritodoctoressanctihyadumnuncupati.la: Nec immérito Doctóres sancti Hýadum nuncupatióne signántur. Græco quippe elóquio hýetos plúvia vocátur, et Hýades nomen a plúviis accepérunt, quia ortæ procul dúbio imbres ferunt. Bene ergo Hýadum appellatióne expréssi sunt, qui, ad statum universális Ecclésiæ quasi in cæli fáciem dedúcti, super aréntem terram humáni péctoris, sanctæ prædicatiónis imbres fudérunt.

sienimpredicationissermopluvianonessetmo.en: For if the word of preaching were not rain, Moses would by no means have said: Let my speech be expected as the rain; and the Truth would in no wise have said by Isaias: I will command my clouds to rain no rain upon it; and that which we brought forward a little before: Therefore the stars of rain have been withheld.
sienimpredicationissermopluvianonessetmo.la: Si enim prædicatiónis sermo plúvia non esset, Móyses mínime dixísset: Exspectétur sicut plúvia elóquium meum; et nequáquam per Isaíam Véritas díceret: Mandábo núbibus meis, ne pluant super eam imbrem; atque hoc, quod paulo ante protúlimus: Quam ob rem prohíbitæ sunt stellæ pluviárum.

dumergohyadescumpluviisveniuntadcelispat.en: While therefore the Hyades come with the rains, the sun is led to the higher spaces of heaven: because, when the knowledge of the Doctors appeareth, while our mind is watered with the shower of preaching, the warmth of faith is increased. And the watered earth advanceth to fruit, when the light of the sky is kindled: because we yield more abundantly the fruit of good works, while through the flame of sacred learning we burn more brightly in the heart. And while through them heavenly knowledge is shown more and more day by day, there is opened to us as it were the springtime of the inward light; that a new sun may shine upon our minds, and, made known to us by their words, may glitter brighter of himself every day. For as the end of the world presseth on, heavenly knowledge advanceth, and with time increaseth more abundantly.
dumergohyadescumpluviisveniuntadcelispat.la: Dum ergo Hýades cum plúviis véniunt, ad cæli spátia altióra sol dúcitur: quia, apparénte Doctórum sciéntia, dum mens nostra imbre prædicatiónis infúnditur, fídei calor augétur. Et perfúsa terra ad fructum próficit, cum lumen ætheris ignéscit: quia ubérius frugem boni óperis réddimus, dum per sacræ eruditiónis flammam in corde clárius ardémus. Dumque per eos diébus síngulis magis magísque sciéntia cæléstis osténditur, quasi intérni nobis lúminis vernum tempus aperítur; ut novus sol nostris méntibus rútilet, et, eórum verbis nobis cógnitus, seípso quotídie clárior micet. Urgénte étenim mundi fine, supérna sciéntia próficit, et lárgius cum témpore excréscit.

vitampetiitateettribuistieidomine.en: He asked life of thee: and thou hast given it him, O Lord.
vitampetiitateettribuistieidomine.la: Vitam pétiit a te, et tribuísti ei, Dómine.

beatusvirquiinventusestsinemaculetquipos.en: Blessed is the man that is found without blemish: and that hath not gone after gold, nor put his trust in treasures of money:
beatusvirquiinventusestsinemaculetquipos.la: Beátus vir, qui invéntus est sine mácula, et qui post aurum non ábiit, nec sperávit in thesáuris pecúniæ:

ideostabilitasuntbonaipsiusindomino.en: Therefore are his goods established in the Lord.
ideostabilitasuntbonaipsiusindomino.la: Ideo stabilíta sunt bona ipsíus in Dómino.

potuitenimtransgredietnonesttransgressus.en: For he could have transgressed, and hath not transgressed: and could do evil things, and hath not done them.
potuitenimtransgredietnonesttransgressus.la: Pótuit enim tránsgredi, et non est transgréssus; fácere mala, et non fecit.

obeativirinsanctapreconiaoinestimabilisd.en: O the holy praises of the blessed man N.! O the inestimable love of charity! who, while he despised the pomp of the world,
obeativirinsanctapreconiaoinestimabilisd.la: O beáti viri N. sancta præcónia! o inæstimábilis diléctio caritátis! qui, dum sæculi pompam contémpsit,

cuiviverechristusfuitetmorilucrum.en: To whom to live was Christ, and to die was gain.
cuiviverechristusfuitetmorilucrum.la: Cui vívere Christus fuit, et mori lucrum.

derideturiustisimplicitashuiusmundisapie.en: The simplicity of the just man is laughed to scorn. The wisdom of this world is to cover the heart with devices, to veil the meaning with words: to show forth as true the things that are false, to prove false the things that are true. This prudence truly is learned by young men by use; this is learned by children for a price; they that know it, despising others, are proud: they that know it not, being subject and timid, admire it in others: because this same iniquity of double-dealing is loved by them, cloaked under a fair name, while perversity of mind is called refinement.
derideturiustisimplicitashuiusmundisapie.la: Deridétur justi simplícitas. Hujus mundi sapiéntia est, cor machinatiónibus tégere, sensum verbis veláre: quæ falsa sunt, vera osténdere; quæ vera sunt, falsa demonstráre. Hæc nimírum prudéntia usu a juvénibus scitur hæc a púeris prétio díscitur; hanc qui sciunt, céteros despiciéndo supérbiunt: hanc qui nésciunt, subjécti et tímidi in áliis mirántur: quia ab eis hæc éadem duplicitátis iníquitas nómine palliáta dilígitur, dum mentis pervérsitas urbánitas vocátur.

hecsibiobsequentibusprecipithonorumculmi.en: This wisdom teacheth its followers to seek the heights of honours, to rejoice in the vanity of temporal glory once obtained, to return manifold the evils inflicted by others; when strength sufficeth, to yield to none that resist; when the power of strength is lacking, whatever they cannot accomplish by malice, to feign it under a peaceable goodness. But on the contrary, the wisdom of the just is this: to feign nothing for show, to lay open the meaning by words, to love true things as they are, to shun false things; to show good things freely, to bear evil rather than to do it; to seek no revenge for injury, to count contumely for truth's sake a gain.
hecsibiobsequentibusprecipithonorumculmi.la: Hæc sibi obsequéntibus præcipit honórum cúlmina quærere, adépta temporális glóriæ vanitáte gaudére, irrogáta ab áliis mala multiplícius réddere: cum vires súppetunt, nullis resisténtibus cédere: cum virtútis possibílitas deest, quidquid explére per malítiam non valent, hoc in pacífica bonitáte simuláre. At contra, sapiéntia justórum est: nil per ostensiónem fíngere, sensum verbis aperíre, vera ut sunt dilígere, falsa devitáre; bona gratis exhibére, mala libéntius toleráre quam fácere; nullam injúriæ ultiónem quærere, pro veritáte contuméliam lucrum putáre.

sedheciustorumsimplicitasderideturquiaab.en: But this simplicity of the just is laughed to scorn; because by the wise of this world the virtue of purity is believed to be foolishness. For everything that is done innocently is without doubt thought foolish by them; and whatsoever truth approveth in deed soundeth foolish to carnal wisdom. For what seemeth more foolish to the world than to show the mind by words, to feign nothing by crafty device, to return no insults for injuries, to pray for them that curse, to seek poverty, to forsake possessions, not to resist him that robbeth, to offer the other cheek to him that striketh?
sedheciustorumsimplicitasderideturquiaab.la: Sed hæc justórum simplícitas deridétur; quia ab hujus mundi sapiéntibus puritátis virtus fatúitas créditur. Omne enim quod innocénter ágitur, ab eis proculdúbio stultum putátur; et quidquid in ópere véritas ápprobat, carnáli sapiéntiæ fátuum sonat. Quid namque stúltius vidétur mundo, quam mentem verbis osténdere, nil cállida machinatióne simuláre, nullas injúriis contumélias réddere, pro maledicéntibus oráre, paupertátem quærere, posséssa relínquere, rapiénti non resístere, percutiénti álteram maxíllam præbére?

lampascontemptaapudcogitationesdivitumse.en: A lamp despised in the thoughts of the rich. It often happeneth that each of the elect, who is being led to eternal felicity, is weighed down here by continual adversity; that abundance of goods supporteth him not, nor the glory of dignities showeth him honourable, nor any throng of followers attendeth him, nor any pomp of apparel setteth him off in the eyes of men.
