But he is seen as contemptible by all, and is esteemed unworthy of the favour of this world; and yet before the eyes of the hidden Judge he shineth with virtues, he glittereth with the merits of his life: he feareth to be honoured, he shunneth not to be despised: he afflicteth his body with continence, he groweth fat in soul by love alone: he ever prepareth his mind for patience, and, standing upright for justice, he exulteth in the insults he receiveth: he suffereth with the afflicted from his heart, he rejoiceth in the prosperity of the good as in his own, he carefully ruminateth in his mind the food of the sacred word, and, when questioned, knoweth not how to say anything with a double tongue.
lampascontemptaapudcogitationesdivitumse.la: Lampas contémpta apud cogitatiónes dívitum. Sæpe contíngit, ut eléctus quisque, qui ad ætérnam felicitátem dúcitur, contínua hic adversitáte deprimátur; non hunc rerum abundántia fúlciat, non dignitátum glória honorábilem osténdat, nulla ei obsequéntium frequéntia súppetat, nulla hunc humánis óculis véstium pompa compónat. A cunctis vero despicábilis cérnitur, et hujus mundi grátia indígnus æstimátur; sed tamen ante occúlti júdicis óculos virtútibus émicat, vitæ méritis corúscat: honorári métuit, déspici non réfugit: corpus continéntia áfficit, sola in ánimo dilectióne pinguéscit: mentem semper ad patiéntiam præparat, er, eréctus pro justítia, de percéptis contuméliis exsúltat: afflíctis ex corde compátitur, de bonórum prosperitátibus quasi de própriis lætátur, sacri verbi pábula in mente sollícitus rúminat, et, inquisítus, quódlibet éloqui duplíciter ignórat.

declamdeverbisevangeccenosnet.en: Declamation on the words of the Gospel, Behold we, nn. 1 and 2
declamdeverbisevangeccenosnet.la: Declam. de verbis Evang. Ecce nos n. 1 et 2

fidelissermetdignumomniacceptionecolloqu.en: A faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, is the converse of Simon Peter and of Jesus. For obedience is familiar and friendly to salvation; but an obedience firm and stable, which is founded upon a rock. For obedience is better than sacrifices, and to refuse to obey is like the sin of witchcraft. Whence the Saviour himself also preferred this virtue even to life, choosing rather to lay down his life than not to fulfil obedience. Lastly, the very name of Jesus, which is above every name, and in which every knee is bowed, is, the Apostle being witness, the reward of obedience.
fidelissermetdignumomniacceptionecolloqu.la: Fidélis sermo, et dignum omni acceptióne collóquium Simónis Petri et Jesu. Familiáris síquidem et amíca salúti obediéntia est; sed obediéntia firma et stábilis, quæ fundáta est super petram. Mélior est enim obediéntia quam víctimæ, et acquiéscere nolle, ut peccátum ariolándi est. Unde et vitæ quoque ipse Salvátor prætulit hanc virtútem, éligens magis ánimam pónere, quam obediéntiam non implére. Postrémo et ipsum nomen Jesu, quod est super omne nomen, et in quo fléctitur omne genu, Apóstolo teste, obediéntiæ remunerátio est.

libetproindesacratissimohuicinteressecol.en: It pleaseth me therefore to be present at this most sacred converse, and to perceive with the inmost ear of the heart what is said. For I think that the words of this lesson are those of which the Church crieth to her immortal Bridegroom from the ends of the earth: For the sake of the words of thy lips, I have kept hard ways. These, in truth, are the words that have persuaded men throughout the whole world to contempt of the world and to voluntary poverty. These are they that fill cloisters with monks, and deserts with anchorites. These, I say, are the words that spoil Egypt and carry off all its best vessels. This is the word living and effectual, converting souls by a happy emulation of holiness and by the faithful promise of truth.
libetproindesacratissimohuicinteressecol.la: Libet proínde sacratíssimo huic interésse collóquio, et íntima cordis aure percípere, quæ dicúntur. Arbitror enim, verba lectiónis hujus ea esse, de quibus ad immortálem Sponsum a fínibus terræ clamat Ecclésia: Propter verba labiórum tuórum ego custodívi vias duras. Hæc nempe sunt verba, quæ contémptum mundi in univérso mundo, et voluntáriam persuasére homínibus paupertátem. Hæc sunt, quæ mónachis claustra replent, desérta anachorétis. Hæc, inquam, sunt verba, quæ Ægýptum spóliant, et óptima quæque ejus vasa dirípiunt. Hic sermo vivus et éfficax, convértens ánimas felíci æmulatióne sanctitátis, et veritátis promissióne fidéli.

dixitenimsimonpetrusadiesumeccenosreliqu.en: For Simon Peter said to Jesus: Behold, we have left all things. Well, very well, and not to thy folly. For the world passeth away, and the concupiscence thereof: and it is more expedient to leave these things than to be left by them. Behold, saith he, we have left all things, and have followed thee. For indeed he rejoiced as a giant to run the way, and thou couldst not follow him running if thou wert laden. But neither is it an unprofitable exchange to have left all things for him who is above all. For together with him all things are given: and when thou hast laid hold of him, he alone shall be all in all to those who for his sake have left all things.
dixitenimsimonpetrusadiesumeccenosreliqu.la: Dixit enim Simon Petrus ad Jesum: Ecce nos relíquimus ómnia. Bene, óptime, et non ad isipiéntiam tibi. Nam et mundus transit, et concupiscéntia ejus: et relínquere hæc magis éxpedit, quam relínqui. Ecce, imquit, nos relíquimus ómnia, et secúti sumus te. Nimírum quia exsultávit ut gigas ad curréndam viam, nec curréntem sequi póteras onerátus. Sed nec inútilis commutátio, pro eo, qui super ómina est, ómina reliquísse. Nam et simul cum eo donántur ómnia: et ubi apprehénderis eum, erit unus ipse ómnia in ómnibus, qui pro ipso ómnia reliquérunt.

aitilliiesusamendicovobisverbumconfirmat.en: Jesus said to him: Amen I say to you. A word of confirmation is set before; know thou that what followeth is great. In the regeneration, saith he, when the Son of man shall sit on the seat of his majesty, you also shall sit. You shall overtake, saith he, him whom you follow, that, when he shall sit, you also may sit likewise. O sitting! who will grant me to express in worthy words what I conceive in the affection of my heart concerning this sitting? Nay rather, who will grant me to enjoy the untroubled rest of this sitting, which I desire, which I long for, which I seek?
aitilliiesusamendicovobisverbumconfirmat.la: Ait illi Jesus: Amen dico vobis. Verbum confirmatiónis præmíttitur; magnum nóveris esse, quod séquitur. In regeneratióne, inquit, cum séderit Fílius hóminis in sede majestátis suæ, sedébitis et vos. Consequémini, ait, quem sequímini, ut, cum ipse séderit, et vos páriter sedeátis. O séssio! quis mihi tríbuat, ut dignis éxprimam verbis, quod de sessióne hac cordis affectióne concípio? Immo, quis tríbuat mihi sessiónis hujus imperturbáta frui réquie, quam desídero, quam cúpio, quam requíro?

homiliasanctiioannischrysostomiabbatis.en: Homily by St. John Chrysostom, Abbot

homilincapadrom.en: Homily 7 on ch. 3 of the Epistle to the Romans

sicentuplumhicnonrecipimusnosipsiincausa.en: If we receive not here an hundredfold, we ourselves are the cause, who lend not to him that can repay so much. For tell me, I pray, what great thing did Peter give? was it not only a torn net, and a rod and a hook? Yet God in return opened to him the houses of the whole world, and laid open land and sea together, and granted that all should call him to their own homes, nay, that they should sell what was theirs and bring it to his feet, not even putting the money into his hands; for they dared not do that, so great honour did they pay him together with their bounty.
sicentuplumhicnonrecipimusnosipsiincausa.la: Si céntuplum hic non recípimus, nos ipsi in causa sumus, qui mútuum non damus illi, qui tantum réddere potest. Dic enim, quæso, quid magni dedit Petrus? nonne rete scissum tantum, et cálamum et hamum? Verum vicíssim illi Deus inivérsi orbis domos apéruit, terrámque simul et mare patefécit, dedítque, ut omnes illum in sua vocárent, immo, quæ sua erant, vénderent, et ad illíus pedes afférrent, ne in manus quidem tradéntes pecúniam; neque enim id audébant, tantum illi honórem una cum munificéntia tribuébant.

dicesatillepetrueratquidtumobonenonistap.en: Thou wilt say: But he was Peter. What then, good friend? These things were not promised to Peter only: for he said not: But thou, O Peter, alone shalt receive an hundredfold; but: Whosoever shall leave houses, or brethren, shall receive an hundredfold. For he knoweth no difference of persons; but rather weigheth deeds well done. For God is grateful, both when he oweth to us and when he payeth.
dicesatillepetrueratquidtumobonenonistap.la: Dices: At ille Petru erat. Quid tum, o bone? Non ista Petro tantum promíssa sunt: neque enim dixit: Tu vero, o Petre, céntuplum accípies solus; sed, Quisquis relíquerit domos, aut fratres, céntuplum accípiet. Personárum síquidem differéntiam non cognóscit; sed recte facta magis pensat. Grátiam enim habet Deus, et cum nobis debet, et cum solvit.

aspicitautemdeuscreditoressuoslibentiusq.en: But God looketh more willingly upon his creditors than upon those who have lent him nothing: and those to whom he oweth more, he loveth more. Wherefore, if thou wilt enter into a perpetual friendship with him, see that he oweth thee much. For he is not so delighted with his debtors: for he fleeth those to whom he oweth nothing; but to those to whom he oweth, to these above all he hasteneth.
aspicitautemdeuscreditoressuoslibentiusq.la: Aspicit autem Deus creditóres suos libéntius, quam eos, qui nihil mútuo dedérunt: quibus vero plura debet, eos et plus díligit. Quámobrem, si perpétuam cum illo amicítiam iníre vis, vide, ut multum tibi débeat. Neque enim perínde delectátur suis debitóribus: fugit enim eos, quibus nihil debet; quibus vero debet, ad hos potíssimum accúrrit.

omnemigiturlapidemmoventescuremuschristu.en: Leaving therefore no stone unturned, let us take care to have Christ for our debtor; for this present time is the time of lending. Now, to wit, Christ is set in want: if thou lend him nothing now, assuredly when thou hast departed hence he will have no need of thy goods: for here he thirsteth, here he hungereth: beware therefore lest thou despise him.
omnemigiturlapidemmoventescuremuschristu.la: Omnem ígitur lápidem movéntes, curémus Christum debitórem habére; hoc enim præsens tempus, fænerándi tempus est. Nunc scílicet in indigéntia Christus constitútus est: si jam illi nihil das mútuo, tuórum certe, cum hinc discésseris, níhilo opus habébit: hic enim sitis, hic ésurit: cave ígitur, illum ne despícias.

quevenientesponsoaccepitoleuminvasissuis.en: Who, when the Bridegroom came, took oil in her vessels, and with lamps adorned went in with him to the marriage.
quevenientesponsoaccepitoleuminvasissuis.la: Quæ veniénte Sponso accépit óleum in vasis suis, et ornátis lampádibus introívit cum eo ad núptias.

induitmedominusvestimentosalutisetindume.en: The Lord hath clothed me with the garment of salvation, and with the robe of gladness hath he compassed me, and as a bride
induitmedominusvestimentosalutisetindume.la: Índuit me Dóminus vestiménto salútis, et induménto lætítiæ circúmdedit me, et tamquam sponsam

decoravitmecorona.en: He hath adorned me with a crown.

quasisponsumdecoratumcoronetquasisponsam.en: As a bridegroom decked with a crown, and as a bride adorned with her jewels.
quasisponsumdecoratumcoronetquasisponsam.la: Quasi sponsum decorátum coróna et quasi sponsam ornátam monílibus suis.

simileestregnumcelorumdecemvirginibusque.en: The kingdom of heaven is like to ten virgins, who taking their lamps
simileestregnumcelorumdecemvirginibusque.la: Símile est regnum cælórum decem virgínibus, quæ accipiéntes lámpadas suas

exieruntobviamsponsetsponse.en: Went out to meet the bridegroom and the bride.

quinqueautemexeiseruntfatueetquinqueprud.en: And five of them were foolish, and five wise.
quinqueautemexeiseruntfatueetquinqueprud.la: Quinque autem ex eis erunt fátue, et quinque prudéntes.

exlibroscyprianiepiscopietmartyrisdedisc.en: From the book of St. Cyprian, Bishop and Martyr, on the discipline and dress of Virgins
exlibroscyprianiepiscopietmartyrisdedisc.la: Ex libro S. Cypriáni, Epíscopi et Mártyris, de disciplína et hábitu Vírginum

libdehabvirgn.en: Book on the dress of Virgins, nn. 3-5

nuncnobisadvirginessermestquarumquosubli.en: Now our discourse is to virgins, whose care is the greater as their glory is the more sublime. They are the flower of the Church's growth, the grace and ornament of spiritual favour, a joyful nature, a work of praise and honour whole and incorrupt, the image of God answering to the holiness of the Lord, the more illustrious portion of the flock of Christ. Through them and in them the glorious fruitfulness of mother Church rejoiceth and abundantly flourisheth: and the more plenteous virginity addeth to its number, the more doth the joy of the mother increase. To these we speak, these we exhort with affection rather than with authority: not that we, the last and least and very conscious of our lowliness, claim anything for the licence of censure; but that, being the more cautious in solicitude, we fear the more from the assault of the devil.
nuncnobisadvirginessermestquarumquosubli.la: Nunc nobis ad vírgines sermo est, quarum quo sublímior glória est, major et cura est. Flos est ille ecclesiástici gérminis, decus atque ornaméntum grátiæ spiritális, læta índoles, laudis et honóris opus íntegrum atque incorrúptum, Dei imágo respóndens ad sanctimóniam Dómini, illústrior pórtio gregis Christi. Gaudet per illas atque in illis lárgiter floret Ecclésiæ matris gloriósa fœcúnditas: quantóque plus copiósa virgínitas número suo addit, tanto plus gáudium matris augéscit. Ad has lóquimur, has adhortámur affectióne pótius quam potestáte: non quod, extrémi et mínimi et humilitátis nostræ ádmodum cónscii, áliquid ad censúram licéntiæ vindicémus; sed quod ad sollicitúdinem magis cauti, plus de diáboli infestatióne timeámus.

nequeeniminanisheccautiestetvanaformidoq.en: For neither is this caution empty, nor this fear vain, which taketh thought for the way of salvation, which keepeth the life-giving commandments of the Lord; that they who have dedicated themselves to Christ, and, withdrawing from carnal concupiscence, have vowed themselves to God both in flesh and in mind, may finish their work, destined for a great reward, and may study no longer to be adorned or to please any one but their Lord, from whom they also await the reward of virginity, as he himself saith: All men take not this word, but they to whom it is given.
nequeeniminanisheccautiestetvanaformidoq.la: Neque enim inánis hæc cáutio est, et vana formído, quæ ad salútis viam cónsulit, quæ domínica et vitália præcépta custódit, ut quæ se Christo dicáverint, et a carnáli concupiscéntia recedéntes tam carne, quam mente se Deo vóverint, consúmment opus suum magno prǽmio destinátum, nec ornári jam, aut placére cuíquam, nisi Dómino suo, stúdeant, a quo et mercédem virginitátis expéctant, dicénte ipso: Non omnes cápiunt verbum, sed illi quibus datum est.

suntenimspadonesquiexuteromatrissicnatis.en: For there are eunuchs, who were born so from their mother's womb: and there are eunuchs, who were made so by men: and there are eunuchs, who have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven. Again also, by this voice of the Angel, the gift of continence is shown, virginity is proclaimed: These are they who were not defiled with women: for they are virgins: these follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth.
suntenimspadonesquiexuteromatrissicnatis.la: Sunt enim spadónes, qui ex útero matris sic nati sunt: et sunt spadónes, qui coácti sunt ab homínibus; et sunt spadónes, qui seípsos castravérunt propter regnum cœlórum. Dénuo quoque per hanc Angeli vocem continéntiæ munus osténditur, virgínitas prædicátur. Hi sunt, qui cum muliéribus se non coinquinavérunt: vírgines enim permansérunt: hi sunt qui sequúntur Agnum quocúmque íerit.

nequeenimtantummasculiscontinentiegratia.en: For neither doth the Lord promise the grace of continence to men only, and pass over women: but since the woman is a portion of the man, and was taken and formed from him, in almost all the Scriptures God speaketh to the first-formed, because they are two in one flesh, and in the male the female also is signified. But if continence followeth Christ, and virginity is destined for the kingdom of God, what have they to do with earthly dress and with ornaments, whereby, while they long to please men, they offend God?
nequeenimtantummasculiscontinentiegratia.la: Neque enim tantum másculis continéntiæ grátiam Dóminus repromíttit, et féminas prǽterit: sed quóniam fémina viri pórtio est, et ex eo sumpta atque formáta est, in Scriptúris fere ómnibus ad protoplástum Deus lóquitur, quia sunt duo in carne una, et in másculo simul significátur et fémina. Quod si Christum continéntia séquitur, et regno Dei virgínitas destinátur: quid est illis cum terréno cultu, et cum ornaméntis, quibus dum homínibus placére géstiunt, Deum offéndunt?

sermodeverbisdominicapiiiv.en: Sermon 93 on the words of the Lord, ch. 2-4
sermodeverbisdominicapiiiv.la: Sermo 93 de verbis Domini, cap. II-IV

intelligamuscarissimiadomnesnosidestadun.en: Let us understand, dearly beloved, that this parable pertaineth to us all, that is, to the whole Church altogether; not to the rulers alone, nor to the people alone, but to all without exception. These five and five virgins are all the souls of Christians whatsoever. But, that we may tell you what by God's inspiration we perceive, not souls of whatever kind, but such souls as have the Catholic faith, and are seen to have good works in the Church of God: and yet of these very ones five are wise, and five are foolish.
intelligamuscarissimiadomnesnosidestadun.la: Intelligámus, caríssimi, ad omnes nos, id est, ad univérsam omníno Ecclésiam, istam pertinére parábolam, non ad solos præpósitos, nec ad solas plebes: sed prorsus ad omnes. Istæ quinque et quinque vírgines, omnes omníno sunt ánimæ Christianórum. Sed, ut dicámus vobis, quod Deo inspiránte sentímus, non qualescúmque ánimæ; sed tales animæ, quæ habent Cathólicam fidem, et habére vidéntur bona ópera in Ecclésia Dei: et tamen ex ipsis quinque sunt prudéntes, et quinque fátuæ.

etvirginessuntetrepellunturparumestquiav.en: They are virgins, and yet are shut out. It is little that they are virgins, and have lamps. Virgins, by reason of abstinence from the unlawful things of the senses; they have lamps, by reason of good works. Of which works the Lord saith: Let your works shine before men. Likewise he saith to the disciples: Let your loins be girt, and lamps burning in your hands. In the girt loins, virginity; in the burning lamps, good works. If therefore abstinence from unlawful things is good, whence virginity hath received its name, and good works are praiseworthy, which are signified by the lamps; why are five admitted, and five shut out?
etvirginessuntetrepellunturparumestquiav.la: Et vírgines sunt, et repellúntur. Parum est quia vírgines sunt: et lámpades habent. Vírgines, propter abstinéntiam ab sensibus; lámpades habent, propter ópera bona. De quibus opéribus Dóminus dicit: Lúceant ópera vestra coram homínibus. Item discípulis dicit: Sint lumbi vestri accíncti, et lucérnæ ardéntes. In lumbis accínctis, virgínitas; in lucérnis ardéntibus, ópera bona. Si ergo ab illícitis abstinéntia bona est; unde virgínitas nomen accépit, et ópera bona laudabília sunt, quæ significántur lampádibus: quare quinque admittúntur, et quinque repellúntur?

aliasdixitprudentesaliasstultasundeintue.en: Some he called wise, others foolish. Whence do we see it? whence do we discern it? By the oil. Oil signifieth something great, yea very great. Thinkest thou it is charity? We say this by way of inquiry; we do not hasten to a judgment. Why oil seemeth to me to signify charity, I will tell you. The Apostle saith: And I shew unto you yet a more excellent way. If I speak with the tongues of men and of Angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal. This is the more excellent way, that is, charity, which is rightly signified by oil. For oil riseth above all liquids.
aliasdixitprudentesaliasstultasundeintue.la: Alias dixit prudéntes, alias stultas. Unde intuémur? unde discérnimus? De óleo. Aliquid magnum signíficat óleum, et valde magnum. Putas, num cáritas est? Quæréndo dícimus, non senténtiam præcipitámus. Unde mihi videátur óleum caritátem significáre, dicam vobis. Apóstolus dicit: Adhuc supereminentiórem vobis viam demónstro. Si linquis hóminum loquar et Angelórum, caritátem autem non hábeam, factus sum æraméntum sonans, aut cýmbalum tínniens. Ipsa est superéminens via: id est cáritas, quæ mérito óleo significátur. Omnibus enim humóribus óleum superéminet.

sermodeverbisdominicapviviiietx.en: Sermon 93 on the words of the Lord, ch. 6-8 and 10
sermodeverbisdominicapviviiietx.la: Sermo 93 de verbis Domini, cap. VI-VIII et X

disceptemusfratresdequinquevirginibuspru.en: Let us discuss, brethren, the five wise virgins and the five foolish. They would go forth to meet the bridegroom; to go with the heart, to await his coming. But he tarried. While he tarrieth, they all slept. What is this sleep? Lest perchance, while the bridegroom tarried, because iniquity aboundeth, the charity of many should grow cold, he added and said: But he that shall persevere unto the end, he shall be saved. The coldness of charity therefore crept not upon them; charity grew not cold in them, but is fervent unto the end. There is another sleep, which no man escapeth. Do ye not remember the Apostle saying: And I will not have you ignorant, brethren, concerning them that are asleep; that is, concerning them that are dead? Be she a foolish virgin, be she a wise virgin, all suffer the sleep of death. At the last trumpet all shall rise.
disceptemusfratresdequinquevirginibuspru.la: Disceptémus, fratres, de quinque virgínibus prudéntibus et quinque fátuis. Voluérunt ire óbviam sponso, corde ire, exspectáre ejus advéntum. Sed ille tardábat. Dum tardat ille, dormiérunt omnes. Quid est somnus iste? Ne forte tardánte sponso, quóniam abúndat iníquitas, refrigéscit cáritas multórum, subjécit et ait: Qui autem perseveráverit usque in finem, hic salvus erit. Non ergo eis obrépsit frigus caritátis, non in eis refríguit cáritas; sed fervet usque in finem. Est álius somnus, quem nemo evádit. Non recordámini Apóstolum dicéntem: De dormiéntibus autem nolo vos ignoráre, fratres: id est, de his qui mórtui sunt? fátua sit virgo, prudens sit virgo, somnum mortis omnes patiúntur. Ad novíssimam tubam surgent omnes.

prudentesautemilletuleruntoleumsecuminva.en: But the wise took oil with them in their vessels: but the foolish took no oil with them. There is oil, a great oil. This oil is of the gift of God. Do thou therefore carry it with thee, carry it within, where God seeth; there carry the testimony of thy conscience. But he that walketh for the testimony of another carrieth not oil with him. Let your Charity therefore give heed. The lamps of the wise were burning with the inward oil, with the security of conscience, with inward glory, with inmost charity. Yet the lamps of those foolish ones were burning also. Why were they then burning? Because the praises of men were not lacking.
prudentesautemilletuleruntoleumsecuminva.la: Prudéntes autem illæ tulérunt óleum secum in vasis suis: stultæ vero illæ non tulérunt óleum secum. Ibi óleum, magnum óleum. De dono Dei est hoc óleum. Tu ergo tecum porta, intus porta, ubi videt Deus, ibi porta testimónium consciéntiæ tuæ. Qui autem ámbulat ad testimónium aliénum, óleum non portat secum. Inténdat ítaque Cáritas vestra. Sapiéntium lámpades ardébant de óleo intérno, de consciéntiæ securitáte, de interióre glória, de íntima caritáte. Ardébant tamen et illárum fatuárum. Quare tunc ardébant? Quia non déerant laudes hóminum.

posteaveroquamsurrexeruntidestinresurrec.en: But after they rose, that is, in the resurrection from the dead, they began to trim their lamps, that is, to prepare to render to God an account of their works. And because then there is none to praise, every man is busied with his own cause; there were none to sell oil; their lamps began to fail. The door was shut. And what was said to them? I know you not. Did he not know them, who knoweth all things? What then is: I know you not? I disapprove you, I reprobate you. In my art I acknowledge you not; my art knoweth not vices, and judgeth vices; it knoweth them not by doing them, it judgeth them by reproving them: thus therefore, I know you not. The five wise went, they entered in.
posteaveroquamsurrexeruntidestinresurrec.la: Postea vero, quam surrexérunt, id est, in resurrectióne a mórtuis, cœpérunt aptáre lámpades suas, id est, paráre Deo óperum suórum réddere ratiónem. Et quia tunc nemo est qui laudet, omnis homo causæ suæ vacat; non erant, qui óleum vénderent, cœpérunt defícere lámpades. Clausum est óstium. Et quid illis dictum est? Non novi vos. Non illas novit, qui ómnia novit? Quid ergo est: Non novi vos? Improbo vos, réprobo vos. In arte mea non vos agnósco; ars mea nescit vítia, et júdicat vítia; nescit faciéndo, júdicat arguéndo: sic ergo non novi vos. Iérunt, intravérunt quinque prudéntes.

sintinvobisquinqueprudentesadistampruden.en: Let there be in you five wise, belonging to that prudence of the number five. For the hour will come, and when we know not, it will come. Thus did the Gospel close: Watch ye, because ye know not the day nor the hour. Watch with the heart, watch with faith, watch with hope, watch with charity, watch with works: and when thou shalt sleep in the body, the time will come that thou rise. And when thou shalt have risen, prepare thy lamps. Then let them not be put out; then let them be quickened with the inward oil of conscience: then let that bridegroom embrace thee with bodiless bonds, then let him bring thee into the house where thou shalt never sleep, where thy lamp can never be put out. But today we labour, and our lamps flicker amid the winds and temptations of this world; but let our flame burn with strength, that the wind of temptation may rather increase the fire than put it out.
sintinvobisquinqueprudentesadistampruden.la: Sint in vobis quinque prudéntes ad istam prudéntiam quinárii númeri pertinéntes. Véniet enim hora, et quando nescímus, véniet. Sic clausit Evangélium: Vigiláte, quia nescítis diem neque horam. Corde vígila, fide vígila, spe vígila, caritáte vígila, opéribus vígila: et quando córpore dormíveris, véniet tempus ut surgas. Cum autem surréxeris, præpara lámpades. Tunc non exstinguántur, tunc interióre consciéntiæ óleo vegeténtur: tunc sponsus ille incorpóreis néxibus amplectátur, tunc te introdúcat in domum, ubi numquam dórmias, ubi nunquam possit tua lampas exstíngui. Hódie vero laborámus, et lámpades nostræ inter ventos sæculi hujus tentationésque flúctuant; sed árdeat in róbore flamma nostra, ut ventus tentatiónis áugeat ignem pótius, quam exstínguat.

magnaquedamdevirginitatedisserueratdicen.en: He had discoursed great things of virginity, saying: There are eunuchs, who have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven; and, He that can take, let him take it. Neither was he ignorant that virginity is held in great esteem by the many, since the thing is by nature sublime: which is evident from this, that neither in the Old Testament was it practised by those holy men of old, and in the New it is commanded by no necessity of law. For he commanded it not, but left it to the will of the faithful.
magnaquedamdevirginitatedisserueratdicen.la: Magna quædam de virginitáte disserúerat dicens: Sunt eunuchi, qui seipsos castravérunt propter regnum coelórum; et, Qui potest cápere, cápiat. Nec ignorábat, de virginitáte magnam esse vulgo existimatiónem, quippe cum sit ea res natúra sublímis: quod inde patet, quia neque in véteri Testaménto a priscis illis sanctísque viris culta fuit, et in novo nulla legis necessitáte jubétur. Non enim id imperávit, sed fidélium voluntáti permísit.

nonestautemcorporumetpecunieparcupiditas.en: Now the desire of bodies and of money is not equal; but that of bodies is much keener and more vehement. The weaker therefore the foe they wrestle with, the less worthy of pardon are they, if they be overcome. Therefore also he called them foolish; because, having overcome in the greater contest, they lost all in the easier.
nonestautemcorporumetpecunieparcupiditas.la: Non est autem córporum et pecúniæ par cupíditas; sed ácrior multo atque veheméntior illa córporum est. Quanto ígitur cum imbecillióre luctántur, tanto minus vénia dignæ sunt, si vincántur. Idcírco etiam fátuas appellávit; quóniam, majóri certámine superáto, in facíliore totum perdidérunt.

lampadesautemhoclocoilludipsumvirginitat.en: And by lamps in this place he calleth that very gift of virginity and the purity of holiness; and by oil, kindness, almsgiving, help bestowed upon the needy. And while the bridegroom tarried, they all slumbered and slept. He showeth again that no small space of time cometh between, that he might lead the disciples, who expected his kingdom to come soon, away from that opinion; for that they hoped: wherefore he often calleth them back from such a hope.
lampadesautemhoclocoilludipsumvirginitat.la: Lámpades autem hoc loco illud ipsum virginitátis domum appéllat et sanctimóniæ puritátem; óleum vero benignitátem, eleemósynam, impénsum indigéntibus auxílium. Tardánte autem sponso dormitavérunt omnes, et dormiérunt. Non parvum témporis rursus spátium interjéctum osténdit, ut discípulos, regnum ipsíus mox futúrum exspectántes, ab ea opinióne dedúceret; id enim illi sperábant: quaprópter crebro ab hujúsmodi eos spe révocat.

pulchrafaciesedpulchriorfidebeatesnrespu.en: Fair of face, but fairer in faith, blessed art thou, N.; despising the world, thou shalt rejoice with the Angels:
pulchrafaciesedpulchriorfidebeatesnrespu.la: Pulchra fácie, sed púlchrior fide, beáta es, N., réspuens mundum, lætáberis cum Angelis:

quampulchresamicameaquampulchresetsuavis.en: How beautiful art thou, my love, how beautiful art thou and sweet! thy eyes are doves' eyes:
quampulchresamicameaquampulchresetsuavis.la: Quam pulchra es, amíca mea, quam pulchra es et suávis! óculi tui columbárum:

inventabonamargaritadeditomniasuetcompar.en: Having found a good pearl, * she gave all that she had, and bought it.
inventabonamargaritadeditomniasuetcompar.la: Invénta bona margaríta * dedit ómnia sua, et comparávit eam.

ideoquelucerneiusnonexstingueturinsempit.en: Therefore her lamp shall not be put out for ever.
ideoquelucerneiusnonexstingueturinsempit.la: Ideóque lucérna ejus non exstinguétur in sempitérnum.

sermdediversisnovitestamentilocis.en: Sermon 67, on divers places of the New Testament.
sermdediversisnovitestamentilocis.la: Serm. 67. de diversis novi Testamenti locis.

egomaximecommemorationesdiligomartyrumdi.en: I most of all love the commemorations of the Martyrs; I love and embrace them; all indeed, but then especially when the contests of women are set forth. For the weaker the vessel, the greater the grace, the more illustrious the trophy, the more signal the victory: not because of the weakness of the sex of the champions, but because the enemy is now overcome by those very means by which he had overcome.
egomaximecommemorationesdiligomartyrumdi.la: Ego máxime commemoratiónes díligo Mártyrum, díligo, et ampléctor; atque omnes quidem, sed tum præcípue, cum mulíerum certámina proponúntur. Quanto enim infírmius est vas, tanto major est grátia, tanto illústrius est trophǽum, tanto insígnior est victória, non ob imbecillitátem sexus athletárum, sed quod per ea, quibus vícerat inimícus, nunc étiam vincátur.

permulieremvicitpermulieremsuperatusesth.en: By a woman he conquered, by a woman he was overcome. This was formerly his weapon: this hath now become the instrument of his slaughter; this vessel hath appeared invincible. She of old sinned first, and died: this one died, that she might not sin. She of old, puffed up with the hope of a vain promise, violated the laws of God: this one despised the present life, that she might not forswear her faith in her benefactor.
permulieremvicitpermulieremsuperatusesth.la: Per mulíerem vicit, per mulíerem superátus est. Hoc illíus ántea telum erat: hoc illíus nunc cædis factum est instruméntum, hoc vas appáruit insuperábile. Peccávit illa prior, et mórtua est: ista mórtua est, ne peccáret. Illa tum fútilis promíssi spe infláta, Dei leges violávit: hæc vitam præséntem contémpsit, ne fidem in suum benefactórem ejuráret.

quamigiturdeincepssperarepoteruntexcusat.en: What excuse then can men hereafter hope for, if they be soft and slothful; what pardon indeed, when women bear themselves bravely and manfully, when they gird themselves so nobly for the contests of godliness? She had a weak body, and a sex liable to injury; but grace coming upon her hid the weakness of all these.
quamigiturdeincepssperarepoteruntexcusat.la: Quam ígitur deínceps speráre póterunt excusatiónem viri, si molles sint, et ignávi; quam vero véniam, cum fórtiter ac viríliter se gerant mulíeres, cum ádeo se generose ad certámina pietátis accíngant? Fuit ili corpus imbecíllum, et obnóxius sexus injúriæ; verúmtamen ómnium horum imbecillitátem advéniens grátia occultávit.

nihilenimestnihilplanepotentiusestcoquim.en: For there is nothing, nothing at all, more powerful than he who with great zeal hath the fear of God fixed in his mind; but though the enemies threaten fire, though the sword, though wild beasts, though anything else, he despiseth all without difficulty; which assuredly this blessed woman also did.
nihilenimestnihilplanepotentiusestcoquim.la: Nihil enim est, nihil plane poténtius est co, qui magno cum stúdio Dei timórem hábeat in mente defíxum; sed quamvis ignes, quamvis ferrum, quamvis béstias, quamvis áliud quidvis minêntur hostes, ómnia nullo negótio contémnit; quod útique Beáta ista étiam fecit.

pulchrafaciesedpulchriorfidebeatesrespue.en: Fair of face, but fairer in faith, blessed art thou; despising the world, thou shalt rejoice with the Angels:
pulchrafaciesedpulchriorfidebeatesrespue.la: Pulchra fácie, sed púlchrior fide, beáta es, réspuens mundum, lætáberis cum Angelis:

extractatusaugustiniepiscopisuperpsalmos.en: From the Treatise of St. Augustine, Bishop, upon the Psalms
extractatusaugustiniepiscopisuperpsalmos.la: Ex Tractatu S. Augustíni Epíscopi super Psalmos

ierusalemqueedificaturutcivitasfratresqu.en: Jerusalem, which is built as a city. Brethren, when David said these things, that city was finished, it was not being built. I know not therefore what city he meaneth, which is now being built, to which living stones run by faith; of whom Peter saith: Be you also as living stones built up, a spiritual house, that is, the holy temple of God. What is: Ye living stones are built together? Thou livest, if thou believest: and if thou believest, thou shalt be made a temple of God; because the Apostle Paul saith: For the temple of God is holy, which you are.
ierusalemqueedificaturutcivitasfratresqu.la: Jerúsalem, quæ ædificátur ut cívitas. Fratres, quando dicébat ista David, perfécta erat illa cívitas, non ædificabatur. Néscio quam ergo civitátem dicit, quæ modo ædificátur, ad quam currunt in fide lápides vivi; de quibus dicit Petrus: Et vos tamquam lápides vivi coædificamini in domum spiritalem, id est, templum Dei sanctum. Quid est, Lápides vivi coædificamini? Vivis, si credis: si autem credis, efficieris templum Dei; quia dicit Apóstolus Paulus: Templum enim Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos.

ipsergomodocivitasedificaturprecidunturd.en: That city therefore is now being built. Stones are hewn from the mountains by the hands of them that preach the truth, they are squared, that they may enter into the everlasting structure. Many stones are still in the hands of the builder: let them not fall from the hands of the builder, that, being made perfect, they may be built together into the structure of the temple. This, then, is that Jerusalem which is built as a city: its foundation is Christ. The Apostle Paul saith: For other foundation no man can lay, but that which is laid, which is Christ Jesus.
ipsergomodocivitasedificaturprecidunturd.la: Ipsa ergo modo cívitas ædificátur. Præcidúntur de móntibus lápides per manus prædicantium veritátem, conquadrantur, ut intrent in structuram sempitérnam. Adhuc multi lápides in mánibus artíficis sunt: non cadant de mánibus artíficis, ut possint perfecti coædificari in structuram templi. Est ergo ista Jerúsalem, quæ ædificátur ut cívitas: fundaméntum ipsíus Christus est. Dicit Apóstolus Paulus: Fundaméntum áliud nemo potest pónere præter id, quod pósitum est, quod est Christus Jesus.

fundamentumquandoponiturinterradesupered.en: When a foundation is laid in the earth, the walls are built above it, and the weight of the walls tendeth downward, because the foundation is laid beneath. But if our foundation is in heaven, let us be built up toward heaven. Bodies built this structure of this basilica, which ye see to have risen so ample: and because bodies built it, they laid the foundation at the bottom. But because we are built spiritually, our foundation is laid at the top. Thither therefore let us run, there let us be built up; because of that Jerusalem it is said: Our feet were standing in thy courts, O Jerusalem.
fundamentumquandoponiturinterradesupered.la: Fundaméntum quando pónitur in terra, désuper ædificantur paríetes, et pondus paríetum ad ima tendit, quia in impositum est fundaméntum. Si autem fundaméntum nostrum in cœlo est, ad cœlum ædificemur. Córpora ædificaverunt istam structúram, quam videtis amplam surrexisse hujus basílicæ: et quia córpora ædificaverunt, fundaméntum in imo posuérunt. Quia vero spiritaliter ædificamur, fundaméntum nostrum in summo pósitum est. Illuc ergo curramus, ibi ædificemur, quia de ipsa Jerúsalem dictum est: Stantes erant pedes nostri in átriis tuis Jerúsalem.

libinlucinfine.en: Book 8 on Luke, at the end

etconfestiminquitviditetsequebaturillumm.en: And immediately, saith he, he saw, and followed him, glorifying God. For otherwise he would not see, unless he followed Christ, unless he preached the Lord, unless he passed by the world. Let us also return into favour with the rich. For we wish not to offend the rich, who would, if it may be, heal all: lest, straitened by the comparison of the camel, and too quickly forsaken in Zacheus, they should have the offence of a just resentment.
etconfestiminquitviditetsequebaturillumm.la: Et conféstim, inquit, vidit, et sequebatur illum, magníficans Dóminum. Áliter enim non vidéret, nisi sequeretur Christum, nisi Dóminum prædicáret, nisi sǽculum præteriret. Cum divítibus quoque in grátiam revertamur. Nólumus enim offendere dívites, qui volumus, si fíeri potest, sanare omnes: ne in cameli comparatione præstricti, et in Zachǽo cítius quam oportuit, derelicti, justæ habeant commotionis offensam.

discantdivitesnoninfacultatibuscrimenher.en: Let the rich learn that guilt cleaveth not to riches, but to those who know not how to use riches. For riches, as they are hindrances to the wicked, so are they helps to virtue for the good. Zacheus certainly was rich, and chosen by Christ: but by bestowing half his goods on the poor, and restoring also fourfold what he had taken by fraud (for the one is not enough, nor hath liberality any grace if the injury remaineth, because not spoils but gifts are sought), he received a more abundant reward than he bestowed.
discantdivitesnoninfacultatibuscrimenher.la: Discant dívites non in facultátibus crimen hærere, sed in iis, qui uti nesciant facultátibus. Nam divítiæ ut impedimenta improbis, ita bonis sunt adjumenta virtútis. Dives certe Zachǽus, et eléctus a Christo: sed dimidium bonórum suórum paupéribus largiendo, reddendo étiam in quadruplum, quæ fraude sustúlerat, (álterum enim non sat est, nec habet grátiam liberalitas, si injúria persevérat, quia non spólia, sed dona quærúntur) uberiorem mercédem quam conferebat, accépit.

etbeneprincepsinduciturpublicanorumquisi.en: And well is a chief of the publicans brought in. Who now would despair of himself, when even this man, whose wealth was from fraud, came to salvation? And he, saith he, was rich: that thou mayest know that not all the rich are covetous. Because he was low of stature. What meaneth it, that the Scripture hath expressed the stature of no other but this man? See lest perchance he was little in malice, or as yet little in faith. For he had not yet promised to restore: he had not yet seen Christ: rightly was he still little. But John was great, because he both saw Christ, and the Spirit as a dove abiding upon Christ, as he himself saith: I saw the Spirit coming down as a dove, and remaining upon him.
etbeneprincepsinduciturpublicanorumquisi.la: Et bene princeps indúcitur publicanorum. Quis jam de se desperet, quando et iste, cui census ex fraude, ad salútem pervénit? Et ipse, inquit, dives. Ut scias non omnes dívites, avaros. Quia statúra pusíllus erat. Quid sibi vult, quod nullius altérius staturam Scriptúra, nisi hujus expressit? Vide ne forte malítia pusíllus, aut adhuc pusíllus fide. Nondum enim reddere promiserat: nondum viderat Christum: mérito adhuc pusíllus. Joánnes autem magnus, quia et Christum vidit, et Spíritum sicut columbam super Christum manentem, sicut ipse ait: Vidi Spíritum descendentem sicut colúmbam, et manentem super eum.

celebritashuiuscongregationisdedicatiest.en: The festival of this assembly is the dedication of a house of prayer. This then is the house of our prayers; but the house of God are we ourselves. If we ourselves are the house of God, we are built in this world, that we may be dedicated at the end of the world. The building, nay rather the building up, hath labour; the dedication, exultation. That which was done here when these walls were rising, the same is done now, when believers in Christ are gathered together. For by believing, as it were, timber and stones are hewn from the woods and mountains: but when they are catechized, baptized, formed, they are as it were hewn, levelled, and smoothed between the hands of the workmen and builders. Yet they make not a house of the Lord, but when they are joined together by charity.
celebritashuiuscongregationisdedicatiest.la: Celebritas hujus congregatiónis, dedicatio est domus oratiónis. Domus ergo nostrárum oratiónum ista, domus autem Dei nos ipsi. Si domus Dei nos ipsi, nos in hoc sǽculo ædificamur, ut in fine sǽculi dedicemur. ædificium, imo ædificatio habet labórem; dedicatio exsultationem. Quod hic fiebat, quando ista surgebant, hoc fit modo, cum congregantur credéntes in Christum. Credéndo enim, quasi de silvis et móntibus ligna et lápides præciduntur: cum vero catechizantur, baptizantur, formantur, tamquam inter manus fabrorum et opificum dolantur, collineentur, complanantur. Verúmtamen domum Dómini non fáciunt, nisi quando caritáte compaginantur.

lignaistetlapidessinonsibicertoordinecoh.en: If these timbers and stones did not hold together in a certain order, if they did not peaceably interlock, if they did not, by holding together, in a manner love one another, no man would enter here. Lastly, when thou seest in any building the stones and timbers holding well together, thou enterest secure, thou fearest not its fall. The Lord Christ, therefore, willing to enter and to dwell in us, said, as it were in building: A new commandment I give unto you: That you love one another. A new commandment, saith he, I give unto you. For ye were old, ye were not yet making a house for me, ye lay in your ruin. Therefore, that ye may be raised out of the oldness of your ruin, love one another.
lignaistetlapidessinonsibicertoordinecoh.la: Ligna ista et lápides si non sibi certo órdine cohærerent, si non se pacífice innecterent, si non se invicem, cohærendo sibi, quodámmodo amarent, nemo huc intraret. Dénique quando vides in áliqua fabrica lápides et ligna bene sibi cohærere, secúrus intras, ruinam non times. Volens ergo Dóminus Christus intrare, et in nobis habitáre, tamquam ædificando dicébat: Mandátum novum do vobis: Ut vos invicem diligatis. Mandátum, inquit, novum do vobis. Veteres enim eratis, domum mihi nondum faciebatis, in vestra ruína jacebatis. Ergo ut eruamini a vestræ ruinæ vetustáte,vos invicem amate.

consideretergocaritasvestraedificariadhu.en: Let your charity therefore consider that this house is still being built throughout the whole world, as was foretold and promised. For when the house is built after the captivity, as another Psalm hath it, it is said: Sing ye to the Lord a new canticle: sing to the Lord, all the earth. What he said there, A new canticle, that the Lord said, A new commandment. For what hath a new canticle, but a new love? To sing is the part of a lover. The voice of this singer is the fervour of holy love. Let us love, let us love freely: for we love the Lord, than whom we find nothing better: let us love him for his own sake, and ourselves in him, yet for his sake.
consideretergocaritasvestraedificariadhu.la: Consideret ergo cáritas vestra, ædificari adhuc istam domum toto, sicut prædictum est et promíssum, orbe terrárum. Cum enim ædificátur domus post captivitátem, sicut habet álius Psalmus, dícitur: Cantáte Dómino cánticum novum: cantáte Dómino omnis terra. Quod ibi dixit, Cánticum novum; hoc Dóminus dixit, Mandátum novum. Quid enim habet cánticum novum, nisi amórem novum? Cantare amantis est. Vox hujus cantoris, fervor est sancti amóris. Amémus, gratis amémus: D(3minum enim amámus, quo nihil mélius invenimus: ipsum amémus propter ipsum, et nos in ipso, tamen propter ipsum.

exlibinlucpropefinem.en: From Book 8 on Luke, near the end
exlibinlucpropefinem.la: Ex Lib. 8 in Luc., prope finem

queautemturbanisiimperiteconfusiomultitu.en: But what is the crowd, but the confusion of the unskilled multitude, which cannot see the summit of wisdom? Therefore Zacheus, as long as he is in the crowd, seeth not Christ: he climbeth above the crowd, and seeth: that is, having now passed beyond the ignorance of the people, he merited to behold him whom he desired. And beautifully he added: Because the Lord was to pass that way: either where the sycamore was, or where he was that should believe; that he might both keep the mystery and sow grace. For he had so come, that through the Jews he might pass to the Gentiles.
queautemturbanisiimperiteconfusiomultitu.la: Quæ autem turba, nisi imperitæ confúsio multitúdinis, quæ vérticem nequit vidére sapiéntiæ? Ergo Zachǽus quámdiu in turba est, non videt Christum: supra turbam ascéndit, et vidit: hoc est, plebis jam transgressus inscítiam, méruit quem desiderabat, aspicere. Pulchre autem addidit: Quia illa parte erat transiturus Dóminus: vel ubi sycomorus, vel ubi creditúrus: ut et mystérium serváret, et grátiam seminaret Sic enim venerat, ut per Judǽos transiret ad Gentes.

vidititaquezacheumsursumiamenimsublimita.en: He saw therefore Zacheus above. For already, by the loftiness of his faith, he stood out among the fruits of new works, as by the height of a fruitful tree. And since we have turned from the figure to morals, it delighteth us, among so many delights of the believers, to relax the mind on the Lord's day, and to mingle festivity. Zacheus in the sycamore, namely the new fruit of a new time, that in this also might be fulfilled that saying: The fig tree hath put forth her green figs.
vidititaquezacheumsursumiamenimsublimita.la: Vidit ítaque Zachǽum sursum. Jam enim sublimitáte fídei inter fructus novarum óperum, velut fœcúndæ altitúdine árboris eminebat Et quóniam de typo ad moralia defleximus, inter tot credéntium voluptates Domínica die relaxare ánimum, festivitátem admiscere deléctat. Zachǽus in sycomoro, novum vidélicet novi témporis pomum, ut in hoc quoque compleretur illud: Arbor fici prodúxit grossos suos.

adhocenimchristusadvenitutexlignisnonpom.en: For to this end Christ came, that from trees not fruits but men might be born. We read elsewhere: When thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee. Nathanael, therefore, under the tree, that is, upon the root, because he was just. For the root is holy. Yet Nathanael was under the tree, because he was under the law: Zacheus above the tree, because above the law. The one was the hidden defender of the Lord, the other his public preacher. The one was still seeking Christ from the law: the other, now above the law, was leaving his own things, and following the Lord.
adhocenimchristusadvenitutexlignisnonpom.la: Ad hoc enim Christus advenit, ut ex lignis non poma, sed hómines nascerentur. Legimus álibi: Cum esses sub árbore fici, vidi te. Ergo Nathánæl sub árbore, hoc est, supra radícem, quia justus. Radix enim sancta. Sub árbore tamen Nathanæl, quia sub lege: Zachǽus supra árborem, quia supra legem. Ille Dómini occúltus defensor, hic públicus prædicator. Ille adhuc Christum ex lege quærebat: iste jam supra legem relinquebat sua, et Ddminum sequebatur.

attenditeinpsalmodedicationisquemmodocan.en: Give heed, in the psalm of the dedication which we have just sung, to the building out of the ruin. Thou hast cut my sackcloth: this pertaineth to the ruin. What then to the building? And hast compassed me with gladness. The voice of the dedication: To the end that my glory may sing to thee, and I may not be pierced. Who is it that speaketh? Know him in his words. If I expound, it is obscure. Therefore I will say his words, and straightway ye know him that speaketh, that ye may love him that speaketh to you. Who is it that could say: Thou hast brought forth, O Lord, my soul from hell?
attenditeinpsalmodedicationisquemmodocan.la: Atténdite in psalmo dedicationis, quem modo cantavimus, ex ruína ædificiorum. Conscidísti saccum meum: hoc pértinet ad ruinam. Quid ergo ad ædificium? Et accinxisti me lætítia. Vox dedicationis: Ut cantet tibi glória mea, et non compúngar. Quis est, qui lóquitur? In verbis ejus agnoscite. Si expono, obscúrum est. Ergo verba ejus dicam, contínuo agnoscitis loquéntem, ut ametis alloquentem. Quis est, qui dícere pótuit: Eruísti Dómine ab inferis ánimam meam?

cuiusanimaiamabinferiserutestnisidequadi.en: Whose soul hath now been brought forth from hell, but his of whom it is said in another place: Thou wilt not leave my soul in hell? A dedication is set forth, and a deliverance is sung; the canticle of the dedication of the house, and it is said: I will extol thee, O Lord, for thou hast upheld me: and hast not made my enemies to rejoice over me. Give heed to the Jews, his enemies, who thought that they had slain Christ, had conquered him as an enemy, had destroyed him as a man like the rest and mortal.
cuiusanimaiamabinferiserutestnisidequadi.la: Cujus ánima jam ab inferis eruta est, nisi de qua dictum est álio loco: Non derelínques ánimam meam in inférno? Proponitur dedicatio, et cantatur liberátio, cánticum dedicationis domus, et dícitur: Exaltábo te Dómine, quóniam suscepísti me: et non jucundasti inimícos meos super me. Atténdite Judǽos inimícos, qui se putabant occidisse Christum, vicisse tamquam inimícum, perdidisse quasi hóminem céteris similem atque mortalem.

resurrexittertiadieeteiusvoxestexaltabot.en: He rose again the third day, and his is the voice: I will extol thee, O Lord, for thou hast upheld me. Give heed to the Apostle saying: For which cause God also hath exalted him. And hast not made my enemies to rejoice over me. They indeed rejoiced in the death of Christ; but at his resurrection, ascension, and preaching some were pricked to the heart. In his preaching therefore, and through the fame of the constancy of the Apostles, some were pricked and converted; some were hardened and confounded; yet none rejoiced.
resurrexittertiadieeteiusvoxestexaltabot.la: Resurréxit tértia die, et ejus vox est: Exaltábo te Dómine, quóniam suscepísti me. Atténdite Apóstolum dicéntem: Propter quod eum exaltávit. Et non jucundasti inimícos meos super me. Ipsi quidem in Christi morte jucundabantur, sed in ejus resurrectióne, ascensione, prædicatióne aliqui compungebantur, In ejus ergo prædicatióne, et per Apostolórum constantiæ diffamatiónem aliqui compungebantur, et convertebantur: aliqui obdurabantur, et confundebantur, nulli tamen jucundabantur.

libinmoraliumcappostmedium.en: Book 27 of the Morals, ch. 27, after the middle
libinmoraliumcappostmedium.la: Lib. 27 in Moralium, cap. 27 post medium

pusillusitaquezacheussycomorumsubiitetdo.en: Little Zacheus therefore climbed into the sycamore, and saw the Lord: because they who humbly choose the foolishness of the world, themselves contemplate the wisdom of God with keen insight. For the crowd hindereth our littleness from seeing the Lord: because the tumult of worldly cares presseth upon the weakness of the human mind, that it may not look upon the light of truth. But we wisely climb the sycamore, if with foresight we hold in mind that foolishness which is commanded by God. For what is more foolish in this world than not to seek what is lost, to yield up our possessions to them that seize them, to return no injury for injuries received, nay rather, when others are added, to show patience?
pusillusitaquezacheussycomorumsubiitetdo.la: Pusíllus ítaque Zachǽus sycomorum súbiit, et Dóminum vidit: quia qui mundi stultítiam humíliter eligunt, ipsi Dei sapiéntiam subtíliter contemplantur. Pusillitatem namque nostram ad vidéndum Dóminum turba præpedit: quia infirmitátem humánæ mentis, ne lucem veritátis intendat, curarum sæculárium tumúltus premit. Sed prudénter sycomorum ascendimus, si provide eam quæ divínitus præcipitur, stultítiam mente tenemus. Quid enim in hoc mundo stúltius quam amíssa non quærére, possessa rapientibus relaxare, nullam pro accéptis injúriis injúriam reddere, imo adjúnctis áliis patientiam præbere?

modoquandoimplenturecclesieputamusiucund.en: Now, when the churches are filled, think we that the Jews rejoice? Churches are built, dedicated, filled: how do they rejoice? Not only do they not rejoice, but they are even confounded, and the voice of him that exulteth is fulfilled: I will extol thee, O Lord, for thou hast upheld me: and hast not made my enemies to rejoice over me. Thou hast not made them rejoice over me: if they believe in me, thou wilt make them rejoice in me. That we may not say much, let us at length come to those things which we have sung. How doth Christ say: Thou hast cut my sackcloth, and hast compassed me with gladness? His sackcloth was the likeness of sinful flesh.
modoquandoimplenturecclesieputamusiucund.la: Modo, quando implentur ecclésiæ, putamus jucundari Judǽos? Ecclésiæ ædificantur, dedicantur, implentur: quómodo illi jucundantur? Non solum non jucundantur, sed étiam confundúntur, et implétur vox exsultantis: Exaltábo te Dómine, quóniam suscepísti me: et non jucundasti inimícos meos super me. Non jucundasti super me: si mihi credant, jucundabis in me. Ne multa dicamus, ad illa, quæ cantavimus, aliquándo veniamus. Quómodo dicit Christus: Conscidísti saccum meum, et accinxisti me lætítia? Saccus ejus erat similitúdo carnis peccáti.

nontibivilescatquodaitsaccummeumibierati.en: Let it not seem vile to thee that he saith, My sackcloth: therein was enclosed thy price. Thou hast cut my sackcloth. We have escaped through that sackcloth. Thou hast cut my sackcloth. In the passion it was cut. How then is it said to God the Father: Thou hast cut my sackcloth? Wilt thou hear how it is said to the Father: Thou hast cut my sackcloth? Because he spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all. For he did it by means of the Jews, who knew it not, that they who knew might be redeemed, and they who denied might be confounded. For they know not what good they have wrought for us by their evil. The sackcloth was hung up, and the wicked one as it were rejoiced. The persecutor cut the sackcloth with the lance, and the Redeemer poured forth our price.
nontibivilescatquodaitsaccummeumibierati.la: Non tibi vilescat, quod ait, Saccum meum: ibi erat inclúsum prétium tuum. Conscidísti saccum meum. Evasimus ad saccum istum. Conscidísti saccum meum. In passióne conscissus est. Quómodo ergo Deo Patri dícitur: Conscidísti saccum meum? Quómodo Patri dicatur, vis audíre: Conscidísti saccum meum? Quia próprio Fílio non pepércit, sed pro nobis ómnibus trádidit illum. Fecit enim per Judǽos nescientes, unde redimerentur sciéntes, et confunderentur negantes. Nesciunt enim quid boni nobis operati sunt malo suo. Suspensus est saccus, et quasi lætátus est ímpius. Conscidit saccum láncea persecútor, et fudit prétium nostrum Redémptor.

cantetchristusredemptorgematiudasvendito.en: Let Christ the Redeemer sing, let Judas the seller groan, let the Jew the buyer blush. Behold, Judas sold, the Jew bought; they did an evil business; both are condemned; seller and buyer have destroyed themselves. Let therefore our Head speak, let him speak for the body slain, for the body dedicated. Let him speak, let us hear: Thou hast cut my sackcloth, and hast compassed me with gladness: that is, thou hast cut my mortality, and hast compassed me with immortality and incorruption. To the end that my glory may sing to thee, and I may not be pierced. What is: I may not be pierced? Let the persecutor no more bear the lance against me, that I may not be pierced. For Christ, rising again from the dead, dieth now no more; death shall no more have dominion over him.
cantetchristusredemptorgematiudasvendito.la: Cantet Christus Redémptor, gemat Judas venditor, erubescat Judæus emptor. Ecce Judas véndidit, Judæus emit, malum negotium egérunt, ambo damnáti sunt, seípsos perdiderunt venditor et emptor. Dicat ergo caput nostrum, dicat pro córpore occiso, pro córpore dedicato. Dicat, audiamus: Conscidísti saccum meum, et accinxisti me lætítia: id est, conscidísti mortalitatem meam, et accinxisti me immortalitate et incorruptióne. Ut cantet tibi glória mea, et non compúngar. Quid est, Non compúngar? Jam contra me non ferat lanceam persecútor, Ut non compúngar. Christus enim surgens a mórtuis, jam non móritur, et mors illi ultra non dominábitur.

homiliavenerabilisbedepresbyteri.en: Homily by the Venerable Bede, Priest.

queimpossibiliasuntapudhominespossibilia.en: The things that are impossible with men are possible with God. For behold, the camel, laying down the burden of his hump, passeth through the eye of the needle; that is, the rich man and publican, leaving the load of riches and despising the wealth gotten by fraud, goeth up by the narrow gate and the strait way that leadeth to life. Who with wonderful devotion of faith, to see the Saviour, made up by climbing a tree what he lacked by nature: and therefore justly, though he himself dared not ask it, he received the blessing he desired, of receiving the Lord as his guest.
queimpossibiliasuntapudhominespossibilia.la: Quæ impossibilia sunt apud hómines, possibilia sunt apud Deum. Ecce enim camélus, deposita gibbi sárcina, per forámen acus transit, hoc est, dives et publicanus, relícto ónere divitiárum, contempto censu fraudum, angústam portam, arctamque viam, quæ ad vitam ducit, ascéndit. Qui mira devotióne fídei ad vidéndum Salvatórem, quod natúra minus habúerat, ascensu supplet árboris: atque ídeo juste, quamvis ipse rogare non aúdeat, benedictiónem Domínicæ susceptionis, quam desiderabat, accépit.

mysticeautemzacheusquiinterpretaturiusti.en: Mystically, Zacheus, which is interpreted justified, signifieth the people believing from among the Gentiles; who, the more he was occupied with worldly cares, the lower he had been brought by crimes that weighed him down. But he was washed, he was sanctified, he was justified in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, and in the Spirit of our God. He sought to see the Saviour entering Jericho, but could not for the crowd: because he longed to share in the grace of faith which the Saviour brought to the world; but the ingrown habit of vices had hindered him from attaining his desire.
mysticeautemzacheusquiinterpretaturiusti.la: Mystice autem Zachǽus, qui interpretátur justificatus, credentem ex Géntibus pópulum significat. Qui quanto curis sæculáribus occupatior, tanto flagítiis deprimentibus erat factus humilior. Sed ablútus est, sed sanctificátus, sed justificatus in nómine Dómini nostri Jesu Christi, et in spíritu Dei nostri. Qui intrántem Jericho Salvatórem vidére quærebat, sed præ turba non póterat: quia grátiæ fídei, quam mundo Salvátor áttulit, participare cupiebat: sed inolita vitiórum consuetúdo, ne ad votum perveniret, obstiterat.

eademnamqueturbanoxieconsuetudinisquesup.en: For the same crowd of hurtful habit, which rebuked the blind man crying out lest he should ask for light, hindereth also the publican looking up, lest he see Jesus. But as the blind man overcame the voices of the crowds by crying out more and more, so the little man must needs surmount the obstacle of the hurtful crowd by seeking higher things, must leave earthly things, and climb the tree of the cross. For the sycamore (which is a tree like the mulberry in its leaves, but surpassing it in height, whence also it is called by the Latins the lofty one) is called the foolish fig. And the same cross of the Lord, which nourisheth believers as a fig, is mocked by unbelievers as foolish.
eademnamqueturbanoxieconsuetudinisquesup.la: Eádem namque turba noxiæ consuetúdinis, quæ supra cæcum clamántem, ne lumen peteret, increpabat; étiam suspicientem publicanum, ne Jesum vídeat, tardat. Sed sicut cæcus turbarum voces magis ac magis clamando devícit: ita pusíllus necésse est turbæ nocentis obstaculum altióra petendo transcendat, terréna relinquat, árborem crucis ascendat. Sycomorus namque (quæ est arbor fóliis moro símilis, sed altitúdine præstans, unde et a Latinis celsa nuncupátur), ficus fatua dícitur. Et eádem domínica crux, quæ credéntes alit ut ficus, ab incredulis irridetur ut fatua.

ergodumnovamconstructionemsanctehuiusecc.en: While therefore we gladly behold the new building of this holy church, which we dedicate this day to the divine name, we find that there is owed by us both the greatest praise to our God, and to your holiness a discourse befitting the building of the divine house. And our discourse will then be fitting, if it have in itself somewhat of edification which may profit to the good of your souls, God building you up within. What we see done here bodily in the walls, let it be done spiritually in your minds: and what we behold finished here in stones and timbers, let it, the grace of God building, be perfected in your bodies.
ergodumnovamconstructionemsanctehuiusecc.la: Ergo, dum novam constructionem sanctæ hujus ecclésiæ libénter attendimus, quam divíno nómini hódie dedicamus, invenimus a nobis deberi et Deo nostro máximam laudem, et sanctitati vestræ congruum de divínæ domus ædificatione sermónem. Tunc autem sermo noster congruus erit, si in se áliquid ædificationis hábeat, quod utilitati animárum vestrarum, Deo vos interius ædíficánte, proficiat. Quod hic factum corporaliter videmus in parietibus, spiritaliter fiat in mentibus: et quod hic perféctum cernimus in lapídibus et lignis, hoc ædíficánte grátia Dei, perficiatur in corpóribus vestris.

principaliterergogratiasagamusdominodeon.en: First of all, therefore, let us give thanks to the Lord our God, from whom is every best gift, and every perfect gift; and let us praise his goodness with all the eagerness of our heart, for that, to build this house of prayer, he visited the mind of his faithful, stirred up their affection, supplied help, inspired them that were not yet willing to will it, and helped the endeavours of their good will to do it: and thereby God, who worketh in his own both to will and to accomplish according to his good will, himself began all these things, himself perfected them.
principaliterergogratiasagamusdominodeon.la: Principaliter ergo grátias agamus Dómino Deo nostro, a quo est omne datum optimum, et omne donum perféctum; et ejus bonitátem tota cordis alacritate laudémus, quóniam ad construendam istam domum oratiónis, fidélium suórum visitávit ánimum, excitávit afféctum, surrogavit auxílium, inspiravit necdum volentibus ut vellent, adjúvit bonæ voluntátis conátus ut fácerent: ac per hoc Deus, qui operátur in suis et velle et perfícere pro bona voluntáte, hæc ómnia ipse coépit, ipse perfécit.

etquiaoperabonainconspectusuonumquamesse.en: And because he never suffereth good works to be vain in his sight, he will give to his faithful, to whom while they wrought he granted the favour of his power, a worthy reward for so great a work. Still further thanks are to be given to our God. For this church, which he caused to be built to his name, he hath caused also to be honoured the more with the relics of the holy Martyrs.
etquiaoperabonainconspectusuonumquamesse.la: Et quia ópera bona in conspéctu suo numquam esse permittit inánia, fidélibus suis, quibus operántibus præbuit virtútis suæ favórem, tríbuet condignam pro tanta operatióne mercédem. Adhuc ámplius agendæ sunt grátiæ Deo nostro. Hanc enim ecclésiam, quam fecit nómini suo construi, fecit étiam sanctórum Mártyrum relíquiis ámplius honorari.

etcumvenissetadlocumsuspiciensiesusvidit.en: And when he was come to the place, Jesus looking up saw him. The Saviour, walking through Jericho, came to the place where Zacheus, running before, had climbed up into the sycamore: because, having sent through the world the heralds of his word, in whom he himself in truth both spoke and went, he came to the people of the nations, who, being already lifted up by faith in his passion, burned also to be made blessed by the known face of his Godhead. Looking up he saw him, because he chose him, lifted up by the grace of faith from earthly desires, and standing out above the unbelieving crowds. For with God to see is to choose or to love. Whence is that saying: The eyes of the Lord are upon the just. For we also see the things we love; from those which we abhor we hasten to turn away our gaze.
etcumvenissetadlocumsuspiciensiesusvidit.la: Et cum venísset ad locum, suspiciens Jesus vidit illum. Perambulans Jericho Salvátor, venit ad locum, ubi præcúrrens Zachǽus sycomorum conscenderat: quia missis per mundum sui verbi præconibus, in quibus ipse nimírum et loquebátur et ibat, venit ad pópulum natiónum, qui passiónis ejus fide jam sublimis exsistens, étiam divinitátis ejus ardébat agnita fácie beari. Suspiciens vidit illum, quia per grátiam fídei a terrenis cupiditatibus elevátum, turbisque infidélibus præeminentem elégit. Vidére enim Dei, elígere vel amáre est. Unde est illud: Óculi Dómini super justos. Nam et nos quæ amámus, vidére; ab his, quæ exsecramur, intúitum festinamus avértere.

viditergoiesusvidentemsequielegiteligent.en: Jesus therefore saw him that saw him, because he chose him that chose him, and loved him that loved him. This order of advancing, to wit, of coming through faith in the Lord's Incarnation to the knowledge of his Godhead, as it were of beholding the face of Jesus through the sycamore, the excellent Doctor showeth, when he saith: For I judged not myself to know anything among you, but Jesus Christ, and him crucified. And likewise reproaching others: You are become, saith he, such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat; calling milk the weak things of the temporal dispensation, strong meat the high things of the eternal majesty.
viditergoiesusvidentemsequielegiteligent.la: Vidit ergo Jesus videntem se, quia elégit eligentem se, et amávit amántem. Hunc sane órdinem proficiendi, hoc est, per fidem domínicæ Incarnationis ad cognitionem divinitátis perveniendi, quasi per sycomorumJesu fáciem speculandi Doctor egrégius osténdit. cum ait: Non enim judicavi scire me áliquid inter vos, nisi Christum Jesum, et hunc crucifíxum. Itémque áliis exprobrans: Facti estis, inquit, quibus lacte opus sit, non solido cibo. Lac infirma temporariæ dispensatiónis, solidum cibum árdua perpetuæ majestátis appellans.

etdixitadeumzacheefestinansdescendequiah.en: And he said to him: Zacheus, make haste and come down; for this day I must abide in thy house. And he made haste and came down, and received him with joy. The Lord abode once in the house of the prince of the pharisees, that is, he taught in the synagogue of the Jews: but because with venomous tongue they carped at him for not being washed before dinner, for healing on the sabbath, for receiving publicans and sinners, for disputing against avarice, and for doing the other things worthy of God; wearied with their crimes, he departed and fled away, saying: Your house shall be left to you desolate. But this day he must abide in the house of little Zacheus; that is, the grace of the new light shining forth, he must rest in the humble heart of the believing nations.
etdixitadeumzacheefestinansdescendequiah.la: Et dixit ad eum: Zachǽe, festinans descénde, quia hódie in domo tua opórtet me manére. Et festinans descéndit, et excépit illum gaudens. Manébat aliquándo Dóminus in domo príncipis pharisæorum, hoc est, in Judæórum synagóga docebat: sed quia non baptizátum ante prandium, sábbato curantem, publicanos et peccatóres recipientem, contra avarítiam disputantem, et cétera digna Deo gerentem, lingua venenata carpebant: pertæsus eórum facinora, discéssit et aufugit, dicens: Relinquetur vobis domus vestra desérta. Hódie autem in domo pusilli Zachæi opórtet illum manére: hoc est, novæ lucis grátia coruscante, in húmili credéntium natiónum corde quiéscere.

communisomniumdomusestecclesiainquamvobi.en: The Church is the common house of all, into which, you having entered first, we enter, keeping the form of the disciples: and therefore, as soon as we have entered, we offer peace to all in common, that we may follow the law given to them. Let none therefore be torpid with sloth: let none have his mind hanging upon worldly things, when the priests have now entered to preach. For no small punishment hangeth over this thing. Truly I would a thousand times rather, having entered the house of any one of you, be repulsed, than, preaching here, not be heard. This would be more grievous to me than that, since indeed this house is more my own than that.
communisomniumdomusestecclesiainquamvobi.la: Commúnis ómnium domus est Ecclésia, in quam, vobis prius ingressis, nos intramus, discipulórum formam retinentes: ideóque commúniter ómnibus statim atque ingressi fuerimus, ut illis datam legem sequámur, pacem offerimus. Nemo ígitur socórdia torpeat: nemo sæculáribus rebus suspénsum ánimum hábeat, cum jam ad prædicándum sacerdótes intraverint Non enim parva huic rei imminet pœna. Equidem millies pótius malim in domum alicújus vestrum ingréssus destitui, quam hic prǽdicans non audiri. Hoc mihi molestius esset, quam illud, quando quidem magis própria hæc est, quam illa.

namhicmagneillenostreopespositesunthicsp.en: For here those great riches of ours are laid up, here all our hope. For what in this place is not great and wonderful? For this table is far more precious and more pleasant; and this lamp than that, as they know who, anointed with oil in faith, have been freed from sicknesses. This chest also is much better, and more necessary. For it containeth not garments, but mercy shut up within: although they be few that possess it. Here also is a couch far more excellent than that: for the rest of the divine Scriptures is sweeter than any bed.
namhicmagneillenostreopespositesunthicsp.la: Nam hic magnæ illæ nostræ opes pósitæ sunt, hic spes nostra omnis. Quid enim hoc loco non magnum est et admirándum? Nam hæc mensa longe pretiosior est atque jucúndior: et lucérna hæc, quam illa, ut norunt qui cum fide óleo perúncti, a morbis liberáti sunt. Arca étiam hæc multo mélior, magísque necessaria. Non enim vestes, sed misericórdiam inclúsam cóntinet: quamvis pauci sint, qui eam possideant. Hic et lectulus est valde illo præstantior: divinárum enim Scripturárum réquies quovis lecto suavior est.

etquidemsiconcordiaperfecteservareturano.en: And indeed, if concord were perfectly kept by us, we should have no other house besides this. And that what I have said is not hard, those three thousand and five thousand men bear witness, who had one house, and one table, and one soul. For the multitude of believers, he saith, had but one heart and one soul. But because we are far from their virtue, and are divided by our houses, at least when we come together here, let us do this with all zeal. For although in other things we be poor and needy, in this place at least, when we come in here to you, receive us with charity: and when I say, Peace be to you, answer, And with thy spirit, not with the voice only, but with the mind also.
etquidemsiconcordiaperfecteservareturano.la: Et quidem si concórdia perfecte servarétur a nobis, nullam áliam domum præter hanc haberemus. Hoc autem quod dixi, non esse durum, testantur illa tria míllia, et quinque míllia hóminum, quibus et domus una, et mensa una, et ánima una erat. Multitúdinis enim credéntium, inquit, unum erat cor, et ánima una. Sed quia longe ab illórum virtúte absumus, et per domos disjúncti sumus, saltem quando huc convenimus, id omni stúdio faciámus. Nam etsi in áliis rebus páuperes, et ínopes sumus, hoc loco saltem, cum huc ad vos intramus, cum caritáte nos suscipite: cumque, Pax vobis, dico: Et cum spíritu tuo, non voce solum, sed ánimo quoque respondete.

etcumviderentomnesmurmurabantdicentesquo.en: And when all saw it, they murmured, saying, that he was gone to be a guest with a man that was a sinner. It is manifest that the Jews ever hated the salvation of the Gentiles. For it is written: But the next sabbath day, the whole city almost came together to hear the word of God. And the Jews seeing the multitudes, were filled with envy, and contradicted those things which were said by Paul. And elsewhere the faithful brethren also disputed against the prince of the Apostles, saying: Why didst thou go in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them?
etcumviderentomnesmurmurabantdicentesquo.la: Et cum vidérent omnes, murmurabant, dicéntes, quod ad hóminem peccatórem divertisset. Maniféstum est, Judǽos semper Géntium odisse salútem. Scriptum est enim: Sequénti vero sábbato pene univérsa cívitas convénit audíre verbum Dei. Vidéntes autem turbas Judǽi repléti sunt zelo, et contradicebant iis, quæ a Paulo dicebántur. Et álibi, fidéles étiam fratres advérsus Apostolórum príncipem disceptabant, dicéntes: Quare introisti ad viros præpútium habéntes, et manducasti cum illis?

stansautemzacheusdixitaddominumeccedimid.en: But Zacheus standing, said to the Lord: Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have wronged any man of any thing, I restore him fourfold. While others calumniated him as a sinner, Zacheus himself standing, that is, persisting in the truth of the faith which he had begun, proveth that he was not only converted from being a sinner, but also had his conversation among the perfect. For the Lord saying: If thou wilt be perfect, go, sell all that thou hast, and give to the poor; whosoever lived innocently before his conversion may, being converted, give all to the poor.
stansautemzacheusdixitaddominumeccedimid.la: Stans autem Zachæus, dixit ad Dóminum: Ecce dimidium bonórum meórum Dómine do paupéribus: et si quid áliquem defraudavi, reddo quadruplum. Áliis calumniántibus hóminem peccatórem, ipse Zachǽus stans, id est, in ea quam coéperat fídei veritáte persistens, non solum se ex peccatore conversum, sed étiam inter perfectos probat esse conversatum. Dicénte enim Dómino: Si vis perféctus esse, vade, vende ómnia quæ habes, et da paupéribus: quisquis ante convérsiónem innocenter vixit, ómnia convérsus potest dare paupéribus.

atquialiquafraudesustulitprimoheciuxtale.en: But he that hath taken anything by fraud ought first to restore it according to the law, then to give what remaineth to him to the poor. And so he also, because he keepeth nothing for himself, hath dispersed all his goods, hath given to the poor; his justice remaineth for ever and ever. And this is that wise foolishness which the publican had gathered from the sycamore as the fruit of life: to wit, to restore what was seized, to leave one's own, to despise the visible, to desire even to die for the invisible, to deny oneself, and to long to follow the footsteps of the Lord who is not yet seen.
atquialiquafraudesustulitprimoheciuxtale.la: At qui áliqua fraude sústulit, primo hæc juxta legem reddere, deínde quod sibi remanserit, debet dare paupéribus. Ac sic et ipse, quia sibi nil retinet, ómnia sua dispergit, dat paupéribus, justítia ejus manet in sǽculum sǽculi. Et hæc est sápiens illa stultitia quam de sycomoro publicanus quasi fructum vitæ legerat: rapta vidélicet reddere, própria relínquere, visibilia contemnere, pro invisibilibus étiam mori desideráre, seípsum abnegare, et ejus, qui necdum videátur, Dómini vestígia sequi concupíscere.

exepistolaprimasanctifelicispapequarti.en: From the first Epistle of St. Felix the Fourth, Pope.
exepistolaprimasanctifelicispapequarti.la: Ex Epístola prima sancti Felícis Papæ quarti.

tabernaculummoysendominoprecipientefecis.en: We read that Moses, at the Lord's command, made and hallowed the tabernacle, with its table and altar, and the other vessels and utensils for fulfilling the divine worship: and we know that he not only hallowed them with divine prayers, but also, at the Lord's bidding, anointed them with the unction of holy oil. And in what manner these things were done, and how none other than the priests, anointed with the holy unction and consecrated to the Lord with holy vestments, and the Levites, handled these sacred things, carried them, set them up and took them down, is found in the law of the Lord, in those very institutions which at the Lord's command were written by Moses.
tabernaculummoysendominoprecipientefecis.la: Tabernáculum Móysen, Dómino præcipiente, fecísse et sacrasse, cum mensa et altári ejus, et céteris vasis et utensilibus ad divínum cultum explendum, legimus: et non solum divínis précibus ea sacrasse, sed étiam sancti ólei unctióne, Dómino jubente, perlinisse novimus. Qualiter autem hæc facta sint, et quómodo ipsa sacra non álii, quam sacerdótes sacra unctióne delibuti, Dominoque cum véstibus sanctis sacrati, et Levitæ tractabant, ferebant, erigebant et deponebant: in ipsis institutionibus, quæ jubente Dómino conscriptæ sunt per Móysen, in lege Dómini reperitur.

qualiterergodavidregumpiissimusamplifica.en: In what manner therefore David, the most pious of kings, enlarged the worship of God, and would have built a temple to the Lord, but was forbidden because of the much blood which he had shed, and himself had gathered the expenses; and how Solomon also, his son, by the command and with the help of God, accomplished that very thing which he had desired to do, and consecrated the temple with the altar and the rest for performing the divine worship: is read in the book of Kings. Solomon therefore made at that time a solemn feast, and all Israel with him, a great multitude, from the entrance of Emath to the river of Egypt, before the Lord our God seven days and seven days, that is, fourteen days, and on the eighth day he sent away the people.
qualiterergodavidregumpiissimusamplifica.la: Qualiter ergo David, regum piíssimus, amplificaverit cultum Dei, et templumDomino ædificare volúerit, sed propter multum sánguinem quem effuderat, prohibitus est, et ipse collegerat expensas: Salomon quoque, fílius ejus idípsum, quod ipse fácere optaverat, jubente et auxiliante Deo perfécit, et templum cum altári, et réliqua ad divínum cultum peragéndum consecrávit: in libro Regum légitur.
