Fecit ergo Salomon in témpore illo festivitátem celebrem, et omnis Israël cum eo, multitúdo magna ab introitu Emath usque ad rivum Ægýpti, coram Dómino Deo nostro septem diébus, et septem diébus, id est, quatuórdecim diébus, et in die octáva dimísit pópulos.

solemnitatesdedicationumecclesiarumetsac.en: The solemnities of the dedications of churches and of priests are to be solemnly celebrated every year, the Lord himself giving the example, who came to the feast of the dedication of the temple, to celebrate the same festival with the rest of the people, giving to all the pattern of doing so; as it is written: And it was the feast of the dedication at Jerusalem: and it was winter. And Jesus walked in the temple, in Solomon's porch. And that the dedication is to be celebrated for eight days, ye will find in the book of Kings, when the dedication of the temple was ended.
solemnitatesdedicationumecclesiarumetsac.la: Solemnitates dedicationum ecclesiárum et sacerdótum, per síngulos annos solémniter sunt celebrandæ, ipso Dómino exémplum dante, qui ad festum dedicationis templi, ómnibus id faciéndi dans formam, cum réliquis pópulis eámdem festivitátem celebratúrus venit, sicut scriptum est: Facta sunt encænia in Jerosólymis, et hiems erat, et ambulabat Jesus in templo in pórticu Salomonis. Quod autem octo diébus encænia sint celebranda, in libro Regum, perácta dedicatione templi, reperietis.

inhomiliaryhiemdetempdomipostepiph.en: In the Winter Homilies, on the Season, the First Sunday after the Epiphany
inhomiliaryhiemdetempdomipostepiph.la: In Homiliary Hiem de Temp. dom. I post Epiph.

materiesuinquitevangelistaconservabatomn.en: His mother, saith the Evangelist, kept all these words in her heart. Let us also, my brethren, imitate the loving Mother of the Lord, by keeping ourselves also all the words and deeds of our Lord and Saviour fixed in our heart. By meditation day and night on these words and deeds of the Lord let us drive back the troublesome assaults of vain and hurtful thoughts: by frequent converse upon them let us take care both to restrain ourselves and our neighbours from idle fables and from the ill-sweetened talk of detraction, and to come to the frequent praise of God. Let us learn therefore the chastity of the holy Virgin in all things, who, no less modest in mouth than in body, kept the arguments of faith in her heart.
materiesuinquitevangelistaconservabatomn.la: Mater Jesu, inquit Evangelísta, conservábat ómnia verba hæc in corde suo. Imitémur et nos, fratres mei, piam Dómini Matrem, ipsi quoque ómnia verba et facta Dómini ac Salvatóris nostri fixo in corde conservándo. Horum Dómini verbórum et actórum meditatióne diúrna et noctúrna importúnos inánium nocentiúmque cogitatiónum repellámus incúrsus: horum crebra collatióne et nos et próximos nostros a fábulis supervácuis et male dulcorátis detractiónum collóquiis castigáre, atque ad divínæ frequéntiam laudis accédere curémus. Discámus ergo sanctæ Vírginis in ómnibus castitátem, quæ non minus ore pudíca, quam córpore, arguménta fidei conservábat in corde.

delaudibusvirgmatrishomiln.en: On the praises of the Virgin Mother, Homily 2, n. 3
delaudibusvirgmatrishomiln.la: De laudibus Virg. Matris Homil. 2, n. 3

letarepateradamsedmagistuohevamaterexsul.en: Rejoice, O father Adam, but more do thou, O mother Eve, exult; both, I say, be comforted over your daughter, and such a daughter. For the time is at hand when the reproach shall be taken away, and the man shall have no cause against the woman: who indeed, while he was imprudently trying to excuse himself, hesitated not cruelly to accuse her, saying: The woman, whom thou gavest me, gave me of the tree, and I did eat. Wherefore run, O Eve, to Mary; run, O mother, to thy daughter; let the daughter answer for the mother; let her make satisfaction for the mother: for behold, if the man fell through a woman, now he is not raised up save through a woman.
letarepateradamsedmagistuohevamaterexsul.la: Lætáre pater Adam, sed magis tu, o Heva, mater, exsúlta; ambo, inquam consolámini super fília, et tali fília. Instat namque tempus, quam jam tollátur oppróbrium, nec hábeat vir qui causétur advérsus féminam: qui útique, dum se imprudénter exsuráre conarétur, crudéliter illam accusáre non cunctátus est, dicens: Múlier quam dedísti mihi, dedit mihi de ligno, et comédi. Proptérea curre, Heva, ad Maríam; curre, mater, ad fíliam; fília pro matre respóndeat; ipsa pro matre satisfáciat: quia ecce si vir cécedit per féminam, jam non erígitur nisi per féminam.

indormitbmariehomilia.en: On the Falling-asleep of the B. Mary, homily 2

tutelatuaimmortalisestmarietintercessiov.en: Thy protection is immortal, O Mary; and thy intercession is life; and thy patronage perpetual. For unless thou didst go before, none would become spiritual; none would adore God in the Spirit. For then was man made spiritual, when thou, O Mother of God, wast made the dwelling of the Holy Ghost: none is filled with the knowledge of God save through thee, O most holy one. None is saved save through thee, O Mother of God; none is free from dangers save through thee, O Virgin Mother; none is redeemed save through thee, O Mother of God; none hath obtained the gift of mercy save through thee, O thou who wast worthy to contain God. For who so defendeth sinners? But thou, who art mighty with God by a mother's authority, obtainest the excellent grace of forgiveness even for them that sin grievously. For thou canst not but be heard, since God, as to his true and spotless Mother, in all things, and through all things, and in all things, doeth thy will. Hence rightly every afflicted one fleeth to thee; the weak cleaveth to thee; he that is assailed by war setteth thee against his enemies.
tutelatuaimmortalisestmarietintercessiov.la: Tutéla tua immortális est, María; et intercéssio, vita; et protéctio perpétua. Nisi enim, tu præíres, nemo spiritális eváderet; nemo in Spíritu Deum adoráret. Tunc enim spiritális factus est homo, cum tu, Deípara Spíritus Sancti habitáculum effécta es: nemo Dei cognitióne replétus est nisi per te, o sanctíssima. Nemo salvus nisi per te, o Deípara; nemo periculórum expers nisi per te, Virgo parens; nemo redémptus nisi per te Dei Mater; nemo domum per misericórdiam consecútus, nisi per te, o digna, quæ Deum cáperes. Quis enim tantópere peccatóres deféndit? Tu autem, quæ matérna auctoritáte in Deum pólleas, étiam iis qui enórmiter peccant, exímian remissiónis gratiam concílias. Non enim potes non exaudíri, cum Deus, ut veræ ac intemerátæ Matri suæ, quoad ómnia, et per ómnia, et in ómnibus, morem gerat. Hinc mérito, afflíctus quisque ad te cónfugit; infírmus tibi adhaéret; bello petítus te hóstibus oppónit.

quidadmariamaccederetrepidethumanafragil.en: Why should human frailty fear to approach to Mary? There is nothing harsh in her, nothing terrible; she is all sweet. Turn over more diligently the whole course of the Gospel history: and if perchance thou find in Mary anything of rebuke, anything hard, in fine any sign even of slight indignation, hold her henceforth suspect, and fear to approach her. But if thou find, as indeed they are, that all things that pertain to her are rather full of goodness and grace, full of meekness and mercy, give thanks to him who in his most kind compassion hath provided for thee such a mediatrix, in whom there can be nothing to suspect. Lastly, she hath been made all things to all; with most abundant charity she hath made herself a debtor to the wise and to the unwise. To all she openeth the bosom of her mercy, that all may receive of her fulness: the captive redemption, the sick healing, the sorrowful consolation, the sinner pardon, the just grace, the Angel joy. She discusseth not past merits, but showeth herself easy to be entreated by all, most merciful to all; lastly, she compassionateth the necessities of all with a most ample affection.
quidadmariamaccederetrepidethumanafragil.la: Quid ad Maríam accédere trépidet humána fragílitas? Nihil austérum in ea, nihil terríbile; tota suávis est. Revólve diligéntius evangélicæ históriæ sériem univérsam: et si quid forte increpatórium, si quid durum, si quod dénique signum vel ténuis indignatiónis occúrrerit in María, de cétero suspéctam hábeas, et accédere vereáris. Quod si, ut vere sunt, plena magis ómnia pietátis et grátiæ, plena mansuetúdinis et misericórdiæ, quæ ad eam pértinent, invéneris, age grátias ei, qui talem tibi mediatrícem benigníssima miseratione provídit, in qua nihil possit esse suspéctum. Dénique ómnibus ómnia facta est, sapiéntibus et insipiéntibus copiosíssima caritáte debitrícem se fecit. Omnibus misericórdiæ sinum ejus áperit, ut de plenitúdine ejus accípiant univérsi, captívus redemptiónem, æger curatiónem, tristis consolatiónem, peccátor véniam, justus grátiam, Angelus lætítiam. Ipsa prætérita non díscutit mérita, sed ómnibus sese exorábilem, ómnibus clementíssimam præbet, ómnium dénique necessitátes amplíssimo quodam miserátur afféctu.

sitperteexcusabilequodperteingerimusfiat.en: Through thee may that be excused which through thee we bring before him; may that be granted which with faithful mind we ask. Receive what we offer, grant in return what we ask, excuse what we fear, for thou art the only hope of sinners. Through thee we hope for the pardon of our offences, and in thee, most blessed one, is the expectation of our rewards. Holy Mary, succour the wretched; help the faint-hearted; comfort the sorrowful; pray for the people; plead for the clergy; intercede for the devout female sex: let all feel thy help, whosoever celebrate thy holy commemoration.
sitperteexcusabilequodperteingerimusfiat.la: Sit per te excusábile quod per te ingérimus; fiat impetrábile quod fida mente póscimus. Accípe quod offérimus, redóna quod rogámus, excúsa quod timémus, quia tu es spes única peccatórum. Per te sperámus véniam delictórum et in te, beatíssima, nostrórum est expectátio præmiórum. Sancta María, succúrre míseris; juva pusillánimes; réfove flébiles; ora pro pópulo; intérveni pro clero; intercéde pro devóto femíneo sexu: séntiant omnes tuum juvámen, quicúmque célebrant tuam sanctam commemoratiónem.

infestovisitbmvhom.en: On the feast of the Visitation of the B.V.M., Homily 2

magnificatanimameadominumetexultavitspir.en: My soul doth magnify the Lord: and my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. Which words, though they rightly befit all the perfect, yet it most became the blessed Mother of God to utter them, who, singular by the privilege of her merit, burned with spiritual love of him in whose bodily conception she rejoiced. Who rightly could exult with a special joy above the other saints in Jesus, that is, in her Saviour; because him whom she knew to be the everlasting author of salvation, she knew was to be born of her flesh by a temporal birth, so that in one and the same person he was truly both her son and her Lord.
magnificatanimameadominumetexultavitspir.la: Magníficat ánima mea Dóminum; et exultávit spíritus meus in Deo salutári meo. Quæ cum ómnibus perféctis verba recte convéniant, máxime tamen ea beátam Dei Genitrícem proférre decébat, quæ mériti privilégio singuláris spirituáli ipsíus dilectióne flagrábat, cujus corporáli conceptióne gaudébat. Quæ jure in Jesu, id est, in salutári suo speciáli præ céteris sanctis gáudio pótuit exultáre, quia quem perpétuum salútis auctórem nóverat, hunc ipsum temporáli ortu de carne sua nascitúrum esse sciébat quátenus in una eadémque persóna veráciter suus et filius esset et Dóminus.

quamviliadeseipsasenseritedocetetquodomn.en: She teacheth how lowly she thought of herself, and that whatever good of merit she had, she received it by the bounty of heavenly grace, saying: Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid: for behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. For she showeth that in her own judgment she had been a lowly handmaid of Christ, but declareth that by the regard of heavenly grace she was suddenly exalted, and so greatly glorified, that her pre-eminent blessedness is rightly wondered at by the voice of all nations. She added also the gifts of the divine goodness, which she had wondrously received, praising them with worthy thanksgiving: Because he that is mighty hath done great things to me; and holy is his name. She attributeth nothing therefore to her own merits, who referreth all her greatness to the gift of him who, being essentially mighty and great, is wont to make his faithful, from little and weak, strong and great.
quamviliadeseipsasenseritedocetetquodomn.la: Quam vília de seípsa sénserit édocet, et quod omne quidquid boni mériti hábuit, hoc supérna grátia largiénte percéperit, dicens: Quia respéxit humilitátem ancíllæ suæ: ecce enim ex hoc beátam me dicent omnes generatiónes. Húmilem quippe Christi ancíllam suo judício se fuisse demónstrat, sed respéctu se grátiæ celéstis repénte sublimátam pronúntiat, atque in tantum glorificátam, ut sua beatitúdo præcípua mérito cunctárum géntium voce mirétur. Addidit étiam adhuc divínæ pietátis múnera, quæ mirabíliter accépit, digna gratiárum actióne colláudans. Quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est, et sanctum nomen ejus. Nihil ergo suis méritis tríbuit, quæ totam magnitúdinem ad illíus donum refert, qui essentiáliter potens et magnus exístens, fidéles suos de parvis atque infírmis fortes fácere consuévit, et magnos.

beatamariavirgointerhominesaudiresolamer.en: The blessed Virgin Mary alone among men merited to hear before all: Thou hast found grace. How much? As much as he had said: full. And truly full, which should pour itself upon and into the whole creation with a bountiful shower: for thou hast found grace with God. When he saith these things, the Angel himself also marvelleth, either that a woman alone, or that all men had merited life through a woman: the Angel is astonished that the whole God should come within the narrow confines of a virgin's womb, for whom the whole creation together is narrow. Hence it is that the Angel tarrieth, hence it is that he calleth the virgin by her merit, addresseth her by grace, scarcely revealeth the cause to her as she heareth, that he may raise her understanding, and scarcely calmeth her after her long trembling.
beatamariavirgointerhominesaudiresolamer.la: Beáta María Virgo, inter hómines audíre sola méruit præ ómnibus: invenísti grátiam. Quantam? Quantam díxerat: plenam. Et vere plenam, quæ largo imbre totam fúnderet et infúnderet creatúram: invenísti enim grátiam apud Deum. Hæc cum dicit, et ipse Angelus mirátur, aut féminam tantum, aut omnes hómines vitam meruísse per féminam: stupet Angelus, totum Deum veníre intra virginális úteri angústias, cui tota simul angústa est creatúra. Hinc est, quod remorátur Angelus, hinc est, quod vírginem vocat de mérito, de grátia compéllat, vix causam prodit audiénti, sane ut sensum promóveat, vix longa trepidatióne compónit.

cuminsuaestimationetamhumilisessetmarian.en: Though Mary was so lowly in her own esteem, she was nevertheless also great-souled in believing the promise; so that she who reckoned herself nothing else but a little handmaid doubted not in any wise that she was chosen for this incomprehensible mystery, and believed that she would presently be the true Mother of God and man. This truly doth the privilege of divine grace work in the hearts of the elect, that neither doth humility make them faint-hearted, nor greatness of soul arrogant: but rather they work together, so that not only doth no exaltation creep in from greatness of soul, but thence chiefly is humility advanced: that they may be found the more God-fearing, and not ungrateful to the giver of gifts; and in turn, that no faint-heartedness may steal in on the occasion of humility; but the less each one is wont to presume of himself even in the least things, the more may they trust in the divine power even in all great things.
cuminsuaestimationetamhumilisessetmarian.la: Cum in sua æstimatióne tam húmilis esset María, nihilóminus et in promissiónis credulitáte magnánimis, ut quæ nihil áliud quam exíguam sese reputábat ancíllam, ad incomprehensíbile hoc mystérium nullátenus se dubitáret eléctam, et veram Dei et hóminis Genetrícem créderet mox futúram. Agit hoc nimírum in córdibus electórum grátiæ prærogatíva divínæ, ut eos nec humílitas pusillánimes fáciat, nec magnanímitas arrogántes: magis autem cooperéntur sibi, ut non solum nulla ex magnanimitáte subíntret elátio, sed hinc máxime provehátur humílitas: ut inveniántur eo ámplius timoráti, et largitóri múnerum non ingráte, ac vicíssim ex occasióne humilitátis pusillanímitas nulla subrépat; sed quo minus de sua quisque vel in mínimis præsúmere consuévit, eo ámplius étiam in magnis quibúsque de divína virtúte confídant.

obsecrovosfilioliemulaminimansuetudinems.en: I beseech you, my little children, emulate her meekness, if ye love Mary; if ye strive to please her, emulate her modesty. For nothing is so fitting for man, nothing so becoming to a Christian, and nothing so beseemeth above all a monk. And indeed the virtue of humility shineth forth clearly enough in the Virgin from this very meekness. Truly humility and meekness are foster-sisters. For as pride is the mother of presumption, so true meekness proceedeth only from true humility.
obsecrovosfilioliemulaminimansuetudinems.la: Obsecro vos, filíoli, æmulámini mansuetúdinem, si Maríam dilígitis; si conténditis ei placére, æmulámini modéstiam ejus. Nihil enim tam idóneum hómini, nihil tam cóngruum christiáno, maximésque mónachum nihil adeo decet. Et quidem manifésta satis in Vírgine ex hac ipsa manuetúdine virtus humilitátis elúcet. Nimírum collactáneæ sunt humílitas et manuetúdo. Sicut enim mater præsumptiónis elátio, sic manuetúdo vera nonnísi ex vera humilitáte procédit.

cuiservatestvictorianisimarieipsaproculd.en: For whom was the victory reserved, but for Mary? She without doubt crushed the venomous head, who brought to nothing every suggestion of the wicked one, as well from the allurement of the flesh as from the pride of the mind. And what other woman was Solomon seeking, when he said: Who shall find a valiant woman? For the wise man knew the weakness of this sex, its frail body, its slippery mind. Yet because he had read that God had promised, and saw that it was fitting, that he who had conquered through a woman should be conquered through her, he said, greatly marvelling: Who shall find a valiant woman? That is to say: If thus both the salvation of us all, and the restoration of innocence, and the victory over the enemy hang upon the hand of a woman; it is altogether necessary that a valiant one be provided, who may be fit for so great a work.
cuiservatestvictorianisimarieipsaproculd.la: Cui serváta est victória, nisi Maríæ? Ipsa procul dúbio caput contrívit venenátum, quæ omnímodam malígni suggestiónem tam de carnis illécebra, quam de mentis supérbia dedúxit ad níhilum. Quam vero áliam Sálomon requirébat, cum dicébat: Mulíerem fortem quis invéniet? Nóverat quippe vir sápiens hujus sexus infirmitátem, frágile corpus, lúbricam mentem. Quia tamen et Deum légerat promisísse, et ita vidébat congrúere, ut qui vícerat per féminam, vincerétur per ipsam, veheménter admírans ajébat: Mulíerem fortem quis invéniet? Quod est dícere: Si ita de manu féminæ pendet et nostra ómnium salus, et innocéntiæ restitútio, et de hoste victória; fortis omníno necésse est ut provideátur, quæ ad tantum opus possit esse idónea.

totisergomedulliscordiumtotisprecordioru.en: With all the marrow of our hearts therefore, with all the affections of our breasts, and with all our desires, let us venerate this Mary; for such is the will of him who willed that we should have all through Mary. This, I say, is his will, but for our sakes. My little children, she is the sinners' ladder, she is my greatest confidence, she is the whole ground of my hope. For what? Can the Son either repel her, or suffer a repulse? Can the Son not hear, or not be heard? Neither, plainly. Thou hast found, saith the Angel, grace with God. Happily so. She will ever find grace, and it is grace alone that we need; truly it is grace alone whereby we are saved. Why do we desire other things, brethren? Let us seek grace, and let us seek it through Mary, for what she seeketh she findeth, and cannot be disappointed. Let us seek grace, but grace with God: for with men favour is deceitful. Let others seek merit; let us study to find grace. For what? Is it not of grace that we are here? Truly it is of the mercies of the Lord that we are not consumed.
totisergomedulliscordiumtotisprecordioru.la: Totis ergo medúllis córdium, totis præcordiórum afféctibus, et votis ómnibus Maríam hanc venerémur; quia sic est volúntas ejus, qui totum nos habére vóluit per Maríam. Hæc, inquam, volúntas ejus est, sed pro nobis. Filíoli, hæc peccatórum scala, hæc mea máxima fidúcia est, hæc tota rátio spei meæ. Quid enim? Potéstne Fílius aut repéllere, aut sustinére repúlsam? Non audíre, aut non audíri Fílius potest? Neutrum plane. Invenísti, ait Angelus, grátiam apud Deum. Felíciter. Semper hæc invéniet grátiam, et sola est grátia qua egémus; nimírum sola est grátia, qua salvámur. Quid nos ália concupíscimus, fratres? Quærámus grátiam, et per Maríam quærámus, quia quod quærit, ínvenit, et frustrári non potest. Quærámus grátiam, sed grátiam apud Deum: nam apud hómines grátia fallax. Quærant álii méritum, nos inveníre grátiam studeámus. Quid enim? Num grátiæ est quod hic sumus? Profécto misericórdiæ Dómini est, quod non sumus consúmpti nos.

quiddicebasoadammulierquamdedistimihided.en: What didst thou say, O Adam? The woman, whom thou gavest me, gave me of the tree, and I did eat. These are words of malice, whereby thou rather increasest than blottest out thy fault. Yet Wisdom hath conquered malice. For a woman is given for a woman, a wise one for a foolish, a humble one for a proud; who, instead of the tree of death, may offer thee the taste of life, and instead of that poisonous food of bitterness, may bring forth the sweetness of the eternal fruit. Change therefore the word of wicked excuse into the voice of thanksgiving, and say: Lord, the woman whom thou gavest me, gave me of the tree of life, and I did eat; and it is become sweeter than honey to my mouth, because in it thou hast quickened me. For behold, to this end was the Angel sent to the Virgin. O Virgin to be admired and most worthy of all honour! O woman to be venerated, wonderful above all women, the restorer of our parents, the quickener of their posterity!
quiddicebasoadammulierquamdedistimihided.la: Quid dicébas, o Adam? Múlier quam dedísti mihi, dedit mihi de ligno, et comédi. Verba malítiæ sunt hæc, quibus magis áugeas quam déleas culpam. Verúmtamen Sapiéntia vicit malítiam. Rédditur nempe fémina pro fémina, prudens pro fátua, húmilis pro supérba; quæ pro lingo mortis gustum tibi pórrigat vitæ, et pro venenóso cibo illo amaritúdinis, dulcédinem páriat fructus ætérni. Muta ergo iníque excusatiónis verbum in vocem gratiárum actiónis, et dic: Dómine, múlier quam dedísti mihi, dedit me de ligno vitæ, et comédi; et dulce factum est super mel ori meo, quia in ipso vivificásti me. Ecce enim ad hoc missus est Angelus ad Vírginem. O admirándam et omni honóre digníssimam Vírginem! O féminam venerándam, super omnes féminas admirábilem, paréntum reparatrícem, posterórum vivificatrícem!

missusestangelusadvirginemvirginemcarnev.en: The Angel was sent to the Virgin; a virgin in flesh, a virgin in mind, a virgin by profession, a virgin in fine such as the Apostle describeth, holy in mind and body; not newly nor by chance found, but chosen from the beginning, foreknown by the Most High and prepared for himself, kept by the Angels, foreshadowed by the Fathers, promised by the Prophets. To say a few things out of many, what other woman doth God seem to thee to have foretold, when he saith to the serpent: I will put enmities between thee and the woman? And if thou still doubtest whether he spoke of Mary, hear what followeth: She shall crush thy head. For whom was this victory reserved, but for Mary?
missusestangelusadvirginemvirginemcarnev.la: Missus est Angelus ad Vírginem; vírginem carne, vírginem mente, vírginem professióne, vírginem dénique, qualem descríbit Apóstolus, mente et córpore sanctam; nec nóviter, nec fortuíto invéntam, sed a sǽculo eléctam, ab Altíssimo præcógnitam, et sibi præparátam, ab Angelis servátam, a Pátribus præsignátam, a Prophétis promíssam. Ut pauca loquar de plúribus, quam tibi áliam prædixísse Deus vidétur, quando ad serpéntem ait: Inimicítias ponam inter te et mulíerem? Et si adhuc dúbitas an de María díxerit, audi quod séquitur: Ipsa cónteret caput tuum. Cui hæc serváta victória est, nisi Maríæ?

beataprogeniesundechristusnatusest.en: Blessed is the stock from which Christ was born.
beataprogeniesundechristusnatusest.la: Beáta progénies, unde Christus natus est.

oquamgloriosestvirgoqueceliregemgenuit.en: O how glorious is the Virgin, who brought forth the King of heaven!
oquamgloriosestvirgoqueceliregemgenuit.la: O quam gloriósa est Virgo, quæ cæli Regem génuit!

felixnamquesessacravirgomarietomnilauded.en: For happy art thou, O holy Virgin Mary, and most worthy of all praise.
felixnamquesessacravirgomarietomnilauded.la: Felix namques es, sacra Virgo Mária, et omni laude digníssima.

myrrhetguttetcasiaavestimentistuisagradi.en: Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume thy garments, from the ivory steps: out of which the daughters of kings have delighted thee in thy honour.
myrrhetguttetcasiaavestimentistuisagradi.la: Myrrha et gutta et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a grádibus ebúrneis, ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.

benedictetvenerabilisesvirgomaria.en: Blessed and venerable art thou, O Virgin Mary,
benedictetvenerabilisesvirgomaria.la: Benedícta et venerábilis es, Virgo María,

cuiusvisceramerueruntportaredominumchris.en: Whose womb merited to bear Christ the Lord.
cuiusvisceramerueruntportaredominumchris.la: Cujus víscera meruérunt portáre Dóminum Christum.

canutusquartussuenonisesthritiidanorumre.en: Canute the Fourth, son of Sweyn Estridsen, king of the Danes, conspicuous for faith, piety, and uprightness of manners, gave from his tender years a pattern of excellent holiness. Having obtained his father's sceptre with the highest acclamation of all, he began to apply himself diligently to the furthering of religion, to increase the churches with revenues, and to adorn them with precious furniture. Then, burning with zeal for spreading the faith, he attacked barbarous kingdoms in just warfare, and brought the conquered and subject nations under the Christian law. And being glorious with very many victories, and increased in riches, he cast down his royal diadem at the feet of Christ crucified, subjecting himself and his kingdom to him who is King of kings and Lord of lords. He chastised his body with fasts, hair-shirts and scourges. He was ever constant in prayer and contemplation, lavish toward the poor, beneficent toward all: nor did he ever turn aside from the path of justice and of the divine law.
canutusquartussuenonisesthritiidanorumre.la: Canutus quartus, Suenonis Esthritii Danorum regis filius, fide, pietate et morum honestate conspicuus, eximiæ sanctitatis a teneris annis specimen dedit. Paternum sceptrum summa omnium acclamatione adeptus, religioni promovendæ sedulo incumbere, ecclesias reditibus augere, et pretiosa supellectili ornare cœpit. Tum zelo propagandæ fidei succensus, barbara regna justo certamine aggressus, devictas subditasque nationes christianæ legi subjugavit. Victoriis autem plurimis gloriosus, et divitiis auctus, regale diadema ad Christi crucifixi pedes abjecit, se et regnum illi subjiciens, qui Rex regum est, et Dominus dominantium. Corpus suum jejuniis, ciliciis et flagellis castigavit. In oratione et contemplatione assiduus, erga pauperes profusus, erga omnes beneficus semper fuit: nec umquam a justitiæ divinæque legis semita deflexit.

hisaliisquevirtutibusimbutusadsupremumpe.en: Endowed with these and other virtues, the holy king was hastening to the highest summit of perfection. Now it happened that the kingdom of England was invaded by William, duke of the Normans, with a formidable army. And when the English implored the help of the Danes, and the king had resolved to succour them, he committed the conduct of the war to Olaf his brother. Who, enticed by the desire of reigning, turned his arms to the king's destruction, stirring up the soldiers and the people against him. Nor were incitements to the rebellion lacking. For when the king, by laws put forth, had ordained that tithes should be paid to the churches, that the precepts of God and of the Church should be observed, and that transgressors should be punished, very many perverse and wicked men, being embittered, began first to make tumult, then to stir up the common people, and at length to plot the death of the most holy king.
hisaliisquevirtutibusimbutusadsupremumpe.la: His aliisque virtutibus imbutus, ad supremum perfectionis apicem sanctus rex properabat. Accidit autem ut Angliæ regnum a Wilhelmo Normandorum duce, formidabili exercitu invaderetur. Anglis vero, Danorum opem implorantibus, cum succurrere rex decrevisset, belli expeditionem Olao fratri commisit. Qui regnandi cupiditate illectus, arma vertit in regis perniciem, militibus et populo contra illum concitatis. Nec defuerunt rebellioni fomenta. Cum enim rex, editis legibus, decimas ecclesiis solvi, Dei et Ecclesiæ præcepta servari, transgressores puniri sanxisset, plerique perversi ac scelerati homines exacerbati, primum quidem tumultuari, tum plebem commovere, ac tandem sanctissimo regi necem moliri cœperunt.

sciensigiturrexfuturorumpresciusmortemsi.en: The king therefore, foreknowing the things to come, and knowing that death was at hand for him for justice' sake, having foretold it, went to the church of St. Alban the Martyr at Odense, as to the place of combat: and being fortified with the sacraments, he commended his agony to the Lord. Soon the multitude of the conspirators, coming thither, tried to set fire to the church, to break down the doors and to burst in. And when they could not accomplish this, approaching the windows, they ceased not to hurl with great violence stones and arrows at the holy king, who was praying on bended knees for his enemies: until, pierced by the blows of stones and darts, and at length by a lance, falling down before the altar with outstretched arms, he was crowned with a glorious martyrdom, Gregory the Seventh then sitting on the apostolic throne. God afterwards made his Martyr illustrious by many miracles. For Denmark, oppressed by grievous famine and divers calamities, paid the penalty of the sacrilege committed. Many also, afflicted with divers sicknesses, obtained remedy and health at his tomb. And when the queen tried secretly to carry off his sacred body by night and to translate it elsewhere, she was terrified by a great brightness sent from heaven, and desisted from her purpose.
sciensigiturrexfuturorumpresciusmortemsi.la: Sciens igitur rex, futurorum præscius, mortem sibi propter justitiam imminere; ea prænuntiata, ad ecclesiam sancti Albani Martyris Othoniæ, tamquam ad locum certaminis, profectus est: et sacramentis munitus, agonem suum Domino commendabat. Mox ibi adveniens conjuratorum multitudo, ecclesiæ ignem admovere, fores confringere et in eam irrumpere tentarunt. Quod cum perficere non possent, ad fenestras accedentes, saxa et sagittas in sanctum regem, flexis genibus pro inimicis orantem, magno impetu jaculari non cessarunt: donec lapidum et telorum ictibus, ac tandem lancea confossus, glorioso martyrio, ante altare extensis brachiis procumbens, coronatus est, sedente in apostolico throno Gregorio septimo. Multis postea miraculis Martyrem suum illustravit Deus. Nam gravi penuria et diversis calamitatibus oppressa Dania, patrati sacrilegii pœnas luit. Plures étiam variis languoribus afflicti, ad ejus tumulum remedium et incolumitatem consecuti sunt. Cumque regina sacrum ejus corpus noctu clam surripere, et alio transferre conaretur, emisso cælitus ingenti splendore perterrita, a proposito cessavit.

anicetussyrusimperatoremarcoaurelioanton.en: Anicetus, a Syrian, ruled the Church in the time of the emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus. He decreed that clerics should not let their hair grow long. Five times in the month of December he ordained seventeen priests, four deacons, and nine bishops for divers places. He lived in the pontificate eight years, eight months, and twenty-four days. Crowned with martyrdom for the faith of Christ, he was buried on the Appian Way in the cemetery which was afterwards called that of Callistus, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of May.
anicetussyrusimperatoremarcoaurelioanton.la: Anicetus Syrus, imperatore Marco Aurelio Antonino, praefuit Ecclesiae. Decrevit ne clerici comam nutrirent. Quinquies mense Decembri ordinavit presbyteros decem et septem, diaconos quatuor, episcopos per diversa loca novem. Vixit in pontificatu annos octo, menses octo, dies viginti quatuor. Propter Christi fidem martyrio coronatus, sepultus est via Appia in ccemeterio, quod postea Callisti appellatum est, decimo quinto Kalendas Majas.

deusquisancteritetantamgratiamconferredi.en: O God, who didst vouchsafe to bestow upon Saint Rita so great grace that she loved her enemies, and bore in her heart and on her brow the marks of thy charity and passion: grant us, we beseech thee, by her intercession and merits, so to spare our enemies and to contemplate the sorrows of thy passion, that we may attain the rewards promised to the meek and to them that mourn:
deusquisancteritetantamgratiamconferredi.la: Deus, qui sanctæ Ritæ tantam grátiam conférre dignátus es, ut inimícos dilígeret et in corde ac fronte caritátis et passiónis tuæ signa portáret: da nobis, quǽsumus, ejus intercessióne et méritis; inimícis nostris sic párcere et passiónis tuæ dolóres contemplári, ut promíssa mítibus ac lugéntibus prǽmia consequámur:

petronillasanctipetrifiliavirgoformacorp.en: Petronilla, the daughter of St. Peter, was a virgin of excellent beauty of body, but much more excellent in beauty of soul: when she was sick, blessed Peter was asked why he, who healed others, did not restore health to his own daughter; he answered: Because it is expedient for her. Yet, that he might leave to none room to doubt of his power, he bade her rise from her bed and serve the guests. A little after she fell back into the same sickness; and when at length she had recovered from it, Count Flaccus, moved by her fame, loved her without even having seen her, and earnestly strove that she should be given him in marriage.
petronillasanctipetrifiliavirgoformacorp.la: Petronilla, sancti Petri filia, virgo forma corporis eximia, sed animi pulchritudine multo præstantior fuit: quæ ægrota cum esset, à beato Petro quæsitum est, cur, qui alienos sanaret, filiæ suæ sanitatem non restitueret? respondit: quia sic expedit ei. Veruntamen, ut nemini de sua potestate dubitandi locum relinqueret, eam furgere jussit è lecto, et conuiuis ministrare. Quæ paulo post in eundem morbum recides, ex eo cum aliquando conualuisset, ejus fama cómotus, ne visam quidem Flaccus Comes adamauit, enixeq. contendit, ut sibi daretur in matrimonium.

petronillaautemintelligensvirginitatisue.en: But Petronilla, perceiving that snares were being laid for her virginity, which she had dedicated to Jesus Christ, by the most bitter enemy of mankind, took a space of three days to deliberate, and spent all that time in fasting and prayer, constantly asking of her heavenly spouse that he would not suffer violence to be done to her holy purpose: and so on the third day God came to the help of the virgin: for, burning with the love of her divine spouse, when she had received the Eucharist, he called her to the heavenly nuptials. Her body, buried on the Ardeatine Way, was afterwards translated by Paul the First, Pontiff, into the Basilica of the prince of the Apostles.
petronillaautemintelligensvirginitatisue.la: Petronilla autem intelligens virginitati sue, quam Jesu Christo dicarat, ab acerrimo humani gene ris hoste parari insidias; sumpto sibi tridui spatio ad deliberandum, totum illud tepus in jejuniis, et oratione consumpsit, alliduè petens à cælesti sponso, ne sancto proposito suo vim afferri pateretur: itaque subuenic die tercio virgini Deus: nam eam diuini sponsi amore flagrantem, ubi Eucharistiam sumpsisset, ad cælestes nuptias euocauit. Cujus corpus in via Ardeatina sepultum, postea à Paulo primo pontifice in Basilicam principis Apostolorum translatum est.

brevepiixdieisept.en: Brief of Pius X of 18 Sept. 1908

sermoaliasepistoladegazophylacio.en: Sermon, otherwise Epistle 34, on the Treasury

libadversusheresescapaliasnum.en: Book 3 against Heresies, ch. 18, otherwise 20, nn. 5-6
libadversusheresescapaliasnum.la: Lib. 3 adversus Haereses cap. 18, alias 20, num. 5-6

sanctamariasuccurremiserisiuvapusillanim.en: Holy Mary, succour the wretched, help the faint-hearted, comfort the sorrowful, pray for the people, plead for the clergy, intercede for the devout female sex: let all feel thy help, whosoever celebrate thy solemn Commemoration.
sanctamariasuccurremiserisiuvapusillanim.la: Sancta María, succurre míseris, juva pusillánimes, réfove flébiles, ora pro pópulo, intérveni pro clero, intercéde pro devóto femíneo sexu: séntiant omnes tuum juvámen, quicúmque célebrant tuam solémnem Commemoratiónem.

exiissocietatisiesusodalibusquiecclesiei.en: Of those members of the Society of Jesus who most adorned the beginnings of the Church in North America about the middle of the seventeenth century, God chose eight most pure victims for himself, that the seeds of faith, watered with their blood, might thereafter grow up into more abundant harvests. All these Martyrs, born in France and, except two laymen, raised to the priesthood, were sent by their Superiors into the Canadian Mission, which was then called New France; and after innumerable apostolic journeys from the city of Quebec through those various immense regions, and most severe labours for one and the same cause of religion, though not at one and the same time nor place, they were most cruelly put to death. As the leaders and masters of these are rightly reckoned John de Brebeuf, born of a noble family at Condé in the diocese formerly of Bayeux, now of Coutances, and Isaac Jogues, of Orleans, men burning with a strenuous and apostolic zeal, greatly given to mortification, most closely united to God in prayer, and sometimes enlightened also by heavenly visions. Not unlike them were their four companions, priests: Anthony Daniel, of Dieppe, Gabriel Lalemant and Charles Garnier, of Paris, and Noel Chabanel, of Mende; who all faithfully discharged the sacred ministry in various villages, chiefly among the Hurons.
exiissocietatisiesusodalibusquiecclesiei.la: Ex iis Societatis Jesu sodalibus, qui Ecclesiæ in America boreali exordia medio sæculo septimo maxime illustrarunt, octo purissimas hostias sibi elegit Deus, ut fidei semina earum sanguine irrigata in uberiores segetes deínde succrescerent. Omnes hi Martyres, in Gallia nati et, præter duos laicos, sacerdotio aucti, in Missionem Canadensem, quæ Novæ Galliæ tunc vocabatur, a Superioribus missi, post innumeros ex urbe Quebecensi per varias illas immensas regiones apostolicos excursus, asperrimosque labores ob unam eamdemque religionis causam, etsi non uno eodemque tempore nec loco, crudelissime necati sunt. Horum veluti duces ac magistri merito censentur Joannes de Brebeuf, Condæi in diocesi olim Baiocensi nunc Constantiensi nobili genere ortus, et Isaacus Jogues, aurelianensis, viri strenuo et apostolico zelo incensi, mortificationi maxime dediti, cum Deo in oratione conjunctissimi, cælestibus étiam visionibus quandoque illustrati. Ab iis haud absimiles erant quatuor socii sacerdotes Antonius Daniel, dieppensis, Gabriel Lalemant et Carolus Garnier, parisienses, Natalis Chabanel, mimatensis; qui omnes variis in pagis potissimum inter Hurones sacris muneribus fideliter fungebantur.

sanctituidominemirabileconsecutisuntiter.en: Thy Saints, O Lord, have followed a wonderful way, serving thy commandments, that they might be found unhurt in the mighty waters:
sanctituidominemirabileconsecutisuntiter.la: Sancti tui, Domine, mirabile consecuti sunt iter, servientes præceptis tuis, ut invirentur illæsi in aquis validis:

frequentesfinitimorumiroquensiumincursio.en: The frequent inroads of the neighbouring Iroquois, often laying waste the Huron mission, not seldom brought the life of the Fathers into the utmost peril. In the year one thousand six hundred and forty-two, Isaac Jogues, with René Goupil, a temporal coadjutor of the Society of Jesus, while journeying from the city of Quebec to the Hurons, fell into the hands of the Iroquois, who tortured him and his companion most cruelly and reduced them to slavery. In the same year, on the twenty-ninth day of September, René, being ordered by a barbarous old man to be slain in hatred of the saving cross, breathed forth his most pure soul near Auriesville, in the present State of New York. Isaac, the next year, having found an occasion of escape, returned into France; but after a year, seeking America again, and going once and again to the same barbarians, formerly his executioners, with John de la Lande, likewise a coadjutor of the Society of Jesus, on the eighteenth day of October in the year one thousand six hundred and forty-six, in the present diocese of Albany, being struck with a hatchet, he obtained the palm of martyrdom. And on the following day his companion John, crowned with the same crown, flew away to heaven.
frequentesfinitimorumiroquensiumincursio.la: Frequentes finitimorum Iroquensium incursiones, Huronicam missionem sæpe vastantes, haud raro in supremum discrimen Patrum vitam vocabant. Anno millesimo sexcentesimo quadragesimo secundo, Isaacus Jogues, cum Renato Goupil, Societatis Jesu coadjutore temporali, ex urbe Quebecensi ad Hurones iter faciens, in Iroquenses incidit, qui eum ejusque socium dirissime torquent et in servitutem redigunt. Eodem anno die vigesima nona Septembris, Renatus, in odium salutiferæ crucis a barbaro sene interfici jussus, prope Auriesville, in hodierno Neo-Eboracensi Statu, candidissimam animam efflavit. Isaacus anno proximo, aufugiendi occasionem nactus, in Galliam revertit; sed post annum Americam repetens et semel atque iterum ad eosdem barbaros, suos olim carnifices, cum Joanne de la Lande, Societatis Jesu item coadjutore, progressus, die decima octava Octobris anno millesimo sexcentesimo quadragesimo sexto, in hodierna diocesi Albanensi, acinace percussus martyrii palmam consecutus est. Postero vero die ejus socius Joannes, eadem redimitus corona, ad cælum evolavit.

annomillesimosexcentesimoquadragesimooct.en: In the year one thousand six hundred and forty-eight, on the fourth day of July, Anthony Daniel, who had the care of the village of St. Joseph among the Hurons, fearlessly defending his flock against the invading Iroquois, pierced with arrows and with fiery bullets, laid down his life at the doors of the church, a good shepherd for his sheep. In the following year, on the sixteenth day of March, John de Brebeuf, rightly called the apostle of the Hurons, being taken by the Iroquois together with Gabriel Lalemant, after long and most cruel tortures, the barbarians themselves marvelling at the unconquered fortitude of the champion of Christ, died gloriously in the village of St. Ignatius, in the region of Canada now called Ontario; whom on the morrow Gabriel Lalemant followed by the same bloody way and with the same virtue. And in the month of December of the same year one thousand six hundred and forty-nine, on the eve of the Immaculate Conception of the blessed Virgin Mary, Charles Garnier, pierced with wounds and struck with an axe, ended a most innocent life by a glorious death. Lastly, on the following day, Noel Chabanel, treacherously set upon by an apostate Huron and cast into a river, obtained the longed-for palm of martyrdom in the Mission so dear to him, to whose service, nature resisting in vain, he had bound himself for ever by a heroic vow. These eight first Martyrs of North America the Supreme Pontiff Pius the Eleventh, in the holy year one thousand nine hundred and twenty-five, enrolled among the Blessed, and five years later inscribed in the calendar of the Saints.
annomillesimosexcentesimoquadragesimooct.la: Anno millesimo sexcentesimo quadragesimo octavo, die quarta Julii Antonius Daniel, qui pagi Sancti Joseph inter Hurones curam gerebat, contra invasores Iroquenses gregem suum impavidus defendens, sagittis et ignitis glandibus confossus, ad templi fores bonus pastor pro ovibus animam posuit. Anno proximo, die decima sexta Martii, Joannes de Brebeuf, Huronum apostolus merito nuncupatus, una cum Gabriele Lalemant, ab Iroquensibus comprehensus, post diuturnos sævissimosque cruciatus, ipsis barbaris invictam Christi pugilis fortitudinem demirantibus, in pago Sancti Ignatii in hodierna Canadensi regione Ontario nuncupata, gloriosus occubuit; quem postridie Gabriel Lalemant eadem cruenta via eademque virtute secutus est. Mense autem Decembri ejusdem anni millesimi sexcentesimi quadragesimi noni, in pervigilio Immaculatæ Conceptionis beatæ Mariæ Virginis, Carolus Garnier, vulneribus confossus et securi percussus, innocentissimam vitam glorioso exitu conclusit. Postero demum die, Natalis Chabanel, ab Hurone apostata dolose invasus et in profluentem dejectus, in dilecta sibi Missione, cui perpetuo colendæ, natura frustra obsistente, heroico voto se obstrinxerat, optatam martyrii palmam adeptus est. Hos octo Americæ borealis primores Martyres Pius Undecimus Pontifex Maximus, anno sacro millesimo nongentesimo vigesimo quinto, Beatorum numero, eosque quinque post annis Sanctorum fastis ascripsit.

quiconfiduntinillumintellegentveritateme.en: They that trust in him shall understand the truth: and they that are faithful in love shall rest in him.
quiconfiduntinillumintellegentveritateme.la: Qui confidunt in illum, intellegent veritatem: et fideles in dilectione acquiescent illi.

noteinevangelicaslectionesindiefestoomni.en: Notes on the Gospel lessons: on the feast of All Saints, after the beginning
noteinevangelicaslectionesindiefestoomni.la: Notæ in evangelicas lectiones: in die festo Omnium Sanctorum, post initium

notabochristumlongealiterquamhuncmundumd.en: I shall note that Christ teacheth and declareth concerning blessedness far otherwise than this world. For it is proper to the world falsely to place man's happiness in perishable and fleeting things, which must be left here; just as if it were said: Happy is the people that hath these things. Nay rather, those whom Christ here declareth blessed, the foolish world accounteth only as wretched and unhappy, and is wont to despise and turn away from them; so that hence also Christ himself testifieth to the Apostles: Amen, amen I say to you, that you shall lament and weep, but the world shall rejoice: and you shall be made sorrowful. And rightly said Solomon: He that walketh in the right way, and feareth God, is despised by him that goeth by an infamous way.
notabochristumlongealiterquamhuncmundumd.la: Notabo Christum longe aliter quam hunc mundum, de beatitudine docere atque pronuntiare. Mundi etenim est proprium rebus caducis et fluxis, quæ hic relinquendæ sunt, mentiri hominis felicitatem, perinde ac si dicatur: Beatus populus, cui hæc sunt. Immo vero quos Christus beatos hic pronuntiat, eos insipiens mundus tantum pro miseris et infelicibus ducit, eosdem de more contemnit atque aversatur, ut hinc étiam Christus ipse testetur Apostolis: Amen, amen dico vobis, quia plorabitis et flebitis vos; mundus autem gaudebit, vos autem contristabimini. Recteque dixit Salomon: Ambulans recto itinere et timens Deum, despicitur ab eo qui infami graditur via.

beatidemumsuntquipersecutionempropterius.en: Blessed lastly are they that suffer persecution for justice' sake, and by their unconquered patience obtain the eternal kingdom of Christ. To this kind of blessedness none are more to be referred than Stephen the protomartyr and the other most valiant soldiers and martyrs of Christ: since, being dragged as sheep to the slaughter, they strove even unto blood for Christian justice, so that no force or savagery of enemies, no bitterness of tribulation or temptation, could lead them away and separate them from the confession of the faith, the charity of Christ, the doctrine of the Church, and the path of justice. O happy they, who could testify with a good conscience: Who then shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall tribulation? or distress? or famine? or nakedness? or danger? or persecution? or the sword? But in all these things we overcome, because of him that hath loved us. We have passed through fire and water, and thou hast brought us out into a refreshment.
beatidemumsuntquipersecutionempropterius.la: Beati demum sunt qui persecutionem propter justitiam patiuntur, suaque invicta patientia Christi regnum æternum obtinent. Ad hoc genus beatitudinis, nulli magis quam protomartyr Stephanus aliique fortissimi Christi milites ac martyres referendi sunt: quoniam velut oves ad occisionem pertractæ, ad sanguinem usque pro justitia christiana certarunt, nulla ut hostium vis atque barbaries, nulla tribulationis vel tentationis acerbitas eos a fidei confessione, Christi caritate, doctrina Ecclesiæ et justitiæ tramite potuerit abducere ac separare. O felices illi qui bona testari conscientia potuerunt: Quis nos separabit a caritate Christi? Tribulatio? an angustia? an fames? an nuditas? an periculum? an persecutio? an gladius? In his omnibus superamus propter eum qui dilexit nos. Transivimus per ignem et aquam, et eduxisti nos in refrigerium.

pretereafelicesomnesquihancscalamiacobsu.en: Moreover, happy are all they who to this day ascend this ladder of Jacob, marked by the eight steps above, leaving all hindrances behind, so that daily they overcome their deadly enemies, the world, the flesh and Satan, and by the pursuit of virtues make for themselves a step to blessed immortality. But far happier still are they who have made an end of fighting and conquering, and, the very labour of ascending being finished, have come to the crown of the contest; and now, like soldiers that have received their discharge and served their time, enjoy the highest rest, and dwell in the heavenly tabernacle, laden with a most ample reward. Nor is there any doubt that the holy Martyrs and godly Doctors flourish above the other elect unto everlasting ages, since for their heroic virtues they obtain by a special privilege the aureole, as the Theologians call it, and an excellent laurel.
pretereafelicesomnesquihancscalamiacobsu.la: Præterea felices omnes qui hanc scalam Jacob, superioribus gradibus octo distinctam, in hunc usque diem ascendunt, relictis omnibus impedimentis, ita ut capitales hostes, mundum, carnem ac satanam, cotidie vincant sibique virtutum studio gradum faciant ad beatam immortalitatem. Verum longe feliciores et illi, qui pugnandi et vincendi fecere finem et, ipso ascendendi labore confecto, ad certaminis coronam pervenerunt jamque, veluti rude donati et emeriti milites, quiete summa potiuntur, et in cælesti tabernaculo habitant, mercede amplissima cumulati. Nec dubium quin sancti Martyres piique Doctores præ ceteris florescant electis in perpetuas æternitates, quoniam ob virtutes heroicas aureolam, sicut Theologi vocant, et excellentem lauream peculiari privilegio consequentur.

daquesumusomnipotensdeusutquibeatinmarty.en: Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God, that we who keep the solemnity of blessed N., thy Martyr, may be helped by his intercession with thee.
daquesumusomnipotensdeusutquibeatinmarty.la: Da, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui beáti N., Mártyris tui, solémnia cólimus, ejus apud te intercessiónibus adjuvémur.

uteniminfirmaturpeccatoradversisitaiustu.en: For as the sinner is weakened by adversity, so the just man is strengthened by temptations. Thus did the Saints fight against sin; thus were they made both stronger by labouring and victors by dying. No athlete can be called stronger without a contest, none can be crowned without a victory. No soldier hath subdued the enemy without battle; none without war hath deserved well of his commander. Thou hast, O Christian, fit arms wherewith to overcome the foe; thou hast most strong weapons wherewith to vanquish the enemy.
uteniminfirmaturpeccatoradversisitaiustu.la: Ut enim infirmátur peccátor advérsis, ita justus tentatiónibus roborátur. Sic dimicárunt advérsus peccátum Sancti; sic, et laborándo fortióres, et moriéndo victóres effécti sunt. Nullus athlétes sine certámine fórtior dici, nullus sine victória póterit coronári. Nemo miles sine prœlio hostem subjécit; nemo sine bello imperatórem proméruit. Habes, christiáne, competéntia arma, quibus hostem expúgnes; habes fortíssima tela, quibus inimícum debelles.

beatipatrisnmeritaiamintutopositasecurim.en: Let us without fear magnify the merits of the blessed Father N., now placed in safety; who, holding manfully the helm of faith, hath now cast the anchor of hope in a calm haven, and hath brought the ship, full of heavenly riches and eternal merchandise, to the longed-for shore; who held the shield of the fear of God unwearyingly against all adversaries, until he came to the victory. For what was the whole course of his life, but one conflict with a watchful enemy?
beatipatrisnmeritaiamintutopositasecurim.la: Beáti Patris N. mérita, jam in tuto pósita, secúri magnificémus; qui, gubernáculum fídei viríliter tenens, ánchoram spei tranquílla jam in statióne compósuit, et plenam cæléstibus divítiis et ætérnis mércibus navem, optáto in líttore, collocávit; qui contra omnes adversários scutum timóris Dei támdiu infatigabíliter ténuit, donec ad victóriam perveníret. Quid enim fuit totus vitæ illíus cursus, nisi uníus cum vígili hoste conflíctus?

quantishiccecisaviaveritatiserrantibuset.en: To how many blind, wandering from the way of truth and already hanging from the highest crag over the abyss, did he restore their lost sight, and repair that vision whereby Christ might be seen? Into the deaf ears of how many, condemned by the stopping of unbelief, did he pour the precious hearing to receive the voice of the heavenly commandments; that, when God called them to mercy, they might answer by obedience? How many wounded inwardly did he cure of their infirmity by the art of his angelic mouth and of his prayers?
quantishiccecisaviaveritatiserrantibuset.la: Quantis hic cæcis, a via veritátis errántibus et de summa jam in profúndum rupe pendéntibus, amíssum réddidit visum; et illum, quo Christus viderétur, reparávit intúitum? Quantórum áuribus surdis et infidelitátis obturatióne damnátis, ad percipiéndam vocem cæléstium mandatórum, pretiósum infúdit audítum; ut, vocánti Deo ad misericórdiam, respondérent per obediéntiam? Quantos intrínsecus vulnerátos, angélici oris arte et oratiónum, ab infirmitáte curávit?

necimmeritodoctoressanctihyadumnuncupati.en: And not without reason are the holy Doctors signified by the name of the Hyades. For in the Greek tongue rain is called hyetos, and the Hyades took their name from rains, because when they rise they without doubt bring showers. Well therefore are they expressed by the name of the Hyades, who, brought to the state of the universal Church as it were to the face of heaven, have poured the showers of holy preaching upon the dry earth of the human breast. For if the word of preaching were not rain, Moses would by no means have said: Let my speech be expected as the rain; and the Truth would in no wise have said by Isaias: I will command my clouds to rain no rain upon it; and that which we brought forward a little before: Therefore the stars of rain have been withheld.
necimmeritodoctoressanctihyadumnuncupati.la: Nec immérito Doctóres sancti Hýadum nuncupatióne signántur. Græco quippe elóquio hýetos plúvia vocátur, et Hýades nomen a plúviis accepérunt, quia ortæ procul dúbio imbres ferunt. Bene ergo Hýadum appellatióne expréssi sunt, qui, ad statum universális Ecclésiæ quasi in cæli fáciem dedúcti, super aréntem terram humáni péctoris, sanctæ prædicatiónis imbres fudérunt. Si enim prædicatiónis sermo plúvia non esset, Móyses mínime dixísset: Exspectétur sicut plúvia elóquium meum; et nequáquam per Isaíam Véritas díceret: Mandábo núbibus meis, ne pluant super eam imbrem; atque hoc, quod paulo ante protúlimus: Quam ob rem prohíbitæ sunt stellæ pluviárum.

deusquinosbeatorumnetnconfessorumtuoruma.en: O God, who gladdenest us by the yearly solemnity of thy blessed Confessors N. and N.: mercifully grant, that we who keep their heavenly birthday may also imitate their deeds.
deusquinosbeatorumnetnconfessorumtuoruma.la: Deus, qui nos beatórum N. et N. Confessórum tuórum ánnua solemnitáte lætíficas: concéde propítius; ut quórum natalítiæ cólimus, étiam actiónes imitémur.

nequeeniminanisheccautiestetvanaformidoq.en: For neither is this caution empty, nor this fear vain, which taketh thought for the way of salvation, which keepeth the life-giving commandments of the Lord; that they who have dedicated themselves to Christ, and, withdrawing from carnal concupiscence, have vowed themselves to God both in flesh and in mind, may finish their work, destined for a great reward, and may study no longer to be adorned or to please any one but their Lord, from whom they also await the reward of virginity, as he himself saith: All men take not this word, but they to whom it is given. For there are eunuchs, who were born so from their mother's womb: and there are eunuchs, who were made so by men: and there are eunuchs, who have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven.
nequeeniminanisheccautiestetvanaformidoq.la: Neque enim inánis hæc cáutio est, et vana formído, quæ ad salútis viam cónsulit, quæ domínica et vitália præcépta custódit, ut quæ se Christo dicáverint, et a carnáli concupiscéntia recedéntes tam carne, quam mente se Deo vóverint, consúmment opus suum magno prǽmio destinátum, nec ornári jam, aut placére cuíquam, nisi Dómino suo, stúdeant, a quo et mercédem virginitátis expéctant, dicénte ipso: Non omnes cápiunt verbum, sed illi quibus datum est. Sunt enim spadónes, qui ex útero matris sic nati sunt: et sunt spadónes, qui coácti sunt ab homínibus; et sunt spadónes, qui seípsos castravérunt propter regnum cœlórum.

denuoquoqueperhancangelivocemcontinentie.en: Again also, by this voice of the Angel, the gift of continence is shown, virginity is proclaimed: These are they who were not defiled with women: for they are virgins: these follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth. For neither doth the Lord promise the grace of continence to men only, and pass over women: but since the woman is a portion of the man, and was taken and formed from him, in almost all the Scriptures God speaketh to the first-formed, because they are two in one flesh, and in the male the female also is signified. But if continence followeth Christ, and virginity is destined for the kingdom of God, what have they to do with earthly dress and with ornaments, whereby, while they long to please men, they offend God?
denuoquoqueperhancangelivocemcontinentie.la: Dénuo quoque per hanc Angeli vocem continéntiæ munus osténditur, virgínitas prædicátur. Hi sunt, qui cum muliéribus se non coinquinavérunt: vírgines enim permansérunt: hi sunt qui sequúntur Agnum quocúmque íerit. Neque enim tantum másculis continéntiæ grátiam Dóminus repromíttit, et féminas prǽterit: sed quóniam fémina viri pórtio est, et ex eo sumpta atque formáta est, in Scriptúris fere ómnibus ad protoplástum Deus lóquitur, quia sunt duo in carne una, et in másculo simul significátur et fémina. Quod si Christum continéntia séquitur, et regno Dei virgínitas destinátur: quid est illis cum terréno cultu, et cum ornaméntis, quibus dum homínibus placére géstiunt, Deum offéndunt?

permulieremvicitpermulieremsuperatusesth.en: By a woman he conquered, by a woman he was overcome. This was formerly his weapon: this hath now become the instrument of his slaughter; this vessel hath appeared invincible. She of old sinned first, and died: this one died, that she might not sin. She of old, puffed up with the hope of a vain promise, violated the laws of God: this one despised the present life, that she might not forswear her faith in her benefactor. What excuse then can men hereafter hope for, if they be soft and slothful; what pardon indeed, when women bear themselves bravely and manfully, when they gird themselves so nobly for the contests of godliness?
permulieremvicitpermulieremsuperatusesth.la: Per mulíerem vicit, per mulíerem superátus est. Hoc illíus ántea telum erat: hoc illíus nunc cædis factum est instruméntum, hoc vas appáruit insuperábile. Peccávit illa prior, et mórtua est: ista mórtua est, ne peccáret. Illa tum fútilis promíssi spe infláta, Dei leges violávit: hæc vitam præséntem contémpsit, ne fidem in suum benefactórem ejuráret. Quam ígitur deínceps speráre póterunt excusatiónem viri, si molles sint, et ignávi; quam vero véniam, cum fórtiter ac viríliter se gerant mulíeres, cum ádeo se generose ad certámina pietátis accíngant?

fuitilicorpusimbecillumetobnoxiussexusin.en: She had a weak body, and a sex liable to injury; but grace coming upon her hid the weakness of all these. For there is nothing, nothing at all, more powerful than he who with great zeal hath the fear of God fixed in his mind; but though the enemies threaten fire, though the sword, though wild beasts, though anything else, he despiseth all without difficulty; which assuredly this blessed woman also did.
fuitilicorpusimbecillumetobnoxiussexusin.la: Fuit ili corpus imbecíllum, et obnóxius sexus injúriæ; verúmtamen ómnium horum imbecillitátem advéniens grátia occultávit. Nihil enim est, nihil plane poténtius est co, qui magno cum stúdio Dei timórem hábeat in mente defíxum; sed quamvis ignes, quamvis ferrum, quamvis béstias, quamvis áliud quidvis minêntur hostes, ómnia nullo negótio contémnit; quod útique Beáta ista étiam fecit.

sobriiestoteetvigilatequiaadversariusves.en: Be sober and watch: because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, goeth about seeking whom he may devour: whom resist ye, strong in faith: knowing that the same affliction befalls your brethren who are in the world.
sobriiestoteetvigilatequiaadversariusves.la: Sóbrii estóte, et vigiláte: quia adversárius vester diábolus tamquam leo rúgiens círcuit, quærens quem dévoret: cui resístite fortes in fide, sciéntes eámdem passiónem ei, quæ in mundo est, vestræ fraternitáti fíeri.
