natalemsanctiioannisfratrescarissimihodi.en: We celebrate this day, dearly beloved brethren, the birthday of St. John: which we read was granted to none of the Saints before. For the birthday of the Lord alone and of blessed John is celebrated and kept throughout the whole world. For this one a barren woman brought forth, that one a virgin conceived: in Elizabeth barrenness is overcome, in blessed Mary the wont of conception is changed. Elizabeth, by knowing a husband, bore a son: Mary believed the Angel, and conceived. Elizabeth conceived a man, and Mary a man: but Elizabeth a man only, Mary God and man.
natalemsanctiioannisfratrescarissimihodi.la: Natálem sancti Joánnis, fratres caríssimi, hódie celebrámus: quod nulli umqua Sanctórum légimus fuísse concéssum. Solíus enim Dómini, et beáti Joánnis dies nativitátis in univérso mundo celebrátur et cólitur. Hunc enim stérilis péperit, illum virgo concépit: in Elísabeth sterílitas víncitur, in beáta María conceptiónis consuetúdo mutátur. Elísabeth virum cognoscéndo, fílium génuit: María Angelo crédidit, et concépit. Hóminem concépit Elísabeth, hóminem et María: sed Elísabeth solum hóminem, María Deum et hóminem.

magnusigiturioannescuiusmagnitudinietiam.en: Great therefore is John, to whose greatness even the Saviour beareth witness, saying: There hath not risen among them that are born of women a greater than John the Baptist. He excelleth the rest, he standeth out above all: he surpasseth the Prophets, he goeth beyond the Patriarchs: and whosoever is born of woman is less than John. Perchance someone will say: If among them that are born of women John is the greater, is he greater than the Saviour? God forbid. For John was born of a woman, but Christ was born of a virgin. The one came forth from the recesses of a corruptible womb, the other was brought forth from the flower of a spotless virgin.
magnusigiturioannescuiusmagnitudinietiam.la: Magnus ígitur Joánnes, cujus magnitúdini étiam Salvátor testimónium perhibet, dicens: Non surréxit inter natos mulíerum major Joánne Baptísta. Præcéllit céteros, éminet univérsis: antecéllit Prophétas, supergréditur Patriárchas: et quisquis de mulíere natus est, inférior est Joánne. Dicet fortásse áliquis: Si inter natos mulíerum Joánnes major est, major est Salvatóre? Absit. Joánnes enim natus mulíeris, Christus autem vírginis natus est. Ille corruptíbilis úteri sínibus effúsus est, iste impollútæ vírginis flore progénitus.

siergointelligimusmysteriumfratresmeiioa.en: If therefore, my brethren, we understand the mystery, John is man, Christ is God. Let man be humbled, that God may be exalted, according to that which John himself said of the Lord: He must increase, but I must decrease. That man might be humbled, John was born on this day, from which the days begin to decrease: that God might be exalted, Christ was born on that day from which the days begin to increase. A great mystery, dearly beloved brethren. Therefore we celebrate the birthday of John as also that of Christ, because his birth also is full of mystery. Of what mystery, but of our humility, as the birth of Christ is full of the mystery of our exaltation?
siergointelligimusmysteriumfratresmeiioa.la: Si ergo intellígimus mystérium, fratres mei, Joánnes homo est, Christus Deus est. Humiliétur homo, ut exaltétur Deus, secúndum illud quod de Dómino ipse Joánnes dixit: Illum opórtet créscere, me autem mínui. Ut humiliarétur homo, hódie natus est Joánnes, quo incípiunt decréscere dies: ut exaltétur Deus, eо die natus est Christus, quo incípiunt créscere dies. Magnum sacraméntum, fratres caríssimi. Ideo celebrámus natálem Joánnis sicut et Christi, quia et ipsa natívitas plena est mystério. Quo mystério, nisi humilitátis nostræ, sicut natívitas Christi plena est mystério altitúdinis nostræ?

dehomiliasanctiambrosiiepicopi.en: From the Homily of St. Ambrose, Bishop.

ioannesestinquitnomeneiusnonpoteratelisa.en: John, saith she, is his name. Elizabeth could not be ignorant of the Lord's forerunner, she who had prophesied Christ. And well is it added: Because there was none of his kindred that was called by this name: that thou mayest understand that the name was not of the family, but of the prophet. Zachary also is asked by signs: but because unbelief had taken from him speech and hearing, what he could not with the voice, he spake with his hand and with letters.
ioannesestinquitnomeneiusnonpoteratelisa.la: Joánnes est, inquit, nomen ejus. Non póterat Elísabeth Dómini ignoráre prænúntium, quæ prophetáuerat Christum. Et bene ádditur: Quia nemo in cognatióne ejus vocabátur hoc nómine: ut intélligas nomen non géneris esse, sed vatis. Zacharías quoque nutu interrogátor: sed quia incredúlitas ei affátum eripúerat et audítum, quod voce non póterat, manu et lítteris est locútus.

scripsitautemdicensioannesestnomeneiuset.en: And he wrote, saying: John is his name. And here the name is not imposed, but confirmed. And rightly his tongue was forthwith loosed: because that which unbelief had bound, faith loosed. Let us also therefore believe, that we may speak; that our tongue, which is bound with the bonds of unbelief, may be loosed by the voice of reason.
scripsitautemdicensioannesestnomeneiuset.la: Scripsit autem dicens: Joánnes est nomen ejus. Et hic nomen non impónitur, sed astrúitur. Meritóque contínuo resolúta est lingua ejus: quia quam vínxerat incredúlitas, fides solvit. Credámus et nos ígitur, ut loquámur; ut lingua nostra, quæ incredulitátis vínculis est ligáta, ratiónis voce solvátur.

scribamusspiritumysteriasivolumusloquisc.en: Let us write the mysteries in spirit, if we would speak: let us write the forerunner of Christ, not on tables of stone, but on the fleshly tables of the heart. For he that speaketh John prophesieth Christ. Let us speak John, let us speak Christ also: that our mouth too may be opened, which, as in so great a priest, after the manner of a dumb beast, the reins of a wavering faith were restraining.
scribamusspiritumysteriasivolumusloquisc.la: Scribámus spíritu mystéria, si vólumus loqui: scribámus prænúntium Christi, non in tábulis lapidéis, sed in tábulis cordis carnálibus. Etenim qui Joánem lóquitur, Christum prophétat. Loquámur Joánnem, loquámur et Christum: ut nostrum quoque os possit aperíri, quod in sacerdóte tanto, irrationális modo pécudis, fræna nutántis fídei coërcebant.

nonsinecausafactumputemusfratrescarissim.en: Let us not think it came to pass without reason, dearly beloved brethren, that the most glorious princes of the Christian faith, Peter and Paul, on one day, in one place, suffered the sentence of one tyrant. They suffered on one day, that they might come to Christ together: in one place, that Rome might not lack either of them: under one persecutor, that an equal cruelty might bind both. The day therefore, I think, was appointed for their merit, the place for their glory, the persecutor for their virtue. And in what place, then, did they endure martyrdom? In the city of Rome, which holdeth the princedom and headship of the nations; to wit, that where the head of superstition was, there the head of holiness might rest; and where the princes of the Gentiles dwelt, there the princes of the churches might abide.
nonsinecausafactumputemusfratrescarissim.la: Non sine causa factum putemus, fratres carissimi, quod gloriosissimi Christianæ fidei principes Petrus et Paulus, una die, uno loco, unius tyranni toleravere sententiam. Una die passi sunt, ut ad Christum pariter pervenirent: uno in loco, ne lateri Roma deesset: sub uno persecutore, ut æqualis crudelitas utrumque constringeret. Dies ergo, puto, pro merito, locus pro gloria, persecutor decretus est pro virtute. Et in quo tandem loco martyrium pertulerunt? In urbe Roma, quæ principatum et caput obtinet nationum; scilicet ut ubi caput superstitionis erat, illic caput quiesceret sanctitatis; et ubi gentilium principes habitabant, illic ecclesiarum principes morarentur.

cuiusautemmeritisintbeatissimipetrusetpa.en: But of what merit are the most blessed Peter and Paul we may understand from this, that whereas the Lord enlightened the region of the East by his own passion, he vouchsafed, that it might be nothing less, to enlighten the quarter of the West in his stead with the blood of the apostles. And although his passion sufficeth us for salvation, yet their martyrdom also hath been given us for an example. On this day therefore the blessed apostles shed their blood: but let us see the cause why they suffered; to wit, that among other wonders they also by their prayers cast down that magician Simon from the void of the air in a headlong fall.
cuiusautemmeritisintbeatissimipetrusetpa.la: Cujus autem meriti sint beatissimi Petrus et Paulus, hinc possumus intelligere, quod cum Dominus Orientis regionem propria illustraverit passione; Occidentis plagam, ne quid minus esset, vice sui apostolorum sanguine illuminare dignatus est. Et licet illius passio nobis sufficiat ad salutem, tamen étiam horum martyrium nobis contulit ad exemplum. Hodierna igitur die beati apostoli sanguinem profuderunt: sed videamus causam quare isti perpessi sunt, scilicet quod inter cetera mirabilia étiam magum illum Simonem orationibus suis de aëris vacuo præcipiti ruina prostraverunt.

cumenimidemsimonsechristumdiceretettamqu.en: For when the same Simon said that he was Christ, and asserted that he could ascend by flying, as a son to his father, and, lifted up by magic arts, had suddenly begun to fly: then Peter, kneeling down, prayed to the Lord, and by holy prayer overcame the magic lightness. For the prayer ascended to the Lord before the flight, and the just petition arrived before the wicked presumption; Peter, set upon earth, obtained what he asked before Simon reached the heavenly places whither he was making. Then therefore Peter brought him down from the high air as one bound, and, dashing him headlong upon a rock, broke his legs: and this in reproach of that deed, that he who a little before had tried to fly suddenly could not walk, and he who had taken to himself wings lost his feet.
cumenimidemsimonsechristumdiceretettamqu.la: Cum enim idem Simon se Christum diceret, et tamquam filium ad patrem asseret volando se posse conscendere, atque elatus subito magicis artibus volare cæpisset: tunc Petrus fixis genibus precatus est Dominum, et precatione sancta vicit magicam levitatem. Prior enim ascendit ad Dominum oratio, quam volatus, et ante pervenit justa petitio, quam iniqua præsumptio; ante Petrus in terris positus obtinuit quod petebat quam Simon perveniret in cælestibus, quo tendebat. Tunc igitur Petrus velut vinctum illum de sublimi ære deposuit, et quodam præcipitio in saxo elidens ejus crura confregit: et hoc in opprobrio facti illius, ut qui paulo ante volare tentaverat, subito ambulare non posset, et qui pennas assumpserat, plantas amitteret.

oratdedormdeipare.en: Oration 2 on the Falling-asleep of the Mother of God

iubilemusinarcadominideitotoanimetmurica.en: Let us rejoice with all our soul in the ark of the Lord God, and the walls of Jericho shall fall, the hostile fortresses, I say, of the adverse powers. Let us exult in spirit with David. For the ark of the Lord hath this day come to rest. Let us cry out with Gabriel, who holdeth the first place among the angels: Hail, full of grace: the Lord is with thee. Hail, inexhaustible sea of joy. Hail, only relief of troubles. Hail, remedy of all the sorrows of the heart. Hail, holy virgin, through whom death was cast out, and life brought in.
iubilemusinarcadominideitotoanimetmurica.la: Jubilemus in arca Domini Dei toto animo, et muri cadent Hiericontini, contrariarum, inquam potestatum infestæ munitiones. Cum David exsultemus spiritu. Arca enim Domini hodie requievit. Clamemus cum Gabriele, qui primum locum obtinet inter angelos: Ave gratia plena: dominus tecum. Ave gaudii pelagus inexhaustum. Ave unicum molestiarum levamen. Aue omnium cordis dolorum medicamentum. Ave sancta virgo per quam mors quidem fuit expulsa, vita autem introducta.

desermonesanctiioannisdamasceni.en: From the Sermon of St. John Damascene

oratdedormitionedeiparesubfinem.en: Oration 2 on the Falling-asleep of the Mother of God, near the end
oratdedormitionedeiparesubfinem.la: Orat. 2 de Dormitione Deiparæ, sub finem

exantiquaaccepimustraditionequodtemporeg.en: We have received from ancient tradition, that at the time of the glorious falling-asleep of the blessed Virgin, all the holy Apostles, who were journeying through the world for the salvation of the Gentiles, being borne aloft in a moment of time, came together at Jerusalem. And when they were there, there appeared to them a vision of angels, and the psalmody of the heavenly Powers was heard; and so with divine glory she gave up her holy soul into the hands of God. But her body, which had in an unspeakable manner received God, being borne forth with the hymnody of angels and apostles, was laid in a tomb at Gethsemane; in which place the song of the Angels continued for three days together.
exantiquaaccepimustraditionequodtemporeg.la: Ex antíqua accépimus traditióne, quod témpore gloriósæ dormitiónis beátæ Virginis, univérsi quidem sancti Apóstoli, qui orbem terræ ad salútem Géntium peragrábant, moménto témporis in sublíme eláti, convenérunt Jerosólymis. Cumque illic essent, eis vísio appáruit angélica, et audíta est psalmodía cæléstium Potestátum; et sic cum divína glória in manus Dei sanctam trádidit ánimam. Ejus autem corpus, quod Deum ineffábili quadam ratióne suscépit, cum angélica et apostólica hymnodía elátum, in lóculo fuit depósitum Gethsemane; quo in loco Angelórum cantus mansit tres dies contínuos.

tuveroosacrorumsepulcrorumsacratissimump.en: But thou, O most sacred of sacred sepulchres, after the sepulchre of the Lord, which gave the beginning of life, which was the fountain of resurrection (for I will speak with thee as with a living thing), where is that pure gold which the hands of the apostles laid up in thee? Where are the riches which cannot be consumed? Where is the new volume, in which God the Word was unspeakably written without hand? Where is the abyss of grace? Where is the sea of healings? Where is that desirable body of the virgin Mother of God?
tuveroosacrorumsepulcrorumsacratissimump.la: Tu vero o sacrorum sepulcrorum sacratissimum, post domini quidem sepulcrum, quod uitæ dedit principium, quod fuit fons resurrectionis, (tecum enim loquar tamquam cum animato) ubinam est aurum illud purum, quod manus apostolorum in te condiderunt! Ubi divitiæ, quæ consumi nequeunt! Ubi novum uolumen, in quo ineffabiliter deus uerbum sine manu inscriptum fuit! Ubi abyssus gratiæ? Ubi pelagus curationum? Ubi est desiderabile illud deiparæ uirginis corpus?

posttresautemdiesangelicocantucessantequ.en: But after three days, the song of the Angels ceasing, the Apostles that were present opened the tomb (since Thomas alone, who had been absent, came after the third day, and desired to venerate the body that had received God); but in no part could they find her sacred body. And when they had found only the things in which she had been laid, and were filled with an unspeakable fragrance which came forth from them, they closed the tomb. Astonished at the wonder of this mystery, they could think only this, that he who was pleased to take flesh of the Virgin Mary, and to be made man and to be born, though he was God the Word and the Lord of glory, and who after the birth kept her virginity incorrupt; the same was pleased also, after she had departed, to honour her immaculate body, kept incorrupt, by translating it before the common and universal resurrection.
posttresautemdiesangelicocantucessantequ.la: Post tres autem dies angélico cantu cessante, qui áderant Apóstoli (cum unus Thomas, qui abfúerat, post tértium diem venísset, et, quod Deum suscéperat, corpus adoráre voluísset), túmulum aperuérunt; sed omni ex parte sacrum ejus corpus nequáquam inveníre potuérunt. Cum ea autem tantum inveníssent, in quibus fúerat compósitum, et ineffabili, qui ex iis proficiscebátur, essent odóre repléti, lóculum clausérunt. Ejus mystérii obstupefácti miráculo, hoc solum cogitáre potuerunt, quod, cui plácuit ex María Vírgine carnem súmere, et hóminem fíeri et nasci, cum esset Deus Verbum, et Dóminus glóriæ, quique post partum incorrúptam servávit ejus virginitátem; eídem étiam plácuit, et ipsíus, postquam migrávit, immaculátum corpus, incorrúptum servátum, translatióne honoráre ante commúnem et universálem resurrectiónem.

quidqueritisinsepulcreamqueadcelestiatra.en: Why seek ye in the sepulchre her who hath been translated to the heavenly tabernacles? why demand ye of me an account of my keeping? I cannot resist the divine commands. The most sacred body imparted holiness to me also, for it filled me with the fragrance of a most precious ointment, and made me a divine temple; leaving the linen cloths, it went away, caught up on high, angels, archangels, and all the heavenly powers accompanying it. Now angels surround me; now divine grace dwelleth in me. Therefore I am become a house of healing for the sick. I am a perpetual fountain of healings: I am a remedy against devils: I am a city of refuge for all that flee unto me.
quidqueritisinsepulcreamqueadcelestiatra.la: Quid quæritis in sepulcro eam, quæ ad cælestia translata est tabernacula? cur a me custodiæ rationem exposcitis? Non possum ego divinis jussis resistere. Sacrosanctum corpus mihi quoque sanctitatem impertivit quod me pretiosissimi unguenti fragrantia replevit, et divinum templum effecit relictis sindonibus, abiit raptum sublime, comitantibus angelis, archangelis, et omnibus cælestibus potentiis. Nunc me circumdant angeli; nunc divina in me habitat gratia. Ergo evasi officina medicinæ ægrotantibus. Ego sum fons perennis curationum: Ego remedium aduersus dæmones: Ego civitas refugii omnibus ad me confugientibus.

aderanttunccumapostolissanctissimustimot.en: There were present then with the Apostles the most holy Timothy, the first bishop of the Ephesians, and Dionysius the Areopagite, as he himself testifieth in those things which he wrote to the aforesaid Timothy concerning blessed Hierotheus, who himself also was then present, speaking thus: For even among the inspired Prelates themselves, when we also, as thou knowest, and many of our holy brethren, had come together to behold the body that gave the beginning of Life and received God (and there were present also James the brother of the Lord, and Peter, the supreme and most ancient summit of theologians): the sacred body having been seen, it pleased all, as each was able, to celebrate in hymns the infinite goodness of the divine power.
aderanttunccumapostolissanctissimustimot.la: Aderant tunc cum Apóstolis sanctíssimus Timotheus, primus epíscopus Ephesiórum, et Dionysius Areopagíta, sicut ipse testátur in iis, quæ de beáto Hierótheo, qui ipse quoque tunc áderat, scripsit ad prædíctum Timótheum, sic dicens: Nam étiam apud ipsos a Deo afflátos Sacrórum antístites, quando nos quoque, ut nosti, et multi ex sanctis nostris frátribus, ad contuéndum corpus, quod Vitæ princípium dedit, et Deum suscépit, convenissémus (áderat autem et Dómini frater Jacóbus, et Petrus, supréma et antiquíssima theologórum súmmitas): et viso sacro córpore, plácuit ómnibus, prout quisque póterat, hymnis celebráre infínitam bonitátem divínæ poténtiæ.

innativitatebmv.en: On the Nativity of the B. V. M.

remanseruntergoinilladomodebetotiosa.en: They remained therefore in that house ... ought to be idle.
remanseruntergoinilladomodebetotiosa.la: Remanserunt ergo in illa domo... debet otiosa.

erantergoinillastatisauditis.en: There were therefore in that ... having been heard.
erantergoinillastatisauditis.la: Erant ergo in illa ... statis auditis.

inquantumautemhocdatdeus.en: But in so far as this ... God giveth.
inquantumautemhocdatdeus.la: In quantum autem hoc ... dat deus.

itaquedominuslibenteringredituretineiusq.en: And therefore the Lord willingly entereth, and reclineth in the affection of him that hath believed. But again the envy of the faithless is kindled, and a figure of the punishment to come is foreshown. For while the faithful feast and recline in that kingdom of heaven, faithlessness shall be tormented with fasting. At the same time it is shown how great a difference there is between the zealots of the Law and those of grace; that they who follow the law suffer the eternal hunger of a fasting mind: but they who have received the word into the inward parts of the soul, being refreshed by the abundance of heavenly food and of the fountain, cannot hunger and thirst.
itaquedominuslibenteringredituretineiusq.la: Itaque Dominus libenter ingreditur, et in ejus qui crediderit, recumbit affectu. Sed rursus accenditur invidia perfidorum, et futuræ pœnæ species præfiguratur. Epulantibus enim fidelibus, et in illo cœlorum recumbentibus regno, perfidia jejuna torquebitur. Simul ostenditur quantum intersit inter æmulos Legis et gratiæ, quod illi qui legem sequuntur, jejunæ mentis famem patiantur æternam: qui vero verbum in interioribus animæ receperunt, alimenti cœlestis et fontis ubertate recreati esurire et sitire non possunt.

etideoquianimoieiunabantmurmurabantdicen.en: And therefore they that fasted in mind murmured, saying: Why doth he eat and drink with publicans and sinners? This is the serpent's voice. For the serpent uttered this as his first word, saying to Eve: Why hath God commanded you, that you should not eat of every tree? They therefore pour forth the venom of their father, who say: Why doth he eat and drink with publicans and sinners? Whence the Lord, by eating with sinners, forbiddeth us not to enter into a feast even with Gentiles, saying: They that are in health need not a physician, but they that are ill.
etideoquianimoieiunabantmurmurabantdicen.la: Et ideo qui animo jejunabant, murmurabant dicentes: Quare cum publicanis et peccatoribus manducat et bibit? Serpentina vox ista est. Denique hanc primam vocem serpens emisit, dicens Evæ: Quid utique dixit Deus: Nolite manducare ex omni ligno? Ergo patris sui venena diffundunt, qui dicunt: Quid utique cum publicanis et peccatoribus manducat et bibit? Unde Dominus cum peccatoribus manducando, etiam cum gentilibus non prohibet nos inire convivium, dicens: Non egent qui sani sunt, medico, sed qui male habent.

indominfraoctassumptbmarievirg.en: On the Sunday within the Octave of the Assumption of the B. Virgin Mary
indominfraoctassumptbmarievirg.la: In Dom. infra Oct. Assumpt. B. Mariae Virg.

eiuscorpuspostearomamnicolaoprimopontifi.en: These things moved Trajan to send a messenger to the Crimea, who tied an anchor about Clement's neck, and cast him into the deep of the sea. After it had been done, while the Christians were praying on the shore, the sea went back three miles, and when they followed it, they found a grotto of marble, in form like a temple, and therein a stone coffin wherein was laid the body of the Martyr, and, hard by, the anchor wherewith he had been sunk. Then were the country people moved to receive the faith of Christ. The body of Clement was afterwards brought to Rome, in the time of Pope Nicholas I, and buried in his own Church. A Church was also built in the Crimea, in the place where God had made the water to break forth. Clement lived as Pope nine years, six months, and six days. He held two Ordinations in the month of December, wherein he made ten Priests, two Deacons, and fifteen Bishops for diverse places.
eiuscorpuspostearomamnicolaoprimopontifi.la: (English data with its first sentence left in Latin) Ejus corpus postea Romam Nicolao Primo Pontifice translatum, in Ecclesia ipsius

inillotemporedixitiesusphariseisparabola.en: At that time, Jesus spoke to the Pharisees this parable: A certain man gave a great supper, and he invited many. And he sent his servant at supper time to tell those invited to come, for everything is now ready. And they all with one accord began to excuse themselves. The first said to him, ‘I have bought a farm, and I must go out and see it; I pray you hold me excused.’ And another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am on my way to try them; I pray you hold me excused.’ And another said, ‘I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.’ And the servant returned, and reported these things to his master. Then the master of the house was angry and said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in here the poor, and the crippled, and the blind, and the lame.’ And the servant said, ‘Sir, your order has been carried out, and still there is room.’ Then the master said to the servant, ‘Go out into the highways and hedges, and make them come in, so that my house may be filled. For I tell you that none of those who were invited shall taste of my supper.’
inillotemporedixitiesusphariseisparabola.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Iesus pharisǽis parábolam hanc: Homo quidam fecit cœnam magnam, et vocávit multos. Et misit servum suum hora cœnæ dícere invitátis, ut venírent, quia iam paráta sunt ómnia. Et cœpérunt simul omnes excusáre. Primus dixit ei: Villam emi, et necésse hábeo exíre et vidére illam: rogo te, habe me excusátum. Et alter dixit: Iuga boum emi quinque et eo probáre illa: rogo te, habe me excusátum. Et álius dixit: Uxórem duxi, et ídeo non possum veníre. Et revérsus servus nuntiávit hæc dómino suo. Tunc irátus paterfamílias, dixit servo suo: Exi cito in pláteas et vicos civitátis: et páuperes ac débiles et cæcos et claudos íntroduc huc. Et ait servus: Dómine, factum est, ut imperásti, et adhuc locus est. Et ait dóminus servo: Exi in vias et sepes: et compélle intrare, ut impleátur domus mea. Dico autem vobis, quod nemo virórum illórum, qui vocáti sunt, gustábit cœnam meam.

sequentiasanctievangeliisecundumlucam.en: Continuation + of the Holy Gospel according to Luke
